Quoniam magnus es tu, et faciens mirabilia; You are Deus solus magnus. Nemo se dicat magnum. Futuri werent qui se dicerent magnos: contra hos dicitur, T« is Deus solus magnus.

Nam quid magnum dicitur Deo, quia ipse est solus Deus magnus? Quis hoc nescit, quia ipse est Deus magnus? Sed quia futuri erant, qui se dicerent magnos, et Deum facerent parvum; contra illos dicitur, tu es solus Deus magnus. Etenim quod tu dicis, impletur, non quod illi dicunt, qui se dicunt magnos. Quid dixit Deus per Spiritum suum? Omnes gentes quotquot fecisti, venient, et adorabunt coram te, Domine. Quid dicit nescio quis, qui se dicit magnum? Absit: non adoratur Deus in omnibus gentibus; perierunt omnes gentes, only Africa remansit. Hoc tu dicis, qui te dicis magnum; aliud dicit qui est solus Deus magnus. Quid dicit who is so-
Narrations about the Psalms

They will love and adore you. I see what the only exalted God said; The falsely exalted man remains silent, and all the more fallaciously exalted because he disdained being small. Who deigned to become small? He who said: Anyone who wants to be great among you must be your servant. If anyone intends to be a servant of his brothers, do not separate them from their mother; because by wanting to be exalted and not healthily small, God, who opposes the proud and gives grace to the humble because he alone is exalted, fulfills everything he predicted and contradicts the cursers. Those who say that the Church perished throughout the world and is only left in Africa insult Christ. If you said to this one: You will lose the fifth, perhaps he would turn your hand; and he dares to say that Christ lost his inheritance redeemed by his blood! See, brothers, how great an injury I do to him; The Scripture says: In the multitude of the people is the glory of the king, and in the scarcity of the people the affliction or ignominy of the prince. Then you insult Christ by saying that his people were reduced to this trifle. Were you born, did you become a Christian to deny the glory of Christ, of whom you claim to bear on your forehead the sign that you destroyed in your heart? In the multitude of the people is the glory of the king; Recognize your king, glorify him, assign him a great people. What big town will I assign to you? Do not assign it to him because of the feelings of your heart, and in this way you will assign him the appropriate one. What will I use to assign it to him, you say? Pay attention to this: All the nations that you made, O Lord, will come and worship you. Say this, confess this, and you will assign him a large town, because all the towns in conlus Deus magnus? Omnes gentes quotquot fecisti, venient, et adorabunt coram te, Domine, Video quod dixit solus Deus magnus; taceat homo false magnus; ideo fallaciter magnus, quia dedignatur esse parvus. Quis parvus esse dedignatur? This is what I said. Quicumque vult Inter vos maior esse, dixit Dominus, erit vester servus (Mt 20,26). Ule si servus vellet esse fratrum suorum, non eos separaet a marre ipsorum: sed curn vult esse magnus, et non vult esse salubriter parvus; Deus qui superbis resistit, humilibus autem dat gratiam (Iac 4,6), quia solus est magnus, implet omnia quae praedixit, et contradicit maledicentibus. Christo enim tales maledicunt, who dicunt quia periit Ecclesia de toto orbe terrarum, et remansit in sola Africa.

If you say illis, Perdes villam mam; forte non a te temperaret manum: et dicit Christum perdidisse haereditatem suam redemptam sanguine suo! Quam autem faciat íniuriam videte, fratres. Scriptura dicit: In lata gente gloria regís; in diminutione populi contritio principis (Prov 14:28). Ergo hanc iniuiiam facis Christo, utdicas populum eius ad istam exiguitatem diminutujn. Ideo natus es, ideo christianum te dicis, ut ínvideas gloriae Christi, cuius signum te in fronte portare asseris, et de corde perdidisti? In lata gente gloria regís: agnosce regem tuum; da illi gloriam, da illi latam gentem. Quam latam gentem dabo, inquis? Noli ex tuo corde daré, et recte dabis. Where do you wonder? Ecce hinc da: Omnes gentes quotquot fecisti, venient, et adorabunt cofam te, Domine. Dic hoc, confitete hoc, et dedisti latam gentem: quia om-
Request for help from God

Together they constitute a single people and He is the unity. As the Church is the same as Churches, and Churches, Church; Thus the town is the same as all towns. Before they were towns, many towns; Now it is one town. Why just one town? Because there is only one faith, one hope, one charity, one single desire. In short, why shouldn't there be only one people, if there is only one country? The homeland is celestial; the homeland is Jerusalem. He who is not a citizen of it does not belong to this town. Everyone who is a citizen of it belongs to the only people of God. This people extends throughout the four parts of the world, from east to west, from the north to the sea. God says this: Glorify God from the east to the west, from the north to the sea. He who alone is exalted said this, and he fulfilled it. Stop speaking against the only exalted one who did not want to be small, because there cannot be two exalted ones, God and Donato. 15 [v. l l ]. Guide me, Lord, in your path and I will walk in your truth. Christ is your way, your truth and your life. Therefore it is Body with respect to him, and Body of him. I am the way, the truth and the life. Guide me, Lord, on your path. On what path? And I will walk in your truth. It is one thing to guide on the path, and another to guide on the path. See a man in complete poverty, who needs no help at all. Those who are out of the way, are not Christians or are not yet Catholic, be led to the way; but as soon as you have been taken and set on the path, and have been made Catholics in Christ, let them be guided by him in the same path so that they do not perish. Without a doubt, there are already two people in one; ipsa est unitas. Quomodo enim Ecclesia et Ecclesiae, illae Ecclesiae quae Ecclesia; sic illa gens quae gentes: antea gentes,mulae gentes; manner a gens. Quare a gens? Quia a fides, quia a spes, quia a charitas, quia an exspectatio. Postremo quare non una gens, si una patria? Patria caelestis est, patria Ierusalem est: quisquís inde civis non est, ad istam gentem non pertinet; quisquís autem inde civis est, in una gente Dei est. Et haec gens ab oriente in occidentem, ab aquilone et mari distenditur per quatuor parts totius orbis. Hoc Deus dicit: Ab oriente et occidente, ab aquilone et mari date gloriam Deo. Hoc praedixit, hoc implevit, qui solus est magnus.

Desinat ergo hoc dicere contra solum magnum, qui noluit esse parvus: quia non possunt esse duo magni, Deus et Donatus. 15 [v. l l ]. Deduc me, Domine, in via tua, et ambulabo in veritate tua. Via tua, veritas tua, vita tua, Christus. Ergo Corpus ad illum, et corpus de illo. Ego sum via, et veritas, et vita (lo 14,6). Deduc me, Domine, in vita tua. In what way? Et ambulabo in veritate tua. Aliud est, ut ducat ad viam; aliud, ut deducat in via. Vide hominem ubique pauperem, ubique adiutorio egentem. Qui praeter viam sunt, christiani non sunt, aut catholici nondum sunt, deducantur ad viam: sed cum perducti fuerint ad viam, et catholici in Christo facti fuerint; ab ipso deducantur in ipsa via, ne cadant. Certe iam ambulant in via. Deduc me, Domine, in via tua: certe iam in via tua sum, deduc me ibi. Et ambulabo in
narrations about the Psalms
Request for help from God

along the way. Guide me, Lord, on your path: I am already certainly on your path, guide me on it. And I will walk in your truth: as you guide me, I will not err; If you abandon me, I will err. Pray, then, that he may not abandon you, but guide you to the end. How do you guide? Continuously admonishing, always giving you his hand. And the arm (power) of God, to whom was it manifested? Giving you his Christ gives you his hand; Giving you his hand, he gives you his Christ. It leads to the path leading towards its Christ. He guides the way carrying in his Christ, and Christ is the truth. Then guide me, Lord, in your path and I will walk in your truth. In him who truly says: I am the way, the truth and the life. If you lead in the way and in the truth, where do you lead if not to life? Then in it you guide towards it. Guide me, Lord, in your path and I will walk in your truth. 16. Let my heart be glad to fear your name. Therefore in joy there is fear. But how will there be joy if there is fear? Isn't fear usually sad? There will be joy without fear at some time; but now joy comes with fear, since complete security and perfect joy do not yet exist. If joy is completely missing, we faint; If we have perfect security, we do not rejoice. Spread joy and instill fear, so that from the pleasure of joy it leads us to the abode of security. Giving us fear will not make us rejoice and stray badly from the path. That is why the psalm says: Serve the Lord with fear and rejoice in him with trembling. Thus also says the Apostle: With fear and trembling work out your salvation, for it is God who works in you. Then, brothers, more

We should well fear for everything prosperous that happens to us; since what you think is prosperous is rather temptation. An inheritance falls to our lot, abundant riches come to us, unexpected happiness flows; all this is temptation; Be careful that they do not corrupt you. Everything that is conformed to Christ and to the fraternal charity of Christ is counted as prosperous. If perhaps you won your wife who belonged to Donato's party; if perhaps your children believed that they were pagans; if perhaps you profited from your friend, who wanted to drag you to the theater and you took him to church; If perhaps a certain opponent and enemy of yours who became furiously angry, and, once his anger is over, becomes meek and recognizes God, and does not criticize you, but despises what is evil with you, you will say that these are things worthy of joy. What do we rejoice in if we do not rejoice in these things? Or what other joys do we have outside of these? But since tribulations, temptations, dissensions, schisms and a series of evils abound, without which this century cannot be found; Until iniquity disappears, we do not believe ourselves safe in that joy, but let our hearts be so glad that they fear the name of the Lord, so that they will not rejoice on the one hand and be hurt on the other. Do not expect happiness in the pilgrimage. Pretending to possess it here is more a bond of the body than human security. May my heart rejoice that I fear your name.

veritate tua: you deduct, non errabo; If you resign, I err. Ora ergo ut non dimittat, sed usque in finem deducat. How do I deduce? Always continuing, always giving warm manum suam. Et brachium Domini cui reveiatum est? (Is 53,1). Dando enim Christum suum, dat manum suam; giving manum suam, Christum suum dat. Ad viam ducit, perducing ad Christum suum; in via deducit, deducing in Christo suo: Christus autem veritas. Deduc me ergo, Domine, in via tua, et ambulabo in veritate tua: in illo utique qui ait, Ego sum fia, et veritas, et vita. Nam qui in via et veritate deducís, quo nisi ad vitam perducis? You deduce ergo in illo, ad illum. Deduc me, Domine, in via tua, et ambulabo in veritate tua. 16. lucundetur cor meum, ut timeat nomen tuum. Ergo timor in iucunditate est. Et quomodo iucunditas, si timor? Nonne timor amarus solet esse? Erit aliquando iucunditas sine timore, moda iucunditas cum timore: nondum est enim plena securitas, nec perfection iucunditas. Si nulla iucunditas, deficímus; If plena securitas, male exsultamus. Ergo et iucunditatem aspergat, et timorem incutiat, ut de dulcedine iucunditatis perducat nos ad sedem securitatis: dar timorem, non nos faciat male exsultare, et recedere de via. Ideo dicit psalmus, Servite Domino in timare, et exsultate ei cum tremore (Ps 2,11): sic et apostolus Paulus dicit, Cum timore et tremore vestram ipsorum salutem operamini; Deus enim est qui operatur in vobis (Phil 2,12.13). Quidquid ergo prosperum

come, fratres, magis metuendum est: quae putatis prospera, magis temptationes sunt. Venit haereditas, venitcopia rerum, abundat circumfluentia nescio cuius felicitatis: temptationes sunt istae; cávete ne vos ist corruptant. Quidquid etiam prosperum est secundum Christum et germanam charitatem Christi: si forte lucratus es uxorem mam quae Fuit in parte Donati; si forte crediderunt filii tui qui fuerunt pagani; si forte lucratus es amicum tuum qui te volebat seducere ad theatra, et tu eum duxisti ad ecclesiam; si forte contradictor nescio quis inimicus tuus et rabide saeviens, deposita illa rabie factus est mitis, et agnovit Deum, nec oblatrat adversus te, sed clamat tecum adversus malum: ista iucunda sunt. Unde enim gaudemus, si de his non gaudemus? aut quae sunt alia gaudia nostra, nisi ista? Be quia abundant et tribulationes, et temptationes, et dissensiones, et schismata, et caetera mala, sine quibus non potest esse saeculum hoc, doñee transeat iniquitas; exsultatio illa non nos faciat securas, sed ita iucundetur cor nostrum, ut timeat nomen Domini, ne abunde iucundetur, aliunde fairtur. Securitatem non exspectetis in peregrinatione: quando illam hic voluerimus, viscum erit corporis, non securitas hominis. Iucundetur cor meum, ut timeat nomen tuum. 17 [v.12.13]. Confitebor tibi, Domine Deus meus, in tofo corde meo, et glorificabo nomen tuum in aeternum; quoniam mercy tua magna est super me, et eruisti animam meam ex inferno inferiore. Quod
17 [v. 12-13]. I will praise you, O Lord my God, with all my heart, and I will glorify your name forever; because your mercy is great toward me, because you brought my soul out of
Ennarrations on the Psalms

lower hell. Do not worry, brothers, because what I have just told you does not explain to you as certain; Well, I am a man and I only dare to say what I can understand from the Holy Scripture; Don't expect anything from me. Neither I nor you have yet experienced hell. Maybe this has another meaning, and it's not hell. This passage is not clear. However, since the Scripture, which cannot be contradicted, says: You brought my soul out of the lower hell, let us understand that there are two hells: the upper and the lower. Because how do you say lower hell if it is not because there is a higher hell? I would not call a thing hell (lower or abyss) if it were not for the similarity of the upper (or upper) part. It appears clear, brothers, that there is a certain celestial abode that belongs to the angels; she is the life of ineffable joys; there is immortality and incorruption; there all things are permanent according to the gift and grace of God. That is the superior region of beings. If the former is superior, this, where flesh and blood dwell, where corruption, birth and death, decession and succession, mortality and inconstancy, fear, greed, dread, uncertain joy, weak hope and perishable goods occur, is earthly; and I believe that this entire region cannot be compared to the heaven of which I spoke shortly before. However, without comparing this region with the other, the former is superior (it is at the top), this is inferior (it is at the bottom). After death, where do we go from here if there is no hell more inferior than this hell, in which we live in flesh and in this mortality? For the body is dead, says the Apostle, because of sin. Then tamdicimus, fratres, hoc si non vobis tanquam certus exposuero, ne succenseatis. Homo sum enim, et quantum conceditur de Scripturis sanctis, tantum audeo dicere: nihil ex me. Infernum nec ego expertus sum adhuc, nec vos: et fortassis alia via erit, et non per infernum erit. Incerta sunt haec. Verum quia dicit Scriptura, cui contradici non potest, Eruisti animara meam ex inferno inferiore; intelligimus tanquam duo inferna esse, superius, et inferius: nam unde infernum inferius, nisi quia est infernum superius? Aliud non diceretur infernum, nisi in comparatione illius superioris partís.

Videtur ergo, fratres, esse inhabited quaedam caelestis Angelorum: ibi vita ineffabilium gaudiorum, ibi immortalitas et incorruptio, ibi omnia secundum Dei donum et gratiam permanentia. Illa pars rerum superna est. Si ergo illa superna est; haec terrena, ubi caro et sanguis, ubi corruptibilitas, ubi nativitas et mortalitas, ubi decessio atque successio, ubi mutabilitas et inconstantia, ubi timotes, cupiditates, horrores, laetitiae incertae, spes fragilis, caduca substantia; puto quia omnis ista pars non potest comparan illi cáelo de quo loquebar paulo ante: si ergo illi partí haec pars non comparatur, illa superna est, haec inferna. Et post mortem quo hinc, nisi sit infernum inferius hoc inferno, in quo sumus in carne, et is this mortalitate? Corpus enim mortuum est, ait Apostolus, propter peccatum (Rom 8:10). Ergo et hic sunt mortui; ut non mireris quia infernum dicitur, si mortuis abundat. Non enim ait, Corpus
Request for help from God

Well there are dead people in this world; So don't be surprised because it is called hell if it abounds in dead people. Well, it does not say the body must die, but rather the body is dead. Our body still lives, and yet, in comparison with the body that is to be similar to that of the angels, we see that the body of man is dead although it still lives united to the soul. But, in addition to this hell, that is, this part of hell, there is another one below, where the dead will go, and from where God wanted to take our souls by sending his Son there. In fact, brothers, the Son of God was sent to these two kinds of hell, delivering from both sides. The first was sent being born, the second dying. Therefore, it is his voice that is heard in the psalm, and this not because any man conjectures it, but because the Apostle affirms it when he explains the verse of the psalm: For you will not abandon my soul in hell. Then it is his voice that says you freed your soul from the lower hell; or ours, uttered by Christ our Lord himself; because he went to hell so that we would not remain in it. 18. I will present another sentence. Perhaps in hell there is a lower region, where those who have seriously sinned are thrown. Well, we cannot establish with complete precision that Abraham was not in certain places in hell; for the Lord had not yet descended into hell to take from there the souls of all the saints who had preceded him, and yet Abraham was there in complete rest. Furthermore, a certain rich man, being tormented in hell, when he saw Abraham, lifted up his eyes. No moriturum est; thirst, Corpus mortuum est. Adhuc habet vitam utique corpus nostrum; et tamen comparatum corpori illi, quod futurum est qualia sunt Angelorum corpora, invenitur corpus hominis mortuum, quamvis adhuc habens animam. Sed rursus ab hoc inferno, id est ab hac parte inferni, est aliud inferius, quo eunt mortui; unde voluit Deus eruere animas nostras, etiam illuc mittens Filium suum. Etenim, fratres, propter ista duo inferna missus est Filius Dei, undique liberans. Ad hoc infernum missus est nascendo, ad illud dying.

Propterea vox eius est in illo psalmo, non quoquam nomine coniiciente, sed Apostólo exponente, ubi ait: Quoniam non derelinques animam meam in inferno (Ps 15,10; Acts 2,27). Ergo aut ipsius vox est et hic, Eruisti animam meam ex inferno inferiore: aut nostra vox per ipsum Christum Dominum nostrum; Quia ideo ille pervenit usque ad infernum, ne nos remaneremus in inferno. 18. Aliam etiam opinionem dicam. Fortassis enim apud ipsos inferos est aliqua pars inferior, quo truduntur impii qui plurimum peccaverunt. Etenim apud inferos utrum in locis quibusdam non Fuisset Abraham, non satis possumus defineré. Nondum enim Dominus venerat ad infernum, ut erueret inde omnium sanctorum praecedentium animas, et tamen Abraham in requie ibi erat. Et quidam dives cum torqueretur apud inferos, cum videret Abraham, levavit oculos. Non eum posset levatis oculis videre, nisi ille esset superius, ille inferius. Et quid ei re-
^.narratives about the Psalms

I could have seen him raising my eyes, unless he had been above and the rich man below. But what did Abraham answer when the rich man said to him, Send Lazarus so that, having wet his finger, he may let a drop of water fall on my tongue, because I am tormented in this flame: Son, remember that you received good things on earth, and Lazarus bad things. Now, however, he rests here and you are tormented, and to this he adds: You see that between us and you there is a great abyss, so that neither we can pass over you, nor from there you can pass over us. Then perhaps considering these two hells, in one of which the souls of the just rested, and in the other the souls of the wicked are tormented, praying here a certain individual who already belonged to the body of Christ, and praying with the voice of Christ, said that God freed his soul from the lower hell, because he was freed from falling into the sins for which he could have been taken to the torments of the lower hell. If a doctor, seeing that you are going to fall into an imminent illness due to a certain job, tells you: Take care of yourself, treat yourself this way, rest and eat these foods, because, if you don't do this, you will get sick; and you, fulfilling his prescription, see yourself free from the disease, what do you rightly say to the doctor? You freed me from illness; not the one you had fallen into, but the one you were going to fall into. The same thing happens to an individual who, having a difficult lawsuit, for which he had to be confined in jail, when presented with a lawyer who defends him by bringing him out, what does he say to her, thanking him? You freed me from jail. Likewise, if a debtor must be hanged, and another individual cancels the debt for him, it is also said: He saved him from hanging. In all these cases they were not already condemned, spondit Abraham, cum diceret, "Pater Abraham, mitte Lazarum, ut intinguat digitum suum, et stillet in linguam meam, quoniam crucior in hac flamma? Fili", ait, "memento quia recepisti bona in vita tua; Lazarus autem mala: nunc autem hic requiescit, tu vero torqueris. Et super haec", ait, "Inter nos et ros magnum chaos firmatum est;

Ergo Inter ista duo fortasse inferna, quorum in uno quieverunt animae iustorum, in altero torquentur animae impiorum, attendens quídam orans hic, iam hic in corpore Christi positus, et orans in voce Christi, eruisse Deum animam suam ab inferno inferiore dixit, quia liberavit se a talibus peccatis peí quae posset deduci ad storm inferni inferioris. Quemadmodum si medicus videat tibi imminentem aegritudinem forte ex aliquo labore, et dicat, Parce tibi, sic te tracta, requiesce, his cibis utere; nam si non feceris, aegrotabis: tu autem si feceris et salvus fueris, recte dícis medico, Liberasti me ab aegritudine; non in qua iam eras, sed in qua futurus eras. Nescio quis habens causam molestam, mittendus erat in carcerem; come alius, defendit eum: gratias agens quid dicit? Eruisti animam meam de carcere. Suspendendus erat debitor; solutum est pro eo: liberatus dicitur de suspended. In his omnibus they were not;
Request for help from God

But since they had such faults that, if they had not been helped, they would already find themselves in such punishments, hence it is rightly said that they were freed from those punishments, where they were prevented from being taken because of their liberators. Therefore, brothers, whether this or that is the true sentence, recognize in me, in this matter, a researcher of the word of God, not a reckless affirmer. And you brought my soul out of the lower hell. 19 [v. 14]. The transgressors of the law have risen up against me, O God! Who do you call lawbreakers? Not to the pagans, who did not receive the law. No one transgresses the law that he has not received. The Apostle says strictly: Where there is no law, there is no transgression. He calls its transgressors prevaricators of the law. Brothers, who are these? If we listen to the voice of the Lord, the transgressors of the law were the Jews. They rose up against me, breaking the law. They did not keep the law, and accused Christ as if he had broken the law. The lawbreakers rose up against me. And the Lord suffered what we know. Do you think your body is suffering from any of this now? How is this to happen? If they called the father of families Beelzebui, how much more so his servants! The disciple is not more than the teacher, nor the servant more than his master. Therefore the Body also suffers because of the transgressors of the law; and they also rise up against the Body of Christ. But who are the lawbreakers? Do the Jews dare to rise up against Christ? No, because they do not cause us great tribulation. They have not yet believed, they have not yet recognized health. Against the Body of Christ the evil ones rise up sed quia talibus mentís agebantur, ut nisi subventum esset, ibi essent; inde se recte dicunt liberari, quo per liberatores suos non sunt permissi perduci. Ergo, fratres, sive illud, sive illud sit; hic me scrutatorem verbi Dei, non temerarium affirmatorem teneatis. Et eruisti animam meam ex inferno inferiore. 19 [v.14]. Deus, praetereuntes legem insurrexerunt super me. Quos dicit praetereuntes legem? Non Paganos, qui non acceperunt legem. Nemo enim praeterit quod non accepit: dicit Apostolus definite, Ubi enim lex non est, nec praevaricatio (Rom 4:15). Praetereuntes legem, praevaricatores legis dicit. Quos ergo intelligimus, fratres?

Si ab ipso Domino accipiamus hanc vocem, praetereuntes legem ludaei erant. Insurrexerunt super me praetereuntes legem: non servaverunt legem, et accusaverunt Christum, quasi ipse praetereuntes legem. Praetereuntes legem insurrexerunt super me. Et passus est Dominus quae novimus. Whores nihil tale patitur Corpus eius mode? Unde fieri potest? If patrem families Beekebub vocaverunt; How much domestic magis eius? Non est discipulus super magistrum, nec servus super dominum suum (Mt 10,25.24). Patitur et corpus praetereuntes legem; et insurgunt super Corpus Christi. Praetereuntes legem qui sunt? Numquid forte ludaei audent insurgere super Christum? Non: nam nec ipsi nobis valde faciunt tribulationem. Nondum enim crediderunt, nondum salutem agnoverunt. Insurgunt super corpus
Ennarrations on the Psalms

Christians, from whom the Body of Christ endures daily tribulations. All the schisms, all the heresies, all those who live badly within themselves and try to impose their customs on those who live well, and drag them to their way of being and corrupt good customs with perverse conversations, all of these, breaking the law, rose up against me. Let every pious soul speak; speak every Christian soul. Whoever does not suffer from this, do not speak. If you are a Christian soul, you know that you endure evils; If you recognize your suffering in yourself, recognize your voice here. If it is far from suffering, it is foreign to this voice. In order not to be a stranger to suffering, walk the narrow path and begin to live godly in Christ, because you need to endure this persecution. All, says the Apostle, who desire to live piously in Christ will endure persecutions. O God, the transgressors of the law have risen against me, and the synagogue of the powerful has sought my soul. The synagogue of the powerful is the congregation of the proud. What do I say? He didn't say iterum, again, but adhuc, still. Because iterum sitiet, they will be thirsty again, it appears as if, fed up, he turned away and, having digested, drank again. What was written is this: Qui edunt te, ADHUC esurient, those who eat you, still feel hungry. In this way, when they eat, they feel hungry, and those who drink you, in the same way, when drinking, feel thirsty. What does "drinking, they feel thirsty" mean? They never get enough. So if this sweetness is to be ineffable and everlasting, now, what does it ask of us, brothers? Unfeigned faith, firm hope and ardent charity, and may man walk along the path that God commanded him, and may he endure temptations and accept consolation.

SERMON 1. The psalm that was now sung is brief in words, but of great weight for its sentences. The whole thing was read, and you have seen in what short time it was finished. Now, as soon as the Lord deigns to grant me, I will explain your charity, having been incited by our most blessed Father, who is present. The unexpected proposition would overwhelm me if I were not instantly helped by the proposer's prayer. Take care of your charity. In this psalm a certain city is sung and remembered, of which we are citizens since we are Christians. Waiting for her, we make a pilgrimage while we are mortal and we turn to her; But, as the road was barely visible as it was almost completely intercepted by bushes and thistles, the king of the same city made a path so that we could reach it. Then, walking in Christ, and still on a pilgrimage until we arrive, and sighing for the desire of a certain ineffable rest that exists in that city, of which what was promised to us was said, which eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor entered into the heart of man, let us sing in such a way that we long. Because whoever wishes, even if the tongue is silent, sings with the heart. Whoever does not desire, even if he hurts the ears of men with any cry, remains silent for God. Let's see what the twelve thrones mean. It is a symbolism of universality, since the Church was to extend throughout the entire globe of the earth, from which this building, the Church, is called to the connection of Christ. Therefore, since this building must come from all sides to be judged, there are twelve thrones, just as there are twelve doors through which one enters that city from all sides. 1 [v.l}. The title of this 87th psalm contains something that offers a new subject to the expositor. In no verse of the other psalms was what is read here recorded: In favor of Melech; to be sung alternatively. I have already said on other occasions what I thought was what "psalm song" and "psalm song" mean. The words for the sons of Korah, which are usually recorded in the titles of the psalms, have also been frequently discussed; I also explained what it means for the jin. But what follows: In favor of Melech; to be sung alternately, is unusually recorded in this psalm. However, in favor of Melech can be translated in Latin as pro choro, in favor of the choir, since the Hebrew word Melech means choir. So what does it mean: In favor of the choir; to be sung alternatively, but perhaps the choir responds by harmonizing with the one who sings? Thus I believe that not only this psalm was sung, but also others, although they have other titles, which I think was done for the sake of variety, so as not to cause boredom. When they translated this word zimos from the books of the Greek philosophers into Latin, they translated it with the name wrath. This does not have to be disputed at length. However, if we must use another word, we will more tolerably say indignation than fury. Since fury, according to the property of the Latin language, does not usually apply to the healthy. Then what does it mean that your anger was consolidated on me if not that those who did not know the glory of God believed this? They believed that the wrath of God was not only aroused, but also consolidated upon Him, whom they could carry to death; and not to any death, but to what they considered the most execrable of all, that is, even death on a cross. Hence the Apostle says: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us, because it is written: "Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree." It continues in the psalm with this verse: et omnes suspensions tuas, and all your suspensions; or as some translated: et omnes fluctus tuos, and all your waves; or as others also: et omnes elationes tuas super me induxisti, and all your elevations you cast upon me: omnes suspensions tuae et fluctus tui super me ingressi sunt, and all your suspensions and waves. they penetrated me; or as some better translated: super me transierunt, they passed over me, since in Greek it is written dielzon, not eiselzon. Then in donetiam hoc irae verterint in latinum: ñeque de hac re diutius disputandum est; latinum habet eloquium, non solet esse sanarum, Quid ergo est, In me confirmata est ira tua; nisi quemadmodum illi putaverunt, qui Dominum gloriae non cognoverunt? sed quam prae caeteris exsecrabilius habebant, id est, usque ad mortem crucis perducere potuerunt.

Unde dicit Apostolus: Christus redeemed us from maledicto Legis, factus pro nobis maledictum; scriptum est enim, Maledictus omnis qui pendet in ligno (Gal 3:13). Et ideo eum eius obedientiam usque ad extremem humilitatem commendare vellet, Humiliavit, inquit, semetipsum, factus obediens usque ad mortem: quod eum parum videretur, adiecit, mortem autem crucis (Phil 2,8). Proprer hoc, quantum mihi videtur, etiam in isto psalmo talis versus sequitur: Eí omnes suspensions tuas; vel, sicut quidam sunt interpretati, omnes fluctus tuos; aut, sicut alii, omnes elationes tuas super me induxisti. Scriptum est et in alio psalmo, Omnes suspensiones tuae, et fluctus tui super me ingressi sunt (Ps 41,8): vel, sicut quidam melius transtulerunt, super me transierunt; SiíjAeov enim est in graeco, non EicrñAeov. Ubi ergo utrumque positum est, et suspensions et fluctus,

When the two words suspensions et fluctus were recorded, suspensions and waves, they could not be replaced one by the other. I already explained these two words, saying that the suspensions are the threats, and the hearings are the same sufferings, which also come from the judgment of God. But in Psalm 41 it was said: omnes super me transierunt, they all passed over me, and in this one we are commenting on: omnes super me induxisti, you cast them all over me. Then there, even when some of these things took place, however, he wanted it to be understood that in those words super me transierunt, passed over me, all the evils that he announced were enclosed, and here he enclosed them in the words super me induxisti, you cast them on me. Therefore, either things pass that do not touch, such as suspensions or elevations, or those that do touch, such as waves. However, by not saying: "All the exaltations passed over me," but you cast them upon me, he designates that all those that were to come threatened, well they threatened, while all the things that were predicted about his passion were foreshadowed in the prophecy as future. 8 [v.9.10]. You took my acquaintances away from me. If we understand that He said my acquaintances by those He knew, then they will be all of them, because who does He not know? But he calls those who knew him acquaintances insofar as they could know him then. Without a doubt, until then they knew that he was innocent, even if they only thought that he was a man and not God. He was also able to call the good known, whom He had to receive or recognize, just as He called the bad unknown, whom He had to reject or condemn, to whom He had to say in the end: I do not know you. In what he added: They considered me an abomination, those whom he called his strangers can also be understood, because they likewise non ibi potuerunt poni pro suspensionibus fluctus. Quae duo sic exposuimus, ut suspensions diceremus comminationes, fluctus autem iam ipsas passiones: quae utraque veniunt de iudicio Dei. Sed illic dictum est, Omnes super me transierunt; hic vero, Omnes super induxisti me. Illic ergo etsi quaedam acciderunt; omnia tamen mala quae illis verbis intelligi voluit, super me transierunt, dixit: hic vero, super me induxisti. Transeunt enim, sive quae non attingunt, sicut suspensions; sive quae attingunt, sicut fluctus.

Cum autem, Omnes suspensions, non ait, super me transierunt, sed super me induxisti; omnia quae impendebant evenisse significat: impendebant autem, quamdiu in prophetiafutura imminebant, omnia quae de illius passione praedicta sunt. 8 [v.9-10]. Longe, inquit, fecisti notos meos ame. Si eos quos noverat acceperimus dictum esse notos meos, omnes erunt: nam quem ille non noverat? Sed eos dicit notos, quibus et ipse notus erat, quantum eum tune nosse potuerunt; cene vel hactenus quod sciebant eum innocentem, etiamsi hominem tantummodo, non et Deum putabant. Quamvis et bonds quos proveet, notos dicere potuerit; sicut malos quos improbaret, ignotos, quibus in fine dicturus est, Non novi vos (Mt 7,23). They hated that kind of death; but it is better understood by those whom he previously said were his persecutors. I was delivered and it didn't come out. Should we understand why he did not come out that his disciples were outside when he was judged, or rather, in another more sublime sense, that is, he hid me in my interiorities, he did not manifest me, he did not declare me, he did not make me known; and, for the same reason, it continues: Are my eyes exhausted by poverty? To whose eyes should we understand what he is referring to? If we understand that they are those of the flesh, in which he suffered, we do not read that they had been exhausted in the passion of need, that is, that they had languished or fainted as if from hunger, in such a way that it devastated them, since he was handed over after having supped and on the same day he was crucified. If we understand that they are the inner eyes, how did they become exhausted by necessity, when the inefficient light resided in them? He undoubtedly called his eyes the most exalted, principal and eminent members that he loved in his body, of which he himself is the head. Speaking of this body, and taking the likeness of ours, the Apostle says: If the whole body were eyes, where would the ear be found? If everything were ears, where would the sense of smell be? If all were one member, what would it be a body? However, now there are many members and one body. The eye cannot say to the hand: "I don't need you." And if the hand says: "I do not belong to the body, because I am not an eye," does it not therefore belong to the body? He clearly explained what he meant by these words when he said: But you are the body and members of Christ. Therefore, also those eyes, that is, the holy apostles, a intelligi quos notos suos dixit, quia et ipsi genus illius mortis horrebant; sed melius intelligitur de his de quibus suis persecutoribus supetius loquebatur. who had not revealed the flesh and blood to his Son, but his Father, who is in heaven, to the point that Peter said: You are Christ, the Son of the living God, seeing him delivered and suffering so many evils, not seeing him as they wanted, because he did not come out, that is, because he did not manifest himself in his virtue and power, but remained hidden in his interior and, as if defeated and powerless, he endured all the sufferings, fainted or were exhausted by the destitution, as if their food, that is, their light, had been taken away from them. 9- And I cried, he says, to you, O Lord! If we want to understand the word day by time, and, above all, taking into account that this word was recorded here in the feminine genus, which in such a genus almost usually means only time in the Latin language, although this does not happen in Greek, since in this language the word day always has a feminine genus, and that is why I judge that our Latin translators rendered it like this, then the question presses us more closely - Well, how did he extend his hands for all the time, if he did not reach to have them spread out on the cross for a single day? taking the whole for the part, because Scripture usually uses this way of speaking, I can't think of an example in which the whole can be taken for the part when the whole is added to a word. For in what the Lord said in the Gospel: Thus shall the Son of Man also be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth, the whole is not unusually taken for the part, because he did not say all the three days and all the three nights. Only one was complete or total, the one in the middle, since the other two were only parts; the first, the last, and the last, the first. If in this prophecy of the psalm he did not predict in these words his cross, but rather his prayer, which we know and remember that he addressed, as a man, to God the Father, as the Gospel attests, long before his passion and on the day of it and on the cross itself, yet nowhere do we read that he prolonged it for the entire day. Therefore, we can consistently understand by "stretching out your hands all day long" his perpetual good work, from which his will never departed. 10 [v. l l ]. But since his good works only benefited those predestined to eternal life and not all men or those among whom he performed them, he then adds: Will you perchance perform miracles for the benefit of the dead? If we believe that he said this for those whom he resurrected, he did great wonders for the dead, since some of them revived; and likewise a great miracle was wrought before the dead, because the Lord descended into hell and from there ascended victorious to heaven. Then by these words: Do you perform miracles in quia isto genere locutionis uti etiam sancta Scriptura consuevit; non mihi oceurrit exemplum, totum pro parte etiam tune posse accipi, quando ipsum verbum additur et dicitur totum. Nam et in eo quod dixit Dominus in Gospel, Sic erit et Filius hominis in corde terrae tribus diebus et tribus noctibus (Mt 12:40); ideo totum pro parte non insolenter accipitur, quia non ait, Totis tribus diebus et totis tribus noctibus: unus quippe medius Fuit totus dies, duorum autem partes; first last, last first.

Si autem non cruzem suam in hac prophetia Psalmi significavit his verbis, sed oratíonem, quam eum ex forma servi fudisse Deo Patri, Gospel teste, didicimus, ubi eum et longe ante passionem, et sub die passionis, et in ipsa cruz orasse meminimus; nusquam hoc eum toto die fecisse legimus. Proinde expedient for external manus all die continuationem bonorum operum intelligere possumus, a quorum never intende cessavit. 10 [v. l l ]. Sed quia solis praedestinatis ad aeternam salutem, non autem ómnibus hominibus, nec ipsis inter quos facta sunt, eius bona opera profuerunt; ideo consequenter adiecit: Numquid mortuis facies mirabilia? Hoc enim si de his dictum putaverimus, quorum caro exanimis facta est; magna mirabilia facta sunt mortuis, eum quidam eorum etiam revixerunt (ib. 27,52): et quod Dominus penetravit inferna, atque inde mortis victor ascendit, magnum mortuis miraculum factum est. What follows: Or will the doctors resurrect them, and they will praise you?, means that the doctors will not resurrect men to praise you. Well, if we understand that under the name of giants the proud are insinuated, of whom the Apostle says: Where is the wise? Where is the lawyer? Where is the researcher of this world? Quantumlibet ergo excellentes verbi praedicatores, et veritatis etiam per miracula suasores, tanquam magni medici, agant cum hominibus; si mortui sunt et tua gratia non revixerunt, Numquid mortuis facies mirabilia; aut medid exsuscitabunt, et hi quos exsuscitabunt, confitebuntur tibi? Haec enim confessio indicat vivos: non sicut alibi scriptum est, A mortuo, velut qui non sit, perit confessio (Eccli 17,26). 11 [v.12]. Numquid enairabit quis in tomb mercym tuam, et veritatem tuam in perditione? Subauditur quod supra dictum est, ut etiam iste versus ita se habeat, ac si dictum sit, Numquid enarrabit quis veritatem tuam in perditione? Misericordiam quippe et veritatem amat Scriptura coniungere, máxime in Psalmis. Quod vero ait, in perditione, alio verbo repetivit quod supra dixerat, in sepulcro. Sic autem dictum est, in sepulcro, ut intelligantur ii qui sunt in sepulcro, qui et superius significati sunt nomine mortuorum, ubi ait, Numquid mortuis facies mirabilia? Animae namque mortuae corpus sepulcrum est. Unde Domi-

whitened children on the outside, which appear outwardly beautiful to men, and inside are full of dead men's bones and all filth; So you also appear righteous to men on the outside, but inwardly you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity. 12 [v.13}. Will your wonders be known in the darkness, and your justice in a forgetful land? It means the same in darkness as in a forgetful land. Under the name of darkness the infidels are symbolized; For this reason the Apostle says: In former times you saw darkness. In the same way, the land that forgets is the man who forgot God. The soul of the infidel can reach such dense darkness, that the fool says in his heart: There is no God. All this thought is intertwined in this way: I cried to you, O Lord!, in my sufferings; All day long I stretched out my hands to you; That is, I did not desist from executing my works in order to glorify you. Then why do the wicked rage against me if it is not because you will not do wonders for the dead? That is to say, they will not excite to faith nor revive the doctors to praise you, those in whom your hidden grace does not work, by which they must be brought to believe, because no one comes to me apart from him whom you bring. For who will narrate your mercy in the tomb? That is, (the mercy) of the dead soul, whose death is hidden under the weight of the body; and who (will narrate) your truth in destruction?, that is, in such a death, in which he is incapable of believing and perceiving any of these things. Will your wonders and justice be known in the darkness wildebeest in Gospel talibus dicit: "Similes cstis sepulcris dealbatis, quae foris apparent hominibus speciosa, intus vero plena sunt ossibus mortuorum et omni spurcitia: sic et vos a foris quidem paretis hominibus iusti; intus autem pleni estis hypocrisi et iniquitate (Mt 23,27 et 28). 5,8).

of this death?, that is, in the man who, forgetting you, lost the light of life. 13 [v. 14]. Here another question arises: What use is made of these dead? What does the Lord do for them for the benefit of the body of Christ that is the Church? Manifest through them the grace of God with respect to the predestined, who were called according to God's plan. Hence the same body says in another psalm: My God, His mercy will go before me. My God made himself known to me in my enemies. Then also here he continues and says: And I, Lord, cried to you. In these words it must be understood that our Lord Jesus Christ speaks on behalf of his body, that is, of the Church. What do you mean and me? That we were once, by nature, children of wrath, like the rest. But I cried out to you to save me. For who distinguishes me from the other children of wrath, when I hear the Apostle rebuke terribly and say to the ungrateful: Who distinguishes you? What do you have that you haven't received. And if you received it, why do you boast as if you had not received it? Health belongs to the Lord. The giant, with all his great strength, will not be saved. Only he who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved, as it was written. And how will they call upon Him in whom they did not believe? And how will they believe Him whom they did not hear? And how will they hear without preaching? Or how will they preach if they are not sent? As it is written: "How beautiful are the feet of those who preach peace, who proclaim good things!" These are the doctors who heal the one who was wounded by the thieves; but the Lord was the one who led him to the inn, because they are only workers in the

field of the Lord, and it is nothing that plants or waters, but God, who gives the increase. That is why I also cried out to the Lord, that is, I called on the Lord to save me. And how could I call upon him if he did not believe? And how should I believe if I do not hear? But so that I would believe what I had heard, He brought me; Because in secret it was not any doctor who revived the death of the heart, but He. Many heard, because their voice spread throughout the earth, and their words to the ends of the world. But faith is not for everyone, that is, not everyone believed, and God knows who believed. And, therefore, they would not have been able to believe if the mercy of God had not come forward. So that you do not understand this vineyard as another and, abandoning the men involved in it, think that it is land, it says: The vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel. Don't understand anything else; Let the house of Israel understand that it is my vineyard; understand that she did not give me grapes, but thorns; understand that she was ungrateful to the one who planted and cultivated her, ungrateful to the one who watered her. Then, if the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel, what did he say in anger? I will command my clouds not to rain water on it. And, in truth, he did so; For when the apostles were sent as clouds to rain on the Jews, when they rejected the word of God, since they produced thorns instead of grapes, the apostles said to them: We were sent to you; -But, since you rejected the word of God, we go to the people. From then on the clouds began to stop raining water on that vineyard. If the preachers of truth are clouds, let us investigate

first why they are clouds. They are heavens, they are clouds; They are heavens because of the brilliance of truth and they are clouds because of the concealment of the flesh. Because of the very darkness of the flesh, that is, because of the very darkness of the clouds, the Apostle says: Judge nothing before its time until the Lord comes and illuminates what is hidden or hidden from darkness. Now you perceive what the man speaks, but you do not see what he contains in his heart. You see what falls from the clouds, you don't see what is hidden in them. Which eye penetrated the clouds? Well, to calm the sea, what am I saying? To weaken the fierceness of the sea, what did you do in the sea itself? You humiliated the proud as a wounded man. There is a certain proud dragon in the sea of ​​which the Scripture says: There I will command the dragon to bite him; There is a dragon of which it is said: This is the dragon that you formed to be mocked, whose head crushes on the water. You—says the psalmist—humiliated the proud as a wounded man. You humbled yourself, and the proud was humbled. The proud man held the proud by his pride. The great one humbled himself, and, believing in Him, he became the proud little one. As the little one was supported by the example of the great who did little, the devil lost what he had, because the proud only retained the proud. By offering such a great example of humility, men learned to condemn their pride and imitate the humility of God. Thus, appareret arida compluenda, reliquae autem Gentes mare erant in amaritudine sterilitatis suae; quid faciunt praedicatores tui spargentes veritatem in circuitu tuo, quoniam fremunt fluctus maris? quid faciunt? Securae ergo pergant clouds; diffuse veritatem mam in circuitu tuo, non timeant rábidos fluctus: Tu dominiois potestatt maris. Because he was our guarantor. But you canceled this bond, this decree, with your blood. Then you wounded the one who took away so many men. And with the power of your arm you scattered your enemies. 12 [v.12.13]. Yours are the heavens and yours is the earth. For you they rain, they rain on your land. Yours are the heavens, through which your truth is announced around you. Yours is the land, which received the truth that surrounds you. Anyway, what did he make of that rain? You laid the foundation of the globe of the earth and all that it contains; you created the north and the sea. He has no power against you, against his Creator. Although the world can, due to its malice, be cruel through perverse will, yet does it exceed the measure imposed by the Creator, who made all things? Why do I fear the north, why should I fear the sea? Surely the devil is in the north, who said: I will set my throne in the north and I will be like the Most High; but you humiliated the proud as a wounded man. Therefore what you did in them serves more for your greater dominion than their will for evil. You created the north and the sea.

14 [v.14]. The power lies in your arm. No one arrogates him to himself. In your arm is the power; For you we were created, you defend us. In your arm lies the power; May your hand be strengthened and your right hand be lifted up. 15 [v.15]. Justice and judgment are the foundation of your throne.

13. Thabor et Hermón in nomine tuo exsultabunt. Montes isti intelliguntur, sed aliquid significant. Thabor et Hermón in nomine tuo exsultabunt. Thabor interpret dicitur Veniens lumen. Sed unde venit lumen de quo dictum est, Vos estis lumen mundi (Mt 5,14); nisi ab illo de quo dictum est, Erat lumen verum, quod illuminat omnem hominem venientem in hunc mundum? (1.9). Iliud ergo lumen quod est lumen mundi, ab illo lumine venit quod non aliunde accenditur, ut timendum sit ne exstinguatur. Ergo venit lumen ab illo, luzern illa quae non ponitur sub modio, sed super candelabrum, veniens lumen Thabor. Hermon autem interpretatur Anathema eius. Merit venit lumen et factum est anathema eius. Cuius, nisi diaboli, vulnerati, superbi? Ut ergo illuminaremur, abs te datum est; ut anathema nobis esset qui nos in suo errore et superbia detinebat, a te nobis est. Ergo Thabor et Hermón in nomine tuo exsultabunt: non in meritis suis, sed in nomine tuo. Dicent enim isti, Non nobis, Domine, non nobis, sed nomini tuo da gloriam; propter mare saeviens: ne forte dicant Gentes, Ubi est Deus eorum? (Ps 113 seconds 1.2). 14 [v.14]. 13. Tabor and Herman will rejoice in your name. These are mountains, but they symbolize something. Tabor and Herman will rejoice in your name. Tabor is said to mean coming light. But where does the light come from of which it was said: You are the light of the world, but from him of whom it was written: It was the true light that illuminates every man who comes into this world? Therefore, that light that is the light of the world comes from that Light that does not come on from anyone, so that, for the same reason, its extinction is not feared. Then, the light coming from Tabor, comes from Him who is a lamp, which is not placed under the bushel, but on the lampstand. Hermon means anathema to him. No wonder the light came and he became anathema or execration. From whom but the devil, the proud, the wounded? You enlightened us, you anathematized in our favor the one who held us in error and pride. Then Tabor and Hermon will rejoice in your name; not on their merits, but on your name. For these say: Not to us, Lord, not to us, but to your name, give glory; and, paying attention to the rage of the sea, they add: Lest the nations say: "Where is your God?"

God. Understand that there is so much grace that the tongue is not able to explain it, and you will have understood what joy or rejoicing is. 17. Finally, if you understood joy as it refers to grace, hear the recommendation of grace itself: Blessed are the people who know joy or rejoicing. What joy or rejoicing? See if it is not that of grace, see if it is not God's and not yours. Lord, in the light of your face they will walk. That Tabor, that is, the light that comes (for this means Tabor), if it does not walk in the light of your face, it will be extinguished by the wind of pride. Lord, they will walk in the light of your face and rejoice in your name all day long. Tabor and Hermon will rejoice in your name. If they want it to be all day, it has to be in your name. If, on the other hand, they rejoice in his name, they will not rejoice all day, for they will not remain in joy when they rejoice in themselves, for they fall through pride. So that they may rejoice all day long, they must rejoice in your name and be exalted in your righteousness. Not in his, but in yours; Let it not happen that, having zeal for God, they have him, but not according to knowledge. Of some it is noted by the Apostle that they had zeal for God, but not according to science: Not knowing, they say, the justice of God and, wanting to establish their own and not exalting themselves in your light, they did not submit to the justice of God. On the contrary, the people who know rejoicing (they did not know him according to complete knowledge, and blessed is the people who do not ignore, but know rejoicing), in what should they rejoice, in what should they be exalted except in your name, walk.

At last your justice and your judgment will be revealed; now they are hidden. It was said of your judgment in another psalm: In favor of the hidden things of the Son, there will be a manifestation of your judgment and your justice. Some will be placed on the right, others on the left; and the unbelievers will tremble with fear when they see what they now mockingly do not believe, and the righteous will rejoice when they see what they now believe without seeing it. Justice and judgment are the basis of your throne; this will certainly be seen on the day of judgment. Now what? Mercy and truth go before your face. I would fear the basis of your throne, that is, your justice and your coming judgment, if your mercy and your truth did not precede you. But why should I fear your judgments at last, when, preceding your mercy, you erase my sins and, showing the truth, you fulfill your promises? Mercy and truth go before your face. All the ways of the Lord are mercy and truth.

And like the moon. What moon? It fills her eternally. This moon that we perceive with our bodily eyes, although it is full, however, the next day it begins to decrease after having been full. Like an eternally full moon, he says; thus his throne will be perfect as the moon, but as a full moon forever. If his throne is like the sun, why is it also like the moon? Scripture usually symbolizes the mortality of the flesh by the moon, taking into account its increase and decrease, its passing form. Finally, Jericho also means moon; No wonder that man who went down from Jerusalem to Jericho fell into the hands of thieves, since from immortality he descended into mortality. Therefore this flesh is similar to the moon, which at all times and in each month supports growth and decrease; but this our flesh will be perfect in the resurrection and a faithful witness in heaven. Therefore, if we only perfected ourselves in the soul, we would only be compared to the sun; If we only perfected ourselves in the body, we would only be compared to the moon. But since God perfects us in the soul and in the body, it was said, paying attention to the soul: Like the sun in my presence, because only God sees the soul; and it was said and like the moon attending to the flesh, that it will be perfect eternally in the resurrection of the dead. It was also said: And a faithful witness in heaven, because all these true things were announced for the resurrection of the dead. I beg you to hear this again

and clearer and that you retain it. Well, I see that they understood it, but others perhaps still ask: "What did he say?" Nothing in the Christian faith is contested as much as the resurrection of the flesh. In fact, He who was born to be a sign of contradiction, and who resurrected his flesh to go out to meet the contradictor, and who was able to heal his members in such a way that the wounds did not appear, reserved the scars on his body to heal the wound of doubt in the heart. Nothing is so vehemently, so pertinaciously, so obstinately and ardently contested as regarding the resurrection of the flesh. Many Gentile philosophers disputed at length about the immortality of the soul and wrote, leaving behind many and varied books, in which they stated that the human soul was immortal; It may happen that this earthly flesh can ascend to heaven. For this reason, this moon, eternally full, is a faithful witness in heaven against all the challengers. 6 [v.39-46] All these things were promised about Christ; and how true, how clear, how evident they are! But you rejected and reduced your Christ to nothing; you abolished the alliance of your servant; you destroyed his sanctuary; you put fear in his fortress.

Let us love the Lord, our God; let us love his Church; Him as Father, her as mother; Him as Lord, her as Slave, because we are children of the Slave. But this marriage is united with great charity. No one offends one and favors the other. Let no one say: "I worship idols, I consult augurs, diviners, but I do not abandon the Church of God; I am Catholic." By withholding the mother, you offend the father. Another says: "Far be it from me; I do not consult diviners, I do not go in search of augurs, I do not attempt sacrilegious divinations, I do not go near worshiping demons, I do not worship stones, but I belong to the party of Donato." No wonder he did not say: "You existed from everlasting and you will exist to everlasting," but rather he recorded the verb in the present tense (saying you are, you exist), thus insinuating that the essence of God is absolutely immutable. In it there is no was and will be, but only is. In fact, seventy and eighty years add up to one hundred and fifty; The book of Psalms hints that this number is sacred. The number one hundred and fifty contains in its meaning the same condition as the number fifteen. This number is formed by the sum of seven and eight. The days of our life are in themselves seventy years, and at most, in the strongest, eighty. One thing is in ipsis, in themselves, and another in potentatibus, in the strongest. In ipsis, in itself, is the same as in the years or in the same days, which suggests that it means in temporal things, and that is why there are seventy, because in the Old Testament temporal things appear to be promised. But, if we do not look at the same years, but at the strongest ones, that is, if we do not consider temporal things, but eternal things, then there are eighty, which is hinted at in the New Testament by the hope of renewal and eternal resurrection. And what happens to them is work and pain; That is to say, anyone who transcends this faith and seeks something more finds work and pain. It can also be understood in this way: that, even when we are established in the New Testament, which is implied by the number eighty, this our life is endowed with more pain and suffering as we groan within ourselves waiting for the adoption of children and the redemption of our body, since by hope we were saved, and what we do not see, we patiently wait. All this belongs to the mercy of God. Hence he continues and says: Because meekness has come upon us and we are corrected. The Lord corrects whom he loves and scourges everyone whom he accepts as a son, for he also gives certain strong men the sting of the flesh, by which they are buffeted so that they do not become conceited by the greatness of his revelations and that virtue is perfected in weakness.
