In ipsis, hoc est in annis vel diebus ipsis quod datur intelligi in temporalibus rebus: ideo septuaginta; quia temporalia promitti videntur in Vetere Testament.

Si autem, non in ipsis annis, sed in potentatibus, id est, non in rebus temporalibus, sed in aeternis, octoginta anni; quod Novum Testamentum in spe est renovationis et resurrectionis in aeternum: et amplius eorum labor et dolor; id est, quisquís hanc fidem transgreditur, et amplius aliquid quaerit, labores invenit et dolors. Potest et sic intelligi: Quia licet in Novo Testament constituti simus, quod octogenarius significat numerus, amplius habet haec vita nostra laborem et dolorem, dum in nobismetipsis ingemiscimus, adoptionem esspectantes redemptionem corporis nostri: spe enim salvi facti sumus; et quod nondum videmus, per patientiam exspectamus (Rom 8:23-25). Et hoc ad memoriam Dei pertinet: unde sequitur, et dicit, Quoniam supervenit super nos mansuetudo, et corripiemur. Quem enim diligit Dominus, corripit; flagellat autem omnem filium, quem recipit (Hebr 12,6): et dat etiam magnis quibusdam stimulum carnis, a quo colaphizentur, ne extollantur in magnitudeine revelationum suarum, ut virtus in infirmitate per-
Ennarrations on the Psalms

corripiemur, we will be corrected, but erudiemur, we will be instructed, which refers to the same meekness. No one can be indoctrinated without work and pain, because virtue is perfected in weakness. 11 {v.11-12]. Who knows the power of your anger and {knows how} to calculate it according to the fear that is owed to you? For very few men, he says, is it possible to know the power of your anger, because with many you become more angry when you forgive them, so that the work and pain with which you correct and indoctrinate those you love so that they are not tormented with eternal punishment, is understood to not belong to anger, but rather to your meekness, for this is how it is read in another psalm: The sinner angered the Lord; He will not seek him based on the magnitude of his anger. Then who knows, that is to say, how small a number of men there are who know the power of your anger and who know, as this also goes without saying, to calculate it taking into account the fear that is due to you? It is difficult to find anyone who knows how to calculate your anger in such a way, due to the fear that is due to you, and at the same time understands that it belongs to it that you forgive not a few with whom you appear that you become more angry, so that the sinner may hasten on his path and receive greater goods at the end. The power of human anger disappears by killing the body; but God has power to punish here and to send to hell after the death of the body. Likewise, few scholars understand that vain and seductive happiness is a greater wrath of God. This was not known to him whose feet almost slipped, because he envied sinners when he saw their peace; but he knew it when he entered the sanfíciatur (2 Cor 12,7.9). Quidam sane codices non habent, corripiemur; sed erudiemur, quod ad eamdem mansuetudinem revocatur. Non enim potest erudiri quisquam sine labore et dolore; quia virtus in infirmitate perficitur. 11 [v.11.12]. Quis novit potestatem irae tuae} et prae timore tuo iram tuam dinumerare? Valde paucorum hominum est, inquit, nosse irae tuae potestatem; quia plerisque ita magis, cum parcis, irasceris, ut non ad iram, sed potius ad mansuetudinem tuam pertinere intelligatur labor et dolor, quo corripis erudisque quos diligis, ne poenis excrucientur aeternis: sicut enim legitur in alio psalmo, Irritavit Dominum peccator; pro magnitudeine irae suae non exquiret (Ps 10:4).

Quis ergo novit, id est, quotusquisque reperitur qui noverit potestatem irae tuae, et prae timore tuo iram tuam dinumerare? Etiam hic subauditur, quis novit. Quam difficile invenitur qui noverit ita prae timore tuo dinumerare iram tuam, ut etiam hoc addat, et ad eam intelligat pertinere, quod nonnullis, quibus plus irasceris, parcere videaris, ut prosperetur peccator in via sua, et maiora recipiat in novissimo? Potestas quipjje humanoe irae cum corpus occiderit, amplius non habet quid faciat; Deus vero habet potestatem et hic puniré, et post corporis mortem mittere in gehennam (Mt 10:28). Et a paucis eruditis maior eius ira intelligitur vana et seductoria felicitas impiorum. Hanc He non noverat, cuius penis commoti sunt pedes, quia zelavit in peccatoribus, pacem peccatorum intuens: sed didicit eam, cum
Deprecation of mercy

tuary of the Lord and understand his end; where few enter in order to learn to calculate the wrath of God taking into account the fear that is due to him and to count among the number of punishments the prosperity of evil men. 12. Make your right hand thus known. The Greek codices record this better than some Latin ones who wrote: "Make me known or thus make your right hand known to me." What does it mean to make your right hand known? Your Christ, of whom it was said: The arm or power of the Lord, to whom was it revealed? Let Him be known in such a way that through Him your faithful will rather learn to ask for and expect the rewards of faith, which do not appear in the Old Testament, but are revealed in the New; so that they do not think that the happiness of earthly and temporal goods must be held, desired and loved as great, so that their feet are not moved when they also see them in those who do not adore you and so that their steps do not slip when they do not know how to calculate your anger. Finally, attending to the prayer of the man of God, he made his Christ known in such a way that he demonstrated with his sufferings that those gifts that seemed to be celebrated or extolled in the Old Testament, where the shadows or symbolisms of future things are found, should not be coveted, but rather the eternal ones. The right hand of God can also be understood in this sense: that it is that in which he will separate his righteous from the wicked, because it also demonstrates itself very well in this way when it punishes everyone whom it accepts as a son and does not allow him to dwell any longer on his sins, becoming angry, but rather punishes perversities with meekness so that, corrected, he will cointraret in sanctuarium Dei, et intelligeret in novissima (Ps 72,2.3.17); quo pauci intrant, ut discant prae timore Dei dinumerare iram eius, et prosperitatem hominum malorum numero applicare poenarum. 12. Dexteram tuam sic notam fac. Hoc enim magis habent codices graeci; non sicut quidam latini, Dexteram tuam notam fac mihi.

Quid est ergo, Dexteram tuam sic notam fac; nisi Christum tuum, de quo dictum est, Et hrachium Domini cui revelatum est (Is 53,1), sic notum fac, ut in eo discant fideles tui ea magis to possess you et sperare praemia fidei quae non apparent in Vetere Testament, sed revelatur in Novo; ne arbitrentur pro magno habendam et cupiendam vel adamandam esse terrainrum ac temporalium bonorum felicitatem, et commoveantur pedes eorum, cum eam viderent et in eis qui te non colunt; et gressus eorum effundantur in lapsum, dum nesciunt dinumerare iram tuam? Denique secundum hanc orationem hominis sui, sic notum fecit Christum suum, ut suis passionibus demonstraret, non ea muñera quae videntur sonare in Vetere Testament, ubi sunt umbraefuturum, sed aeterna esse concupiscenda. Potest in isto sensu etiam Dei dexterá intelligi, in qua iustos suos ab impiis segregabit: quia et ipsa bene sic innotescit, cum flagellat omnem filium quem recipit, nec in peccatis suis prosperan sinit plus irascendo, sed in mansuetudine, sinistra flagellat, ut emendatum ad dexteram ponat (Mt 25,32.33). Et illud quod plerique codices habent, Dex-
{!.narratives about the Psalms

foulbrood on the right hand. What many codices write: "Let me know your right hand," can be applied to both things: now to Christ, now to eternal happiness. For, as God, He has no right of a corporeal species, just as He has no wrath stirred by the passions. 13. What he adds: the compeditos corde in sapientia, and to those held at heart by wisdom, other codices write et scholars..., to those indoctrinated by wisdom. The Greek word has such a similar sound in both meanings that a single syllable distinguishes the sound a little. But since they are indoctrinated in wisdom, those who, as it is written, put their foot in their fetters, but not the foot of the body, but the foot of the heart, bound in this way, as with ties of gold, do not depart from the path of God nor flee from it; In whichever of these two ways it is read, the truth of the sentence is saved. Also, those who were subjected or indoctrinated from the heart by wisdom, God made them so knowledgeable in the New Testament that they despised all things through faith, which is detested by the impiety of the Jews and Gentiles, and they tolerated being deprived of the things that were held to be great promises in the Old Testament by those who judged carnally. 14 [v. 13]. And since they made themselves known in such a way that they despised those promises and testified, through their torments, to the desire for eternal ones, for which they were called witnesses, who in Greek are called martyrs, for the same reason they suffered many cruel and temporary misfortunes. This man of God looks at this and the prophetic spirit, prefigured in the word of Moses, and says: Return, O Lord, until how much teram tuam notam fac mihi, ad utrumque referri potest, sive ad Christum, sive ad aeternam felicitatem: nam Deus ita non habet corporalis formae dexteram, sicut nec iram commotionibus turbuJentam. 13- Quod vero adiungit, Et compeditos corde in sapientia: alii codices non habent, compeditos, sed, erudites. Verbum enim graecum ita in utraque significatione similiter sonat, ut una syllaba paululum differat.

Sed cum illi erudiantur in sapientia, qui iniiciunt, sicut scriptum est, pedem in compedes eius (Eccli 6,25) (non utique pedem corporis, sed pedem cordis), et eius velut aureis vinculis illigati a via Dei non exorbitant, nec íiunt ab illo fugitivi; quodlibet horum legatur, save this sententia veritatis. Et ipsos enim compeditos, vel erudites corde in sapientia sic notos Deus fecit in New Testament, ut pro fide quam Iudaeorum et Gentilium detestabatur impietas, omnia contemnerent; et eis se privari paterentur, quae magna putant promissa in Vetere Testament qui carnaliter iudicant. 14. hoc attendit iste homo Dei, et spiritus propheticus per Moysi vocabulum figuratus, et ait: Convertere, Domine; quousque? et deprecabilis this knew servos tuos. Vox est eorum,
Deprecation of mercy

do?, and be exorable to your servants. This is the voice of those or the voice pronounced in favor of those who, enduring many misfortunes when persecuted in this world, make themselves known, held in their hearts by wisdom, so that due to so many evils they do not turn away from God, heading towards the goods of this century. It was said: Turn back, O Lord! How long?, as the following was recorded elsewhere: How long will you turn your face away from me? So that those who very carnally attribute to God the form of a human body may know that the access or recess of his face is not effected by a movement similar to the movements of our body, remember the previous words of the present psalm: You set our iniquities before you, and our world {our life}, in the illumination of your face. Then how does he say here turn to be propitious, as if, in anger, he had turned away his face, whereas there he insinuates in such a way that he is angry, that he did not turn his face from his iniquities or from his life, for which he had been angry, but rather placed them before him and in the illumination of his face? What is said, until when? It is a word of prayerful justice, not of indignant impatience. What was written here deprecabilis this, be exorable, others recorded the verb deprecare by the noun deprecabilis. Whoever wrote deprecabilis this avoided ambiguity, because the verb deprecan has an active and passive meaning, and thus deprecatur means begs, the one who begs; and also deprecatur, it is begged, he who is begged. Well, we say deprecor you, I beg you, and deprecar you, I am begged by you. 15 [v.14-15}. Then, anticipating with hope those future goods and considering them as already present, he says: vel pro eis, qui plana, persequente isto saeculo, mala tolerantes, innotescunt compediti corde in sapientia, ut nec tantis malis coacti refugiant a Domino ad huius saeculi bona. Secundum autem illud quod alibi scriptum est, Quousque avertis faciem tuam a me? (Ps 12,1). Etiam hoc dictum est, Convertere, Domine; quousque? Et ut sciant qui multum carnaliter Deo tribuunt humani corporis formam, aversionem vultus eius et convetsionem non fieri motu simili motibus corporis nostri; in hoc eodem psalmo recolant superiora: Posuisti iniquitates nostras in conspectu tuo, saeculum nostrum in illuminatione vultus tui.

Quomodo ergo hic dicit, Convertere, ut sit propitius, quasi faciem avertisset iratus; cum ibi sic insinuet itatum, ut non averterit faciem ab iniquitatibus et saeculo eorum quibus irasceretur, sed ea potius in conspectu suo et in illuminatione vultus sui posuetit? Quod autem dicitur, quousque, verbum est orantis iustitiae, non indignantis impatientiae. Sane quod hic positum est, deprecabilis este; alii verbum e verbo, deprecare, intetptetati sunt. Sed qui ait, deprecabilis esto, vitavit ambiguum; quia deptecari commune verbum est: nam et ille deprecatur qui deprecationem fundit, et ille cui funditut; dicimus enim, Deptecor te, et, deptecor a te. 15 [v.14.15]. Deinde illa bona quae future sunt, spe anticipans, et velut iarn facra deputans: Repleti sumus, inquit, mam misericordia tua,
Enurrations on the Psalms
Deprecation of mercy

We have been filled with your mercy since the morning. Then in these night-like sufferings and pains the lamp of prophecy was lit for us like a torch in a dark place until the day shines and the morning star dawns in our hearts, for blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God. Then the righteous will be satisfied with that good, now they hunger and thirst as they walk by faith on a pilgrimage towards the Lord. Hence it is also said: You will fill me with joy with your face. In the morning they will stand before you and contemplate; or as others translated: You satisfied us in the morning with your mercy; then they will be satisfied, as it says elsewhere: I will be satisfied when your glory appears. Hence it is also said: Show us the Father and it is enough for us. In the same way says the Lord: I will show myself to him. Until it happens, no good will satisfy us; nor should it satisfy us, so that our desire is not stopped along the way, because until it is achieved it must be walked. We have been filled with your mercy since the morning and we have rejoiced and been glad all our days. That day is the day without end. All those days exist at the same time; That is why they satisfy, since no way is given to those who come where everyone exists without having come and, existing, they do not cease to exist. They all exist at the same time, because one is the one who remains and does not pass away; this one is eternity. These are the days of which it is said: Who is the man who loves life and desires to see good days? These days are called years elsewhere, where it is said to God: You are always the same and your years have no jin. These are not

the years that are considered for nothing or the days that passed as a shadow, but are real days, the number of which he who said wanted to know: Make me known, O Lord!, my jin, where arriving, remain and from now on do not seek anything else, and the number of my days that IS. Certainly he who is, not he who is not; because the days of which he then speaks there: See that you have made my days old, are not, because they do not stop; They do not remain, because they pass with very accelerated movement, since there is not an hour in them in which we remain in such a way that part of it has not passed and, when another comes, none of it stops while remaining. On the contrary, those years and days in which we will not cease to exist, but will be endlessly restored, do not disappear. Let our soul be inflamed longing for those days, feel a burning and insatiable thirst so that there we may be filled, there we may be satisfied, there we may say what we announce here: We have been satisfied since the morning with your mercy and we have rejoiced and rejoiced during all our days. We have rejoiced for the days in which you humiliated us, for the years in which we saw misfortunes. 16 [v.16]. Now, then, while we are still in the days of calamity, let us say this: Look at your servants and at your works. Your servants are your works, not only insofar as they are men, but also insofar as they are servants, that is, insofar as they obey your commandments. We are His workmanship; not only in Adam, but also created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand for us to walk in.

Ergo in his velut nocturnis Iaboribus et doloribus prophetia nobis accensa est, sicut luzern in obscuro loco, doñee dies luzcat, et lucifer oriatur in cordibus nostris (2 Petr 1,19). Beati enim mundi corde, quia ipsi Deum videbunt. Tune replebuntur eo bono iusti, quod nunc esuriunt et sitiunt (Mt 5,8.6), cum per fidem ambulantes pilgrimage to Domino (2 Cor 5,6). Unde et illud dicitur, Replebis me laetitia cum vultu tuo (Ps 15,11). Mane astabunt et contemplabuntur (Ps 5,5); et, sicut alii dixerunt interpretates, Satiati sumus mane misericordia tua, tune satiabuntur: sicut enim alibi ait, Satiabor, dum manifestabitur gloria tua (Ps 16,15). Unde dicitur, Ostend nobis Vatrem, et sufficit nobis; atque ipse Dominus ait, Osteniam meipsum Mi (lo 14,8.21): quod doñee fiat, nihil boni nobis sufficit; nec sufficere debent, ne desiderium nostrum in via remaneat, quod doñee perveniat extendendum est. Repleti sumus mane misericordia tua; et exsultavimus, et iucundati sumus in omnibus diebus nostris. Dies ille, dies est sine fine. Simul sunt illi omnes dies; ideo satiant. Non enim succedentibus cedunt, ubi non est aliquid quod non veniendo nondum sit, et veniendo iam non sit. Omnes simul sunt, quia unus est qui stat et non transit: ipsa est aeternitas. Hí sunt dies de quibus dicitur: Quis est homo qui vult vitam, et diligit videre dies bonds? (Ps 33,13). Hi dies et alio loco anni appellantur, ubi Deo dicitur: T» autem idem ipse es, et anni tui non deficient. Non enim anni sunt qui pro nibilo

habentur, aut dies sunt qui sicut umbra declínaverunt (Ps 101,28.12): sed dies sunt qui sunt, quorum numerum notum sibi fiert precabatur qui dicebat, Notum fac mihi, Domine, finem meum (quo perveniendo maneam, et nihil ulterius iam requiram), et numerum dierum meorum qui est; utique qui est, non qui non est. Quia dies isti, de quibus et illie consequenter dicit, Ucee veteres posuisti dies meos (Ps 38,5.6), non sunt, quia non stant, non manent, celérrima mutabiliate transcurrunt; nec una hora in eis invenitur in qua ita simus, ut non alia pars eius transierit, alia ventura sit, nulla stet ut sit. lili autem anni et dies non deficiunt, in quibus nec nos deficiemus, sed sine defectu reficiemur. Exaestuet anima nostra illorum dierum desiderio, sitiat ardenter atque vehementer; ut illie repleamur, ibi satiemur, ibi dicamus quod hic praedicimus: Satiati sumus mane misericordia tua; et exsultavimus, et iucundati sumus in omnibus diebus nostris. Laetati sumus pro diebus quibus nos humiliasti, annis quibus vidimus mala. 16 [v.16]. Nunc autem in diebus adhuc malignis dicamus quod sequitur: Et réspice in servos tuos, et in opera tua. Ipsi enim servi tui opera tua sunt, non solum ut nomines sint, sed etiam ut sint servi tui, id est obedientes iussis tuis. Ipsius enim sumus figmentum, non solum in Adam, sed etiam creati in Christo Iesu, in operibus bonis, quae praeparavit Deus ut in illis ambulemus (Eph 2,10). Deus est enim qui operatur in nobis et velle et operani, pro bona volúntate (Phil 2,13). Et directs files

I sing of God's providence over the righteous

For God by benevolence is the one who works in us to will and to act. And govern their children to be upright in heart, to whom God is good; for the God of Israel is good, but to the upright in heart. Not like the one whose feet were moved because, upon contemplating the peace of sinners, he began to dislike God, as if he were ignorant of these things, as if he did not care about them and did not care about the government of the human race. 17 [v.17}. And let the splendor of the Lord our God be upon us. Hence it is said: The light of your face is engraved in us, O Lord! And rule in us the works of our hands, so that we do not do them for the reward of earthly things, for then they will not be straight, but crooked. Many codices end the psalm here, but in not a few it is read below: and govern the work of our hands. The most careful and learned ones annotate this last part of the verse with a little star called an asterisk, which indicates things that are found in the Hebrew or other Greek translators and are not found in the version of the Septuagint. If we want to explain this little verse, it seems to me that its meaning is this: that all our good works need charity, because the perfection of the law is charity. For having said in the previous verse: The works of our hands govern in us, in this last one he did not say works, but governs the work of our hands, as if he wanted to demonstrate in the last verse that the works were a single work, since then the works that are directed to this single end are right. The end of the precept is the charity of a pure heart, the con-

good science and unfeigned faith. Therefore the only work in which they are all contained is faith that works through love. Hence the Lord also says in the Gospel: This is the work of God, that you believe in Him whom He sent. Then, since in this psalm the old life and the new, the mortal life and the vital life are clearly and sufficiently distinguished, that is, the life in which one dies and the life in which one lives, the years that are considered for nothing and the days full of mercy and true joy, that is, the punishment of the first man and the kingdom of the second, taking into account this, I think that the name of the man of God Moses was assigned to the title so that by this he would be made known, to those who piously and rightly investigate the Scriptures, the law of God, which was given by Moses, in which it seems that God only or almost only promises rewards of earthly goods for good works; and, without a doubt, something is hidden beneath the veil as this psalm claims to contain. But when anyone passes to Christ, the veil will be removed from him and his eyes will be enlightened so that he may consider the wonders of the law of God, granted to him by Her Whom we say: Remove the veil from my eyes and I will consider the wonders of your law.

eorum: ut sint recti corde, quibus bonus est Deus. Bonus enim Deus Israel, sed rectis corde. Non sicut ille cui commoti sunt pedes, quia pacem peccatorum intuenti displicere coeperat Deus, quasi ista nesciens, quasi ista non curans, et ab humani generis gubernatione dissimulans (Ps 72, 1-14). 17 [v.17]. Et sit splendor Domini Dei nostri super nos. Unde dicitur, Signature est super nos lumen vultus tui, Domine (Ps 4,7). Et opera manuum nostrarum directs super nos: ut non ea pro rerum terrenarum mercede faciamus; tune enim non direct, sed curve sunt. Huc usque psalmum istum multi codices habent; sed in nonnullis legitur alius ultimus versus, Et opus manuum nostrarum directs. Cui versui diligentes et docti praenotant stellam, quos asterisks vocant, quibus significative ea quae in hebraeo vel alus interpretibus graecis reperiuntur, in Septuaginta vero ¡interprete non sunt. Quem versum si velimus exposee, id mihi videtur habere sententiae, quod ornnia bona opera nostra, unum opus est charitatis: plenitudo enim Legis charitas (Rom 13:10). Nam superiore veisu son dixisset, Et opera manuum nostrarum direct super nos; isto ultimo non opera, sed opus dixit manuum nostrarum direct: tanquam ultimo versu volens ostendere ipsa opera unum opus esse, id est, ad unum opus dirigí. Tune enim recta sunt opera, cum ad hunc unum finem diriguntur: finís enim praecepti est charitas de corde puro, et

conscientia bona, et fide non ficta (1 Tim 1:5). Opus ergo unum est, in quo sunt omnia, fides quae per dilectionem operatur (Gal 5,6): unde etiam Dominus in Evangelio dicit, Hoc est opus Dei, ut credatis in eum quem ille misit (lo 6,29). Cum ergo in isto psalmo, et vita vetus et vita nova, et vita mortalis et vita vitalis, et anni qui pro nihilo habentur et dies habentes plenitudinem misericordiae veraeque laetitiae, id est, et poena primi hominis et regnum secundi, satis aperteque distincta sint; ad hoc existimo hominis Dei Moysi nomen titulo eius inscriptum, ut eis qui pie recteque setutantur Scripturas, eo moda intimaretur etiam legem Dei, quae per Moysen ministrata est, ubi pro bonis operibus sola vel penis sola praemia tierrarum bonorum Deus polliceri videtur, sine dubio habere sub velamento tale aliquid, quale iste psalmus ostendit. Sed cum quisque transietit ad Christum, auferetur velamen (2 Cor 3:16), et revelabuntur oculi eius, ut considert mirabilia de lege Dei; donor illo cui dicimus, Revela oculos meos, et considerabo mirabilia de lege tua (Ps 118,18).

1. This psalm is the one with which the devil dared to tempt our Lord Jesus Christ. Let us hear, then, to instil
1. Psalmus iste est de quo Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum diabolus tentare ausus est. Audiamus ergo, ut possimus instructi resistere
Ennarrations on the Psalms
I sing of God's providence over the righteous

Truly we can resist the tempter, not boasting about ourselves, but about Him who was first tempted so that we would not be overcome in temptation. Jesus Christ had no need to be tempted; His temptation serves as a lesson for us. If we pay attention to what the devil responds, in order to respond the same when he tempts us in the same way, we enter through the door, as you heard when reading the gospel. What is it like to enter through the door? Enter through Christ, for He said: I am the door. What is it to enter for Christ? Imitate the ways of Christ. In what ways should we imitate the ways of Christ? Perhaps in the sublimity with which God is found in the flesh? Does He perhaps exhort us and demand of us to do the miracles that He did? Or, since our Lord Jesus Christ now and always rules with the Father over the whole world, does He invite man, making him His imitator, to rule with Him the heaven and the earth and all the things that are contained in them? Or that he himself is also the creator through whom all things are made, just as they were all made through Christ? Our Lord Jesus Christ, God and Savior, does not invite you to do these works that He did from the beginning, and of which it is recorded: All things were made by Him; nor to do what He did on earth. He doesn't tell you this: "You will not be my disciple if you do not walk on the sea, or if you do not raise a four-day-old dead, or if you do not restore sight to a man blind from birth." It doesn't tell you this. What is entering through the door? Learn from me, for I am meek and humble in heart. What He became for you, this is what you must pay attention to in Him to imitate Him. He worked miracles, and even before being born of Vir-

gene Maria. And who ever did this except Him of whom it was said: He alone works great wonders? Those who executed them in times past could only execute them in the name of Him; Thus Elijah raised a dead man by virtue of Christ. Or is it that perhaps Peter is greater than Christ, because Christ resurrected the sick with his word and Peter healed them with his shadow, since as he passed by they presented them to him so that his shadow could reach them, as we read in the Acts of the Apostles? So was Peter more powerful than Christ? Who would be so crazy as to claim this? Why did Saint Peter have so much power? Because Christ was in Peter. Therefore he said: All those who came are thieves and robbers; that is, those who came of their own free will, but not sent by me; those who came without being called by me, those in which I was not and those in which I did not introduce. Therefore, all the miracles that were performed, both by those before Christ and by those who came after, were performed by the Lord Himself, because they were performed by His effectiveness. Nor does He exhort you to perform those miracles that He Himself performed before becoming human. What does he exhort you to? To imitate what he would not have been able to do if he had not become a man. Would he have been able to endure torment if he were not a man? Without becoming human he would not have been able to die or be crucified. Therefore, when you endure the discomforts of this age, which the devil inspires either openly by men or secretly by himself, as in Job, be strong and long-suffering and dwell in the strength of the Most High, as this psalm says, since, if you depart from his strength, not being able to help yourself, you will fall.

Mode opus est ut oculos fidei habeamus, et videamus quia exaltantur ad tempus, et plangent in aeternum; et quibus datur potestas in servos Dei temporaliter, dicetur eis: lte in ignem aeternum, qui paratas est diabolo et angeüs eius (Mt 25,32-41). Sed si habeat quisque oculos, sicut dixit, oculis tuisconsiderabis; non est leve videre impium florentem in hoc saeculo, et habere ad illum oculos, ut consideres fide quid ille passurus est in fine, si se non correxerit: quia qui moda tonare volunt, postea fulminantur. Verumtamen oculis tuisconsiderabis, et retributionem peccatorum videbis. 12 [v.9]. Quoniam tu es, Domine, spes mea. Ecce come ad illud, quare non cadat a ruina et daemonio meridiano: Quoniam tu es, Domine, spes mea; altissimum posuisti rejugium tuum. Quid est quod in alto est refugium tuum? Multi enim sic sibi faciunt refugium Dei, quo fugiant a temporalibus aestibus. In high is enim refuge Dei, valde in occulto

It serves to free you from the wrath to come. Inside and very high you placed your shelter. No evil will come near you nor will a scourge come near your tabernacle, because he has commissioned the angels to guard you in all your ways. In their hands they will carry you so that you will never hurt your foot against the stone. These are the words that the devil said to our Lord Jesus Christ when he tempted him. But since they must be considered diligently, so as not to tire you out I will leave them for tomorrow, because tomorrow I must also preach to you. Therefore, I will begin from this passage of the psalm, so that it will not happen that, due to your weariness, in wanting to finish dark things briefly, I muddle them up and fail to understand them. SERMON

1. I have no doubt that those of you who attended the sermon yesterday will remember that lack of time prevented me from finishing the psalm that I had begun to expound, and, therefore, a part of it was postponed until today. Remember this, those of you who were there yesterday, and know it, those of you who were missing. For this reason I ordered the Gospel lesson to be recited from which the Lord was tempted with these same words of the psalm, which you heard now. Christ was tempted so that the Christian would not be defeated by the tempter. The Master wanted to be tempted in all things in which we are tempted; how he wanted to die, because we died; As he wanted it, what escapes ab ira ventura. Intus "alrissimum posuisti refugium tuum. Non accesont ad te mala, et flagellum non appropinquabit tabernacle tuo. Quoniam Angelis suis mandavit de te, ut custodiant te in ómnibus viis tuis. In manibus tollent te, nequando offendas ad lapidem pedem tuum." Ista sunt verba quae diabolus dixit Domino Iesu Christo, quando illum tentavit. Sed quia dilígentius considerada sunt, ne vos fatigemus, differamus in crastinum (quia et crastino debentur vobis sermo), ut ab isto loco Psalmi rursus incipiamus, propter taedium vestrum; ne cum volumus finiré res obscuras, praecipitemus, et non perveniant ad intelligentiam vestram. SERMO

1. Sicut non dubito meminisse Chariratem vestram, qui hesterno die sermoni adfuistis, psalmum quem coeperamus exposere, ne ad terminum perveniret, anguish temporis impedivit; et dilata est pars eius in hodiernum diem. Hoc qui here adfuistis, recordamini, qui non adfuistis, cognoscite. Propterea fecimus ipsam lectionem Evangelii recitari, ubi Dominus tentatus est per ea verba Psalmi, quae hic audistis (Mt 4,6). Ideo tentatus est Christus, ne vincatur a tentatore christianus. lile quippe magister in ómnibus tentari voluit, quia tentamur; sicut morí voluit, quia morimur; sicut resurgere voluit, quia resurrectuti sumus. Illa enim quae

resurrect, because we also had to resurrect; For that which He who became man for us, being God, by whom we were made, performed as man, performed for us. I do not regret repeating many times to your charity what I frequently recommend to you so that perhaps many of you who cannot read or because you do not have time or because you do not know, at least, by hearing frequently, do not forget what you must believe for your health. Certainly, by repeating these things, I will annoy some; But I don't worry about forming others in the faith. I know that there are many who have very good memories and who know what I have to say because they have dedicated themselves to divine reading, and perhaps they want me to say things that they do not know; But, if you are faster and lighter, remember that you are walking the path in the company of others who are heavier and clumsier. When two companions walk the same path and one of them is lighter than the other, it is easy for the looser one, and not the slower one, to make them go together; Because, if the fastest person wants to walk as much as he can, the slowest person will not follow. Then it is necessary for the fastest one to slow down and shorten his pace so as not to leave behind the slower companion. What I said that I repeated many times and now I repeat it again in the sense that the Apostle says: Writing to you the same thing, for me it is not difficult and for you it is useful, is this: that our Lord Jesus Christ, as a totally perfect man, is head and body. The head is that man who was born of the Virgin Mary, who suffered under the power of Pond or Pilate, who was buried, and rose again, and ascended to heaven, and is otendit in nomine, qui factus est propter nos homo, cum esset Deus pet quem facti sumus, propter nos ostendit. Et saepe commendavimus Charitati vestrae, quod nos saepe iterare non piget; ut quia forte multi vestrum legere non possunt, quia non eis vacat legete, aut litteras non norunt, sakem assidue audiendo non obliviscantur salubrem fidem suam. Certe ea repeating quibusdam molesti videoamur, dum tamen quosdam aedificemus. Novimus enim multos esse et memoria praevalentes, et lectionis divinae studiosos, qui ea quae dicturi sumus noverunt; et forte nos ea volunt dicere quae non noverunt. Sed si celeriores sunt, intueantur quia cum tardioribus ambulant viam.

Quando autem duo committees unam viam ambulant, quorum est unus celerior, alter tardior, in potestate celerioris est ut cum illo ambulet tardior, non in potestate tardioris; quia si velit celerior tantum faceré quantum potest, tardior illum non sequitur. Opus est ergo ut celerior refrenet celeritatem suam, et non telinquat comitem tardiorem. Hoc est ergo quod dixi me saepe dixisse, et nunc iterum dico: sicut dicit Apostolus, Eadem scribere vobis, mihi quidem non pigrum, vobis autem tutum (Phil 3,1)- Dominus noster Iesus Christus, tanquam totus perfectus vir, et caput, et corpus: caput in illo homine agnoscimus, qui natus est of Matia virgine, passus sub Pontio Pilato, sepultus, resurrexit, ascendit in caelum, sedet ad dexteram Patris, inde illum exspectamus iudicem vivorum atque mortuorum; hoc est caput Ecclesiae (Eph 5,23). Corpus huius capitis Ecclesia est, non quae hoc

sitting at the right hand of the Father, from where we hope that he will come as judge of the living and the dead; This, then, is the Head of the Church. The Body of this Head is the Church; not only the one that is here, but also the one that is spread throughout the entire earth; and not only that of now, but that which existed from Abel to those who are to be born and believe in Christ until the end of the world; That is, the Church is all the people of saints who belong to a city. This city is the Body of Christ, which has Christ as its Head. The angels are also our fellow citizens, with the difference that we pilgrimage and work and they wait in the city for our arrival. From that city to which we are heading, letters were sent to us, the holy Scriptures, which exhort us to live well. But shall I say that we only received letters from there? The King himself came down and made a way for us on this pilgrimage, so that, walking in it, we may not err, nor faint, nor fall into the hands of thieves, nor fall into the snares that are placed by the wayside. Then let us know the total and complete Christ united with the Church; to Him alone, who was born of the Virgin Mary and is head of the Church, that is, to the Mediator between God and men, Christ Jesus; who is a Mediator so that those who have strayed from God may be reconciled through Him, for the middle is between two. We had departed from the majesty of God and had offended him with our sins; Hence the Son was sent as Mediator so that with his blood he would pay the debt of our sins, for which we were separated from God, and thus, placing himself in the middle, he would bring us closer and reconcile us with Him from whom we were separated by our sins and crimes. He is our Head, He is God loco est, sed et quae hoc loco et per totum orbem terrarum: nec illa quae hoc tempore, sed ab ipso Abel usque ad eos qui nascituri sunt usque in finem et credituri in Christum, totus populus sanctorum ad unam civitatem pertinentium; quae civitas Corpus est Christi, cui caput est Christus. Ibi sunt et Angelí cives nostri: sed quia nos peregrinamur, laboramus; illi autem in civitate exspectant adventum nostrum. Et de illa civitate unde peregrinamur, litterae nobis venerunt: ipsae sunt Scripturae, quae nos hortantur ut bene vivamus. Quid dicam venisse litteras?

Ipse rex descendit, et factus est nobis via in peregrinatione; ut in illo ambulantes, nec erremus, nec deficiamus, nec in latrocinantes incidamus, nec in laqueos irruamus, qui ponuntur iuxta viam. Talem ergo scientes Christum totum atque universum simul cum Ecclesia; ipsum autem solum natum de virgine, caput Ecclesiae, mediatorem scilicet inter Deum et homines Christum Iesum (1 Tim 2:5): ad hoc mediatorem, ut eos qui recesserant, per se reconciliet; medius enim non est nisi inter duos. Recesseramus a maiestate Dei, et peccato nostro offenderamus eum: missus est Filius mediator, qui sanguine suo solveret peccata nostra, quibus separabamur a Deo; et interpositus redderet nos eí et reconciliaret, a quo aversi in peccatis nostris et delictis tenebamur. Ipse est caput nostrum,
I sing of God's providence over the righteous

equal to the Father, Word of God by whom all things were made. It is God to create and man to restore, God to form and man to reform. Looking at this one, let us hear the psalm. Take care of your charity. The teaching and doctrine of this school is such that it will help you understand not one psalm, but many, if you apply this rule. Sometimes the psalms, and not only the psalms, but also the prophecy, speak in such a way of Christ that they only recommend the Head; Others from the Head pass to the Body, that is, to the Church, without appearing to have changed person. This happens because the Head is not separated from the Body, but rather it is spoken of as one. Let your charity understand what I say. It is clear to everyone what is said in the psalm of the passion of the Lord: They pierced my hands and my feet and counted all my bones; They divided my clothes among themselves and cast lots for my tunic. The Jews are also ashamed of this when they hear it, since a prophecy was evidently announced about the passion of our Lord Jesus Christ. Our Lord Jesus Christ was sinless, and yet at the beginning of the psalm he says: O God, my God, why have you forsaken me? The voices of my crimes separate me from my health. Then you see what is said in person of the Head and what in person of the Body. The crimes are ours; the passion, of the Head; but for his passion in our favor he pays what is due for our crimes. This is also what happens in this psalm. 2 [v.1-8].
Let us briefly remember the verses that

ipse est Deus aequalis Patri, Verbum Dei per quod facta sunt omnia (lo 1,3): sed Deus ut creaet, homo ut recrearet; Deus ut faceret, homo ut reficeret. Hunc intuentes, sic audiamus Psalmum: intendat Chantas Vestra. Disciplina est ista et doctrina scholae huius, quae vobis valeat non ad unum psalmum intelligendum, sed ad multos, si teneatis hanc regulam. Aliquando psalmus, non solum psalmus, sed et omnis prophetia, aliquando sic loquitur de Christo, ut caput solum commendet, et aliquando a capite it ad corpus, id est ad Ecclesiam, et non videtur mutasse personam; quia non separatur caput a corpore, sed tanquam de uno loquitur. Videat enim Chantas Vestra quod dico. Manifestus est certe omnibus psalmus ubi de passione Domini dicitur: "Foderunt manus meas et pedes; dinumeraverunt omnia ossa mea: diviserunt sibi ropa mea, et super vestimentum meum miserunt sortem." Hoc et Iudaei quando audiunt erubescunt; evidentissime enim prophetia de passione Domini nostri Iesu Christi prolata est. Delicta autem non habebat Dominus noster Iesus Christus; et tamen in capite ipsius psalmi dicit: Deus, Deus meus, utquid me dereliquisti? Longe a salute mea verba delictorum meorum (Ps 21,17.18.19.2). Videtis ergo quid dicatur ex persona capitis, quid ex persona corporis. Delicta ad nos pertinent, passio pro nobis ad caput pertinet: sed propter passionem illius pro nobis, et quod ad nos pertinet delictorum solvitur. Sic et in isto psalmo. 2 [v.1-8]. lam istos versus fresterna die tractavimus: breviter com-

we were yesterday He who dwells in the strength of the Most High will dwell in the protection of the God of heaven. In these verses I recommended to your charity that no one trust in himself, but rather put all his hope in Him in whom our strength resides and by whose support we conquer, not by our presumption. The God of heaven protects us if we say to the Lord the following: He will say to the Lord: "You are, my God, my protector and my refuge; I will wait for Him, because He will deliver me from the trap of the hunters and from the harsh word." We said that many, fearing the harsh word, fall into the hunters' trap. For example, a man is insulted because he is a Christian; Despite being so, he falls into the devil's trap because of this harsh word. Another man is also insulted because he lives well among many Christians who live worse; For fear of these harsh, insulting words, he falls into the snares of the devil, ceasing to be wheat on the threshing floor, turning into chaff. He who waits on the Lord is freed from the trap of hunters and harsh words. How does God protect you? He will protect you behind his back; That is, he will place you in front of his chest to protect you with his wings if, now recognizing your weakness, you flee, like a weak chick, to hide under the mother's wings so as not to be snatched away by the kite. Milan are the aerial powers, the devil and his angels, who seek to put an end to our weakness. Let us run to take shelter under the wings of mother Wisdom, because she also became sick for us, since the Word became flesh. Just as the hen sickens before her chickens to protect them with her wings, so our Lord Jesus Christ, who, having the form of God, did not judge ramemoremus illos. Qui habitat in adiutorio Altissimi, in protectione Dei falls commorabitur. Hoc commendavimus Charitati Vestrae in istis versibus, ne quisquam ín se spem ponat, sed totam spera suam in illo ponat, in quo sunt vires nostrae; ex adiutorio enim eius vincimus, non ex nostra praesumptione. Protegit ergo nos Deus caeli, si dicamus Domino quod sequitur: Dicet Domino, Susceptor meus es tu, et refuge meum, Deus meus, sperabo in eum; quoniam ipse eruet me of muscipula venantium, et a harsh verb. Diximus quia multi finientes asperum verbum incidunt in muscipulam venantium. Insultatur homini, quia christianus est; et poenitet illum, quia christianus factus est, et ab rough verb íncidit in muscipulam diaboli.

Insultatur etiam homini, quia Inter multos christianos melius vivit; et timens áspera verba insuitatorum, incidit in laqueos diaboli, ut non sit triticum inarea, sed paleam sequatur. Qui autem in Deo sperat, eruitur a muscipula venantium et a harsh verb. How did Deus protect you? inter scapulas sitas obumbrabit tibí: id est, ante pectus suum te ponet, ut alis suis te protegat; si modo agnoscas infirmitatem tuam, ut quasi pullus infirmus fugias sub alas matris, ne a milvo rapiaris. Thousand vi sunt enim aereae potestates, diabolus et angeli eius: rappere volunt infirmitatem nostram. Fugiamus sub alas matris Sapientíae, quia et ipsa Sapientia infirmata est propter nos; quia Verbum caro factum est (lo 1,14). Sicut infirmatur gallina cum pullis suis, ut protegat

He wanted to be equal to God, to sicken with us and protect us under his wings, he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, made in the likeness of men and found in habit as a man. And you will wait under his wings. His truth will surround you with a shield; you will not fear the night terror. The temptation of ignorance is fear at night, and sins committed consciously are the arrow that flies by day, since by night we mean ignorance, and by day we mean knowledge. There are those who sin through ignorance and there are those who sin knowingly: those who sin through ignorance are struck down by the night terror, those who sin knowingly are wounded by the arrow that flies by day. When this happens in the most violent pursuits, it lasts until noon, and anyone who falls due to that heat falls as if due to the meridian demon. In fact, many fell due to that heat, as I already explained to you yesterday, since, once the furious persecution was unleashed, it was said: "Let Christians be tormented until they deny being Christians." Before, confessing, they were killed; then they were tormented to deny; and as every prisoner was tormented until he denied, the Christian was tormented during the time he confessed, leaving him free when he denied. Great was, therefore, the fury of the pursuers. All those who fainted in that temptation fell as if at the hands of the meridian demon. And how many fell! Many who expected to sit with the Lord and judge, fell at his side; and, likewise, many others who were waiting to be placed on the right among the holy plebs eos alis suis (Mt 23:37): sic Dominus noster Iesus Christus, qui cum in forma Dei esset, non rapinam arbitratus est esse aequalis Deo, ut infirmaretur nobíscum, et alis suis protectet nos, semetipsum exinanivit formam servi accipiens, in similarityinem hominum factus, et habitu inventus ut homo (Phil 2,6 et 7). Et sub alis eius sperabis. Scuto circumdabit te veritas eius; non limebis a nocturnal timore. Tentationes ignorantiae, timor nocturnus; peccata scientiae, sagitta volans per diem: in nocte enim ignorantia intelligitur, in die manifestatio. Sunt qui ignorantes peccant, sunt qui scientes peccant: qui ignorantes peccant, a timore nocturna supplantantur; qui scientes peccant, a flying sagitta per diem percussi sunt. Haec autem cum in gravioribus persecutionibus fiunt, quousque perveniatur tanquam ad meridiem, quicumque illo calore ceciderit, tanquam a daemonio meridian cadet.

Et multi a calore isto ceciderunt, sicut iam exposuimus hesterno die Charitati vestrae; quia fervente persecutione dictum est, Torqueantur Christiani, doñee negent quod christiani sunt. Cum antea solerent confessi percutí, ad hoc postea torquebantur ut neget: et cum omnis reus tamdiu torqueatur, quamdiu neget; Christianorum confessio torquebatur, negatio dimittebatur. Erat ergo tune magnus aestus persequentium. Quicumque in illa temptatione ceciderunt, tanquam a daemonio meridian ceciderunt. Et quanti ceciderunt! Multi qui se sperabant sessuros cum Domino et judicaturos, illi a latere ceciderunt. multi item qui se perabant ad dexteram futures, in plebe sancta

breastplate, like simple citizens who supply provisions to the soldiers, and to whom it must be said: I was hungry, and you gave me food, who will be many, also fell from their hope; and many more of this kind, because there are more, since those who are to judge with the Lord are fewer than those who are to stand before Him. But the state of the latter will not be the same. For some will be placed on the right and others on the left; some to reign and others to be punished; some to hear: Come, blessed of my Father; receive the kingdom, and others to hear: Go into the eternal fire that was prepared for the devil and his angels. Then those who will fall through the ruin and the demon meridian will be a thousand on the side, and ten thousand on the right. But he won't come close to you. Who? The demon meridian will not take you down. No wonder he doesn't take down the Head. But neither will He overthrow those who adhered to the Head in the manner in which the Apostle says: The Lord knows His own. For there are some so predestined that the Lord knows that they belong to his Body. Those who are not attacked by temptation so as to overthrow them are included in what was written: He will not come near you. But lest some weak ones focus their attention on the sinners, who were allowed to torment the Christians with so many and such intense kinds of tribulations, and say: "Why did God want to allow the impious and wicked to be so angry against the servants of God?", look a little with your eyes, with the eyes of faith, and you will see the reward that is finally given to the sinners, to whom so many things are now allowed to exerstipendiate. provincial tanquam, qui annonam militibus praebent, quibus dici habet, Esurivi, et dedistis mihi manducare (ad dexteram enim erunt multi); et de ipsa spe ceciderunt, et plures índe, quia plures ibi. Pauciores enim qui cum Domino iudicabunt, et plures qui stabunt ante illum: sed non una conditio eorum. Alii ad sinistram, alii ad dexteram; alü ut regnent, alii ut puniantur; alii ut audientat, Venite, benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum; alii ut audiant, lte in ignem aeternum, qui praeparatus est diabolo et angelis eius (Mt 25,32-41). Ergo qui a ruina et daemonio meridiano cadent, mille a latere, et dena milüa a dextris. Ad te autem non appropinquabit: quid? Daemonium meridianum te non deiicit. Quid mirum si caput non deicit?

Sed non deiicit et illos qui sic haerent capiti, quomodo ait Apostolus, Novit Dominus qui sunt eius (2 Tim 2,19). Sunt enim quidam ita praedestinati, ut noverit Dominus qui pertineant ad Corpus ipsius. Cum ergo ad hos non accesot illa tentatio, ut deiiciat eos; isti íntelliguntur in eo quod scriptum est, Ad te autem non appropinquabit. Sed ne illi peccatores quibus tanta licuit exercere in Christianos, attendantur a quibusdam infirmis, et dicatur, Ecce, quid voluit Deus, ut tantum impiis et sceleratis liceat in servos Dei? modicum considers oculis tuis, oculis fidei, et videbis retributíonem peccatorum in

quote you, for the psalm continues: However, you will look with your eyes and see the reward of sinners. 3 [v.9-12]. Because you, Lord, are my hope, you have placed your refuge high. No evil will come near you. The psalmist says to the Lord: For you are, Lord, my hope, you have placed your refuge on high. Evils will not come near you and the scourge will not come near your tabernacle. Below are written in the psalm the words that you heard the devil say: Because he commissioned his angels to guard you in all your ways. In their hands they will carry you so that you will never hurt your foot against the stone. Who is he saying this to? To whom he said: Because you are, Lord, my hope. I believe that it should not be explained to Christians who the Lord is. If by Him they understand God the Father, how will the angels take Him in their hands so that He does not hurt His foot against the stone? Then you see that our Lord Jesus Christ, while speaking about the Body, suddenly began to speak about the Head. Now, then, the Head was designated when it is said: For you are, Lord, my hope, you have placed your refuge on high. You placed your refuge very high, because you are, Lord, my hope. What does this mean? Let your charity pay attention to why you are, Lord, my hope, you placed your refuge on high. We should no longer be surprised by what he just said; For this reason he continues: Nor will evils come near you. Because? Because you placed your refuge very high. Not even the scourge will come near your tabernacle. Because? Because you placed your refuge very high. We do not read in the Gospel that the angels ever carried the Lord in their hands so that he would not stumble fine, quibus modo tanta permittuntur, ut exerceatis. Hoc enim sequitur: Verumtamen oculis tuisconsiderabis, et retributíonem peccatorum videbis. 3 [v.9-12]. Quoniam tu es, Domine, spes mea, altissimum posuistt refugium tuum. Non accessent ad te mala. Domino dicit: Quoniam tu es, Domine, spes mea; altissimum posuisti refugium tuum. Non accessent ad te mala; et flagellum non appropinquabit tabernacle tuo. Deinde iam verba quae audistis dicta a diabolo: Quoniam Angelis suis mandavit de te, ut custodiant te in ómnibus viis tuis. In manibus tollent te, nequando offendas ad lapidem pedem tuum. Cui hoc dicit? Cui dixit, Quoniam tu es, Domine, spes mea. Iam puto non esse exponendum Christianis quis sit Dominus. Si Deum Patrem intelligunt, quomodo illum tollent Angelí in manibus, ne offendat ad lapidem pedem suum?

Videtis ergo quia et Christus Dominus, dum loqueretur de corpore, súbito coepit loqui de capite. Caput nostrum appellatum est moda, cum diceretur: Quoniam tu es, Domine, spes mea; altissimum posuisti refugium tuum. Ideo posuisti altissimum refugium ttium, quoniam tu es, Domine, spes mea. against the stones, and yet we believe it. This has already been fulfilled and prophesied, because it had to be fulfilled. But it cannot be said that Christ has to come later so as not to bruise his foot against the stone, since he will only come to judge. When was it fulfilled? Take care of your charity. 4. But first of all listen to these little verses: Because you are, Lord, my hope, you have placed your refuge on high. The human race knew the death of man, but was unaware of his resurrection; Therefore, he had reason to fear and had no reason to wait for him. Then He who instilled the fear of death for our teaching, rose first of all, giving us the hope of resurrection with a view to the prize of future and eternal life. He died after many, but was resurrected before all. Dying, He suffered what many had already suffered, and, rising, He did what no one had done before Him. For when will this happen to the Church? At the end of the world. Preceded in the Head what the members expect, since your charity already knows how they behave towards each other. Let the Church therefore say to Jesus Christ, its Lord; Let the Body say to its Head: Because you, Lord, are my hope, you have placed your refuge on high; That is, you rose from the dead and ascended to heaven so that, ascending, you would place your refuge high and become hope for me, who distrusted the earth and did not believe that I would rise again. Now I believe it, because my Head ascended to heaven, and where the Head went, the members will also go. So that they would not become criminals of the law, having not received grace, and, being criminals, remain bound to the law, since the same stumbling block is a crime, the Lord freed those who were criminals under the law so that they would not stumble in the law. Thus, so that the feet of this Head would not incur the crime of the law, the Holy Spirit was sent to provide love and deliver from fear. Fear did not fulfill the law, love fulfilled it. Men feared and did not fulfill it, they loved and fulfilled it. How did they love and fulfill it? They feared and stole other people's things; They loved and gave their own. Therefore it is not surprising that the Lord ascended to heaven in the hands of the angels so that his foot would not stumble against the stone. So that those who, belonging to his body, worked on the earth, traveling around the entire world, would not become criminals of the law, he removed fear from them and filled them with love. Peter denied three times out of fear; the Holy Spirit had not yet come; but as soon as he received him he began to preach fearlessly; and thus, he who at the voice of a servant denied three times, having received the Holy Spirit, confessed, among the scourging of the princes, the one he had denied. Nor is it surprising that the Lord took away the triple fear with triple love. Well, having risen, the Lord said to Peter: Peter, do you love me? He did not say, "Peter, are you afraid of me?" Because if he were still afraid, he would strike his foot against the stone. "Do you love me?" he says. He answers: I love you. It was enough to have told him once. For me, who cannot see the heart, it would be enough for me. How much more would it be enough for the Lord, who saw with what tender love Peter said: I love you! But the Lord is not content with me answering him once. He asks him again, and Pedro answers again: I love you. For the third time he questioned him, and then, Peter being saddened because it seemed to him that the Lord doubted his love, he said to him: Lord, you know all things; you know that I love you. The Lord acted in this way with him as if telling him: "Three times you denied me out of fear; loving me you must confess me as many times." He filled his disciples with this love and charity. Because? Because he placed his refuge very high; because, glorified, verunt, et donaverunt suas. Ergo non est mirandum quia ideo in manibus Angelorum assumptus est Dominus in caelum, ne offenderet ad lapidem pes eius: ne illi qui in terra laborabant in corpore eius, peragrantes totum orbem terrarum ieront rei Legis, subtraxit ab eis timorem, et implevit eos amore. Timorese Petrus ter negavit (Mt 26,69-75); nondum enim acceperat Spiritum sanctum: accepto postea Spiritu sancto, cum fiducia coepit praedicare. Qui ad vocem ancillae ter negavit; I accept Spiritu sancto, inter flagella principum confessus est quem negaverat (Acts 2,5, etc.). Non mirum; quia Dominus ipsum trinum timorem trino amore dissolvit.

The other things, brothers, are clear, because they have already been discussed many times. You will walk on the asp and the basilisk and trample the lion and the dragon. You know who the serpent is and how the Church tramples on it by not being defeated by it, since it guards against all its cunning. When the martyrs were killed, the angry lion appeared; When the heretics attack, the sneaky dragon appears. You defeated the lion; Also defeat the dragon. The lion did not subdue you, nor the dragon deceive you. Let us prove that the devil was a lion when he was clearly angry. Saint Peter, exhorting the martyrs, says: Do you not know that your enemy the devil circles around you, like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour? Being a furious lion, he sought in the light of day who to devour. How does he stalk as a dragon? For the heretics. Saint Paul, fearing these so that the integrity of the faith that the Church carries in her heart would be corrupted by them, says: I betrothed you to a single man to present you, as a chaste virgin, to Christ; But I fear, lest as the serpent cunningly deceived Eve, so your minds also become depraved from chastity toward Christ. There are few women in the Church who preserve bodily virginity, but that of the heart is preserved by all the faithful. 1. Pay attention to the psalm. May the Lord grant me to discover the mysteries contained in it, even though the same things are exposed in various and diverse ways due to the fatigue of the spirit. For God teaches us only the song of faith, hope and charity. That of faith, so that, believing in Him whom we do not see, we may have firm faith in Him while we do not see Him; and so, when we are no longer told: "Believe what you do not see," but: "Rejoice, because you see," let us rejoice when we see him, and the vision of his light replaces our faith. That of hope, so that our hope is immutable and established in him, and does not waver, fluctuate, or be moved, just as the God himself in whom it is established cannot be moved. Now there is hope; later, when reality is possessed, there will be none. It is called hope as long as one does not see what one hopes for, as the Apostle says: The hope that is seen is not hope, because what someone sees, what does he expect? If we wait for what we do not see, we wait patiently. So now, while the promise arrives, patience is needed. No one is patient in good things; It is in bad things that patience is required of man. Is this why he who promises deceives? The doctor takes the scalpel to cut away what is unhealthy and says to the one who has to cut it: "Be patient, endure, tolerate." In pain it demands patience, but after pain it promises health. He who endures pain before the doctor's scalpel would faint in the pain he suffers if he did not try to achieve the health he does not have. There are many pains, both interior and exterior, in this world; What's more, they don't stop; Scandals are the order of the day, and only those who walk in the path of God perceive them. He is told in all the divine pages to tolerate the present and wait for the future; love him who does not see so that he hugs him when he sees him. Charity, the third of the virtues, which is combined in us with faith and hope, is the greatest of the three. Faith has for its object things that are not seen; when they are seen, it will disappear and the vision will take place. Hope, which has as its object things that are not possessed, will disappear when we possess them, because we no longer hope for what we have. Charity is only dedicated to growing more and more. If we love the one we do not see, how should we love him when we see him! Let our desire therefore grow. We are only Christians for the future century. No one expects present goods, no one promises the happiness of the world, since he is a Christian. Still, use temporary happiness as you can, however you can, when you can, and as much as you can. When you have it, thank God for this comfort; When you fail, also give thanks to God's plan. Always be grateful, never ungrateful. caress, and threaten; Say, therefore, (the Christian) what you heard in the psalm: It is good to praise the Lord and to sing to your name, O Most High! 2 [v. l]. The title of the psalm is as follows: Psalm of song; for Saturday. Note that today is also Saturday. This day is currently celebrated by Jews with a certain amount of bodily, languid, negligent and dissolute leisure. Well, they indulge in frivolities; and, therefore, when God commands them to keep the Sabbath, they dedicate it to the things it prohibits. We rest from bad deeds, they from good deeds. It is better to plow than to dance. They rest from good works, but not from frivolous ones. God declares the Sabbath to us. Which? First see where it is. Our Saturday is inside, in the heart. Many rest physically, but are agitated in conscience. No bad man can enjoy the Sabbath or rest, because his conscience is never at peace, and, therefore, he necessarily lives disturbed. However, he who has a good conscience enjoys tranquility, and the same tranquility is the Sabbath or rest of the heart; For he attends to the promising God, and, if by chance he suffers in the present, he looks with hope to the future, and all fog of sadness disappears, as the Apostle says: Rejoicing in hope. Our Saturday is, therefore, the joy in the peace of our hope. In this psalm it is recommended and sung how the Christian man is not disturbed in the Sabbath of his heart, that is, in the rest, in the tranquility and in the peacefulness of his conscience. Hence this declares the origin of the perti gratus sit; amat enim ille semper, sive blandiatur, sive minetur: et dicat quod audistis in Psalmo, Bonum est confiten Domino, et psallere nomini tuo, Altissime. 2 [v.l]. Titulus Psalmi habet, Psalmus cuntid in diem sabbati. Ecce et hodiernus dies sabbati est: hunc in praesenti tempore otio quodam corporaliter languid et fluxo et luxurioso celebrant Iudaei. Vacant enim ad nugas; et cum Deus praeceperit sabbatum (Ex 20:8), illi in his quae Deus prohibet exercent sabbatum. Vacatio nostra a malis operibus, vacado illorum a bonis operibus est. Melius est enim arare, quam jumpe. lili ab opere bonus vacant; ab opere nugatorio non vacant. Nobis sabbatum indicit Deus. What? Primo ubi sit videte. Intus est, in corde est sabbatum nostrum.

Multi enim vacant membris, et tumultuantur conscientia. Omnis homo malus, sabbatum habere non potest: nusquam enim illi conquiescit conscientia; necesse est in perturbationibus vivat. Cui autem bona est conscientia, tranquillus est; et ipsa tranquilinas sabbatum est cordis. Attendit enim promissorem Dominum; et si laborat in praesenti, extenditur spe futuri, et serenatur omne nubilum tristitiae; sicut dicit Apostolus, Spe cries (Rom 12,12). Ipsum autem gaudium in tranquilízate spei nostrae, sabbatum nostrum est. Hoc commendatur, hoc cantatur in isto psalmo, quomodo sit homo christianus in sabbato cordis sui, id est, in vacatione et tranquillitate et serenitate conscientiae suae non perturbatus.

confusion of men and at the same time teaches you to celebrate the Sabbath in your heart. 3 [v. 2]. The first thing you should do, if you advance in something, is to praise God for what you advanced, since it is a gift from Him, not your merit. Begin the Sabbath not attributing to yourself what you received as if you had not received it, nor excusing yourself from the evil you committed, since it is yours. Perverse men, who lack the Sabbath, attribute their iniquities to God, and good works to themselves. If they did something good, they say: "I did it"; If they committed some evil, they look for someone to accuse so as not to praise or confess God. How do they find someone to accuse? If he is not too impious, he has a hand in who he accuses: "The devil executed him," he says; "he persuaded me," as if Satan had the power to force him. He certainly has the sagacity to insinuate. If Satan spoke and God remained silent, you would have cause for excuse; but your ears are between God, who warns, and the serpent, who suggests. Why do you incline to this and turn away from that? Satan certainly does not cease to dissuade evil, but God does not cease to advise you good. Satan does not force against the will; It is in your power to consent or not to consent. If, under Satan's persuasion, you have committed some evil, leave Satan alone, accuse yourself, so that with your confession you may obtain the mercy of God. Are you trying to accuse the one who can't get forgiveness? Accuse yourself and you will receive forgiveness. Many do not accuse Satan, but fate, for they say: "My bad luck dragged me down." Inde dicit hic, unde solent perturban homines, et docet te agere sabbatum in corde tuo. 3 [v.2]. Primum est, ut tu ipse, si aliquid profecisti, Deo confitearis ex eo quod profecisti, quia muñera ipsius sunt, non merita tua. Hinc incipe sabbatum, non tibi tribuendo quasi non acceperis quod accepisti (1 Cor 4:7); ñeque excusing you ab eo quod facis mali, quia ipsa sunt tua. Perversi enim homines et perturban, qui non agunt sabbatum, mala sua Deo tribuunt, bona sua sibi. Si quid boni fecerit, Ego feci, dicit: si quid mali fecerit, quaerit quem aecuset, ne confiteatur Deo. Et quid est, Quaerit quem aecuset? Si non est valde impius, ad manum habet satanam quem aecuset: Satan fecit, dicit, ipse mihi persuasit: quasi satanás habeat potestatem cogendi. Astutiam suadendi habet.

Be si satan loqueretur, et taceret Deus, haberes unde te excusares: moda aures tuae positae sunt inter monentem Deum, et suggerentem serpentem. Quare huc flectuntur, hinc avertuntur? Non cessat satan suadere malum; sed nec Deus cessat admonere bonum. Satan autem non cogit invitum: in tua potestate est consentiré, aut non consentiré. Si aliquid persuade me satana mali feceris; resign satanam, aecusa te, ut aecusatione tua Dei misericordiam merearis. Expetis illum aecusare qui non habet veniam? Te aecusa, et accipis indulgentiam. Deinde multi non aecusant satanam, sed aecusant fatum. Fatum meum me duxit, dicit. Cum dixeris illi, Quare fecisti? quare peccasti? Et ille: Fato meo malo. Ne dicat, Ego feci, iam manus ad Deum tendit; lingua blasphemat. Nondum quidem hoc aperte dicit,
Unanations on the Psalms

When you say to someone: "Why did you do this, why did you sin", and he answers: "It was my bad luck"; porn say: "I did it", raises his hands to God and blasphemes with his tongue. He doesn't say this obviously, but pay attention and you will see that he says it. You ask him what fate is, and he answers: "The bad star." You insist by asking him: "Who made the stars, who ordered them?" He will only answer that God. Then it remains that either lightly, or through the enchanting augur, or by blaming his neighbor, he accuses God, and thus, God being the punisher of sins, he makes him the author of his sins. But it cannot happen that God punishes what he did; He only punishes what you do to free or save what he did. Sometimes when they sin, leaving aside all excuses, they attribute it directly to God, saying: "God willed it; if he had not willed it, I would not have sinned." The psalm admonishes you not only not to listen so as not to sin, but also to accuse yourself because you sinned. What does this psalm tell us? It is good to confess the Lord. What does it mean to confess the Lord? That in both things, both in the sin, because you committed it, and in the execution of the good, because He did it, you must confess the Lord. You will chant to the name of the Most High if you seek God's glory, not your own; If you praise his name, not yours. If you go in search of God's name, He goes in search of yours; if you despise his name. He will destroy yours. In what way did the Lord say he looked after your name? Just as he told his disciples after sending them to evangelize. Well, having worked many miracles and cast out demons in the name of Christ, upon returning from his preaching they joyfully said to him: Lord, even the demons submitted to us, although they added: in your name, He, seeing that sed tamen attende, et vide quia hoc dicit. Quaeris ab illo quid sit fatum; et dicit, Stellae malae. Quaeris ab illo quis fecit stellas, quis ordinavit stellas; non habet quid tibi responderat, nisi Deus. Restat ergo ut sive per transennam, sive per cannam longam, sive per proximum, Deum aecuset; et cum Deus puniat peccata, Deum faciat auctorem peccatorum suorum. Non potest enim fieri ut puniat quod fecit: punit quod facis, ut liberet quod fecit.

Aliquando autem, dimissis omnibus, omnino directe cunt in Deum; et quando peccant, dicunt: Deus hoc voluit; si nollet Deus, non peccarem. Ad hoc monet ut non solum non auditatur ut non pecces, sed aecusetur quia peccas? Quid ergo nos Docet psalmus iste? Bonum est Domino candy. What is it, Domino candy? In utraque re, et in peccato tuo, quia tu fecisti, et in bono facto, confitere Domino, quia ipse fecit. Tune psalles nomini Dei altissimi: quaerens gloriam Dei, non tuam; nomen ipsius, non fuum. Si enim tu quaeris nomen Dei, quaerit et ipse nomen tuum: si autem tu neglexeris nomen Dei, delet et ipse nomen tuum. Quomodo autem dixi, Quaerit nomen tuum? Quomodo dixit discipulis suis venientibus, posteaquam misit eos evangelizare. Cum fecissent fine miracula, et in nomine Christi daemonia eiecissent, redeuntes dixerunt: Domine, ecce daemonia nobis subiecta sunt. Dixerunt quidem, in nomine tuo; sed ille vidit in eis quia ipsa glorificatione gau-
Praise of divine providence

They rejoiced in that glorification and, conceited, were on the road to pride, because it allowed them to cast out demons; Seeing, I repeat, that they were seeking their own glory, He said to them, seeking their names, indeed, preserving their names with Him: Do not rejoice about this, but rejoice that your names are written in heaven. See where you have your name if you do not despise the name of God. Psalmody, then, to the name of God so that your name may be established in God. What does it mean, brothers, to chant? The psaltery is a type of organ that has strings. Our works are the psaltery. Anyone who performs good works with his hands praises God. He who confesses with his mouth sings to God. Sing with your mouth, chant with your works. So that? 4 [v. 3]. To announce your mercy in the morning, and your truth at night. What does it mean: His mercy is to be announced in the morning, and his truth at night? It is called morning when things are going well for us, and night when the sadness of tribulation overwhelms us. What did he say most briefly? When things go well with you, rejoice in God, because it is because of his mercy. Perhaps you will say if I should rejoice in God when things go well for me, because it is due to his mercy; When I am sad, when tribulation surrounds me, what will I do? When things go well with me, is it due to His mercy? And when things go wrong for me, to his cruelty? If I praise mercy when things go well, will I revile cruelty when things go wrong? No. When things go well, praise mercy, and when things go badly, praise truth, because because it punishes sins debant, et extollebant se, et ibat inde in superbiam, quia licuit íllis expeliere daemonia. Vidit illos quaerere gloriam suam, et ait íllis, quaerens ipse, imo conservans nomina eorum apud se: Nolite gaudere in hoc: gaudete autem quod nomina vestra scripta sunt in cáelo (Le 10, 17.20). Ecce ubi habes nomen, si tu nomen Dei non negligas. Psalle ergo nomini Dei, ut fixum sit apud Deum nomen tuum. Psallere autem quid est, fratres? Psalterium organi genus est; chordas habet. Opus nostrum, psalterium nostrum est: quicumque manibus operatur opera bona, psallit Deo; quicumque ore confitetur, cantat Deo. Sing ore, psalle opetibus. Ad quam rem? 4 [v.3]. Ad annuntiandum mane misericordiam tuam, et veritatem tuam per noctem.

Quid sibi vuk quia mane annuntianda est misericordia Dei, et per noctem veritas Dei? Mane dicitur, quando nobis bene est: nox dicitur, quando tristitia tribulationis est. Quid ergo dixit breviter? Quando tibi bene est, gaude Deo, quia misericordia ipsius est. Iam tu forte says: Si ergo gaudeo Deo, quando mihi bene est, quia misericordia ipsius est; quando in tristitia, in tribulatione sum, quid fació? Mercy ipsius est, quando mihi bene est; crudelites ergo ipsius when male est? If I award mercy, when bene est; reprehendam ergo crudelitatem, quando male est? No. Sed when bene est, lauda misericordiam; quando male, lauda veritatem: quia peccata flagellat, non est iniquus. In nocte erat Daniel, quando orabat: erar enim in captivitate

It is not wicked. When Daniel prayed, he was in the night, in the captivity of Jerusalem, in the power of the enemies. Then the saints endured immense evils; then Daniel himself was thrown to the lions; Then the three young men were thrown into the fiery furnace. When the people of Israel suffered these calamities in captivity, it was night. During the night, Daniel confessed the truth of God, saying in his heart: We have sinned, we have done wickedly, we have committed iniquity: to you, Lord, the glory; to us, the confusion. He announced the truth of God during the night. What does it mean to "announce God's truth during the night"? That, if you suffer any evil, do not attribute it to God, but to your sins. Attribute correction to Him so that you may announce His mercy in the morning and His truth at night. By announcing His mercy in the morning and His truth at night, you continually praise God; You always confess and praise his name. 5 [v. 4]. In the ten-string psaltery with singing on the zither. Now you did not hear the ten-stringed psaltery played. The ten precepts of the law are represented in the ten-stringed psalter. But it is necessary to sing with him, not just take him; for the Jews have the law; Therefore, they carry the psaltery, but they do not touch it. Who touches him? Those who work. But this is little, because those who act with sadness do not touch him. Who are the ones who touch him? Those who do good with joy. Joy is typical of singing; Well, what does the Apostle say? God loves a cheerful giver. Whatever you do, do it with joy; then you do good and certainly good. If you act with sadness, you do not act, but Jerusalem, erat in potestate hostium, is acted. Tune fines mala sancti patiebantur: tune ipse in lacuffl leonum missus est, tune tres pueri in ignem praecipitati sunt (Dan 6:3). Haec patiebatur in captivitate populus Israel: nox erat. Per noctem confitebatur Daniel veritatem Dei; clicebat in oratione, Peccavimus, impie egimus, iniquitatem fecimus: tibi, Domine, gloria, nobis confusio (ib. 9,5.7). Veritatem Dei annuntiabat per noctem. Quid est, veritatem Dei annuntiare per night? Non aecusare Deum, quia pateris aliquid mali; sed tribuere illud peccatis tuis, emendationí ipsius: Ad annuntiandum mane misericordiam ipsius, et veritatem per noctem.

Cum misericordiam annuntias mane, et veritatem per noctem, semper laudas Deum, semper confiteris Deo, et psallis nomini eius. 5 [v.4]. In decachordo psalterio, cum cantico in cithara. Decachordum psalterium non moda audistis. Decachordum psalterium significat decem praecepta I-egis. Sed will sing in illo opus est, non portare psalterium. Nam et Iudaei habent Legem; portant, non psallunt. Qui sunt qui psallunt? Qui operatur. Parum est: qui operantur cum tristitia, nondum psallunt. Qui sunt qui psallunt? Qui cum hilaritate feciunt bene. In psallendo enim hilaritas est. Et quid dicit Apostolus? Hilarem enim datorem diligit Deus (2 Cor 9:7). Quidquid facis, cum hilaritate fac: bonum runc et bene facis. Si autem cum tristitia facis, fit de te, non
