in you, and, therefore, you rather transport the psaltery than you sing. In the ten-string psaltery with singing on the zither, that is, with word and deed. With song it means with the word, and with zither, with the work. If you pronounce only words, you only have the song, but you lack the zither; If you act and remain silent, you will only have a zither. Therefore, if you want to have singing with a zither, speak well and do well. 6 [v. 5]. Because you have rejoiced me, Lord, in your deeds, I will rejoice in the works of your hands. See what it says: "You formed me, you made me live well; if I do something good, I will rejoice in the work of your hands, since, as the Apostle says, we are His workmanship, created for good works." If I had not trained you to do good, you would only know how to do bad. For the Gospel says: He who speaks a lie speaks of his own. And all sin is a lie. Everything that opposes the truth and the law is called a lie. Then what does it mean: He who speaks a lie speaks of his own? That whoever sins, sins of his own harvest. Or b serve the opposite of this sentence. If the one who speaks lies speaks of his own harvest, there is nothing left but the one who speaks truth, speaks of God. And, for the same reason, it is said in another place: Only God is truthful, and every man is lying. By this sentence you are not told: "Look, since you are a man, you are sure to lie", but on the contrary: "See that you are a man, since you are lying." So that you may be truthful, drink the truth, and thus you will speak of God and be truthful. Since you cannot have the truth from yourself, all that remains is to drink from where it flows. How you become dark if you turn away facis; et portas magis psalterium, non cantas. In psalterio decachordo, cum cantico in cithara: hoc est, verbo et opere. Cum song, verb; in cithara, operate. Si verba sola dicis, quasi canticum solum habes, citharam non habes: si operaris, et non loqueris, quasi solam citharam habes. Propter hoc et loquere bene, et fac bene, si vis habere canticum cum cithara. 6 [v.5]. Quia iucundasti me, Domine, in invoice tua, et in operibus manuum tuarum exsultabo. Videtis quid dicat. You fecisti me bene vivostem, you formed me: si quid forte boni fació, in invoice manuum tuarum exsultabo: quomodo dicit Apostolus, Ipsius enim sumus figmentum, creati in operibus bonis (Eph 2,10). Nisi enim te formaet ad opera bona, non nosses nisi opera tua mala.

Qui enim loquitur mendacium, de suo loquitur (lo 8,44): hoc Evangelium dicit. Omne peccatum mendacium est. Contra legem enim et contra veritatem quidquid est, mendacium dícitur. Ergo quid ait? Qui loquitur mendacium, de suo loquitur; id est, qui peccat, de suo peccat. Attendite sententiam contra. Si enim qui loquitur mendacium, de suo loquitur; restat ut qui loquitur veritatem, from Dei loquatur. Ideo dicitur in alio loco: Deus solus verax; omnis autem homo mendax (Rom 3,4). Non tibi dicitur in hac sententia, Vade, securus lieré, quia homo es: imo vide te hominem, quia mendax es; et ut sis verax, bibe veritatem, ut de Deo ructes, ut sis verax. Quia de tuo illam non potes habere, restat ut inde illam bibas, unde fluit.

of light, as the stone is not heated by its own virtue, but by the sun or by fire, and, if you remove it from the heat, it cools, showing that what was heated did not come from it, but from the sun or the fire, so also, if you separate yourself from God, you become cold, and, if you approach Him, you become warm, as the Apostle says: Fervent in the spirit. Likewise, what does it say about light? If you draw near to Him, you will be in the light; hence the psalm also says: Draw near to Him and you will be enlightened and your faces will not be ashamed. Therefore, since you can do nothing good if you are not illuminated by the light of God and warmed by his Spirit, when you notice that you are doing well, praise God and proclaim what the Apostle says, say so that you do not become conceited: What do you have that you have not received?; and if you received it, why do you boast as if you had not received it? Then here the psalm praises God and teaches us good praise, since it says: You rejoiced me, Lord, with your deeds; I will rejoice in the works of your hands, 1. What shall we say about those who live badly and prosper? Whoever loses Saturday has their spirit disturbed. So, when one sees that he, continually performing good works, nevertheless endures calamities, perhaps poverty, hunger, thirst, nakedness, and that perhaps he is in prison having done good, and the one for whom he was imprisoned is overflowing with joy doing evil, at this he lets a perverse thought against God enter into his heart and says: "O God, why do I serve you, why do I obey your commandments? Hic ergo confitetur Deo et docet nos bonam confessionem, quia dicit lucundasti me, Domine, in invoice tua, et in operibus manuum tuarum exsultabo. 7. Quid agimus de illis qui male vivunt, et florent? Hinc enim perturbatum animum habet qui perdit sabbatum: videt se in bonis operibus quotidie versantem, et laborantem in anguish rerum, forte in inopia rei familiaris, forte in fame et siti et nuditate, forte se in carcere bona facientem, et illum a quo in carcerem missus est et mala facientem et exsultantem; et subintrat cor pessima cogitatio adversus Deum, et dicit: Deus, quare tibi servio? quare obedio verbis tuis? Non rapui aliena, non furrum feci, non hominem occidi, non cuiusquam rem concu-

say, I did not bear false testimony against anyone, I did not revile my parents, I did not worship idols, I did not take the name of God in vain; In short, I did not commit a sin." He lists the ten strings, that is, the ten commandments of the law, and examines himself about each one of them, and, seeing that he has not broken even one, he is grieved, because he endures these evils. He also sees that he who I do not say plays some strings, but neither plays the psaltery nor does any good, who consults idols and perhaps appears to be a Christian when he does not suffer any detriment in his goods, but, when he endures in this adversity, he runs to the fortune teller, to the fortune teller, to the astrologer. He sees that the name of Christ is spoken to him and he mocks, he gestures. He is told: "Are you a believer and you consult the astrologer?" But he answers: "Get away from me, leave me alone; the fortune teller found my things for me; otherwise, I would have lost them and would remain crying." Good man! Don't you sign yourself with the sign of the cross of Christ? The law prohibits all this. You are happy because you found your things, aren't you sad that you have perished? How much better it would have been if your clothing had perished than your soul! Making fun of this, he insults his parents, hates the enemy, pursues him to the death, steals when the opportunity presents itself, does not stop uttering false testimony, attacks another's marriage, covets the goods of his neighbor; he does all this, and prospers in riches, in honors, in the glory of the world. That unfortunate man sees him who does good and who endures evil, and then he is disturbed and says: "O God, I believe that you like the evil and that you hate the good, because you love those who do evil." non falsum testimonium adversus aliquem dixi, non patri vel matri ¡niuriam feci, non ad idola inclinatus sum, non accepi nomen Domini Dei in vanum: servavi me a peccato, id est, decem praecepta Legis (Ex 20:1-17), et intertogat se secundum singula, et videt se non. peccasse, nec in uno; et contrístatur quia talia mala patitur. currunt ad pythonem, aut sortilegum, aut mathematicum. Et ille: Recede to me: ipse mihi prodidit res meas; nam lost, et in planctu remansissem. Homo bone, nonne signas te signo crucis Chtisti? Et lex omnia ista prohibet. Gaudes quia res tuas invenisti; It's not sad that you peristi? Quanto melius tunica tua periret quam anima tua? Subsannat in his omnibus; contumeliosus est parentibus, odit inimicum, insectatur usque ad mortem, furatur ubi occasionem invenetit, a false testimony non cessat, insidiatur matrimonial alieno, concupiscit tem proximi sui: facit haec omnia, et flotet in divitiis, in honofibus, in excellentia mundi huius. Videt eum ille miser bene operas, et mala patiens; petturbatur et dicit: Deus, puto, mali tibi placent, et bonds odisti, amas eos qui faciunt ini-

I lie, he lost the Sabbath of the heart. He began to ignore the psaltery; He turned away from there and sings without reason: It is good to praise the Lord and sing to your name, O Most High! Having already lost the Sabbath of the inner man and the rest of the heart having disappeared, and having excluded good thinking, he begins to imitate him who sees that he prospers by living evil and dedicates himself to living in iniquity. However, God is patient, because he is eternal and knows the day of judgment, in which he will judge all things. 8 {v.6). After having shown us this, what does it say? How magnificent are your works, O Lord; your thoughts are too deep! Truly, brothers, there is no sea as deep as this thought of God: let the bad prosper and the good suffer. There is nothing so deep, nothing so high; In this abyss, at this height, every infidel is shipwrecked. Do you want to cross this abyss? Do not depart from the wood of Christ; so you will not be shipwrecked; cling to Christ. What do I want to teach you when I tell you: "Take hold of Christ"? That He wanted to suffer on earth. You heard, when the prophet Isaiah was read, that he did not turn his back from the scourging, that he did not turn his face from the spitting of men, that he did not withdraw his cheek from their insults or chants. Why did he want to suffer all this? To comfort those who suffer. He could have resurrected his body at the end of the world; but, if you had not seen him resurrected, you would have no reason to wait; He did not take long to resurrect his body, so that you still do not doubt. Then he endures and tolerates the tribulations in this world for that end that you saw quitatem. It is as follows: Praise song for David, on the day before the Sabbath, when the earth was founded. Going through in thought what God did during all the days in which he created and ordered the universe, from the first day to the sixth, since he sanctified the seventh, because in it he rested from all the works, which he did exceedingly good, we find that on the sixth day, which is commemorated here, since it says before the Sabbath, all the animals of the earth; and then on the same day he made man in his image and likeness. No wonder He ordered the days in this way, for thus the centuries would also pass from now on before we rested in God; and we will rest if we do good works. As an example of this, it was written of God: And God rested on the seventh day after having done all his exceedingly good works. But he did not become so tired that it was necessary for him to rest, nor does he stop working now, since Christ our Lord clearly says: My Father is working until now. This is said to the Jews, who felt carnally about God, and did not understand that God works in rest and works continually and is always still. Therefore we also, whom God then wanted to prefigure in him, after all good works will obtain rest. However, brothers, all the good works that we perform here in the world before rest, are as if covered with work, since that rest is not yet possessed in reality, but in hope; but, if we were not possessed of hope, we would faint in our work; but good works will pass with difficulty. What is better than giving bread to the hungry? What better thing to do before sabbatum, when fundata est terra. Reminders ergo per omnes dies quid fecerit Deus, quando creavit et ordinavit universa a primo die usque ad sextum diem (septimum enim sanctificavit, quia in illo requievit post omnia opera, quae fecit bona valde), et invenimus eum sixth die fecísse (qui dies hic commemoratur, quia dicit, ante sabbatum) omnia animalia in terra: deinde ipso die fecit hominem ad imaginem et similarityinem suam. Non autem sine causa illi dies sic sunt ordinati, nisi quia et saecula sic cursura erant, antequam requiescamus in Deo. Tune autem requiescimus, si facimus opera bona. Ad hoc exemplum scriptum est de Deo, Requievit Deus seventh die, crib fecisset omnia opera bona valde (Gen 1, et 2,1-3).

Non enim fatiguetus est, ut requiesceret, aut moda non operatur; cum aperte Dominus Christus dicat: Pater meus usque nunc operatur (lo 5,17). 1. As we listened very attentively when this psalm was read, so let us listen now when the Lord reveals the mysteries that He deigned to conceal. For certain sacraments of the holy Scriptures are not hidden so that they may not be manifested, but so that they may be made evident to those who call. Then, if you knock with pious affection and sincere fervor of heart, He who sees why you knock will open them. We all know that many, and I hope we are not one of them, murmur about the patience of God and are sad that wicked and impious men either live on earth or have great power; and, what is more, that the bad ordinarily have greater power against the good, and that many times the bad oppress the good, that the bad rejoice and the good suffer, that the bad are exalted and the good are humiliated. Putantes ergo infirmi frustra se bene vivere, aut invitationntur ad imitandam malitiam eorum quos quasi florete conspiciunt: aut si per infirmitatem vel personae suae vel animi, timent male faceré, ne aliquid illis secundum leges saeculi mali

of character or lack of personality, but not because they love justice, but, to put it more clearly, for fear of being condemned among men by men, fearing to do evil, lest perhaps some harm should come to them due to civil laws, they certainly abstain from evil actions, but not from evil thoughts. And among his wicked thoughts, the main place of iniquity is occupied by that impiety by which God seems to neglect and not care about human things; and, for the same reason, either that it considers the good and the bad as equal, or, what is even more disastrous to think about, that it persecutes the good and favors the bad. He who thinks this way, even if he does no harm to anyone, makes himself very great and is impious in himself; and by his iniquity he does not harm God, but he kills himself. Nor do those who think this way because they are timid harm men; but, nevertheless, God sees their murders, their adulteries, their deceptions and thefts, and punishes them in his thoughts; for He whose eye is not hindered by the flesh from seeing desire, attends to what they want. These, if the opportunity arises, do not do evil, but they reveal their evil intention. Certainly you do not perceive what clearly emerged in his heart, but you understand what was contained in him. A few years ago, almost yesterday, men saw these things, and even those who understand with difficulty knew them. For there exists here a temporally most powerful kingdom, of which God makes a scourge for the human race; and by him he corrects himself if he recognizes in him the scourge of the Father and fears the sentence of the Judge. This great kingdom existing here, many moan in it, murmur, censure, accidat; non quia iustitiam diligunt, sed, ut dicam apertius, timentes damnari Inter homines ab homínibus, abstinent se quidem a factis malis, sed non se abstinent a cogitationibus malis. The intet cogitationes eorum iniquas, praecipue caput iniquitatis illa tenet impietas, qua videtur eís Deus negligere et non cutare res humanos; et aut aequalitet habere bonds et mals; aut etiam, quod est pernicioius cogitate, insectari bonds et malis lavete. Qui talia cogitat, etsi nihil mali alicui faciat, facit plurimum sibi, et in seipsum impius est; et iniquitate sua non laedit Deum, sed interficit se. Ñeque nocent hominibus, quia timidi sunt qui talia cogitant; sed tamen homicide eonim, adultery eorum, frauds et rapinees eorum videt Deus, et punit in cogitationibus eotum.

Quid enim velint, ille attendit, cuius ocuíus non tepellitur carne, ut non videat voluntatern. Such if occasions inveniant, non mali fiunt, sed manifestantur: non ut Sentias quod natum sit manífestum, sed ut íntelligas quod latebat inclusum. Paucis his annis, et prope hesterno die viderunt haec homines, et probaverunt etiam qui late íntelligunt. Erat enim hic una domus potentissima ad tempus, de qua flagellum fecerat Deus generi humano, et punishtum est inde genus humanum; si cognoscat flagellum patris, et timeat sententiam iudicis. Cum etgo esset hic eadem domus magna, muid sub illa gemebant, mutmutabant, reprehendebant, detestabantur, blasphemabant. Quomodo se arctant homines, et dantur divino illo iudicio multi
Ennarrations on the Psalms

they curse, they blaspheme. How men give themselves over to these things and how the just judgment of Goddess gives them the desires of their hearts! But those who censure the same house suddenly become inhabitants of it and endure such things from their fellow men as they themselves a short time before complained about suffering from men. Therefore he is good who, when he can do evil, does not do it, and of whom it was written that he could sin and did not sin, do evil and did not do it. Who is this, and shall we praise him? Because he did wonders in his life. Scripture speaks here of the powerful who are selfless and innocent. Well, the wolf also tries to harm as much as the lion; but, although both desire it equally, nevertheless, they do not harm the same thing. For the lion not only ignores the barking dog, but drives it away; and, approaching the sheepfold, the dogs having stopped barking, he snatches what he can; but the wolf does not dare to enter the flock at the barking of the dogs. But perhaps because he could not, frightened by the dogs, get hold of the prey, he escapes without her innocent? God teaches true innocence: everyone who is innocent is so not because of the fear of punishment, but because of the love of justice. Then certainly he is true and free innocent. He who is innocent because of fear is not innocent, even if he does not cause harm to the one he wants to harm; For he certainly does not harm anyone with an evil action, but he greatly harms himself with a perverse desire. Listen to the Scripture in what way it is harmed: He who loves iniquity kills his soul. Thus, men are greatly mistaken who think that their injustice harms others and not themselves. The iniquity of any man tends to wound the body of others, to cause detriment to property, to in concupiscentias cordis sui? (Rom 1:24). Sudden fiebant ipsius domus illi qui murmurabant de ipsa domo; et ab eis talia homines patiebantur, qualia se pati ipsi a talibus paulo ante querebantur. Bonus ergo ille est, qui et quando potest male faceré, non facit; de quo scriptum est: Qui potuit transgredí, et non est transgressus; et faceré mala, et non fecit. Quis est hic, et laudabimus eum? Fecit enim mirabilia in vita sua (Eccli 31,10.9). Loquebatur Scriptura de potentibus innocentibus.

Et lupus enim tantum vult nocere, quantum leo: dissimiliter nocent, sed non dissimiliter cupiunt. Leo enim non solum contemnit canem latrantem; sed etiam fugat, et venit ad ovile, et obmutescentibus canibus rapit quod potest: lupus non audet inter latratus canum. Numquid propterea quia non potuit auferre a canibus territus, innocentior remeavit? Docet ergo Deus innocentiam, ut quisque innocens sit non timore poenae, sed amore iustitiae. Tune enim liber est innocens, et verus est innocens. Qui autem timore innocens fit, non est innocens, quamvís non noceat cui vult nocere. Non enim nocet alteti per factum malum, sed sibi plurímum per cupiditatem malam. Nam quornodo sibi noceat, audi Scripturam: Qui autem amat iniquitatem, odit animam suam (Ps 10,6). Et revera multum errant homines qui putant iniustitiam suam alus nocere, et sibi non nocere. Ad alios procedit iniquitas cuiuslibet, ut corpoti noceat, ut rem familiam

to seize some property, to violently obtain a slave, to steal gold, silver or something similar that another possesses; This is what iniquity against one's neighbor directs. Therefore, your iniquity hurts another's body, and does it not hurt your soul? 2. Given this simple and true doctrine, which insinuates that good men love justice itself and want to please God through it, they understand that through him their soul has been bathed in a certain intelligible light so that they can execute works of justice and put this light of wisdom before all the things that are loved in the world. Against this doctrine men murmur these things, and, if they do not manage to utter words, yet they ruminate on them in their hearts. Well what do they say? Should I please God with justice? Or does he perhaps like the righteous, campaigning as the wicked camp under his government? These perpetrate infinite iniquities, and yet no evil befalls them. And if by chance some evil befell them, what do they answer when you say to them: "See how many iniquities they committed? But see the payment that was given to them and the end they met!" Then they begin to think about the righteous to whom evils also befell, and they object to us and say: "If some evil happened to him because he was wicked, why did it also happen to him who lived with all justice? Why does he who gave so much alms, He who did so much good in the Church, had such luck, why did he have such an end as the man who perpetrated countless iniquities? "They say these things to show that they do not do evil because they cannot, nor because they do not dare, since the tongue witnesses what the heart wants. But, even though laedat, ut villam invadat, ut mancipium abducat, ut aurum auferat, aut argentum, vel si quid aliud possidet. Ad hoc profertur ad alterum illa iniquitas. Ergo iniquitas tua alieno corpori nocet, tuo animo non nocet? 2.

Contra istam simplicem veracemque doctrinam, qua insinuatur hominibus bonis, ut ipsam iustitiam diligant, et ex ea placeré Deo velint; ab illo intelligant luz quadam intelligibili perfundi animam suam, ut faciant iusta opera, et illam luzm sapientiae ómnibus quae in saeculo diliguntur praeponant: contra istam doctrinam talia murmura sunt hominum; et si non proceedunt in voce, roduntur in corde. Quid ergo dicunt? Will I see placiturus sum Deo per iustitiam? aut iusti illi placent, sub cuius empire mali florent? So much bad committunt, et nihil illis evenit maü. Aut si forte evenit aliquid mali; quid tibi dicunt illi, cum eis coeperis dicere: Ecce quanta fecit mala, quornodo illi redditum est? What exitum habit? Incipiunt illi cogitare iustos quibus mala evenerunt, et opponunt nobis, et dicunt: Si illi propterea mali aliquid accidit, quia iniquus Fuit; illi quare accidit, qui tam iuste vixit? Qui eleemosynas so many fecit, qui tam bien bona operatus est in Ecclesia, quare talem sortem invenit? quare talem exitum habuit, qualem ille homo qui fines iniqua commisit? Ad hoc autem ista dicunt, ut ostendant se propterea non faceré male, quia non possunt, aut quia non audent. Nam quid velit cor, lingua testatur: et quidem, etiamsi lingua obmutesceret et ipsa timore
Ennarrations on the Psalms

tongue, repressed by fear, is silent, God sees what man thinks internally, even if it is hidden from another man. If you want to cure these thoughts of men, whether hidden or emerging in words or actions, this psalm heals them. Then try it and be cured. I hope that in all this crowd that is gathered in this temple and listens to the word of God through me there are no such wounds that need to be healed! I hope there aren't any! However, we do not speak in vain, even if there is no wound in it. By hearing such things, let hearts be instructed in order to heal others. For I believe that every Christian, when he has begun to hear someone say these things, if he is a good believer and believes God perfectly, and has his hope in eternal life, not on earth, not in this life, and does not hear in vain that he puts his heart in heaven, laughs and at the same time grieves those who murmur such things, and says to himself: "God knows what he is doing; I cannot know his plan, I cannot know why he temporarily forgives the wicked or why "The good suffer in this life; but, nevertheless, it is enough for me to know that the good suffers temporarily and the bad prospers temporarily." Therefore the good Christian is safe, and patiently endures the happiness of the evil and the labors of the good, and tolerates until the end of the world, until iniquity disappears. This man is already blessed, and God taught him with his law, and mitigated his evil days, while the hole is dug for the sinner. He who is not yet such, let him hear from me what pleases the Lord. Let him speak many things to the heart, then, who sees better the wound that must be healed.

3. The psalm bears this title, that is, this inscription: Psalm for David; for the fourth day of Saturdays. This psalm should teach us the patience of the righteous in their work. In the face of the happiness of the wicked, teach patience, establish patience. The whole thing, from beginning to end, is about this. Then why does it have this title: For the fourth day of Saturday? The first day after Saturday is Sunday or Lord's Day; the second, the second fair, which worldlings call the day of the moon; the third, the third fair; They call this day Mars; the fourth, the fourth fair, which is called the day of Mercury by the pagans, and also by many Christians, which we do not like, and I hope they correct themselves and do not call it that; They use their own language. However, they are not called that by all peoples; Many call them one way and others another. The Christian must use ecclesiastical usage much better. However, if perhaps someone has been carried away by the habit of pronouncing with his mouth what he disapproves in his heart, he should understand that all those by whose names the stars were called were men and that the stars did not begin to appear in the sky since these men began to exist. They were there before; but, due to certain expired rewards of mortals, those men, according to circumstances, since they had great power and excelled in this world, being loved by men for temporal benefits, not for eternal life, received divine honors. Deceived, then, the ancient worldlings and wanting to deceive, carried away by flattery, since they had received something according to the love of the world, showed

compressa, Deus videret intus quid cogitaret homo, etiamsi alium hominem lateret. Tacitas ergo cogitationes hominum tales, aut etiam erumpentes in verba vel facta, curat iste psalmus, si curari velint. Intendant ergo, et curentur. Atque utinam in hac multitudine tota quae nunc est inter istos parietes, et audit per nos verbum Domini, nulla sint talia vulnera quae curentur; utinam nulla sint. Non tamen rem superfluam facimus dicere, si nulla ibi sunt vulnera. Instruantur corda ad sanandos alios, cum audire talia coeperint. Credo enim quia unusquisque chrístianus, cum audierit aliquem talia dicentem, si bonus fidelis est, et bene credit Deo, et spes eius est in future saeculo, non in hac terra, non in hac vita est, et non frustra audit ut sursum cor habeat; irridet et dolet talia murmurantes, et dicit sibi: Deus novit quid agat, nos non possumus nosse consilium ipsius, quare parcit malis ad tempus, vel quare laborant boní ad tempus; sufficit mihi tamen hoc scire, quia et ad tempus laborat bonus, et ad tempus flotet malus. Qui ergo talis est, securus est; et patienter fert omnes congratulates malorum, et labores bonoruní patienter fert, tolerate, doñee finiatur hoc saeculum, doñee transeat iniquitas. Iam talis beatus est, et erudivit eum Deus de lege sua, et mitigavit eum a diebus malignis, doñee fodiatur peccatori fovea. Qui vero nondum est talis, audiat per nos quod Domino placet. Plura autem ipse dicat in corde, qui melius videt vulnus quod curet.

3. Psalmus hunc titulum haber, id est hanc inscriptionem: Psalmus ipsi David, quarta sabbatorum. Docturus est psalmus iste patientiam in laboribus iustorum: contra iniquorum felicitates patientiamdocet, patientiam aedificat. Hoc habet totus a capite usque in finem. Quare ergo talem habet titulum, in fourth sabbati? Una sabbati, dies dominícus est; second sabbati, second fair, quem saeculares diern Lunae vocant; tettia sabbati, tertia fair, quem diem iüi Martis vocant. Fourth ergo sabbatorum, fourth fair, qui Mercurii dies dicitur a Paganis, et a multis Chrisrianis: sed nollemus; atque utinam corrigant, et non dicant sic. Habent enim linguam suam qua utantur. Non enim et in ómnibus gentibus ist dicuntur:mulae gentes aliae atque aliae aliter atque aliter vocant. Melius ergo de ore christiano ritus loquendi ecclesiasticus procedit. Tamen si quem forte consuetudo traxerit, ut illud exeat ex ore quod improbat corde, intelligat illos omnes, de quorum nominibus appellata sunt sidera, homines Fuisse, nec ex eo esse coepisse ista sidera in cáelo, ex quo illi coeperunt: et ante ibi fuerum; sed per benefit quaedam mortalium mortalia, illi homines pro tempore suo, quia plurimum potuerunt et eminuerunt in hoc saeculo, cum chari essent hominibus, non propter vitam aeternam, sed propter commodum temporale, deferebantur eis divini honores. Veteres enim saeculi decepti, et decipere volentes, in eorum adulationem qui sibi aliquid secundum amorem saeculi praestitissent, si-
Ennarrations on the Psalms

the stars in the sky saying that that star belonged to that one, and the other to the other. Then men, who had not previously looked at the sky to see that these stars were there before these men were born, deceived, believed, and thus this vain opinion was conceived. The devil confirmed this erroneous ruling; Christ cast him down. Therefore, as we speak, the fourth day of the Sabbath is the fourth day from the day of the Lord. Let your charity pay attention to what this title means, for it contains a great mystery, and the truth is hidden. Most of the things in this psalm are clear; They instantly excite and instantly understand each other; but this title, we must confess, is rather obscure. However, with the Lord helping us, the darkness will disappear and you will understand the psalm, because from its frontispiece you will understand it. This psalm has this inscription on its façade: Psalm for David; -for the fourth day of Saturdays. The title is at the threshold; It is fixed to the door of the house. Men always want to know the sign to enter the house safely. Let's go through the Scriptures through the book of Genesis, and we will see that on the first day there was light. In the second, the firmament, which God called heaven. In the third the appearance of the earth and the sea and their separation took place, so that the entire gathering of the waters was called sea, and the arid, land. In the fourth God made the lights in the sky; the sun presiding over the day, and the moon and stars presiding over the night. This he did on the fourth day. Then what does it mean to have taken the psalm's title of the fourth day, in which psalm patience is taught in the face of the happiness of the wicked and dera ostendebant in cáelo, dicentes quod illius esset illud sidus, et illud illius: homines autem qui antea non aspexerant, ut viderent quia ibieront et illa sidera antequam nascerentur, decepti crediderunt; et concepta est opinio vanitatis. Hanc opinionem erroris diabolus confirmavit, Christus evertit. Nos ergo secundum quod loquimur, quarta sabbatorum quartus dies intelligitur a die dominico. Attendat itaque Charitas vestra quid sibi velit iste titulus: hic grande mysterium, et revera occultum.

Nam pleraque ipsius Psalmi manifesté sonant, et manifesté movent, et cyto intelliguntur; hic autem titulus, quod fatendum est, habet non parum obscuritatis: sed aderit Dominus, serenabit nubilum, et videbitis Psalmum, et ex fronte Psalmi cognoscetis eum. In fronte enim habet psalmus iste, Psalmus ipsi David, quarta sabbatorum. In limine est titulus, in postibus fixus est. Volunt homines titulum cognoscere, et sic domum intrare. Recolamus ergo Scripturam sanctam in Genesi, primo die quid sit factum; invenimus luzem: second die quid sit factum; invenimus firmamentum, quod appellavit Deus caelum: tertio die quid sit factum; invenimus speciem terrae et maris, et segregationem, ut omnis congregationtio aquarum vocaretur mare, te arida vocaretur terra. Quarto die, luminaria fecit Deus in cáelo (Gen 1,3-19); solem in potestatem diei, lunam et stellas in potestatem noctis (Ps 135,8.9): hoc quarto die fecit. Quid sibi ergo vult quod de quarto die accepit Psalmus titulum; in quo psalm

the sufferings of the good? See the apostle Saint Paul what he says to the faithful saints confirmed in Christ: Do all things without murmurings and altercations, so that you may be blameless and innocent, pure children of God in the midst of a lost and perverse generation, among whom you shine as lights in the world holding the word of life. The likeness of the luminaries was adduced and applied to the saints so that they would be found without murmuring in the midst of the perverse and lost generation. 4. But so that no one judges that the luminaries of heaven should be honored and adored, since a particular likeness was taken from them to represent the saints, we will first explain, in the name of Christ, that what seems to you does not follow; that the sun, or the moon, or the stars, or the sky must be worshiped, because some likeness was taken from them to symbolize the saints, since there are many things from which the likeness is taken to represent the saints, and yet they are not worshiped. For if you think that everything from which the likeness was taken to personify the saints should be worshiped, worship the mountains and the hills, because it was said: The mountains leaped for joy like rams, and the hills like lambs. You speak now of the saints; I speak of Christ. Therefore worship the lion, because it was said: The lion of the tribe of Judah conquered. He worships the stone, since it was also said: The stone was Christ. Therefore, if you do not worship all these earthly things for Christ, although a certain resemblance was taken from them, then do you, of any creature who takes the resemblance to symbolize the saints, understand thedoctur patientia adversus felicitates malorum, et labores bonorum? Habes Paulum apostolum dicentem sanctis fidelibus roboratis in Christo: "Omnia facite sine murmuratione et disceptatione; ut sitis irreprehensibiles, et sinceres, immaculati filii Dei in medio nationis tortuosae et perversae, in quibus apparetis sicut luminaria in mundo, verbum vitae habentes" (Phil 2,14-16). Similitudo de luminaribus data est ad sanctos, ut sine murmuratione sint in natione tortuosa et perversa. 4.

Sed ne quisquam propterea putet colenda esse et adoranda luminaria caeli, quia inde aliqua similarity ducta est ad significationem sanctorum; prius hoc explicemus in nomine Christi, quam non sit consequens, ut propterea tibi videatur adorandus sol, aut luna, aut stellae, aut caelum, quia aliqua de illis similarity ducta est, qua significarentur sancti; quia fines sunt de quibus ducta est similiarity ad significandos sanctos, quae non adorantur. Si enim quidquid est unde similaro ducitur ad sanctos, adorandum tibi putas; adora montes et colles, quia dictum est: Montes exsultaverunt velut arietes, et colles velut agni ovium (Ps 113,4). Tu de sanctis dicis, ego de ipso Christo dico. Adora leonem, quia dictum est, Vicit leo de tribu luda (Rev 5,5): adora petram, quia dictum est, Petra autem erat Christus (1 Cor 10,4). Si autem non adoras in Christo ista terrena, quamvis de illis similarity quaedam data est; ad meaning saints of quacumque creature ducta fuerit similarity, your
Ennarrations on the Psalms

likeness of the creature and worships its Creator. Our Lord Jesus Christ was called the sun. But perhaps it is this sun that the tiny animals also see with us? No, but He of whom it was said: He was the true light that illuminates every man who comes into this world. And this material light not only illuminates man, but also the donkeys, the beasts and all the animals. However, what illuminates every man, illuminates the heart, where only understanding is found. 5. Let your charity understand those to whom the Apostle said: In the midst of a lost and perverse generation, that is, in the midst of the wicked, among whom you shine as lights in the world, holding fast the word of life. By these words he warned us in a certain way to understand this psalm and know its title. For the saints, in whom the word of life resides, disdain, considering the treatment they have in heaven, all the wicked things that take place on earth. As the luminaries, which advance during the day and night in the sky, having certain revolutions and following their own careers, do not depart from above, fulfilling the celestial movements that their Creator established and prefixed for them despite so many adverse things being offered on earth, so do the saints act; But if they have set their hearts on heaven, if they do not hear and respond in vain that they have set their hearts on heaven, if they imitate Him who says: Our conversation or intercourse is in heaven. Then, as they are on high and think of heavenly things, as it was said: Where your treasure is, there is your heart; therefore, because of these thoughts of heavenly things, they become long-suffering and patient; and thus, intellige similarityinem creaturae, et adora artificem creaturae. Dictus est sol Dominus noster Iesus Christus (Wis 5,6): numquid iste sol quem et minutissima animalia nobiscum vident? Thirst for quo dictum est: Erat lumen verum, quod illuminat omnem hominem venientem in hunc mundum (lo 1,9). Nam lux ista non hominem solum illuminat, sed et iumenta et pécora et omnia animalia: quod autem illuminat omnem hominem, in corde illuminat, ubi intellectum solum habet. 5. Intelligat ergo Charitas Vestra, quibus dixit Apostolus, ln natione tortuosa et perversa, id est, inter iniquos, in quibus apparetis sicut luminaria in mundo, verbum vitae habentes: quodam moda admonuit nos et istum psalmum intelligere, et praenoscere titulum ipsius.

Such enim sancti in quibus est verbum vitae, de conversatione quam habent in cáelo, despiciunt omnia iniqua quae fiunt in terra: et quomodo luminaria in cáelo per diem et per noctem procedunt, peragunt itinera sua, cursus suos certos habent, et committuntur tanta mala, nec deviant desuper stellae fixae in cáelo, agents per tractus caelestes, quae illis praestituit et constituit Creator ipsarum; sic debent sancti, sed si in cáelo figantur corda eorum, si non frustra audiant et responder sursum se habere cor, si imitentur eum qui ait, Nostra autem conversatio in caelis est (Phil 3,20). Quia ergo sunt in supernis, et de supernis cogitant, sicut dictum est, Ubi est thesaurus tuus, ibi est et cor tuum (Mt 6,21); of ipsís caught

While they follow their own path, they do not care about everything that is done on earth, just as they do not care about the birth of the lights of heaven when constituting the days and nights even when they see that an infinite number of perverse things are carried out on the earth. But perhaps it is easy for the righteous to endure the injustices of evils that are not committed against them; (well), just as they endure those that are perpetrated against others, let them also endure those that are committed against them. Well, they should not endure and tolerate them because they are committed against others, and if they are committed against them, they should lose patience. Because, if they lose patience, they fall from the sky. Whoever has his heart fixed on heaven, do not forget that his earth supports on earth. How many things men think about the luminaries, and yet they endure them patiently! For this reason, the righteous must now endure all the false slanders raised against them. I recently said that that star is from Mercury; the other, from Saturn, and the one beyond, from Jupiter. This is an insult to the stars, and yet, when they hear such outrages, are they moved or do they stop pursuing their careers? Well, so also the man who possesses the word of God and is in the midst of a lost and perverse generation, shines like a light in the sky. How many of those who think they honor the sun are deceived about it! Those who say that Christ is the sun are deceived about the sun, for the sun knows that Christ is its Lord and its Creator; and, if he could be indignant, he would be more bitterly indignant against him who honors him falsely than against him who insults him. For the injury done to the Lord is a greater shame to the good servant. How many false things some say about the luminaries! And yet, tationibus supernorum patientes fiunt; et quidquid in terra committitur, sic non curant, doñee peragant itinera sua, quemadmodum non curant luminaria caeli, nisi quomodo exerceant dies et noctes, quamvis tanta mala videant fieri super terram. Sed facile est forte, ut ferant iusti iniquitates malorum, quae non in ipsos fiunt: sed sicut ferunt quae in alios fiunt, sic ferant et quae in ipsos fiunt. Non enim propterea debent ferré et tolerare, quia in alios fiunt: et si in se fiant, non debent lose tolerantiam. Nam qui perdiderit tolerantiam, cecidit de cáelo: qui autem fixum habet cor in cáelo, terra ipsius laborat in terra.

Quanta et de ipsis luminaribus fingunt homines, et patienter ferunt? Quo moda iusti patienter debent ferré omnes etiam de se false criminationes. Hoc ipsum quod iam dudum dixi, quia illa stella Mercurii est, et illa stella Saturni est, et illa stella Iovis est, convicia fiunt stellis. Crux? illae cum audiunt tanta convicia, numquid moventur, aut non exercent cursus suos? Sic et homo qui in natione perversa et tortuosa habet verbum Dei, sicut luminare est fulgens in cáelo. Quanti qui sibi videntur honorare solem, de tilo mentiuntur? Qui dicunt, Christus est sol, mentiuntur de solé. Novit sol Dominum suum esse Christum et Creatorem suum. Et si indignan potest, acerbius indignatur contra false honorantem, quam contra contumeliosum. Servo enim bonus maicr contumelia est iniuria Domini. Quanta

They endure them, tolerate them and are not moved. Because? Because they are in heaven. What is heaven? Let's not overlook this. How men do not lie when they see the moon darken, and say: "The sorcerers reduced it to this state," when at certain times it lacks a certain amount of light by divine disposition! She, who is in heaven, does not care about such human words. What does "is in heaven" mean? Being in the firmament of heaven. Everyone who has his heart set on the firmament, the book of God, does not worry about these things. 6. The sky, that is, the firmament, figuratively symbolizes the book of the law. This is why it is said in a certain place: You spread the sky like a skin. If it is spread like skin or parchment, it is spread or opened, like a book, to be read. But, once time passes, it is no longer read. Then the law is read because we have not yet reached Wisdom, which fills the hearts and minds of those who contemplate, and with which it will not be necessary for anything to be read to us there. Because in what is read to us the words sound and pass; but that Light of Truth does not pass away, but, remaining fixed, intoxicates the hearts of the seers, as it was said: They will be intoxicated with the abundance of your house, and you will give them to drink from the torrent of your delights, because in you, O Lord, is the fountain of life. Contemplate this fountain: In your light—he says—we will see the light. Therefore now, while we know in part and prophesy in part, reading is necessary, as the Apostle says: But when the perfect comes, the imperfect will disappear. But will it not be read in that city of Jerusalem where the Anfalsa of ipsis luminaribus quidam dicunt live? Et ferunt, tolerant, et non moventur. Quare? Quia in cáelo sunt. Caelum autem quid est? Nec hoc praetermittamus: quanta mentiuntuí nomines, quando vident obscurari lunam, et dicunt, Malefici illam deponunt? cum certis temporibus defectum suum habeat secundum Dei dispositionem. Non curat tamen ista verba hominum illa quae in cáelo est. Sed quid est, In cáelo? In firmamento caeli est. Cuius ergo cor in firmamento libri Dei est, ista non curat. 6. Nam caelum, id est, firmamentum, intelligitur per figuram Liber Legis. Ideo quodam loco dicitur, Extendit caelum sicut pellem (Ps 103,2). Si extenditur sicut pellis, tanquam liber est extentus, ut legatur. Transacto autem tempore non legitur.

Propterea enim legitur Lex, quia nondum venimus ad illam Sapientiam quae implet corda et mentes intuentium: et non opus erit ut aliquid ibi nobis legatur. Quia in eo quod nobis legitur, syllabae sonant et transeunt: illa lux veritatis non praeterit, sed fixa permanens ínebriat corda videntium; quomodo dictum est, lenebriabuntur ab ubertate domus tuae, et torrente deliciarum tuarum potabis eos; quoniam apud te est, Domine, fons vitae. Et vide ipsum fontem: In lumine, inquit, tuo videbimus lumen (Ps 35,9.10). Modo ergo lectio necessaria est, quamdiu ex parte cognoscimus, et ex paite prophetamus, sicut dicit Apostolus: cum autem venerit quod perfectum est, auferetur quod ex parte est (1 Cor 13:9-10). Non enim in illa civitate Jerusalem,

gels, and towards which we make a pilgrimage and our pilgrimage groans, because it groans if we know that we are making a pilgrimage, since the homeland is greatly hated by those who believe that things are going well for them while they are on a pilgrimage. Is the Gospel or the Apostle read in the city where the angels live? There they are fed with the Verb or Word of God. In order for this Word to temporarily sound to us, the Word became flesh and dwelt among us. But, with everything, the same law that was written serves as our firmament. If our heart is there, it will not be moved by the iniquities of men. Then it was said: Spread the sky like a skin. But, when the time passes in which there is no need for a book, what will be said? The sky will fold like a book. Therefore, whoever has his heart on high, the same heart is his lamp; It shines in the sky and is not darkened by darkness. For the darkness is below. Darkness is iniquity, but it is not immutable. We already remembered it yesterday. Those who are darkness today, if they want, will be light tomorrow. Those who entered here being darkness, if they want, can be light. So that no one should judge that injustices are things natural to man and that they cannot be changed, the Apostle clearly says: At one time you were darkness, but now you are light in the Lord; walk as children of light. You were, he says, light in the Lord, not in yourselves. Therefore the heart is found in the book; If it is in the book, it is in the firmament of heaven. If the heart is there, it will shine from there and will not be altered by the injustices placed beneath; not because he is already in the flesh in heaven, but because he is there through conversation or dealing with God, as it was said: Our conversation is in heaven. You still cannot imagine ubi Angeli vivunt, unde nos modo peregrinamur, et peregrinatio nostra gemit; gemit autem, si scimus quia peregrinamur; nam odit valde patriam, qui putat sibi bene esse cum peregrinatur: numquid in illa civitate ubi sunt Angeli, Evangelium legitur, aut Apostolus? Verbo Dei pascuntur: quod Verbum Dei, ut sonaret nobis ad tempus, Verbum caro factum est, et habitavit in nobis (lo 1,14). Sed tamen ipsa Lex, quae scripta est, firmamentum nobis est: ibi si sit cor nostrum, non convellitur iniquitatibus hominum. Dictum est ergo, Extendit caelum sicut pellem. Cum autem transeunt tempora necessitatis librorum, quid dictum est? Caelum plicabitur ut liber (Is 34:4).

Qui ergo sursum habet cor, ipsum cor ipsius luminare est: in cáelo fulget, nec vincitur tenebris. Infra enim sunt tenebrae: tenebrae autem iniquitas; non incommutabiles tenebrae. Iam et hesterno die commemoravimus. Be qui hodie tenebrae sunt, si velint, eras lux erunt: qui tenebrae huc ingressi sunt, si velint, iam lux esse possunt. Aperte enim Apostolus, ne quis putaret naturales esse iniquitates, quae mutari non possunt: ​​Fuistis enim, inquit, aliquando tenebrae; nunc autem lux in Domino: sicut fiüi lucis ambulate (Eph 5,8). Lux, inquit, in Domino: non in vobis. Cor ergo in libro: si cor in libro cor in firmamento caeli. Si ibi est cor, inde luzat, et non movebitur iniquitatibus subterpositis: non quia ibi est in cáelo per carnem, sed quia ibi est per conversationem, secundum quod dictum est, Nostra

that city, because you don't see it. Do you want to imagine heaven? Think about the book of God. Listen to the psalm: I will meditate on your law day and night. There it was also said: Blessed is he who is not found in the council of the wicked, nor stands in the way of sinners, nor sits in the pestilential seat, but maintains his will in the law of the Lord. Behold the light in the sky: And he will meditate on the law of the Lord day and night. Do you want to patiently endure all things? Do not come down from heaven and meditate on the law of the Lord day and night. Then his heart is in heaven. If his heart is in heaven, all the injustices that are temporarily committed on earth, all the happiness of evil men, all the sufferings of the righteous, are nothing to him who meditates day and night on the law of the Lord; Therefore, patiently tolerate all things, and, indoctrinated by God, you will be blessed. But how in the firmament of heaven? Because the law is the firmament. Blessed is the man whom you, Lord, instruct and teach your law in order to mitigate him in evil days until the pit is dug for the sinner. Then he sees how the luminaries advance, hide, return, run their own races, divide the day and the night, constitute the years and the seasons; and, despite so many adverse things happening on earth, they enjoy quiet in heaven. What does God teach us? Let us now attend to the psalm.

7 [v. l]. God of revenge is the Lord; The God of vengeance acts fearlessly. Do you think he doesn't punish? The God of revenge punishes. What does the God of revenge mean? The God of vindications. No doubt you murmur against Him for-

that does not punish the bad. Do not murmur, so as not to be among those whom he punishes. A man commits theft and lives; You murmur against God because he who steals from you does not die. If you no longer steal, pay attention; If you no longer steal, go, lest at some time you have stolen. If you are already day, think about your last night. If you are already fixed on heaven, think about earth. Perhaps you will find that you were a thief for a time, and perhaps someone will be displeased, because you also, committing the theft, lived and did not laugh. Just as you, when you committed it, lived so as not to commit it later, do not want, because you have already passed, to tear down the bridge of God's mercy. Don't you know that many will pass through where you passed? Would you exist now to murmur if he who first murmured against you had been heard? And yet, even now you desire punishment from God against the wicked, longing for the thief to die, and you murmur against God because the thief does not die. Weigh the thief and the blasphemer in the scales of justice; You say you are no longer a thief; but, by murmuring against God, you are a blasphemer. The thief spies on man's sleep in order to steal something from him, and you say that God sleeps and does not see man. If you want Him to correct the hand, first correct the tongue. You want Him to correct the heart against man; correct yours against God, lest perhaps, when you ask God for revenge, if it comes, it will reach you first. Because, without a doubt, God will come; He will come and judge those who remain in their iniquity, those who are ungrateful for the gift of His mercy, those who are ungrateful for His patience, who have stored up wrath for themselves against the day of wrath and the manifestation of the righteous judgment of

autem conversalio in caelis est. Non potes cogitare illam civitatem, quia nondum vides. Vis cogitare caelum? Librum Dei cogita. Audi psalmum: Et in lege eius meditabitur die ac nocte. Et ibi beatus dictus est qui non abiit in consilio impiorum, et in via peccatorum non stetit, et in cathedra pestilentiae non sedit; sed in lege Domini Fuit voluntas eius (Ps 1,1.2). Vide luminare in cáelo: Et in lege eius meditabitur die ac nocte. Vult patienter ferré omnia? Non descendat de cáelo, et in lege eius meditetur die ac night. Ergo in cáelo cor eius: si in cáelo cor eius, omnes iniquitates quae fiunt in terra ad tempus, omnes felicitates malorum hominum, omnes labores iustorum medifanti die ac nocte legem Dei, nulli sunt; et patienter tolerat omnia, et erit beatus eruditus a Deo. Et quomodo in firmamento caeli? Quia lex firmamentum est. Beatus vir quem tu erudieris, Domine, et ex lege tua docueris eum: ut mitiges eum a diebus malignis, doñee fodiatur peccatori fovea. Attendite ergo luminaria quomodo procedunt, et occidunt, et redeunt, agunt cursus suos, distinguunt diem et noctem, volvunt annos et tempora; et tanta mala fiunt in terra, illis quietem in cáelo habentibus. Quid est ergo quod nos doctrinat Deus? Iam attendamus Psalmum. 7 [v.l]. Deus ultionum Dominus, Deus ultionum fidenter egit. Your whores quia non vindicat? Vindicat Deus ultionum. What is it, Deus ultionum? Deus vindictarum. In eo cene murmuras, quia non vindicatur in

bad Noli murmurare, ne Inter illos sis in quos vindicatur. Facit ille furtum, et vivit: tu murmuras adversus Deum, quia non moritur qui tibi furtum fecit. Si iam non facis furtum, vide: si enim iam non facis, vide ne aliquando fecisti. Si iam dies es, recolé noctem tuam: si iam fixus in cáelo es, recolé terram tuam. Invenís te furem forte fuesse aliquando; et aliquem alium forte stomachatum, quia et tu furtum faciens vixisti, et non es mortuus: quomodo autem tu quando faciebas, ideo vixisti ut postea non faceres; noli quia tu transisti, velle misericordiae Dei pontem subvertere. Nescis illac multos transituros, qua et tu transiti? Esses modo qui murmurares, si adversus te audiretur qui prior de te murmuravit? Et tamen et nunc optas vindictam Dei in malas, ut fur moritur, et murmuras adversus Deum, quia fur non moritur. Appende in statera aequitatis furem et blasphemum: iam dicis quia fur non es; sed murmuring adversus Deum, blasphemus es. Ule capitat somnum hominis, ut aliquid involet; et tu dicis quia dormit Deus, et hominem non videt. Ergo vis ille ut corrigat manum, prior tu linguam corrige: vis ille ut corrigat cor adversus hominem, tu corrige cor adversus Deum; ne forte eum optas vindictam Dei, si venerit, te priorem inveniat. Nam ille veniet, veniet et iudicabit perseverantes in nequitia sua, ingratos praerogationi misericordiae ipsius, ingratos patientiae ipsius, thesaurizados sibi iram in die irae et revelationis iusti iudicii Dei, qui reddet unicuique seeundum opera

God, who will give to each one according to his works, for he is the God of vengeance, and therefore he works firmly. When he spoke on earth, he forgave no one, because the Lord himself appeared weak in the weakness of the flesh, but powerful in the word. He was not an acceptor of people as far as the princes of the Jews were concerned. How many things he didn't blame them for! And, as it was written, everything was boldly told to them, since it was recorded about Him in the psalm: For the misery of the needy and the groaning of the poor, I will arise immediately, says the Lord. Who are the poor? Who are the needy? Those who have placed only hope in Him in whom alone does not fail. See, brothers, who are the poor and the needy. When Scripture praises the poor, it does not speak of the poor who possess nothing. Perhaps you will find a poor man who, when suffering some injury, only attends to his master, in whose house he perhaps lives, and of whom he is a tenant, servant, client and, for the same reason, he affirms that he suffers without reason, because he belongs to him; His heart and his hope are placed in man, dust in dust. On the contrary, there are some who are rich and temporarily enjoy human honors, and yet they do not place their hope in their money, in their property, in their family, in the splendor of their transitory dignity, but in Him Whom no one succeeds Him, in Him who cannot die, who cannot be deceived or deceived; These, although they appear to possess many worldly riches, nevertheless organize them admirably to help the needy, being counted among the poor of the Lord. Well, sua (Rom 2,4-6): quia Deus ultionum Dominus, Deus ultionum, ideo jidenter egit. Nulli enim pepercit, quando hic locutus est: ipse Dominus erat in carnis infirmitate, sed in virtute sermonis. Non accepit personas principum Iudaeorum. How much did you say? et, quomodo dictum est, veré in fiducia: quia scriptum est in Psalmis de illo, Propter miseriam inopum et gemitum pauperum, nunc exsurgam, dicit Dominus. Who sunt pauperes? who sunt inopes? Qui spem non habent nisi in illo solo, in quo solo spes non fallitur. Attendite, fratres, who are pauperes et inopes.

Non omnino pauperes qui nihil habent, videntur dici ab Scriptura, quando laudantur pauperes. Invenís enim pauperem hominem, qui quando patitur aliquam iniuriam, non attendit nisi patronum suum, in cuius forte domo manet, cuius inquilinus est, cuius colonus est, cuius cliens est; et ideo se indigne pati asserit, quia ad illum pertinet: cor ipsius in homine, spes ipsius in homine, cinis in ciñere. Sunt autem alii qui opulenti sunt, et honoribus secundum tempus humanis fulciuntur; et tamen nec in pecunia sua spem ponunt, nec in fundís suis spem ponunt, nec in familia sua spem ponunt, nec in claritate transitoriae dignitatis; sed totam spem in illo ponunt, cui non succedítur, qui mori non potest, qui fallí et qui fallere non potest: such etsi fines videntur habere secundum saeculum, bene ea tamen gubernant ad refectionem indigentium; inter pauperes Domini numerantur. Vident enim periculose se vivere in hac vita, sentiunt se esse pilgrims; skdiversantur in opulentia divitiarum suarum,

By understanding that they live in danger in this life and realizing that they are pilgrims in it, they stay in the opulence of its riches as a traveler who must continue on the road and must not settle in the inn. So what does the Lord say? For the misery of the needy and the groaning of the poor, I will arise instantly, says the Lord, and will restore them to health. Our health is our Savior; He wanted to place the hope of all the poor and needy in Him. And what does it say? I will act boldly. What does it mean I will act fearlessly? He will not fear, he will not forgive the vices and greeds of men. The honest doctor, armed with the medicinal lancet of the word, heals all wounds. Therefore, he who was announced and prophesied in this way, thus presented himself. And thus he spoke on the mountain, where he said: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. There also those who suffer persecution for righteousness were called blessed; And he added: Because theirs is the kingdom of heaven. And to make them luminous, that is, patient, enduring of all these passing injustices, he adds: You will be blessed when you are persecuted and they say all evil against you. Rejoice and be glad, for you will have great reward in heaven. Then, in the course of the sermon, when he began to teach, despite the crowd surrounding him, he said such things to his disciples that they hurt the faces of the Pharisees and the Jews, who assumed the primacy of the exposition of all the holy Scriptures; who believed themselves to be righteous and who received the obedience of the mob in response to their authority; In these circumstances, as I recorded, he did not forgive and said: When you pray, do not pray like the hypocrites, who like to pray quomodo viator in stabulo, transiturus, non possessurus. Ergo quid Dominus? Propter miseriam inopum et gemitum pauperum nunc exsurgam, dicit Dominus: ponam in salutari. Salutaris noster, Salvator noster est: in illo voluit I will put spem omnium inopum et egentium. Et quid ait? Fiducialiter agam in eo (Ps 11,6). What is it, Fiducialiter agam? Non timebit, non parcet vitiis et concupiscentiis hominum. Veré medicus fidelis, medicinali ferro sermonis instructus, secuit omnia vulnera.

Ideo qui talis praedictus et praenuntiatus, talis etiam inventus est. Loquebatur in monte, ubi dixit: Beati pauperes spiritu, quoniam ipsorum est regnum caelorum. Ibi beati dicti sunt qui persecutionem patiuntur propter iustitiam: in ipso sermone dixit, Quia ipsorum est regnum caelorum. Et ut faceret illos luminaria, id est, patienter tolerant omnia ista iniqua, quae transeunt: Beati eritis, inquit, cum vos persecuti juerint, et dixerint omne malum adversum vos: gaudete et exsultate, quia merces vestra magna est in caelis (Mt 5,3-10.11.12). Deinde in progressu sermonis cum docere inciperet, quamvis eum turba circumdaret, dixit talia discipulis suis, quae ferirent faciem Phatisaeorum et Iudaeorum, qui quasi primatus habebant exponendarum Scripturarum omnium; qui sibi quasi iusti videbantur, vel videri se arbitrabantur, et ad quorum primatum plebis obsequium videbatur obtem-

Because he acted fearlessly, they did not endure his

firmness. As he appeared weak and was clothed in flesh, and had come to die, not to do what sinners did, but to suffer what they suffered; Because he came, I repeat, to this, having acted fearlessly, and they could not bear the courage of his words, what did they do? They seized him, whipped him, abused him, slapped him, spat on him, crowned him with thorns, lifted him up on the cross and finally killed him. But for the simple reason of having acted fearlessly, what next? Arise, you who judge the earth. Do you think that because they captured the humble, they will dominate the Exalted? Do you think that because they judged the mortal they will not be judged by the Immortal? What does it say? Arise, you who acted fearlessly. The wicked, who did not tolerate the boldness of your word, and who, for the same reason, thought that they did something, because by capturing you they crucified you, while they should have captured you with faith, they captured you with persecution. Then you, who acted boldly among the wicked and feared no one and suffered, arise; that is, he is resurrected and goes to heaven. Let the Church also suffer patiently what its Head suffered patiently. Arise, you who judge the earth and give what they deserve to the proud. Brothers, you must give what you deserve. What does it mean that it was said: Arise, you who judge the earth: give what they deserve to the proud? This is prophecy of one who predicts, not the daring of someone who commands. Well, not because the prophet said: Arise, you who judge the earth, Christ obeyed the prophet by resurrecting and going to heaven, but because Christ was going to do this, that is why the prophet predicted it. Therefore, Christ did not do it because the prophet said it, but the prophet prophesied it

perare: non pepercit, et dixit, Quando oratis, non eritis sicut bypocritae, qui amant in synagogis et angulis platearum stantes orare, ut videantur ab hominibus (ib. 6,5); et caetera talia. Tetigit omnes, non timuit aliquem. Et cum terminasset ipsum sermonem, conclusit de ilio scriptura Evangelii sic: "Factum est", inquit, "cum consummasset Iesus verba haec, admirantur turbae super doctrina eius. Erat enim docens eos tanquam potestatem habens; non quasi Scribae eorum et Pharisaei" (ib. 7,28 et 29). Quanta ergo ille de quo dictum est, Erat docens eos tanquam potestatem habens, quanta dixit: Vae vobis, Scribae et Pharisaei hypocritae (ib. 23,13, etc.); quanta in illos coram in faciem? Neminem timuit. Quare? Quia Deus ultionum est. Ideo non parcebat in verbo, ut essent postea quibus parceret in iudicio: quia si nollent accipere verbi medicinalm, incursuri erant utique et inventuri iudicis sententiam. Quare? Quia dixit, Deas ultionum Dominus, Deus ultionum fidenter egit: id est, nulli pepercit in verbo. Who in verbo non pepercit passurus, parcet in sententia iudicatutus? who neminem timuit in humilitate, timebit quemquam in claritate? Ex eo quod iam fidenter egit, cogita quomodo sit acturus in fine saeculi. Noli ergo murmurare adversus Deum, qui quasi parcit malis; be this bonus cui forte ad tempus in flagello non parcat, et in fine parcat in iudicio. Deus ultionum Dominus, Deus ultionum fidenter egit. 8 [v.2]. Et quia fidenter egit, illi non tulerunt fiduciam eius: et

quia humilis venerat, et catne mortali indutus erat, et mori venerat; non faceré quod peccatores, sed pati quod peccatores; quia propterea venerat, cum fidenter egisset, et illi ferré non possent fiduciam eius in verbo, quid fecerunt? Tenuerunt, flagellaverunt, illuserunt, colaphÍ2averunt, sputis iilinierunt, spinis coronaverunt, in cruz levaverunt, postremo occiderunt. Sed quid sequitur quod fidenter egerit? Exaltare, qui indica terram. Puta quia tenuerunt humilem, tenebunt excelsum? Puta quia iudicaverunt mortalem, nonne ab immortali iudicabuntur? Quid ergo ait? Exaltare, tu qui fidenter egisti, et fiduciam verbi mi non sunt passi iniqui, et putaverunt se aliquid egisse, quia te comprehendentes crucifixerunt; qui te debenrent fide comprehendere, comprehenderunt persecutione: tu ergo qui fidenter egisti inter iniquos, et neminem timuisti, et quia passus es, Exaltare; id est, resurge, vade in caelum. Patiatur et Ecclesia patienter, quod passum est caput Ecclesiae patienter. Exaltare, qui indicas terram; redde retributionem superbis. Redditurus est, fratres. Quid est enim quod dictum est, Exaltare, qui indica terram: redde retributionem superbis? Prophetia est praedicentis, non audacia iubentis. Non enim quia dixit Prqpheta, Exaltare, qui indicas terram, obtemperavit Prophetae Christus, ut resurgeret et iret iti caelum; sed quia hoc facturus erat Christus, hoc praedixit Propheta: non ideo fecit Christus, quia Propheta praedixerat; sed ideo Propheta praedixerat, quia ille facturus erat. Videt humilem Christum in spiritu,

•standing •in the synagogues and at the crossroads of the squares to be seen by men, and the rest that is said there. He messed with everyone; notified anyone. And, having finished the sermon, the Gospel Scripture says of Him: And it came to pass that, when Jesus had finished uttering these words, the crowds were astonished at his doctrine, for he taught them as one who has authority, not as his lawyers and Pharisees. How many times did He Who was said to teach them as one who had authority not say: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! How many things he didn't blame them for! He feared no one. Because? Because he is the God of revenge. He did not stop preaching so that later there would be men whom he could forgive at trial; If then they did not want to take the medicine of the word, they had to incur and receive the judge's sentence. Because? Because he said: The Lord is a God of vengeance; the God of vengeance acts fearlessly; That is, he forgave no one with words. Will he who, having to suffer, did not stop speaking, having to judge, forgive when passing sentence? He who feared no one when he was in weakness, will he fear anyone when he was in magnificence? He reconsiders how he must act at the end of the world, taking into account what he fearlessly does now. Do not murmur against God because He seems to forgive the wicked, but be good to Him who perhaps temporarily spares you punishment and finally forgives you in judgment. God of revenge is the Lord; The God of vengeance acts fearlessly. 8 [v.2].

because Christ had to do it. He sees in spirit the humble Christ in life, he sees the humble, who fears no one, who forgives no one in his speeches, and says: He acted fearlessly. He sees him with the intrepidity with which he acted; sees him imprisoned, crucified, humiliated; sees him, resurrected, walking to heaven; He sees him coming from there to judge those at whose hands he suffered all kinds of evils and says: Arise, you who judge the earth; He gives what he deserves to the proud. He will give what they deserve to the proud, not to the humble. Who are the proud? Those for whom it is not enough to do wrong, and, for this reason, they try to defend their sins. But these proud people are not those who crucified Christ, and in whom later wonders were worked when a large number of Jews believed and the blood of Christ was given to them. Certainly these had impious hands that were bloody with the blood of Christ, but He whose blood they had shed washed them. Those who persecuted his body when they saw him mortal, adhered to his body, that is, to the Church. They poured out their price to drink it, because later many were converted. Well, as the apostles worked countless miracles, several thousand men were converted in a single day; and they were so united with them that they sold all their goods and placed the price at the feet of the apostles, giving each one what he needed; and so between them and those who crucified Christ there existed only one soul and one heart in God. But why weren't these people given what they deserved? Because it was said: He will give what they deserve to the proud, and they did not want to be proud. Indeed, seeing that miracles were worked due to videt humilem; neminem timentem, nulli parcentem in verbo, et dicit: Fidenter egit. Videt illum quam fidenter egit, videt illum comprehensum, videt illum crucifixum, videt illum humiliatum, videt illum resurgentem et euntem in caelum, et venturum inde ad iudicium eorum, inter quorum matms passus est omnia mala: Exaltare, inquit, qui indicas terram; redde retributionem. superbis. Superbis reddet, non humilibus. Who sunt superbi? Quibus parum est quod mala faciunt, et defenseré peccata sua volunt. Namque de his qui crucifixerunt Christum facta sunt postea miracula, quando de ipso numero Iudaeorum crediderunt, et donatus est illis sanguis Christi. Impías manus et cruentas de sanguine Christi portabant: lavit eas ípse cuius sanguinem fuderant.

Adiuncti sunt corpori ipsius, id est Ecclesiae, qui cotpus eius moitale, quod videiant, persecuti sunt. Fuderunt pretium suum, ut biberent pretium suum. Namque posts plures conversi sunt. Cuín fines miracula ieront ab Apostolis, aliquot hominum millia una die crediderunt: et tam in propinquo inventi sunt, ut omnia sua quae habebant vendeent, et pretium rerum suarum ad pedes Apostolorumponerent; et unicuique distribuebatur quomodo opus erat; et erat illis una anima et cor unum in Deum; of ipsis crucifixoribus Domini. Sed quare non illis redditum est? Quia, Redde retributionem superbis, dictum est; illi autem noluerunt esse superbi. Etenim cum viderent fine miracula fieri per nomen Christi, quem se putabant interfecisse; commoti miraculis, audierunt a Petro in cuius nomine illa ieront: non enim sibi arrogare

name of Christ, whom they thought they had killed, moved by the miracles, they heard from Peter in whose name they performed them, since the servants did not arrogate to themselves the power of the Lord saying that they performed what He did for them. The servants honored their Lord, for they said that what they admired, they did in the name of Him whom they crucified. Then, humbling themselves, repenting, and troubledly confessing their sin, they asked for advice, saying: Then what are we doing? They do not despair of their health; They go in search of medicine. Peter said to them: Do penance and be baptized, each one of you, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ. Those who repented humbled themselves; then they were not given what they deserved. Because see what this psalm says: Arise, you who judge the earth; give what they deserve to the proud. They were not one of these. The word of the Lord prevailed in them, who, hanging from the cross, said: Father, forgive them, because they do not know what they do. Arise, you who judge the earth. Does he then have to give what he deserves? He will give, but to the proud. 9 [v.3.4]. When? When should you pay back? Now the bad guys triumph; They rejoice, they blaspheme, they eat in all kinds of iniquities. Does this move you? Investigate with pity, do not censure with pride. Does it move you? The psalm pities you and inquires with you, not because it ignores it; Well, he investigates with you what he knows so that you can find in him what you do not know. Just as he who wants to console someone does not encourage him unless he commiserates with him, so the psalm first grieves with him in order to revive him with words of consolation. Well, if he approached him laughing at servi voluerunt potentiam Domini sui, ut dicerent a se factum esse quod ille in ipsis faciebat. Honorem ergo dederunt servi Domino suo: dixerunt quia quae illi mirantur, in nomine ieront eius quem illi crucifixerunt. Et facti sunt humiles, compuncti sunt corde, conturbati sunt confitentes peccatum suum; et consilium quaesierunt, dicentes: Quid ergo faciemus? Non desperant de salute, sed quaerunt medicinal. Tune ait illis Petrus: Agite poenitentiam, et baptizetur unusquisque vestrum in nomine Domini nostri lesu Christi (Act 2,4). Qui egerunt poenitentiam, humiles fuetunt: non ergo illis redditum est. Quia, vide quid dicat psalmus iste: Exaltare, qui judicas terram; redde retributionem superbis.

Ab illo number ergo excepti werent illi; in illis valuit vox illa Domini pendentis in intersection, et dicetis: Pater, ignosce illis, quia nesciunt quid faciunt (Le 23-24). Exaltare, qui judicas terram; redde retributionem superbis. Ergo redditurus est retributionem? Redditurus, be superbis. 9 [v.3.4}. Thirst when? when reddet? Interina mali triumphant, et exsultant mali, blasphemant mali, omnia mala faciunt. Movet you? Cum pietate quaere, non cum superbia reprehende. Movet you? Compatitur tibi et Psalmus, quaerit tecum, non quia nescit; sed ideo tecum quaerit quod scit, ut in illo invenías quod nesciebas. Quomodo qui vult aliquem consolari, nisi condoleat cum illo, non illum erigit: prius cum illo dolet, et sjc eum reficit sermone consolatorio, Si autem ititret ad illum ridens
