his misfortune, he would not do what was read little in the Apostle: Rejoice with those who rejoice and weep with those who weep. As for a man to rejoice with you, first you cry with him; you grieve with him to revive him; so also the psalm, the Spirit of God, who knows all things, seeks you and almost pronounces your very words, for it says: How long, Lord, how long will sinners glory, answer and speak iniquity; Will all those who do injustice speak? What will the charlatans say against God who say: "What good is it for us to live this way?" What do you have to say? Does God care about the things we do? Because they live, they think that God does not know what they do. He sees the evil that befalls them. If the guard or policeman found out about it, he would arrest them; That is why they avoid, in order not to be captured, the gaze of the guard; but no one can hide from the eyes of God, because he not only sees in the chamber of your room, but also in the most intimate part of your heart. Thinking, therefore, that nothing can be hidden from God, knowing that they do evil and knowing what they do, realizing that they live knowing God who would not live knowing the guard, they say to themselves: "These things please God, because if our actions certainly displease Him, as they displease judges, as they displease kings, as they displease emperors, as they displease the prefects of prisons, why How could we hide ourselves from God's gaze as we avoid theirs? Then do these things please God? For this reason it is said to the sinner in another psalm: You did this and I was silent; You suspected through iniquity that I am like you. What does it mean I am similar to you? That as it pleases you luctum eius, non facit quod moda lectum est, dicente Apostolo: Gaudere cum, gaudentibus, flere cum flentibus (Rom 12:15). Ergo ut gaudeat tecum, prius fies cum illo; contristaris cum illo, ut reficias eum: sic et Psalmus et Spiritus Dei, utique omnia sciens, quaerit tecum, quasi verba tua dicit. Usquequo peccatores, Domine, usquequo peccatores gloriabuntur; responder, et loquentur iniquitatem; loquentur omnes qui operantur iniustitiam? Quid loquentur, nisi contra Deum, qui dicunt: Quid nobis prodest quia sic vivimus? What dicturus is it? Will I see curat ista quae facimus Deus? Quia enim vivunt, putant Deum nescire quod faciunt. Vide quid mali illis contingat!

Quia si stationarius sciret, teneret illos; et ideo vitant oculos stationarii, ne statim teneantur: oculos enim Dei vitare nemo potest; Quia non solum in cubicle videt, sed et intima cordis tui. Cogitant et ípsi quia nihil potest Iatere Deum; et quia faciunt, et scíunt quid fecerunt, et vident se vivere sciente Deo, qui non viverent sciente stationario, dicunt sibi: Placent ista Deo; et revera si illi displicerent facta nostra, quomodo displicent iudicibus, quomodo displicent regibus, quomodo displicent imperatoribus, et quomodo displicent commentariensibus, numquid quomodo illorum oculos vitamus, vitare possemus oculos Dei? Ergo placent istista Deo. Ideo in alio psalmo peccatori dicitur, Haec fecisti, et tacui; suspicatus is iniquitatem, quod ero tibi similis. Quid est, ero tibi similis? Ut quomodo tibi placet factum tuum malum, sic putes quia et tnifii

your bad deed, you think it pleases me too. But then he is threatened, so he continues: I will argue with you. Therefore he who said silence does not remain silent. When you said: You did this and I was silent, you suspected because of iniquity that I am like you; but I did not remain silent. When we speak, he does not remain silent; When the reader reads, he does not remain silent; When the psalm sings these things, it is not silent; What's more, all these voices of God extend throughout the entire globe of the earth. Then how is he silent, how is he not silent? He does not keep his word silent, he keeps his revenge silent. Lueque, what does it mean: You did this and I kept quiet? You did this and I didn't punish. You suspected because of your iniquity that I am like you. About the muteness of his revenge, that is, about the cessation of his punishment, he says in another place: I was silent; But will I always be silent? How long, Lord, will sinners; How long will sinners glory, answer and speak iniquity; Will all those who do injustice speak? And then he declares the kind of works: They will answer and speak iniquity. What does they respond mean? That they will respond to the righteous. For example, a random righteous person appears and says: "Do not commit injustice." Because? Because you will die. "You see," they answer, "that I committed injustice; why don't I die? On the contrary, that one did justice and died; why did he die? I committed iniquity; why didn't God annihilate me? You see that that one did justice; why did he take revenge on him like this? Why does he suffer?" This is how the wicked respond, because they have a basis for this response; for God forgives them, and they draw on his patience for his response. God forgives them for one reason, and they respond for another, because they live. The Apostle tells why he forgives them when he explains the plan of God's patience. placet. Et minatur in posterum: Arguam te (Ps 49,21). Ergo non tacet qui dixit, tacui. Cum diceret, Haec fecisti, et tacui; suspicatus is iniquitatem, quod ero tui similis; et non tacuit. Cum enim nos loquimur, ille non tacet; cum enim legit reader, ille non tacet; cum Psalmus ista cantat, ille non tacet: et istae omnes voices Dei per orbem terrarum fiunt. Quomodo ergo tacet, quomodo non tacet? Non tacet in verbo, tacet in vindicta. Quid est ergo, Haec fecisti, et tacui? Haec fecisti, et non vindicavi. Suspicatus es iniquitatem, quod ero tui similis. From ipsa vindictae taciturnitate, id est, from cessatione vindictae, alio loco dicit: tacui; numquid semper tacebo (Is 42:14).

Usquequo peccatores, Domine, usquequo peccatores gloriabuntur; responder, et loquentur iniquitatem; loquentur omnes qut operantur iniustitiam? Et dicit omnia opera. Respondent, et loquentur iniquitatem. What is it, responder? Contra iustum habent quod responder. Venit iustus aliquis, et dicit: Noli faceré iniquitatem. Quare? Ne moriaris. Ecce feci iniquitatem; quare non morior? Ule fecit iustitiam, et mortuus est: quare mortuus est? Ego feci iniquitatem; quare me non abstulit Deus? Ecce, ille fecit iustitiam; et quare sic in illum vindicavit? quare ille sic laborat? responder; hoc est, responder, quia habent quod dicant; quia parcitur illis, de patientia Dei inveniunt argumentum responsionis suae. Parcit ille propter aliud, respondert illi propter aliud, quia vivunt. Quare enim parcat ille, dicit Apostolus, exponit consilium paS.Ag. 21

Do you think, he says, that you are doing such things that you will escape the judgment of God? Or do you despise the riches of his kindness and long-suffering, ignoring that the patience of God calls you to penitence? But you, that is, he who answers and says: "If it displeased God, he would not forgive me," see what he does to himself, hear the Apostle: But you, according to the hardness of your heart, of the impenitent heart, store up wrath for the day of wrath and the manifestation of the righteous judgment of God, who will repay each one according to his works. He multiplies longsuffering, and you increase iniquity. His treasure is found in eternal mercy for those who did not disdain mercy, and yours, on the contrary, is found in wrath. What you add little by little every day, you will find later all together. You accumulate it by putting together very small parts, but you will find it in a pile. You do not pay attention to the tiny sins of every day, do not forget that rivers swell with tiny drops. 10 {v.5.6]. What do, what do they respond, what do they speak iniquitously who act like this and are forgiven? They struck down your people, O Lord! that is, to all those who live in righteousness, over whom all evildoers want to excel. They brought down your people, O Lord, and vexed your inheritance; They killed the widow and the orphans and took the life of the proselyte; that is, to the pilgrim, to the stranger, to the foreigner, because he calls this one a proselyte. Each of these things are clear in themselves; For the same reason, I do not need to stop at his exposition. 11 [v.7]. And they said, "The Lord will not see." He does not attend to estientiae Dei: Existimas, inquit, qui taita agís, quid tu effugies iudicium Dei? An divinas benignitatis et longanimitatis eius contemnis,ignons quia patientia Dei ad poenitentiam te adducit? Tu autem, id est, ille qui responder et dicit, Si displicerem Deo, non mihi parceret Deus: vide quid sibí facit, audi Apostolum: Tu autem secundum duritiam cordis tui et cor impoenitens, thesaurizas tibi iram in die irae et revelationis iusti iudicii Dei, qui reddet unicuique secundum opera sua (Rom 2,3-6). Ule ergo auget longanimitatem, et tu auges iniquitatem. Erit illius thesaurus in sempiterna misericordia in eos qui non contempserunt misericordiam; tuus autem thesaurus in ira invenietur, et quod ponis quotidie per modicum, postea massam inventurus es: minutatim ponis, sed cumulum invenies. Noli attendere minute peccata tua quotidiana; de minutissimis guttis flumina implentur.

10 [v.5.6]. Quid autem illi faciunt, qui respondert et loquentur iniquitatem, quia faciunt et parcitur eis? Populum tttum, Domine, humiliaverunt: id est, omnes qui iuste vivunt, in quos volunt superbire omnes malí. Populum tuum, Domine, htimiliaverunt, et haereditatem tuam vexaverunt: viduam et pupillos interjecerunl, et proselytum occiderunt: id est, peregrinum, advenam, adventitium; ipsum dicit proselytum. Manifesta sunt ist singula, nec opus est in his immorari. 11 [v.7]. Ut dixerunt, Non videbit Dominus. Non attendit ista, ne-

these things; he neglects them, he worries about others; He doesn't understand. These two sayings: one, the one I already hinted at, you did this and I kept silent; You suspected because of iniquity that I am like you, it is typical of the wicked; Well, what does it mean that I am similar to you? That you think I see your actions and that I like them, because I don't punish. The other, that God does not pay attention to these things nor cares to know how I live, since "God does not care about me" is typical of the wicked. "Does God have something in me? Does he remember me or the men themselves?" Senseless! He cared for you so that you existed, and won't he worry that you live well? After the wicked is this saying: And they said, "The Lord will not see, nor will the God of Jacob understand." Yl [v.8]. Now understand, fools of the people, and enter, fools, sometime into sanity. He teaches his people, whose feet can falter when, already living among the number of saints, that is, among the multitude of the children of the Church, they see the happiness of the wicked; when he observes that evil people are roaming around doing iniquity, and, for this reason, he follows in their footsteps and is led to imitate their actions, because he sees, waiting here for the reward, that it is of no use to him to live well. If I waited for it in the future, I wouldn't lose it. You work in the vineyard, do your duty, and you will receive your salary. Before working you do not demand the salary from the father of the family. And do you demand it from God? Tolerance is the assignment of your work and to it belongs reward. You who do not want to tolerate, intend to work little in the vineyard, since the same tolerance belongs to the work, with which you get your salary. If you are negligent, see no gligit ista, alias res curat, non intelligit. Hae enim duae voices sunt malorum: una quam iam dixi, Haec fecisti, et tacui: suspicatus es iniquitatem, quod ero tibi similis. Quid est, quod ero tibi similis? Putas quia video facta tua, et placent mihi, quia non vindico. Alia est vox iniquorum: Quia nec attendit ista Deus, nec advertit ut sciat quemadmodum vivam, non me curat Deus. Etgo inter aliqua me computat Deus? aut will see me numerat Deus? ant ipsos nomines numerat? Unhappy homo! ut esses curavit; ut bene vivas non curat? Istorum ergo ista vox est, Ut dixerunt, Non videbit Dominus, ñeque intelliget Deus lacob. 12 [v.8]. Intelligite never qui insipientes estis in populo, et stulti aliquando sapite.

Populum suum erudít, cui possunt commoveri pedes, quando felicitates iniquorum videt homo, iam bene vivirs in numero sanctorum Dei, id est in numero filiorum Ecclesiae: videt quia florent mali, et faciunt iniquitatem, et aemulatur eos, et adducitur ut imitatetur facta ipsorum; Quia videt quasi nihil sibi prodesse quod bene vivat humilis, hic sperans mercedem. Nam si illam speretfuturam, non illam perdit; quia nondum venit tempus ut accipiat eam. In vinea operaris, fac opus tuum, et accipies mercedem tuam. A patrefamilias do not demand antequam operaris, et a Deo exigís antequam opereris? Et ista tolerantia ad opus tuum pertinet, et hoc ad mercedem pertinet: minus vis faceré in vinea, qui non vis tolerare; quia et ipsa tolerance ad ipsam operationem
Enarraciunes on the Psalms

that not only do you not receive the salary, but that you find punishment, since you wanted to be a lazy worker. The negligent worker, in order not to work what he must, pays attention to the gaze of the father of the family, to the gaze of the one who led him to the vineyard, and thus, when he looks away, he stops working and does not work well; but when his master looks at him, he works hard. Well, God, who took you as a worker, does not take his eyes off you; He doesn't allow you to cheat on him at work; The eyes of the Father of families are always on you. Find a way to deceive him and, if you can, leave the job. Then the psalm speaks to you in case perhaps you thought something inconvenient when you saw the evil ones flourish and your thoughts made your feet waver in the path of the Lord. If none of you is like this, then speak to others through you, saying, Understand now, for they said, The Lord will not see, nor will the God of Jacob understand. Understand now,” he says, “you fools of the people, and come, fools, sometime into sanity.” 13 [v. 9. 10]. Will he who formed the ear not hear? Will he who made you hear have nowhere to hear? Will he who formed the ear not hear? Or he who formed the eye, should he not see? Will he who teaches the nations not argue? Pay attention to this, my brothers, with the keenest attention. Will he who teaches the nations not rebuke? God, without a doubt, teaches people; That is why he sent his word to the men of the entire earth through the angels, the patriarchs, the prophets, the servants and such a great number of preachers as preceded the judge. He also sent his Word, his own Son, to the servants, ut invenías mercedem. Quod si dolosus es, vide ne non solum non accipias mercedem, sed et poenam invenías; quia voluisti esse operanius dolosus. Et quidem operanius dolosus ut incipiat non bene faceré, oculos patrisfamilias attendit, ad illum aspicit qui conduxit ad vineam, ut cum ¡He averterit oculos, cesset, et non bene operetur; cum autem ule converterit oculos, bene operetur. Deus autem qui te conduxit, non avertit oculos; Non tibí licet dolóse operari: super te semper sunt oculi patrisfamilias; quaere ubi illum fallas, et cesa si potes.

Ergo si qui forte aliquid cogitabatis, quando videbatis malos florere, et cogitationes vestrae faciebant nutare pedes vestros in via Dei; vobis loquitur psalmus iste: si autem nullus vestrum talis est, per vos alus loquitur, dices, Intelligite nunc; quia dixerunt illi, Non videbit Dominus, ñeque intelliget Deus lacob. Intelligite, inquit, never qui insipientes estis in populo, et stulti aliquando sapite. 13 [v.9-10]. Qui plantavit aurem, non auditet? Non habet unde auditat, qui tibi fecit unde auditas? Qui plantavit aurem, non auditet? aut qui jinxit oculum, nonconsiderat? Qui erudit gentes, non arguet? Attendite hoc magnopere, fratres mei, Qui erudit gentes, non arguet? Hcc moda facit Deus, erudit gentes: ideo misit verbum suum per orbem terrarum homínibus, misit per Angelos, per Patriarchas, per Prophetas, per servos, per tot praecones antecedents iudicem. Misit et ipsum Verbum suum, misit et ipsum Filium suum; misit servos Filii sui, et in ipsis servís

you of his Son. Now the word of God is preached throughout the entire world and in all parts. Where is it not said to men: "Abandon your ancient iniquities, turn to right paths"? Forgive so that you correct yourselves; He did not take revenge yesterday so that today you may live well. He teaches the people, and will he not rebuke them? Will he not listen to those he teaches? Will he not judge those who sent and distributed his word? If you go to school, you will learn your lesson. And you shouldn't give it? Without a doubt, when you learn it from the Master, you are indoctrinated. The teacher gives you what he has in his hand, and should he not demand that it be returned to him? Or when you begin to teach him the lesson, will you not fear the punishment? Now or then we receive; Later we will appear before the Master to give him an account of all our past things, that is, to render an account to him of all the things that are now given to us. Listen to the Apostle, who says: All of us will appear before the judgment seat of Christ so that there each one may receive what he did while in the body, whether good or bad. He who indoctrinates people, he who teaches man science, will he not argue? He who teaches man knowledge, he who made you know, is he ignorant? 14 [v. l l ]. The Lord knows the thoughts of men, that they are vain. Even though you are ignorant of the thoughts of God, which are just, He knows the thoughts of men, which are vain. But men also knew the thoughts of God; But God makes his counsel known to those who have made friends of him. Therefore, my brothers, do not be discouraged; If you approach the Lord with faith, you will perceive the thoughts of God. Now you learn them, and paraquenomur Filium suum. Per totum orbem terrarum praedicatur ubique verbum Dei. Ubi non dicitur hominíbus: Relinquite iniquitates vestras priores, convertite vos ad itinera straight? Ideo parcit, ut vos corrigatis; ideo hcri non vindicavit, ut hodie bene vivatis. Erudite people; non ergo arguet? non auditurus est quos erudit? non iudicaturus est quibus sermonem praemisit et praeseminavit? In schola si esses, acciperes, et non redderes? Utique quando accipis a magistro, erudiris: committit tibi magister quod praebet; et non exigent when reddis? aut cum coeperis reddere, sine metu eris plaguerum?

Ergo accipimus mode; post statuimur ante magistrum, ut reddamus omnes praeteritas nostras, id est, ut rationem reddamus de his omnibus quae nobis moda erogantur. Audi Apostolum dicentem: "Omnes astabimus ante tribunal Christi, ut illic recipiat unusquisque secundum ea quae per corpus gessit, sive bonum, sive malum (Rom 14,10; et 2 Cor 5,10). Qui erudit gentes, non arguet; qui docet hominem scientiam?" Ipse non scit qui te fecit scire; "quidocet hominem scientiam?" 14 [v. l l ]. Dominus scit cogitationes hominum, quoniam vanae sunt. Nam etsi tu nescis cogitationes Dei, quoniam iustae sunt; ille scit cogitationes hominum, quoniam vanae sunt. Et nomines scierunt cogitationes Dei: sed quibus iam amicus factus est, prodit consilium suum. Et vos, fratres mei, nolite vos contemnere: si cum fide accessitis ad Dominum, auditis cogitationes Dei; eas mode discitis, hoc vobis dicitur, et ad hoc
Ennarrations on the Psalms

you die against God, who teaches man knowledge, it is told to you and it is declared to you why God forgave the wicked: The Lord knows the thoughts of men, that they are vain. Then abandon the thoughts of men, which are vain, that you may understand the thoughts of God, which are wise. But who understands the thoughts of God? The one who is placed in the firmament of heaven. We have already sung this, I have already recorded it and exposed it. 15 [v. 12. 13]. Blessed is the man whom you instruct, Lord, and teach him your law, so that you may soften his bitter days until the joy is dug for the wicked. Here it is declared to you why God forgives the wicked, here you have the ruling of God: the grave is dug for the sinner. You already want to bury him. Don't try to bury him so quickly, the grave is still being dug. What does it mean while the sinner is being dug? Which sinner do you point out? Still a determined man? No. Who? To all kinds of sinful, but proud men. Well, he had already said: Give the proud what they deserve. A sinner indeed was the publican, who had fixed his eyes on the ground and wounded his chest, saying: O God, be merciful to me, a sinner; But, since he was not proud, and God gives what they deserve to the proud, the grave is not dug for him, but for the proud while he gives them what they deserve. Then because of what he says: While the sinner is being punished, he understands the proud. Who is arrogant? He who does not repent of sins by confession so that he can heal by humility. Who is arrogant? He who attributes to himself and denies the mercy of God the few blessings

nesses that you seem to have. Who is arrogant? He who, even when he attributes the good things he does to God, insults those who do not do them and is arrogant over them. Well the Pharisee also says: I thank you, Lord. He didn't say, "I do." He thanked God for the things he did; Then he perceived that he was working well and that he was working through God. So why was he reproached? Because he insulted the publican. Pay attention so that you may perfect yourselves. The first thing that must precede both men and women is the confession of sins, healthy penance, which serves to correct man, not to mock God; and when after penance he has begun to live well, he still has something to think about; in not taking credit for doing well, but in giving thanks to Him by whose grace he came to live well, since He called him and enlightened him. I saw the Lord walking on the sea, trampling the heads of all the proud in this world. The undertaking of trampling on the heads of the proud was symbolized by walking on the raging waves. He also tramples on the Church, because Peter represents it. Saint Peter did not dare to walk on the waters by himself. Well what does it say? Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you over the waters. Jesus walked on them by his own power; Peter, by command of the Lord. Send me—he says—to come to you. Jesus answers him: Come. Therefore, the Church also tramples on the heads of the proud; but as Peter personified the Church and carried human weakness within him, so that it could be fulfilled: If he said, "My foot was moved," he wavered in the sea and cried out, "Lord, save me, for I perish." What was written here in the psalm: Your mercy, Lord, helped me, was said in the Gospel: Jesus stretched out his hand, saying: "Depleted of je, why did you doubt?" It is amazing how God tests men. Will the throne of iniquity be joined to you, since you establish pain in the precept? For this reason he indicated that no wicked person will sit with you and that you will not judge wickedly. And he gives the reason for this understanding, for he says: Because you establish pain in the precept. I understand that the throne of iniquity will not be joined to you, because you have not yet forgiven us. This same thing is recorded in the epistle of the apostle Saint Peter, and for this the apostle adduces the testimony of Scripture, saying: It is time to begin judgment for the house of God; That is, now is the time to judge those who belong to the house of the Lord. If children are punished, what should the wicked expect? For this reason he adds: If it began with us, what will be the end of those who do not believe in the Gospel of God? And then he adduced that testimony: And if the righteous will barely be saved, the sinner and the wicked, where will they appear? How can the wicked be with you, since you do not forgive your believers, in order to test and teach them? But since he does not forgive for the purpose of teaching, therefore he said: You establish pain in the precept. You pretend, you establish, you mean, you shape, you plasma. From here the name jiguli, potters, and the vessel, jictili, made of clay, are derived. We are not talking here about fictam, fact or workmanship, which also means fiction, confusion or lie, but about what is made to be, and which, therefore, has some form in itself, as already said.

1 [v. l }. I would have liked, brothers, to listen more to our Father, but I understand that it is good to obey him. As he who deigns to pray for me has commanded me, I will speak to your charity about this psalm whatever the Lord, our God, deigns to grant me. The psalm is titled: Praise of song; for David. Song praise involves joy, because it is a song, and devotion, because it is also praise. And what else can man praise more than that which pleases him in such a way that he cannot dislike it? The security of praise only comes in the praise of God. The praiser is safe when he is neither afraid nor ashamed of the one he praises. Then let us praise and sing; that is, let us praise with joy and gladness. The same psalm tells us what we are to praise in the following verses. 2. Come, let us rejoice in the Lord. He invites us to the great feast of joy, not of the world, but of God. If there were no evil rejoicing in the world, which must be distinguished from good rejoicing, it would be enough to say: "Come, let us rejoice"; but the salest, quod auditur scribens in corde. Si in cera scriberetur, facile deleretur: scribite illud in cordibus vestris, moribus vestris, et nunquam delebitur.

Being with the body in the same place, loving God, he draws near to Him, and, loving iniquity, he distances himself from Him; Without moving your foot you can move closer or further away. On this path, our feet are our affections. According to the affection that each one has, according to his love, he approaches or distances himself from God. Don't we say many times when we find some dissimilar things: "This is very distant from that"? When we compare, for example, two men, two horses, two dresses, and someone says: "This dress is similar to another, it is the same as that one"; or: "This man is the same as that one", what does the one who contradicts say? "There is no such thing; they are very distant from each other." What does "it is very distant from that one" mean? It is unlike him. They are close, and yet they are distant from each other. On the contrary, if two wicked men, similar in life and customs, meet, one in the east and the other in the west, both are together. In the same way, if two righteous people reside, one in the east and the other in the west, they are both together, because they are united to God. On the other hand, a righteous person and a perverse person, even when they are tied with the same chain, are extremely far apart. Therefore, if through dissimilarity we separate ourselves from God, through similarity we approach Him. Why similarity? By which we were created, by which by sinning we destroy in ourselves, by which we receive again by the remission of sins, which is renewed internally in our mind so that the image of God is engraved again on the coin, that is, on our soul, and thus we restore it to his treasures. Did our Lord Jesus Christ want to show, through the coin, to the tempters what God required? When, plotting a motive for slander regarding Caesar's tribute, they wanted to consult the Teacher of Truth, and upon consulting him tempt him by telling him whether it was lawful to pay tribute to Caesar, what did He tell them? Hypocrites, why do you tempt me? He asked for a coin to be given to him, and it was given: Whose image is it? he asks. They answered: Caesar's. And He answered them: Render to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's. This is as if he said: "If Caesar demands his image, which was carved on the coin, will not God demand his image engraved on man?" Inviting us to this likeness, our Lord Jesus Christ commands us to love our enemies, and sets before us an example of God himself: Be, he says, like your Father who is in heaven, who makes the sun rise on the good and the evil and rains on the just and the unjust. Be perfect like your Father. When he says: Be perfect like Him, he invites us to similarity. If He invites us to likeness, it is evident that, being dissimilar, we had separated ourselves from God, and that we were far from Him through dissimilarity, and that we drew near to Him through similarity, so that what was written might be fulfilled in us: Draw near to God and you will be enlightened. Then this psalm says: Come, let us rejoice in the Lord, to certain men who are distant and who live badly. Where are you going? Where do you retire? Where do you go? What does iubilare mean? Shout for joy or rejoice. The joy that cannot be explained in words and that, however, is witnessed by the shout of the voice, is called rejoicing. Think your charity of those who rejoice in any kind of song and as in a certain contest of worldly joy, and you will see how, among the songs modulated with the voice, they rejoice overflowing with joy when they cannot declare everything with the tongue, so that by those inarticulate cries the affection of the soul may be made known what was conceived in the heart and is not able to express it in words. Therefore if these rejoice in earthly joy, should we not shout for joy, rejoice in heavenly joy, which we certainly cannot express in words? 4 [v.2]. Let us anticipate his face with the confession. The confession of praise concerns the honor of the one who is praised; that of crying, to the repentance of the one who confesses sin. Therefore, men confess when they praise God and when they accuse themselves. Nothing more worthy executes the tongue. Well, we have not already forgotten, so that we want to be warned again about the things that were previously said so that we sing; But many times, due to the affection of the soul, already known words are repeated, not so that they are known, but so that the same repetition can serve as confirmation. It is repeated, therefore, to declare the speaker's affection. From here comes what the Lord says: Truly, truly, I say to you. One was enough really. Why does he say, then, truly truly? Because repetition is confirmation. Then for this he says: In psalmis iubilemus Mi, repeating iubilemus. And what do we say in the psalm? Therefore do not harden your hearts as in irritation, on the day of temptation in the wilderness, where your fathers tempted me. Let such be no longer your parents; do not imitate them. They were your parents; but, if you do not imitate them, they will not be your parents; Yet since you were born to them, they were your parents. If the Gentiles are to come from the ends of the earth, as Jeremiah says: The people from the ends of the earth will come to you and say: "Our fathers worshiped true lies, pretenses, in whom there is no profit"; utrique parieti angle (Eph 11,20); Id est, in Christo prophetia loquitur, et populo Iudaeorum, et populo Gentium. Hodie si vocem eius audieritis, nolite obdurare corda vestra. Aliquando enim audistis vocera illius per Moysen, et obdurastis corda vestra. Per praeconem locutus est, quando obdurastis corda vestra; per se nunc loquitur, mollescant corda vestra. Qui praecones ante se mittebat, ipse vinore dignitus est; Pray suo hic loquitur, qui loquebatur per ora Prophetarum. Hodie ergo si vocem eius audieritis, nolite obdurare corda vestra. 13 [v.9]. Quare dixistí, Nolite obdurare corda vestra? Quia meministis quid soleant faceré patres vestri.

Nolite obdurare corda vestra: quemadmodum in illa amaricatione, secundum diem temptationis in deserto. Recolitis certe, fratres, quod ille populus tentarit Deum (Ex 16,2.3; 17,2.7), acceperit disciplinam, et rectus sit in deserto tanquam ab optimum sessore, frenis legum, frenis praeceptorum; nec sit desertus tamen a Deo etiam indomitus, non solum beneficiis praesentibus, sed etiam virga emendationis non desistente. Nolite ergo obdurare corda vestra: sicut in amaricatione, secundum diem temptationis in deserto, ubi tentaverunt me patres vestri. Iam such non sint patres vestri; nolite eos imitari. Patres vestri werent; sed si non imitati fueritis, patres vestri non erunt: tamen quia de his nati estis, patres vestri erant. Et si Gentes venient ab extreme terrae, sicut dicit Ieremias, Ad te Gentes venient ab extreme terrae, et dicent, Verae mendacia coluerunt patres nostri, simulacra in
Exhortation to praise and obedience to God

if the people abandoned their idols to come to the God of Israel, those whom the God of Israel brought out of Egypt through the Red Sea, in which he overwhelmed the enemies who were pursuing them; those whom he guided in the wilderness and fed with manna; Should those from whom he never turned away the rod of his teaching nor the benefits of his mercy, abandon their God when people draw near to Him? Where your fathers tempted me; They tried and saw my works. For forty years they saw my works and for forty years they exacerbated me. Before them he worked miracles for Moses, and they hardened their hearts more and more. 14 [v. 10]. For forty years I was close to this generation. What does "I was near" or "together" mean? I showed with my portents and miracles not one day nor two, but for forty years I was close to this generation; and I said: "These are always wicked-hearted." "Forty years" means the same as "always." The number forty indicates the totality of time, as if by this number the centuries were completed. That is why the Lord fasted for forty days, during which he was tempted in the desert, and he also remained with the disciples for forty days after the resurrection. In the first forty days he revealed the temptation, and in the last the consolation; for when we are tempted, we are surely comforted. His Body, that is, his Church, must endure temptations in the world, but it does not lack that Comforter who said: See (uibus non est utilitas (Jer 16:19): si Gentes dimiserunt simulacra sua, ut vendeent ad Deum Israel; quos ipse Deus Israel de Aegypto per mare rubrum duxit, in quo inimicos eorum consequentes operuit (Ex 14,21-31); mea. Quadraginta annis viderunt opera mea, quadraginta annis exacerbaverunt me: ante illos miracula in manu Moysi faciebam, et ipsi magis magisque corda obdurabant 14 [v.

Praesentavi me in signis et virtutibus raeis: non uno die, non duobus; sed, Quadraginta annis proximus fue generationi huic; et dixi, Semper isti errant corde. Hoc significaverunt quadraginta anni, quod et semper. Quadragenarius enim iste numerus indicat integritatem saeculorum, tanquam perficiantur saecula per hunc numerum. Ideo Dominus quadraginta diebus ieiunavit, quadraginta diebus tentatus est in eremo (Mt 4,1-11), et quadraginta diebus Fuit cum discipulis post resurrectionem (Act 1,3). Primis quadraginta diebus temptationem, posterioribus quadraginta diebus consolationem otendit; quia cum tentamur, sine dubio consolamur. Corpus enim eius, id est Ecclesia. necesse est temptationes patiatur in hoc saeculo; sed non deest ille consolator qui dixit: Ecce ego vobiscum sum-tisque in consummationem saeculi (Mt 28,20). Et dixi,
Ennarrations on the Psalms

May I remain with you until the end of the ages. And I said: "These are always wicked-hearted." I stayed with them for forty years to show them that they are of such a condition that they continually irritate me until the end of the world. That is why he indicated the entire time of this century by forty years. 15 [v. l l ]. But what? Will there not be others who enter in their place into the rest of God? Did God lose his people when those who were displeased by God's mercy and who opposed Him with a hardened heart were reproved? There is no such thing. God is powerful to raise up from these stones children of Abraham. I said, "These are always wicked of heart. They did not know my ways; I swore to them in my anger, that they will not enter into my rest." I swore to them in my anger that they will not enter my rest. Great terror! We begin this psalm with joy and it ends with immense terror. I swore to them in my anger that they will not enter my rest. It is a great thing for the Lord to speak! But how much more than God swears! You must fear that a man swears, lest by oath he performs what is against his will; but how much more should you fear God, who cannot swear rashly? He wanted the oath to serve to confirm one thing. But by whom does God swear? By himself, since he has no other elder to swear by. By himself he confirms his promises and his threats. Let no one say in his heart: "His promise is true, and his threat is false." As what he promises is true, so what he threatens is true. You must be so sure of rest, happiness, eternity and immortality if you fulfill his Semper isti errant corde. Ad hoc cum lilis fue quadraginta annis, ut ostenderem genus tale hominum, quod me semper exacerbat usque in finem saeculi: quia per illos quadraginta annos, totum saeculum significare voluit. 15. Abrahae? (ib. 3,9). iste: Quibus iuravi in ira mea, Si introibunt in requiem meam.

Loqui Dominum magnum est; How much magis iurare Deum? Iurantem hominem must timere, ne propter iurationem faciat quod contra voluntatem eius est; quanto magis Deum, qui nihil will fear turare potest? Iurationem ad confirmationem voluit esse. Et per quem mrat Deus? Per semetipsum: non enim habet maiorem per quem iuret (Hebr 6,13). Per semetipsum confirmat promissa sua, per semetipsum confirmat mines suas. Nemo dicat in corde suo: Verum est quod promittit; falsum est quod minatur. Sicut verum est quod promittit, sic certum est quod minatur. Tam certus esse you must requie, congratulate yourself,
Praise of the Lord, only God

precepts, as of ruin, of the burning of eternal fire and of damnation with the devil if you despise his commandments. He swore to them in his anger that they would not enter into his rest; However, it is advisable that some enter into it, for it will give some their rest. Then, when they are rejected, we will enter; because, even though some branches were broken off by dissimilarity and unfaithfulness, we were grafted by faith and humility. Then we will enter into your rest. Why did those who entered, those who were chosen, those who did not oppose God with a hardened heart enter? Because it is true that the Lord did not reject his people. PSALM
[PRAISE OF THE LORD, ONLY

1 [v.l]. Lord and brother Severo still defers our joy over the sermon he owes us, since he still recognizes himself as our debtor. If the Lord rejoiced through his mouth all the churches through which he passed, this one should be much more rejoiced, since, starting from it, the Lord immortalized him in the others. But what are we to do but fulfill his will? I said, brothers, that he delays, but he does not disappoint. Therefore, consider him a debtor and do not leave him until he pays the debt. Pay attention to your charity and, in de aeternitate, de immortalitate, si feceris praecepta ipsius, quam certus esse deben de interitu, de ardore ignis aeterni, de damnatione cum diabolo, si contempseris praecepta eius. Iuravit ergo illis in ira sua, ne intrent in requiem ipsius: et tamen oponet aliquos intrare in requiem ipsius; non enim nulli dabitur requies ipsius. lilis ergo reprobatis, nos intrabimus: quia etsi aliqui ex ramis fracti sunt propter dissimüitudinem et infidelitatem, nos propter fidem et humilitatem inseremur (Rom 11,19 et 20). Nos ergo intremus in requiem eius. Unde autem intrarunt illi qui intrarunt, illi qui electi sunt, qui non corde obdurato restiterunt? Quia verum est quod non repellet Dominus plebem suam. PSALMUS

1 [v.l]. Dominus et frater meus Severus adhuc differt laetitiam nostram de sermone quem nobis deben: nam quod debitor teneatur, agnoscit. Omnes enim Ecclesias quacumque transitum fecit, laetificavit Dominus per os ipsius: multo magis ergo ista laetificanda est, de qua caeteris eura Dominus propagavit. Sed quid facturi sumus, nisi ut serviamus voluntati ipsius? Differre illum tamen dixi, fratres, non fraudare. Itaque tenete debitorem, nec dimittatis, nisi cum solverit. Advertat itaque Cha-
Ennarrations on the Psalms

As much as the Lord allows us, let us talk about this psalm something that, without a doubt, you know; but it is pleasant to remember the truth. Perhaps, when reciting its title, some shuddered. The title reads like this: When the house was built after the captivity. When this title was made known, perhaps you contemplated in the text of the psalm the stones that had to be cut from the mountains, the masses that had to be dragged, the foundations that would be laid, the beams that would be used and the columns that would be erected. None of these things he mentions; But if it speaks of something else, does the psalm not agree with its title, and does it say one thing on the title page and another in the song? What do I say? They say the same thing, but you need understanders. Talk about the construction of the house. But let all the stones of this house understand what they sang. The house of God is built, but not in that place where Solomon built it. Solomon certainly built the temple, and about this temple you have now heard what the Lord said. As the disciples contemplated the stones of the temple and its immense mass, they expressed their admiration and astonishment to the Lord; Then the Lord says to them: Truly I say to you, not one stone will be left upon another that will not be torn down. Now such a house is not built. See that it is not built in one place, somewhere, since the psalm begins like this: 2. Sing to the Lord a new song, sing to the Lord all the earth. If the whole earth sings a new song, it is edified when it sings, since singing itself is edifying; but if not, the old song is sung. The lust of the flesh sings the old song; the ritas vestra: quantum donat Dominus, de isto psalmo dicamus aliquid quod quidem iam nostis; sed dulcís est commemoratio veritatis. Forte cum pronuntiaretur titulus eius, cum admiratione aliqui audierunt. Inscribitur enim titulus Psalmi: Quando domus aedificabatur post captivitatem. Hoc titulo praedicto, iam in ipso textu Psalmi exspectabatis fortasse qui lapides praeciderentur de montibus, quae moles attraherentur, quae fundament iacerentur, quae trabes imposingentur, quae columne erigerentur. Nihil horum cantat: et si aliud aliquid, non ergo consonat Psalmus titulo suo, et aliud portat in fronte, aliud in voce? Imo nihil aliud, sed intellectores quaerit. Loquitur enim de aedificatione domus. Omnes lapides ipsius domus intelligant quod cantount. Aedifkatur enim domus Deo, non illo loco ubi aedificavit Solomon.

Aedificavit enim templum (3 Reg 6,1): et de ipso temple audistis moda quae dixerit Dominus. Cum saxa templi et moles hugentes admirarentur discipuli, indicaverunt Domino admirationem et stuporem suum; et Dominus illis: Amen dico vobis, non relinquetur hic lapis super lapidem, qui non destrutut (Mt 24,1.2). Non talis aedifkatur domus. Nam videte ubi aedifkatur, quia non uno loco, aliqua in parte. Sic enim incipit: 2. Sing Domino canticum novum, sing Domino omnis terra. Si canticum novum cantat omnis terra; sic aedifkatur, cum cantat: ipsum cantore, aedifkare est; sed si non vetus cantet. Vetus cantat cupiditas carnis: novum cantat charitas Dei. Quidquid cantaveris of cupiditate,
Praise of the Lord, only God

love of God, the new. Whatever you sing out of greed, you sing according to the old song, since, even when words of a new song sound in the mouth, praise is not beautiful in the mouth of the sinner. It is better that you do not sing the new song than that you sing the old one, because, if you were new and were silent, it would not sound in the ears of men, but your heart would not stop singing the new song, which reaches the ears of God, who made you a new man. Amasy you are silent; Well, love is a voice that addresses God, and love itself is the new song. Hear how it is indeed a new song; The Lord says, A new command I give you: that you love one another. Then all the earth sings the new song; The house is built on it. Therefore all the earth is the house of God. If the whole earth is the house of God, he who does not adhere to it is rubble, not a house; old rubble, of which the ancient temple was a figure, because the demolition of the old was carried out in it to be built the new. How would the old be destroyed? Truly, truly, says Jesus, I say to you that not one stone will be left upon another that will not be demolished. The Stone is Christ; And the Apostle also says: As many of you as were baptized into Christ, you put on Christ. If everyone who is baptized into Christ puts on Christ, who places stone on stone? He who imposes baptism upon baptism. But do not fear: There will be no stone left that will not be demolished. The stones used for the new house that is built after the captivity are united in such a way and are reduced to unity by charity in such a way that there is no longer one stone upon another, but all of them are one single stone. Do not be amazed; This was done by the new song; you sing old; etsi sonant in ore verba cantici novi, non est speciosa Iaus in ore peccatoris (Eccli 15,9). Melius est ut novus taceas, quam ut vetus cantes; quia si fueris novus, et tacueris, auribus hominum non sonat: nam cor tuum non tacet canticum novum; et pervenit ad aures Dei, qui te fecit hominem novum. Diligis, et taces: dilectio ipsa vox est ad Deum, et ipsa dilectio canticum novum est. Audi quia canticum novum est: Dominus dicit, Mandatitm novum do vobis, ut vos invicem diligatis (lo 13,34). Omnis ergo terra cantat canticum novum: ibi aedificatur domus. Omnis ergo terra est domus Dei.

Si omnis terra domus Dei, qui non haeret omni terrae, ruina est, non domus; ruin illa vetus, cuius umbram habebat templum illud vetus. Ibi enim diruebatur vetustas, ut novitas aedificaretur. Et quomodo diruitur vetustas? Amen dico vobis, inquit, non relinquetur lapis super lapidem, qui non destruetur. Lapis Christus est: dicit autem Apostolus, Quotquot in Christo baptizan estis, Christum induistis (Gal 3:27). Si Christum induit quisquís baptizatur in Christo, quis ponit lapidem super lapidem, nisi qui Baptismum super Baptismum imponit? Thirst nolite terreri; non relinquetur qui non destruetur. Lapides enim ad fabricam novam, quae aedificatur post captivitatem, sic colliguntur, et sic illos charitas in unitate constrictit, ut non sit lapis super lapidem, sed unus lapis sint omnes lapides. Ne miremini: hoc fecit canticum novum, id est, hoc fecit innovado charitatis. Ad ipsam structu-
E-narratives about the Psalms

That is, this innovation was due to charity. The Apostle forces us into this structure, and, subjecting us, weaves us together in that unity, saying: Suffering one another with charity, taking care to preserve the unity of the spirit in the vineyard of peace. Where there is unity of Spirit, there is a single stone, but a stone made up of many stones. How did one of many become? Suffering each other with charity. Then the house of the Lord our God continues to be built; It is still being built. This was done, this is being done, this is done by these voices, these readings, this preaching of the Gospel throughout the entire globe of the earth. Building is still continuing. This house grew a lot, it was swelled with many people; However, it has not yet taken possession of all nations; growing, it retains many; It will take over all of them. However, it is contradicted by those who boast of being its relatives and say: "It is already decreasing." Still growing; All the nations that do not yet believe must still believe. So that no one says: "But should that language or nation believe? Should the barbarians believe?" What does it mean for the Holy Spirit to have made himself known in tongues of fire? The hardness of any language is not so great that it is not broken by that fire. We already have that many barbarian nations believed Christ. Places where Roman domination did not reach are already possessed by Christ. What is still closed to those who fight with the sword is open to Him who fights with the log. For the Lord reigned by the tree. Who is the one who fights with the log? Christ. Through his cross he defeated the kings; and, subdued, he fixed it on his forehead; and they boast of it, because their health is found in it. This is done. This is how the house grows; ram nos compingit Apostolus, et in illa unitate nos constrictos compaginat, they say: Sufferentes invicem in dilectione, studentes servare unitatem spiritus, in vinculo pacis (Eph 4,2.3). Ubi imitates Spiritus, unus lapis; sed unus lapis de multis factus. What mode of multis unus factus? Sufferendo invicem in dilectione. Aedificatur ergo domus Domini Dei nostri, aedificatur: hoc fit, hoc agitur, hoc voices istae agunt, hoc lectiones, hoc praedicatio Evangelii toto orbe terrarum; adhuc aedificatur.

Crevit multum domus haec, et fines gentes implevit: nondum tamen omnes gentes occupavit: crescendo fines tenuit, omnes occupatura est; et contradicitur ab eis qui domestics eius se esse gloriantur, et dicitur, Iam decrevit. Adhuc crescit, adhuc crediturae sunt omnes gentes quae nondum crediderunt: ne quis dicat, Et illa Iingua creditura est? et Barbari credituri sunt? Et quid sibi vult quod Spiritus sanctus apparuit in linguis igneis (Act 2,3), nisi quia nullius linguae duritia est quae non illo igne solvatur? Ñeque enim non habemus iam fines gentes Barbaras credidisse Christo: quo nondum porrectum est Romanum imperium, iam Christus possidet; quod adhuc clausum est eis qui ferro pugnant, non est clausum illi qui ligno pugnat. Dominus enim regnavit a ligno. Quis est qui ligno pugnat? Christus. De cruz sua vicit reges, et subiugatis ipsam cruze in fronte fixit; et gloriantur de illa, quia ibi est salus
Praise of the Lord, only God

This is how it is built. That you may know it, hear what follows from the psalm. Workers and builders, see the house: Sing to the Lord a new song, sing to the Lord all the earth. 3 [v.2.3]. Sing to the Lord, bless his name, announce well his health day by day. How does the building grow? Announce, he says, well his health from day to day. It is preached day after day; be built day after day; May my house grow, says God. And as if asking himself about the workers: "Where do you command us to build it? Where do you want your house to grow? Choose a flat, spacious place for us, if you want to build yourself a large house. Where do you command us to proclaim good things day by day?" He makes the place known, saying: Announce his glory to the nations. Announce, he says, his glory among the nations; His glory, not yours. O builders! Proclaim well his glory among the nations. If you want to announce yours, you will fall; If His, you will be built when you build. That is why those who sought to announce his glory did not want to remain in this house, and, for the same reason, they do not sing the new song with the entire earth. Well, they do not communicate with the rest of the world; and therefore they are not builders of the house, but they built a whitewashed wall. How many injunctions does God not utter against the whitewashed wall! There are countless prophetic testimonies for which God curses the whitewashed wall. What is whitewashed wall? Hypocrisy, simulation. Outwardly it shines, inwardly it is mud. What I have to say has already been said; but as it was said by that Spirit that the Lord also deigned to impart to us, we also said it; and eorum. Hoc agitur, sic crescit domus, sic aedificatur: et ut noveritis, sequentia Psalmi audite; See operators and domestic manufacturers. Sing Domino canticum novum, sing Domino omnis terra. 3 [v.2.3]. Sing Domino, benedicite nomen eius, bene nuntiate de die in diem salutare eius. Quomodo crescit aedificium? Bene, inquit, nuntiate de die in diem salutare eius. From die in diem praedicetur; from die in diem, inquit, aedificetur; crescat, inquit Deus, domus mea. Et quasi diceretur ab operaniis, Ubi iubes aedificari? ubi vis crescere domum tuam? Choose nobis aliquem locum aequalem, aliquem locum spatiosum, si tibi amplam domum vis aedificari. Ubi iubes ut bene nuntiemus de die in diem? Ostendit locum: Annuntiate in gentibus gloriam eius.

Gloriam, inquit, eius announced in gentibus: gloriam eius, non gloriam vestram. O stiuctores, gloriam eius bene nuntiate in gentibus. Si gloriam vestram annuntiate volueritis, cadetis; si eius aedificabimini, cum aedificatis. Ideo qui gloriam suam annuntiare voluerunt, noluerunt esse in ista domo; et propterea non cantant canticum novum cum omni terra. Non enim communicant universe orbi terrarum: et ideo non sunt aedificantes in domo, sed parietem dealbatum erexerunfT Quanta minatur Deus parieti dealbato? Sunt testimonia Prophetarum innúmera, und/> maledicit parieti dealbato? Quid est paries dealbatus, nisi hypocrisis, id est simulated? Foris luzet, intus lutum est. Quod dicturus sum, iam dictum est, sed quia eo spiritu dictum est, quem nobis quoque Dominus impertiré dignitatus est,

What we now say in the name of the same Spirit, was also said by those who preceded us. Therefore it must not be overlooked, but must be said, because it was said by God's gift. A certain writer, when speaking of this whitewashed wall, says this: "Just as if you make a door in the wall that is not joined to others, but standing alone, everyone who enters is outside; in the same way, if you are in that part which does not want to sing the new song with the house, but rather build a wall, and it is whitewashed and not cemented, what is the use of having a door? If you enter, you are outside. They did not enter through the door and their The door does not lead in, for the Lord says: I am the door; who enter by the door? Who do not seek their glory, but the glory of God? Who do what was written: Proclaim his glory among the nations. proud; that is why he said that one entered and another ascended. But the one, entering, is received, and the other, ascending, falls into the abyss. Announce his glory in the nations. What does it mean in the nations, and they are few and that is why that part or portion that erected the whitewashed wall can still say: "What then? Are not Getulia, Numidia, Mauretania and Byzantium nations or people? Are the provinces ogent nations? "Destroy the word of God, which builds the house in the entire globe of the earth, the tongue to the hypocritical whitewashed wall. He indicated little when he said: Announce his glory to the nations illud diximus; dictum est. Quidam de isto pariete dealbato cutn diceret, hoc ait: "Quomodo in pariete non coniuncto alus parietibus, sed singulariter erecto, si ostium facías, quisquís intraverit foris est; sic in illa parte quae noluit cantore cum domo canticum novum, sed parietem voluit struere, et hunc dealbatum, non solidatum quid valet quod habet ianuam? Si intraveris foris inveniris." Quia enim ipsi non per ianuam introierunt, et ianoua ipsorum non intromittit.

Dominus enim dicit: Ego sum ianua; for trying me. Who sunt who intrant per ianuam? Qui gloriam Domini quaerunt, non suam. Who intrant per ianuam? Qui faciunt quod dictum est, Bene nuntiate in gentibus gloriam eius. Qui intrat per ianuam, pastor ovium est, ait Dominus; qui autem per alliam partem ascendit, Ule fur est et latro (lo 10,7.9.1.2). Qui per ianuam intrat, humilis est; qui per alliam partem ascendit, superbus est: ideo illum dixit íntrare, illum ascendéré. Sed ille intrando recipitur; Ole ascending praecipitatur. Annuntiate m gentibus gloriam eius. Quid est, in gentibus? Forte gentes nominantur et paucae; et adhuc habet quod dicat illa pars quae erexit parietem dealbatum: Quare non gentes sunt Getulia, Numidia, Mauritania, Byzacium? Provinciae gentes sunt. Auferat sermonem hypocrisi parieti dealbato, sermo Dei, aedificans domum toto orbe terrarum. Parum est quod dixit,
Praise of the Lord, only God

gifts. But, so that you would not think that he excepted other nations or people, he continues and says: His wonders are among all peoples. 4 [v. 4]. Because the Lord is great and worthy of being praised beyond measure. What lord apart from Christ is great and worthy of being praised beyond measure? You certainly know that he appeared as a man, that he was conceived in the womb of a woman, that he was born, that he was nursed and carried in her arms, that he was circumcised, that he offered himself as a burnt offering for man, that he grew; You also know that he was slapped, spit on, crowned with thorns, crucified, killed, and wounded with a spear; you know that he suffered all these things; However, it is great and worthy of being highly praised. Do not despise the little one; consider him great. He became small because you were small; Consider Him great, and in Him you will be great. This is how the house is built, this is how the mass is erected in the same house, this is how the stones used in the building grow. Grow, consider Christ great; The little one is great, and great beyond measure. He exhausted the words; I wanted to express how great he was. But even if all day he was saying: "Big, big", what would he say? Being talking all day, would I ever finish saying big, because the day is ending; and his greatness is before the day, beyond the day, and without day. Then what would I say? That the Lord is great and worthy of being praised beyond measure. What must the tiny tongue say to praise the great? By saying nimis, above all, he utters a word and offers the thought something to reconsider. This is as if he were saying to him: "What I cannot express, you think about it, and when you think about it, understand that it is little." Cornelius go in search of Peter; Peter came to Cornelius; But since Cornelius was a Gentile and neither he nor his companions were circumcised, so that they (Peter and his companions) would not hesitate to evangelize the uncircumcised, before Cornelius himself and those who were with him were baptized, the Holy Spirit descended on them and filled them, and they began to speak in tongues. Peter might have hesitated to baptize the uncircumcised; But as the Holy Spirit came upon them and they began to speak in tongues, that is, the invisible gift was granted, the doubt disappeared and they were all baptized. Furthermore, there it was recorded that the other apostles and the brothers who were in Judea heard how the Gentiles also received the word of God, and blessed God. This is the same thing that is commemorated here: Zion heard it and rejoiced. What did Zion hear that made him rejoice? That the Gentiles received the word of God. A wall had been erected, but the angle had not yet been formed. The Church that existed in Judea was here properly called Zion. Zion heard it and rejoiced, and the daughters of Judea rejoiced. Thus it is written: The apostles and the brothers who were in Judea heard it. Observe if not: The daughters of Judea rejoiced. What did they hear? That the Gentiles also received the word of God, where did this psalm say this? When recording: The heavens announced the justice of God and the people saw his glory. those who glory in their simulations. Zion heard it and rejoiced, and the daughters of Judea rejoiced. Later, some of the circumcision censured Peter, saying, "Why did you enter the house of uncircumcised Gentiles and eat with them?" Then he explained to them how, while he was praying, a kind of plate held by the four ends appeared to him in vision. This type of plate that contained all kinds of animals symbolized all people. It also hung from the four ends, because there are four parts of the world from which all the peoples were to come to the Church; and for this reason there are also four gospels that preach Christ, so that it may be understood that the grace of God belongs to the four parts of the world. Then when this vision was declared to Peter, he revealed and made clear to them all things: how Cornelius believed and how before being baptized the Gentile man came upon him the Holy Spirit. When they heard these things, they were silent and glorified God, saying: Surely God has also given the Gentiles penance leading to life. Behold, Zion heard it and rejoiced, and the daughters of Judea rejoiced because of your judgments, O Lord! Why trials? Because God is not acceptor of people. For Peter himself, when he saw the centurion Corne'iio and those who were with him filled with the Holy Spirit, exclaimed and said: Truly I understand that God is not an acceptor of people. Then the daughters of Judea rejoiced because of your justice, O Lord! What does it mean for your justice? That anyone who serves him is accepted, from whatever town and people they may be. Because he is not only the God of the Jews, but also of the Gentiles.

14 [v.9}. See if this is not the reason why the daughters of Judea rejoiced. And the daughters of Judea rejoiced at your judgments, O Lord! For you are the most excellent Lord over all the earth. Not only over Judea, over Jerusalem, over Zion, but over the entire earth. The judgments of God were spread throughout the earth in order to summon people from everywhere, with whom those who broke themselves off do not communicate, nor understand what was preached, nor see what was fulfilled. For you are the most excellent Lord over all the earth and highly exalted above all gods. What does it mean in a great way, since it speaks of Christ? What does it mean in a big way? Ista civitas Dei vocatur Sion: ergo Ecclesia est Sion. In illa is magnus Deus. In illa esto, et non erit praeter te Deus. Cum autem fuerit in te Deus, quia tu factus es de Sion, membrum de Sion, civis de Sion, pertinens ad societatem populi Dei; excelsus in te erit Deus super omnes populos, super ¡líos qui irascuntur, aut super ¡líos qui irascebantur. Putatis enim quia tune irascebantur, et moda non irascuntur? Irascebantur tune: sed quia plutes erant, aperte irascebantur; mode quia pauci facti sunt, oceulte irascuntur. the musical instruments hear with more delight the voice of God. If music, rightly, delights the ear, so does the word of God delight the heart. Therefore we pray for them when we do not fast on the days of their festivals, so that they may make a spectacle for themselves. For when they see each other they will be displeased; They are not displeased because they do not contemplate themselves. The drunk does not displease himself, but he displeases the sober. Present me a man who already rejoices in God, who lives soberly, who longs for that everlasting peace that God promised him, and you will observe that, when he has seen a man jumping to the music, he feels more pain for the jumper than for the frantic feverish person. Therefore, if we know their evils because we were delivered from them, let us grieve for them; and, if we grieve for them, let us pray for them, and so that we may be heard, let us fast for them. We do not celebrate our fasts during the days of their festivities. We fast during the days before Easter and during various other festivals dedicated to Christ. However, let us fast during those days, so that when they rejoice, we may weep for them. For with their joy they excite our pain and make us remember how unfortunate they still are. But, as we see that many were taken from where we were, we should not despair of them. If they are still angry, let us pray; If the little part of the earth that remains is still moved, let us remain groaning for them so that God also gives them knowledge and they hear with us the words lectabiliter audiunt organum, delectabilius audiant vocem Dei. Non enim quod sonat sine ratione delectat aurem, et vetbum Dei non delectat cor. Sed ideo pro illis oramus, quando diebus illorum festis non ieiunamus, ut fiant sibi ipsi spectaculum. Quando enim viderunt se, displicebunt sibi; sed ideo non sibi displicent, quia non se attendunt. Ebrius non sibi displicet, sed sober displicet. Da hominem qui iam iucundatur in Deo, vivit gtaviter, sigh in illam pacem aeternam quam illi promisit Deus; et vide quia quando respexerit hominem saltantem ad organum, plus illum dolet insanientem, quam phreneticum febrientem. Ergo si novimus mala illorum, quia de ipsis malis et nos liberati sumus, doleamus illos; et si dolemus illos, oremus pro illis; et ut exaudiamur, ieiunemus pro illis. Non enim us our ieiunia celebramus per dies festos illorum.

Alia sunt ieiunia nostra quae celebramus per dies Paschaefutures, per allia atque alia quae solemnia nobis sunt in Christo: per istos autem dies ad hoc ieiunamus, ut quando ipsi laetantur, nos pro illis gemamus. nor placing the good where the bad should be placed. If He cannot err, we err if we do not fear; If we fear now, we will have nothing to fear then. Do not distance yourself from Him and live badly, presuming too much of His mercy; Without a doubt, he loves mercy, but he also loves justice. What does his mercy consist of? In preaching the truth to you now, in calling you now to Him so that you may convert. Utmo praedicet tibi veritatem, utmo clamet ad te ut convertaris. Parva misericordia est, quia vixisti in malis factis, et adhuc non te tulit cum pecares, ut credenti ignosceret peccata tua? Terribile et sanctum nomen eius; et honor regis iudicium diligit. Iniustum est enim iudicium, et omnino non est iudicium, nisi merita reddantur sua cuique, quemadmodum quisque gessit in corpore, sive bonum, sive malum (2 Cor 5:10): et honor regis iudicium diligit. Ergo timeamus, ergo faciamus iustitiam, ergo faciamus aequitatem. 7. Sed quis facit aequitatem? quis facit iustitiam? Homo peccator, homo iniquus, homo perversus, homo aversus a luz veritatis? Quid should I be homo? Convertere se tantum ad Deum, ut ipse in illo formet aequitatem, quam ipse formare non potest, sed deformare. Idoneus est homo ad vulnerandum se; numquid idoneus est ad sanandum se? Quando vult aegrotat, not quando vult arose. Si vult, vivat intemperanter vel in frigore vel in calore; eo die aegrotat, quo voluerit: cum autem vi-

live intemperately, I will begin to get sick, heal whenever I want; He who fell when he wanted to, get up, if he can, when he wants. To get sick he needed his intemperance, to cure he needed the Maker's medicine. Man is self-sufficient to sin; to be justified, if it is not justified by Him who alone is just, it is not sufficient for itself. Then, so that men may surrender to Him to be established in righteousness, this psalm, after having terrified the people and having said: Praise your great name, for it is holy and terrible; and the honor of the king loves judgment, as if already seeking the frightened people and (teaching) how the righteous should live, since they cannot justify themselves, he entrusts them to the Creator of his justice, and, continuing, says: You established equity; you did justice and justice in Jacob. We must also possess judgment, we must possess justice; but in us he establishes judgment and justice that inspires what things should be done. When do we possess justice and judgment? You possess judgment when you discern evil from good, and justice when you follow good and turn away from evil. By discerning you possess judgment and by acting you achieve justice. Turn away from evil and do good; Seek peace and go after it. First you must have judgment and then justice. Why the trial? So that you first judge what is bad and what is good. And why justice? So that you turn away from evil and do good. However, you will not achieve this on your own, for see what he said: You executed judgment and righteousness in Jacob. I sell intemperanter coeperit aegrotare, surgat quando vult; qui iacuit quando voluit, surgat, si potest, quando vult. Ut iaceret aegrotus, intemperantiam suam habuit necessariam: ut surgat autem, necessariam habet artificis medicinalm. Sic ergo ut peccet homo, ipse sibi sufficit ad peccandurn: ut iustificetur, non sibi sufficit, nisi ab illo iustificetur, qui solus est iustus. Ut ergo illi se homines dent formandos ad iustitiam, cum terruisset populos psalmus is^e, et dixisset, Confiteantur nomini tito magno, quoniam terribile et stmctum est; et honor regís iudicium diligit; veluti quaerentes iam populos territos quomodo iusti vivere debenant, quia in seípsis non possunt habere iustitiam, commendavit illis et plasmatorem iustitiae illorum, et secutus ait: Tu parasti aequitatem; iudicium et iustitiam in lacob tu fecisti.

Debemus enim et nos habere iudicium, debenmus habere iustitiam; sed ille in nobis facit iudicium et iustitiam, who us fecit in quibus faceret. Quomodo et nos debenmus habere iudicium et iustitiam? Iudicium habes, quando discernis malum a bono; iustitiam autem, quando sequeris bonum, et declines to malo. Discerndo, iudicium habes; doing, iustitiam habes. Declines to malo, ait, et fac bonum; quaere pacem, et sequere eam (Ps 33:15). Primo must habere iudicium, et postea iustitiam. Quod iudicium? Ut primo iudices quid sit malum, et quid sit bonum. Et quam iustitiam? Declines a malo, et facías bonum. Hoc autem non a te habebis; quia vide quid díxit: Iudicium et iustitiam in lacob tu fecisti.

8 [v.5]. Exalt the Lord, our God. Praise him truly, praise him well. Let us praise him; let us exalt Him who made the righteousness that we possess; He established it in us. For who established righteousness in us except He who justified us? It was said of Christ that he justifies the wicked. Therefore we are wicked, the justifier, since he established in us the same righteousness by which he pleases him, by which he places us on the right and not on the left, by which he will say to those placed on the right: Come, you who are blessed of my Father; receive the kingdom that was prepared for you from the beginning of the world; so that through it he will not place us on the left, among those to whom he will say: Go to the eternal game, which was prepared for the devil and his angels. How much should he not be exalted who is not to crown in us our merits, but rather his gifts! Exalt the Lord, our God. 9. And worship his footstool, for it is holy. What should we worship? His footstool. The base is called a footstool. What the Greeks call ipopodion, the Latins called some scabellum, footstool; others, suppedaneum, bench. But see, brothers, what he commands us to worship. Elsewhere in Scripture it is said: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. Does he then command us to worship the earth, since he said elsewhere that it is the footstool of God? But how are we to worship the earth, since the Scripture clearly says: You shall worship the Lord your God? Yet now he says: Worship his footstool; and, exposing to me what the footstool of its 8 is [v.5]. Exalt yourself Dominum Deum nostrum. Go exalt yourself, bene exalt yourself. Laudemus illum, exaltemus iüum qui fecit ipsam iustitiam quam habemus; ipse in nobis fecit. Quis enim in nobis fecit iustitiam, nisi qui nos iustificavit? De Christo autem dictum est, Qui iustificat impium (Rom 4,5). Nos ergo impii, ille iustificator, quando et ipsam iustitiam ipse in nobis fecit qua illi placeamus, ut ad dexteram nos ponat, et non ad sinistram: ut dicat ad dexteram positis, Venite, benedicti Patris mei, percipite regnum quod vobis paratum est ab origine mundi; non autem ponat ad sinistram, inter eos quibus dicturus est, he in ignem aeternum, qui praeparatus est diabolo et angelis eius (Mt 25,34.41). Qui in nobis coronaturus est non merita nostra, sed dona sua, how much should I exaltari? Exalt yourself Dominum Deum nostrum. 9. Et adórate scabellum pedum eius, quoniam sanctus est.

Quid hajemus adorare? Scabellum pedum eius. Suppedaneum dicitur scabellum: Quod dicunt Graeci ÜTTOTTÓSIOV, dixerunt Latini scabellum; et alii dixerunt, suppedaneum. Be videte, fratres, quid iubeat adorar us. Alio loco Scripturarum dicitur: Caelum mihi sedes est, ierra autem scabellum pedum meorum (Is 66,1). Ergo terram nos iubet adorare, quia dixit alio loco quod sit scabellum pedum Dei? Et quomodo adorabimus tetram, cum dicat aperte Scriptura: Dominum Deum tuum adorabis? (Deut 6,13). Et hic dicit, Adore yourself scabellum pedum eius; exponens autem mihi quod sit scabellum pedum eius, dicit, Terra autem scabellum pedum meorum.

feet, writes: The earth is the footstool of his feet. I am undecided; I am afraid to worship the earth, lest he who made heaven and earth condemn me. On the other hand, I fear to worship the footstool of my Lord, since the psalm tells me: Worship the footstool of his feet. I inquire what his footstool is, and the Scripture tells me: The earth is my footstool. Hesitating, I turn to Christ, because I seek Him here, and I find how the earth is worshiped without impiety, how the footstool of His feet is worshiped without impiety. He took the earth from the earth by taking the flesh of the Virgin Mary; And since He walked through the world in that meat, and gave it to us to eat for our health, and no one eats this meat without first worshiping it, a way was found to worship the footstool of the Lord, not only, without sinning, worshiping Him, but, sinning, not worshiping Him. But does it perchance give life to the flesh? The Lord himself said when he spoke recommending this land: It is the spirit that gives life, the flesh is of no use. Therefore, when you bow down and prostrate before a certain kind of earth, do not look at it as earth, but look at the Holy One, whose footstool is what you worship. You worship for Him; hence he added: Worship his footstool, for it is holy. Who is holy? He for whose honor you worship the footstool of his feet. For this reason also, when you worship him so that you do not retain your thoughts in the flesh, and, therefore, are not quickened by the spirit, he says: It is the spirit that gives life, the flesh is of no use. When 1 the Lord recommended this, he spoke of his flesh and said: If anyone does not eat my flesh, he will not have eternal life in him. Then it is spelledAnceps factus sum: timeo adorare terram, ne damnet me qui fecit caelum et terram; rursus timeo non adorare scabellum pedum Domini mei, quia Psalmus mihi dicit, Adore yourself scabellum pedum eius. Et quia in ipsa carne hic ambulavit, et ipsam carnem nobis manducandam ad salutem dedit; nemo autem illam carnem manducat, nisi prius adoraverit: inventum est quemadmodum adoretur tale scabellum pedum Domini, et non solum non peccemus adorando, sed peccemus non adorando. Numquid autem caro vivificat? Ipse Dominus dixit, cum de ipsa commendatione eiusdem terrae loqueretur: Spiritus est qui vivificat; caro autem nibil prodest. Ideo et ad terram quamlibet cum te inclines atque prosternis, non quasi terram inmearis, sed illum Sanctum curas pedum scabellum est quod adoras; propter ipsum enim adoras: ideo et hic subiecit, Adórate scabellum pedum eius, quoniam sanctus est. Who sanctus is this? In cuius honore you worship scabellum pedum eius. Et cum adoras illum, ne cogitatione remaneas in carne, et a spiritu non vivificeris: Spiritus est enim, inquit, qui vivificat; caro autem nibil prodest. Tune autem, quando hoc Dominus commendavit, de carne sua locutus erat, et dixerat: Nisi quis manducaverit carnem meam,

Some of his disciples, about seventy, said, "This sermon is hard." Who can understand him? And they turned away from Him and henceforth did not walk with Him. What He said to them seemed harsh to them: If anyone does not eat my flesh, he will not have eternal life. They took it foolishly and understood it carnally, and so they judged that the Lord was going to cut off little parts of his body to give them to them, and they said: This sermon is hard. They were tough, not the sermon. In fact, if they had not been hardened, but meek, they would have said to themselves: "He did not say this without reason, he did not say this if it did not contain any sacrament." And, therefore, they would have remained meek with Him and not harsh. And they would have learned from Him what they learned, after they had gone away, those who remained with Him. Because, the twelve disciples having remained with Him, as soon as they left, they warned Him, as if grieving for the death of those who were scandalized by His words, and therefore they went away. Then the Lord instructs them and says to them: It is the spirit that gives life, the flesh is of no use. The words I spoke to you are spirit and life. Understand spiritually what I told you; You are not to eat this body that you see nor are you to drink the blood that those who crucify me will shed. I recommended a sacrament to you; If you understand him spiritually, he will give you life. Even though it must be celebrated visibly, it is nevertheless advisable to understand it spiritually. Exalt the Lord our God, and worship his footstool, for it is holy. 10 [v.6-8].

non babebit in se vitam aeternam. Scandalizati sunt discipuli eius quídam, septuaginta ferme, et dixerunt: Durus est hic sermo; quis potest eum intettigere? Et recesserunt ab eo, et amplius cum eo non ambulavetunt. Durum illis visum est quod ait, Nisi quis manducaverit carnem meam, non babebit vitam aeternam: acceperunt illud stulte, carnaliter illud cogitaverunt, et putaverunt quod praecisurus esset Dominus particles quasdam de corpore suo, et daturus illis, et dixerunt, Durus est hic sermo. Ipsi werent duri, non sermo. Etenim si duri non essent, sed mites essent, dicerent sibi: Non sine causa dicit hoc, nisi quia est ibi aliquod sacramentum latens. Manerent cum illo lenes, non duri; et discerent ab ¡lio, quod, illis discedentibus, qui remanserunt, didicerunt. Nam cum remansissent cum illo discipuli duodecim, illis recedentibus, suggesserunt illi, tanquam dolentes illorum mortem, quod scandalizati sunt in verbo eius et recesserunt. Ule autem instmxit eos, et ait illis, Spiritus est qui vivificat; caro autem nibil prodest: verba quae locutus sum vobis. spiritus est et vita (lo 6,54-64). Spiritualiter intelligite quod locutus sum: non hoc corpus quod videtis, manducaturi estis; et bibituri illum sanguinem, quem fusuri sunt qui me crucifigent. Sacramentum aliquod vobis commendavi; spiritualiter intellectum vivificabit vos. Etsi necesse est illud visibiliter celebrate, oportet also invisibiliter intelligi. Exalt yourself Dominum Deum nostrum, et adore yourself scabellum pedum eius, quoniam sanctus est. 10 [v.6-8]. Moyses et Aaron in sacerdotibus eius, et Samuel in bis
