that the Sun was not born, because they are in darkness, and in the darkness precisely the lions' cubs look for someone to devour. What was said about the eldest lion himself, the prince of the remaining lions? Do you not know that your adversary the devil, like a roaring lion, prowls around looking for someone to devour? They obtain their food from God, because no one can be tempted by the devil if God does not allow it. The holy Job was before the devil, and yet he was very far from him; by the presence it was before him; for power, away from it. When would he have dared to tempt him in the flesh, on the property he owned, if he had not received the power? What is power granted for? To punish the wicked or to test the good. The Lord does all this with justice. The devil has no power over anyone, not even in the slightest, if he is not given the One who possesses the supreme and sublime power. For the same reason, neither the devil nor man enjoys any power over man if they do not receive it from above. The Judge of the living and the dead was before the male judge, and this male judge strutted around, seeing Jesus before him, and said to him: Do you not know that I have the power to kill you or release you? Then he who had also come to teach him by whom he was judged said to him: You would not have power over me if it had not been given to you from above. Therefore, man, the devil and any kind of demons only harm if they have received power, but they do not harm those who progress in virtue. To the wicked they are like fire to hay; to the good, as fire to gold. Judas was devoured like hay; Job, tested like gold. You instituted darkness, and night fell; All the beasts of the forest will roam in it. Here, as you see, the ortus est; tenebrae etiim sunt. Et cum tenebrae sunt, quaerunt catuli leonum, quos devorent. Ipse leo maior, princeps omnium talium leonum, quid de illo dictum est? "Nescitis quia adversarius vester diabolus, tanquam leo rugiens circuit, quaerens quem devoret"? (1 Petr 5:8). Ideo "quaerentes a Deo escam sibi"; quia nec tentari quis potest a diabolo, nisi permittente Deo. Iob sanctus ante diabolum erat, et tamen longe ab illo erat: aspectu ante illum, potestate remotus ab illo. Quando auderet tentare vel carnem, vel facultates eius quas possidebat, nisi accepisset potestatem? Quare autem datur potestas? Aut ad damnandos impios, aut ad testing pios.

Iuste hoc totum Dominus agit; et in neminem habet diabolus potestatem, vel in aliquid eius, nisi ille concedat, cui est potestas summa et sublimis. Sic diabolo, sic homini nulla est potestas in hominem, nisi desuper detur. Stabat iudex vivorum et mortuorum ante hominem iudicem, et inflavit se homo iudex videns ante se Christum, et ait: Nescis quia potestatem babeo occidendi et dimittendi te? At ille qui venerat et cum docere, a quo iudicabatur: Non haberes, inquit, in me potestatem, nisi esset tibi de super data (lo 19,10.11). Et homo et diabolus et quaelibet daemonia nonnisi accepta potestate nocent: sed proficientibus non nocent. Malis ita sunt tanquam ignis feno; bonis ita sunt tanquam ignis auro. Manducatus est ludas ut fenum; probatus est Iob ut aurum. Posuisti tenebras, et facía est nox: illic pertransibunt omnes bestiae silvae.

Beasts of the jungle symbolize something different from before. In verse 11 I said that they symbolize the Gentiles, something different here; They often symbolize different things. Just as the Lord is lamb and lion. And what is more opposite than the lion and the lamb? But what lamb? Who defeated the wolf, who defeated the lion! He is also a stone, he is a shepherd and he is a door. The shepherd enters through the door, for he says: I am the good shepherd; and also says: I am the door. The lion symbolizes the Lord himself, because it is said: The Lion of the tribe of Judah conquered; and it also symbolizes the devil, because it is written: He trampled the lion and the dragon. Learn to understand what is said symbolically, lest perhaps, because you read that the stone symbolizes Christ, you believe that the stone symbolizes him everywhere. Well, it symbolizes different things depending on the circumstances. See the place a letter occupies in the word, and you will understand its value. If you see the first letter in the name of God and think that it always and only has to be placed there, you will erase it from the name of the devil, since the name of God begins with the same letter with which the name of the devil begins, and there is nothing more opposite than God and the devil. See how foolish he is who, dealing with both human and divine things, says of the brief letter D that it should not be written at the beginning of the devil's name; and when asked why, he answered: "Because I read this letter in the name of God." You would laugh at him, because it is not such that you would deign to explain the reason. Do not perceive these divine things so childishly, so that, because I previously said that the beasts of the forest symbolized the Gentiles, and now that they symbolize the demons and the prevaricating angels, some of you may think that he Iam bestiae silvae alio moda: alio enim et alio moda semper ista intelliguntur; quomodo Dominus ipse agnus, ipse leo. Quid tam diversum quam agnus et leo? Sed qualis agnus? Qui vinceret lupum, vinceret leonem. Ipse petra, ipse pastor, ipse ianua. Pastor intrat per ianuam: et dicit, Ego sum pastor bonus; et dicit, Ego sum ianua (ib. 10,7.11). Ipsum leonis nomen Dominum significat; quia, Vicit leo de tribu luda (Rev 5,5), et diabolum; quia, Concuhavit leonem et draconem (Ps 90,13). Discite sic intelligere, cum figúrate ista dicuntut; ne forte ubi legeritis quod Christum significat petra (1 Cor 10:4), ubique petram Christum putetis.

Where does all the creation that is ordered come from, since it flows in order, and is beautiful in order, and is born and dies in order, and all times pass in order? The Jews mock Christ crucified, because it is a scandal to them; Let the pagans mock Christ crucified, because it is foolish for them. For thus says the Apostle: We preach Christ crucified, being a scandal to the Jews and foolishness to the Gentiles, but to those who are called, Jews and Greeks, Christ is the power of God and the Wisdom of God. You made all things in Wisdom. 26. The earth is full of your creature. The earth is full of the creature of Christ. In what way? As we see it. What thing was not created by the Father through the Son? Everything that walks and crawls on the earth, everything that swims in the water, everything that flies in the air, everything that circles in the sky, and especially the earth, is a creature of God, because the whole world was pulchra, ordinate oriens, ordinate occidens, ordinate peragens omnia tempora, unde processit? Ipsa autem Ecclesia quomodo accepit increment, successus, perfectionem? Quomodo destinatur ad finem quemdam immortalitatis? Quibus praeconiis praedicatur? quibus mysteriis commendatur? quibus sacramentis oceultatur? qua praedicatione revelatur? Ubi fecit haec Deus? Video magna opera: Quam magnificata sunt opera tua, Domine! Quaero ubi fecerit, locum non invenio; sed video quid sequatur: Omnia in sapientia fecisti. Ergo omnia in Christo fecisii.

created by Him. to negligence. However, there are creatures that are incapable of wisdom, such as, for example, all beasts, wild animals, trees, which is more, they also lack sense. Then God says this: "I do not demand a share of my wisdom from those whom I did not make in my image, but from those whom I made; and, therefore, I seek the use of what I gave them." Then, men returning to God the things that are God's, and to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, that is, returning to Caesar his image, and to God theirs, they raise their minds not towards themselves, but towards their Artificer, and towards the light whence they come, and towards the spiritual heat by which they boil, and from which, separated, they grow cold, and, removed, they darken, and to which, returning again, they become illuminate And as they piously said: You will illuminate my torch, O Lord! The Apostle says that it is a figure of the one who was to come. What was to happen was foreshadowed, and that is why the Church was made from the side of the Lord, who slept on the cross. Because the sacraments of the Church flowed from the wounded side of the Crucified. What was said to the Church? Hear it now, understand it, be careful: She will observe your head, and you her heel. Subditas est iste capiti tuo, subdetur et corpori eius; haereant tantum membra capiti suo, ut membra eius sint. In it, do not consent. What came to mind is the head of the snake; trample on the head, and you will avoid the other evil movements. What does "stomp on the head" mean? Disdain suggestion. He suggested profit to you, saying: "By this you get a great profit, by this you get gold in abundance; if you commit this fraud, you will become rich." It is the head of the serpent; trample it. What does "stomp on it" mean? Disdain suggestion. But he promised gold in abundance: And what does it profit a man to gain the whole world if he loses his soul? Let the profit of the world perish so as not to cause harm to the soul. Saying this, you kept an eye on the snake's head and trampled on it. But the devil watches your heel. What does "watch your heel" mean? It spies waiting for you to stray from God's path. You watch the first suggestion, he watches your slip. If you slip, you fall; If you fall, it will possess you. To avoid falling, don't go off the path. God prepared a narrow path for you; everything outside of it is slippery. That is why Christ is light and way, since it is said of Him: He is the true light that illuminates every man who comes into this world; and He says of Himself: I am the way, the truth and the life. 1 [v.lj. Psalm 104 is the first among those titled Alleluia. The meaning of this word, or rather of these two words, is praise the Lord. Hence the psalm begins by saying: Confess or praise the Lord and call on his name. This confession must be understood to be one of praise, just as that one: I confess you, O Father! Lord of heaven and earth. Praise is usually followed by the invocation or request, where the person praying expresses the desire. Hence the Sunday prayer also has at its beginning a very brief praise, which is: Our Father, who art in heaven; and then the things that are requested are expressed. Hence it is also said elsewhere in a psalm: We confess you, O God, we confess you and call on your name. This is expressed more clearly in another psalm: I will call upon the Lord with praise, and I will be free from my enemies. Likewise, it also says here: Confess the Lord and call on his name, which is as if he said: Praise the Lord and call on his name. Without a doubt, the one who invokes hears the one who sees the one who praises and the one who perceives the lover sees the one who praises. In what way did the Lord want to demonstrate his love for the good servant in a special way if not in what he said to him: Feed my sheep? Hence this psalm also goes on to say: Declare his works among the nations. Or rather, recording the Greek word, which many Latin codices conserve.

An semper dixit, in tota vita ista qua hic vivitur, ex quo id nos faceré debené cognovimus, quando et inventus quaerendus est? Iam quippe illum invenit fides, sed adhuc eum quaerit spes. Chantas autem et invenit eum per fidem, et eum quaerit habere per speciem: ubi tune sic mvenietur, ut sufficiat nobis, et ulterius non quaeratur. Nisi

and no more search will be made for him. If faith did not find him in this life it would not be said: Seek the Lord; nor would it be said when he had found him: Let the wicked forsake his way, and the wicked man his thoughts. Likewise, if, found by faith, it should not already be sought, it would not be said: If we wait patiently for what we do not see; and also what Saint John says: We know that, when He appears, we will be like Him, because we will see Him as He is. Or is it that perhaps when we see him face to face, as he is, the search must still continue, because without end he must be searched, since without end he must be loved? Well, we usually say to someone present: "I'm looking for you now," that is, I don't love you. Therefore, the beloved is also sought to be present while perpetual charity works so that he does not become absent. For this reason, when someone loves someone, when they see them they want, without becoming bored, for them to always be present, that is, they always try to make them present. In truth, always seek his face means that invention does not constitute the end of this inquisition, by which love is signified, but rather that the investigation of what is found by growing love grows. 4 [v. 5]. Then this passionate praiser moderates himself and uses more intelligible words, feeding the weak and childish love with the earthly wonders of God. Remember, he says, the wonders he did, his wonders and the judgments of his mouth. This passage seems similar to that in which Moses asked God what his name was and told him: I am who I am; and also: This you shall say to the children of Israel: "He who is sent me to vosenim eum in ista vita inveniret fides, non diceretur, Quitente Dominum; et cum inveneritis eum, Derelinquat impius vias suas, et vir iniquus cogitationes suas (Is 55,6.7). item si fide inventus, non adhuc esset perquirendus, non diceretur, "If enim quod non videmus, speramus, per patientiam exspectamus" (Rom 8:25): et quod Ioannes ait, "Scimus quia cum apparuerit, similes ei erimus; "quoniam videbimus eum sicuti est" (1 lo 3,2). diligitur, etiam praesens quaeritur, dum charitate perpetua, ne fiat absens, agitur.

Proinde quem quisque diligit, etiam cum eum videt, sine annoyance semper vult esse praesentem, hoc est, semper quaerit esse praesentem. Et nimirum hoc est, Quaerite faciem eius semper, ut non huic inquisitioni, qua significatur amor, finem praestet inventio, sed amore crescente inquisitio crescat inventi. 4 [v.5]. Iam deinceps temperat se laudator iste ardens, et ad capacia verba descendit; infirmum amorem atque lactentem temporalibus Dei mirabilibus nutriens. Mementote, inquit, mirabilium eius quae fecit, prodigia eius et iudicia oris eius. Qui locus similis videtur illi loco, ubi ad Moysen quaerentem quis esset, cum dixisset, Ego sum qui sum, et, Dices filiis Israel, Qui est, misit me ad vos: quod ex quantulacumque particle rare mens capit: deinceps nomen suum commemoranJ5,, erga nomines gra-

others, whose mind will rarely be able to perceive a small part of the content, then, recording his name again, mercifully moderated his excellence in attention to men, saying: I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob. This is my name forever. In this he wanted it to be understood that also those of whom he affirmed that it was his! God lived with Him forever. He said this so that the little ones could understand it, just as he also said: I am who I am, so that those endowed with the sublime virtue of charity could understand it, according to their capacity, and know how to always seek his face. If it is too much for you to see or seek what He is, remember the wonders He did, His wonders, and the judgments of His mouth. 5 [y.6.7}: To whom is it said: Abraham's seed are his servants, Jacob's sons are his chosen ones? You, descendants of Abraham; You sons of Jacob, remember the wonders he did, his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth. So that no one would attribute this to a single nation, to that of the Israelites according to the flesh, and, therefore, not understand that the race of Abraham are rather the children of the promise than the children of the flesh, to whom the Apostle says when speaking to the Gentiles: You are Abraham's offspring, heirs according to the promise, the psalm continues and says: He is the Lord, our God; His judgments are in all the earth. This is also what the Lord says through Isaiah to free Jerusalem, our mother: He who freed you, He is your God, and will be called God of all the earth. Therefore, is He only the God of the Jews? There is no such thing. The Lord himself is our God; His judgments are in all the earth, because in all the earth his Church is found, in which tiam suam misericorditer temperavit, they say, Ego sum Deus Abraham, et Deus Isaac, et Deus Iacob; hoc mihi nomen est in aeternum (Ex 3,14.13). Ubi intelligi voluit, et illos quorum se Deum dixit, vivere secum in aeternum, et hoc dixit quod capi etiam a parvulis posset: ut, Ego sum qui sum, illi pro captu intelligerent, qui grandibus viribus charitatis nossent quaerere faciem eius semper. Si ergo quod est ipse, multum est ad vos vel videre vel quaerere, Mementote mirabilium eius quae fecit, prodigia eius et iudicia oris eius. 5 [v.6.7]. Et quibus dicitur? Semen Abraham servi eius, filii Iacob electi eius.

Vos semen Abraham, vos filii Iacob, mementote mirabilium eius quae fecit, prodigia eius et iudicia oris eius. Ne quis autem uni genti hoc tribueret Israelitarum secundum carnem, et non intelligeret magis esse semen Abrahae filios promissionis quam filios carnis, quibus Apostolus dicit, cum Gentibus loqueretur, "Vos ergo Abrahae semen estis, secundum promissionem haeredes" (Gal 3:29); sequitur et dicit, "Ipse Dominus Deus noster; in omni terra iudicia eius." Hoc dicitur per Isaiam ad lerusalem liberam, matrem nostram: Et qui eruit te, ipse Deus tuus, universae terrae vocabitur (Is 54,5). An Iudaeorum Deus tantum? Absit (Rom 3,29). Ipse Dominus Deus noster; in omni terra iudicia eius: quia in omni terra Ecclesia eius, ubi praedicantur iudicia eius. Quid ergo ait

His justices are preached. What does it say in another psalm? He announces his word to Jacob, his righteousness and his judgments to Israel; He did not do so with any nation, since he did not manifest his judgments to them. For this reason it was said that he wanted it to be understood that only one nation belonged to the lineage of Abraham, which was called out of all nations, and thus all nations are in it; so that there is only one nation called to adoption. Apart from this, no other nation manifested its judgments, because those who did not believe in them, although their judgments were announced to them, were certainly not manifested to them, since, if they do not believe, they do not understand. 6 [v.8.11]. He remembered "in saeculum", in the century, his alliance. Other codices write in aeternum, eternally, which comes from the ambiguity of Greek. But, if it is to be understood "in the world" and not "eternally", how, when exposing the testament of which he remembered, does he add and say: Of the word which he commanded for a thousand generations? This can still be understood as not being eternal, as consisting of an end. But then he adds: Of what he gave to Abraham, and of his oath to Isaac; and all this was established to Jacob as a precept, and to Israel as an ETERNAL alliance. Here there is no room for ambiguity, since the Greek text writes aionion what our translators always translated as aeternum, eternal, since only some somewhere translated aionion as aeternale, eternal. Unless this happens because atona is vulgarly translated by saeculum, the century, and, therefore, they would like to translate aionion by saeculare and not by aeternum, which I do not remember anyone having dared to do. But if in this place the Old Testament is to be understood by the land of Canaan, since in alid psalmo: "Qui annuntiat verbum suum Iacob, iustitias et iudicia sua Israel; non fecit sic omni genti, et iudicia sua non manifestavit eis" (Ps 147,19-20). Ideo dictum est, quia unam gentem voluit intelligi pertinently ad semen Abrahae; quae vocata est quidem ex ómnibus gemibus, et sic in ea dicuntur omnes gentes, ut una sit gens in adoptionem vocata. Extra istam nulli genti manifestavit iudicia sua: quoniam qui ea non crediderunt, etiamsi annuntiata sunt, manifestata eis utique non sunt; quia nisi credant, non intelligent. 6 [v.8-11]. Memor Fuit in saeculum testamenti sui. Alli codices habent, in aeternum; quod ex ambiguous graeco factum est.

Sed si in hoc saeculum intelligendum est, non in aeternum; quomodo exponens cuius testamenti memor fuerit, adiungit et dicit: Verbi quod mandavit in mille generations? Quod adhuc curo aliquo fine potest intelligi; sed deinde dicit: "Quod disposuit ad Abraham, et iuramenti sui ad Isaac; et statuit illud Iacob in praeceptum, et Israel in testamentum aeternum." Ubi nullus est ambiguitatis locus: alcóviov quippe habet graecus, quod nusquam nostri nisi aeternum interpret sunt; vix autem aliqui alicubi aldbviov aeternale dixerunt. Nisi forte quia aiwva familiarius interpretantur saeculum, alcóviov non aeternum, sed saeculare interpret velint; quod neminem ausum Fuisse commemini. Si autem hoc loco Testamentum Vetus intelligendum est, propter teriam Chanaan; sic enim sermo con-

The discourse is woven like this: And he established it to Jacob as a precept, and to Israel as an eternal alliance, saying: "I will give you the land of Canaan, the rope {lot} of your inheritance", how is it to be understood that it is eternal, since that earthly inheritance cannot be eternal, and also taking into account that it is called the Old Testament because it is destroyed by the New? Nor does it seem that a thousand generations mean something eternal, since they have an end, even though in temporal terms they seem to be many. If it is true that the time of generation, which the Greeks call Guenean, is limited to a few years, since some, from the moment that man can beget, designated it fifteen years, what are these thousand generations, not only counted from Abraham, when this promise was made to him, until the time of the New Testament, but from Adam himself until the end of the world? Well, who will dare to say that this world will last fifteen thousand years? 7. Therefore, it seems to me that it must be understood here that we are speaking of the Old Testament even when it is said by the prophet that it is to be replaced by the New: The day will come, says the Lord, and I will give to the house of Jacob a New Testament, not like the testament that I made to their fathers when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, but of the testament of faith, which the Apostle extols when he proposes to Abraham that we imitate him, and refutes, using This, to those who glory in the works of the law, since Abraham believed God before the circumcision, and it was imputed to him to righteousness. Finally, when he said: He remembered in the century of his testament, texitur, "Et statuit illud" ipsi "Iacob in praeceptum, et" ipsi "Israel in testamentum aeternum, dices, Tibi dabo terram Chanaan, funiculum haereditatis vestrae": quomodo intelligendum est aeternum, cum terrena illa haereditas aeterna esse non possit? Et ideo Vetus Testamentum vocatur, quia per Novum aboletur. Mille vero generationses, nec aeternum videntur aliquid significare; quia utique finem habent, et ad ipsa temporalia nimis tantae sunt.

Quamlibet enim paucis annis generatio determinetur, quam Graeci yeveótv dicunt; quam minimam quidam quindecim annis terminaverunt, ex qua homo incipit posse generare; quae sunt istae mille generations, non solum a tempore Abraham, quando ei facta est ista promissio, usque ad tempus Novi Testamenti, sed ab ipso Adam, usque ad terminum saeculi? Quis enim audeat dicere quindecim annorum millibus hoc saeculum extendedí? 7. Proinde mihi videtur non hic Vetus Testamentum intelligendum, quod Novo esse tollendum dicitur per prophetam, "Ecce dies veniunt, dicit Dominus, et confirmabo domui Iacob Testamentum Novum; non secundum Testamentum quod constituí patribus eorum, cum eduxissem eos de terra Aegypti" (ler 31,31.32): sed testamentum fidei, quod laudat Apostolus, cum Abraham nobis proponit imitandum, et de Legis operibus gloriantes inde convincit, quod Abraham etiam ante circumcisionem credidit Deo, et reputatum est illi ad iustitiam (Gal 3,5.6): Denique cum dixisset, Memor Fuit in saeculum testamenti sui; quod in aeternum intel

We must understand, he eternally remembered the testament of justification and the eternal inheritance that God promised faith, for he says: The testament of WORD that he commanded for a thousand generations. And what does "commanded" mean? When saying I will give you the land of Canaan, it is not a command, but a promise. A command is what we must do, and a promise is what we must receive. Then the command is faith, so that the righteous may live by faith, and with this faith the eternal inheritance is promised. Therefore, in the thousand generations, taking into account the perfection of the number, they are all understood; that is, while all the generations pass, the command must be lived by faith. This is observed by the people of God, the children of the promise, being born and dying until every generation is finished, which is symbolized in the number thousand, because the number ten (that is, the precepts, in attention to the three patriarchs), multiplied by ten, forms the hundred, and this, added ten times, constitutes the thousand; That is, he gave it to Jacob as a precept. These are the three patriarchs of whom he especially says that he is God, and whom the Lord named in the New Testament where he says: Many will come from the east and from the west, and will sit with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven. precept to the promise. If in the precept the work takes place, in the promise the reward. The Lord says: This is the work of God, that you believe in Him whom He sent. Quod enim ait, Tibi dabo terram Chanaan, non mandatum est, sed promissum: mandatum est autem quod faceré deben, promissum quod accipere.

Mille ergo generationses, propter numeri perfectionem, pro omnibus intelligendae sunt; id est, quamdiu generatio generationi sequendo succedit, tamdiu mandatum est vivirdum ex fide. Quod observat populus Dei, filii promissionis nascendo venientes, et moriendo abeuntes, doñee omnis generatio finiatur; quod millenario numero significatum est, quia denarii numeri solidum quadratum decem decies, et hoc decies, ad mille pervenit. Quod disposuit, inquit, ad Abraham, et iuramenti sui ad Isaac. Et statuit ittud Iacob, id est ipsi Iacob, in praeceptum. Ipsi sunt tres patriarchae quorum specialiter se dicit Deum, quos et Dominus nominat in Testament Novo, ubi dicit: Multi ab oriente et occidente venient, et recumbent cum Abraham, et Isaac, et Iacob in regno caelorum (Mt 8,11). Ista es haereditas aeterna. Nam et hic, ubi ait, Statuit illud Iacob in praeceptum; manifestat praeceptum esse fidei: non enim promissum appellaret praeceptum. Si enim opus est in praecepto, merces in promisso: Hoc est opus Dei, Dominus ait, ut credatis in eum quem Me misit (lo 6,29). Hoc ergo

He burned and remembered it eternally as his testament, that is, the word of faith that we announced, he gave it to Jacob as a precept, and to Israel as an eternal testament; For her and the precept fulfilled he would give them something eternal. Saying: I will give you the land of Canaan, the rope [lot} of your inheritance, I ask: How is this eternal if it does not mean something eternal? This is also called the land of promise, a land flowing with milk and honey; and these products symbolize grace, in which one perceives how sweet the Lord is, and to which not all men belong, since faith does not belong to all. Therefore he added: Rope [lot} of your inheritance. Hence in another psalm it is declared that the lineage of Abraham speaks, which is Christ, where it says: The lines [the lots] fell for me in beautiful places, for my inheritance is excellent for me. Why it was called "land of Canaan" is stated by the significance of the name, since Canaan means humble. If we take into account the curse of the holy Noah, by which he told Canaan himself that he would be a servant of his brothers, then we will say that this is also where servile fear comes from. Now: The servant does not remain in the house forever; The son remains forever, says the apostle Saint John. Therefore, with the Canaanite cast out, the land of promise is given to Abraham's lineage, since perfect charity casts out fear so that the son remains eternally in the house. Hence it was said: And it was given to Israel as an eternal testament. 8 [v. 12]. The well-known story then continues according to the veracity of the holy books: When they were scarce verbum quod mandavit, memor in aetemum testamenti sui, hoc est, verbum fidei quod praedicamus (Rom 10:8), statuit illud ipsi Jacob in praeceptum; et ipsi Israel in testamentara aetemum, id est, quod ex ipso verbo et praecepto impleto daturus esset aliquid aeternum. Dicens, Tibi dabo terram Chanaan, funiculum haereditatis vestrae. Quomodo ergo est hoc aeternum, nisi aliquid aeternum meaning? Ipsa enim dicta est terra promissionis, terra fluens lac et mel (Ex 3,8.17). Quod totum significat gratiam, in qua gustatur quam suavis est Dominus (Ps 33,8); ad quam non omnes homines pertinent: non enim omnium est fides (2 Thess 3,2). Ideo addidit, Euniculum haereditatis vestrae.

Unde in alio psalmo, semen Abrahae, quod est Christus, intelligitur loqui, ubi dicit: Funes ceciderunt mihi in praeclaris; etenim haereditas mea praeclara est mihi (Ps 15:6). Cur autem dicta sit terra Chanaan, interpretatio huius nominis aperit; Chanaan quippe interpretatur Humilis. Quod si ad illam referatur sententiam sancti Noe, qua eumdem Chanaan dixit futurum servum fratrum suorum (Gen 9:25), hinc est etiam servilis timor. Servus autem non manet in domo in aeternum; filius manet in aeternum (lo 8,35). Ideo excluso Chananaeo, datur terra promissionis semini Abrahae. Consummata enim charitas foras mittit timorem (1 lo 4,18), ut filius maneat in domo in aeternum. Unde dictum est, Et ipsi Israel in testamentnm aeternum. 8 [v.12}. Deinceps exsequitur historiam in Librorum sanctorum veritate notissimam. Cum essent numero brevi, paucissimi et incolae in ea:

in number, very few and pilgrims in it, that is, in the land of Canaan. When the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac and Jacob lived there, before receiving it as an inheritance, they were very few in their lineage, and also pilgrims in it. Some codices write paucissimos et íncolas and not paucissimi et incolae. In which it appears that those who translated in this way followed the Greek locution to the letter, which cannot be translated into Latin except with this contradiction, which in no way can be tolerated. Well, if we tried to translate this whole phrase verbatim, we would say: In eo esse illos numero brevi, paucissimos et Íncolas in ea. What the Greek records: en to einai autous [in eo esse illos'], is translated into Latin by cum essent, when they were or being, whose verbal locution cannot be followed by the accusative, but by the nominative. Who will say cum essent paucissimos, but cum essent paucissimi, when they were very few or when they were very few? 9 [v.13-15}. Then when they were few in number, or in short numbers, very few and pilgrims in it, they passed from nation to nation and from one town to another town. The latter is a repetition of what he had said: From nation to nation. He did not let anyone harm them, that is, he did not allow them. Greek phrase is nocere illos, and Latin nocere Mis, to cause harm to them. And for them he punished the kings. “Do not touch,” he says, “my anointed ones, and do not harm my prophets.” The psalmist recorded the words of God who punishes or rebukes the kings so that they would not harm the holy patriarchs when they were few in number and very few and pilgrims in the land of Canaan. These words, although not found in his historical books, are nevertheless to be understood or as said id est, in terra Chanaan. Quando ibi patres habitaverunt Abraham, Isaac et lacob, antequam eam acciperent haereditatem, in semine suo paucissimi erant, et incolae in ea. Nonnulli autem codices habent, non, paucissimi et incolae; sed, paucissimos et íncolas. Ubi apparet eos qui ista ita interpret sunt, graecam fuesse locutionem secutos, quae transferri non potest in latinum, nisi cum ea absurditate, quae ferri omnino non possit. Si enim totam ipsam locutionem transferre conemur, dicturi sumus, ln eo esse illos numero brevi, paucissimos et Íncolas in ea. Quod autem ait graecus, ln eo esse illos, hoc est latine, Cum essent: quod verbum non potest casus accusatívus sequi, sed nominativus. Quis enim dicat, Cum essent paucissimos? thirst, Cum essent paucissimi.

9 [v.13-15]. "Cum" ergo "essent numero breves", vel, "numero brevi, paucissimi et incolae in ea, transierunt de gente in gentem, et de regno in populum alterum." Repetitio est eius quod dixerat, "de gente in gentem. Non dimisit hominem nocere eis": id est, non permisit. Graeca autem locutio est, nocere illos; Latin veto, nocere illis. Eí corripuit pro eis reges. Nolite, inquit, tangere christos meos, et in prophetis meis nolite malignan. Verba dixit Dei corripientis vel arguenas reges, ne laedetent sanctos patres, cum essent numero Briefs, et paucissimi atque incolae in terra Chanaan. Quae verba licet in libris eius historiae non
God's Fidelity to the Covenant

covertly, as God speaks with hidden and true visions to the hearts of men, or also as recorded by the angel. Because the king of Gerara and the king of Egypt were divinely warned not to harm Abraham, and another king (that of the Palestinians) was divinely warned not to harm Isaac, when they were very few and pilgrims, before Jacob went to live as a pilgrim in Egypt; all of which is understood to have been commemorated in what is now said in the psalm: They passed from nation to nation, and from one kingdom to another people. But as it occurred to him to ask how, being few in number and very few and pilgrims, they could subsist in a foreign land before passing over and multiplying in Egypt, he then added: He did not allow any man to harm them, and for their sake he punished the kings. Do not touch my Christs or anointed ones and do not harm my prophets. 10. It may rightly raise concern why they were called Christs or anointed before the anointing was established, by which this name was imposed on kings. This was established from Saul, whom David succeeded in the kingdom. From then on all the kings of Judah and Israel were anointed following the holy custom. In this anointing the one true Christ was symbolized, to whom it was said: God, your God, anointed you with the oil of joy upon your sharers. Then, how were they called Christs then? For we read of Abraham that they were prophets, and, without a doubt, what was clearly said of him, the same is to be understood of them. Or were they called Christs because, although latently, they were nevertheless already Christians? For legantur, tamen intelligenda sunt vel latenter dicta, sicut Deus in hominum cordibus loquitur occultis et veracibus visis, vel etiam per Angelum expressa. Nam et rex Gerarum et rex Aegyptiorum divinitus admoniti sunt ne nocerent Abtahae (Gen 12,17-20; et 20,3), et rex alius ne noceret Isaac (ib. 26,8-11), et alii ne nocerent lacob (ib. 31-33); cum essent paucissimi et incolae, antequam ad incolendam Aegyptum cum filiis suis ttansiret lacob: quod intelligitur in eo commemoratum, quod ait, Transierunt de gente in gentem, de regno in populum alterum. Sed quia occurrebat quaetere, antequam transirent et in Aegypto multiplicarentur, quomodo numero breves, paucissimi et incolae in aliena terra perdurare potuerunt, secutas adiunxit, Non permisit hominem nocere eis, et corripuit pro eis reges.

Nolite tangere christos meos, et in prophetis meis nolite malignan. 10. Potest autem merit moveré quomodo fuerint christi appellati, antequam esset unctio, ex qua hoc nomen impositum est regibus: quod a Saüle coepit, cui David successit in regno; atque inde caeteri et reges Iudae et reges Israel continuatione sacratae consuetudinis unguebantur: in qua unctione figurabatur unus verus Christus, cui dicmm est, Unxit te Deus, Deus tuus oleo exsultalionis prae participibus tuis (Ps 54,8). Unde ergo illi iam tune christi appellabantur? Nam prophetas eos Fuisse, legimus of Abtaham; et utique, quod de illo manifesté dictum est, hoc et de illis intelligendum est. An ideo chtisti, quia etiamsi latentet, iam tamen

Although the flesh of Christ comes from them, yet Christ exists before them. For this reason he answers the Jews, saying to them: Before Abraham existed I was. Then, how could they not know this one or how could they not believe in Him, since they were called prophets, because, although hidden, they nevertheless symbolized the Lord? Hence the Lord clearly says: Abraham desired to see my day; He saw him and was glad. No one, whether before his incarnation or after it, without this faith in Christ, was reconciled with God. This was recorded very clearly by the Apostle: There is one God and one Mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus. 11 [v.16]. From now on he begins to narrate how the passage from one nation to another nation and from one kingdom to another people took place, and called—says the psalmist—famine on the land and destroyed all sources of bread. He sent a man before them; Joseph was sold as a slave. For this reason it came to pass that they passed from one nation to another nation and from one kingdom to another people. But the locutions of holy Scripture must not be passed over carelessly. He called, he says, famine upon the earth, as if hunger were a person, or some animated body, or some spirit that could obey the one who called it, whereas hunger is a detriment contracted by the lack of food, and, therefore, is found in those who endure it as an ailment. Well, just as for the disease to disappear, most of the time it is achieved through medication, so hunger is also cured, in a certain way, through food. Then, what Christians? quamvis enim caro Christi ex illis, tamen Christus ante illos: quod et Iudaeis respondit, dicens, Antequam Abraham ieront, ego sunt. Quomodo autem hunc illi ignorant, aut in eum non crederent; cum propterea prophetae dicerentur quia licet occultius, tamen Dominum praenuntiabant? Hence any psalm that does not have hallelujah at the end, nor, they say, does it have it at the beginning; Therefore, if it only seems to have it at the beginning, it rather belongs to the end of the previous psalm. of whom I believe that God was pleased with them, and in the second those who excited anger among the same people are commemorated, to whom, however, the mercy of God was not lacking, since the things that are narrated in it are said in person of those who, converted, ask for forgiveness, and the examples that are given are recorded taking them from those sinners in whom the copious mercy of God appears. This psalm begins as 104; Confess the Lord. But 104 continued: and call upon his name; and this: because he is good, because his mercy endures forever. The many codices that I was able to see, both Latin and Greek, write: Did they irritate you, or what is more expressive in the Greek text: Did they provoke you to anger by rising the sea patribus nostris, tanquam diceret, Peccavimus sicut patres nostri, eorum videlicet imitating peccata? They forgot God, who saved them. How did he save them? Doing wonders in Egypt, wonders in the land of Ham and terrible things in the Red Sea. The wonders themselves are terrible things, because there is no admiration without a certain fear. Although these things could also be called terrible here because they afflicted the adversaries and showed them what they should fear. 21 [v.23]. And he said he would destroy them. Because they forgot the One who saved them by working wonders and made and worshiped the sculpture, being worthy of being annihilated for such a monstrous crime and incredible impiety. He said that he would destroy them, [and would have done so] if Moses, his chosen one, had not stood before him in the destruction. He did not say that he was placed in the destruction, as to break or undo the wrath of God, but in the destruction, that is, in the midst of the punishment that they owed.

receive; that is, he gave himself up for them, saying: If you forgive their sin, forgive them; but, if he is not forgiven, erase me from your book. By this the value of the intercession of the saints for their fellow men before God was demonstrated. Moses being sure that God, through his justice, could not erase him, he begged for mercy so that he would not destroy those whom he could in justice. So, he placed himself in the brokenness before God so that he would turn away his wrath and not annihilate them. 22 [v.24}. And they considered the desirable land for nothing. Had they seen her by chance? Why did they consider the land they had not seen for nothing? Because they didn't believe his words. Without a doubt, if that land from which it was said to flow with milk and honey did not prefigure something great, by whose visible sign it led those who understood its wonders to the invisible grace of the kingdom of heaven, in no way would they be blamed because they held that land as nothing, whose temporal possession we must also value as nothing in order that we may truly love the desirable and free Jerusalem, our mother. But here rather, infidelity is argued, and rightly so; because, considering the desirable land to be nothing, they did not believe the words of God, who leads through certain small things to great things; and, therefore, they, hastening to make themselves happy with temporal things, which they perceived according to the flesh, did not keep—as was said above—the counsel of God. 23 [v.25]. And they murmured in their tents and did not hear the voice of the Lord, which very severely forbade them to murmur.

The sacred letters did not conceal the fact that the Gentiles had this custom. 31. But what does the following mean: "Interfecta est terra in sanguinibus": The earth was killed with blood? If we did not have the gift of God, who wanted his Scripture to be found in many languages, we would think that it was an error on the part of the copyist, and we would say monium, ut intelligamus illam fidei eius titubationem hac sola poena Fuisse correptam, quod in eam terram, quo populum ipse ducebat, non est permíssus intrare. Absit autem ut eum credamus alienatum a regno gratiae Dei, quod significat illa terra promissionis, unde lac et mel defluere dicebatur. Hoc est etúm potius testamentum aeternum quod disposuit ad Abraham, non secundum carnem patiem nostrum, sed secundum fidem. 29 {v.34-36]. lili autem de quorum iniquitatibus iste loquitur psalmus, cum in illam temporalem terram promissionis intrassent, "Non disperdiderunt Gentes, quas dixit Dominus illis. Et commixti sunt Ínter Gentes, et didicerunt opera eorum, et servierunt sculptilibus eorum; et factum est illis in scandalum." Illud quod eas non disperdiderunt, sed eis commixti sunt, factum est illis in scandalum. 30 [v.37-40].

"Et immolaverunt filios suos et filias suas daemoniis: et effuderunt sanguinem innocentem, sanguinem filiorum suorum et filiarum suarum, quas sacrificerunt sculptilibus Chanaan." Immolasse filios suos et filias suas daemoniis et idolis, non eos illa narrat historia; sed ñeque iste psalmus lyingi potest, ñeque Prophetae, qui hoc dicunt multis increpationum suarum locis. Habuisse vero istam consuetudinem Gentes, nec earum litterae tacuerunt. 31. Sed quid est quod sequitur? Et interfecta est terra in sanguinibus. Putaremus enim scriptoris errorem, eumque diceremus pro eo quod est infecta, fecisse interfecta, nisi haberemus beneficium Dei, qui Scripturas suas in multis linguis esse voluit; atque ita esse scriptum, Interfecta
Confession of Israel's rebellions

which was written interfecta est for infecta est, it became infected or stained. But I have seen that efonozoneze was written in the Greek codices that I consulted interfecta est tena in sanguinibus. What does interfecta est terra mean, the earth was killed? That we are faced with a tropic or figurative locution that refers to the men who inhabit the earth, and by this figure the continent is designated by the content, just as we call a bad house that in which bad men live, or a good house that in which good men live. They, therefore, killed their souls by immolating their children and shedding the blood of children, conforming to the crime of strangers, for which it was said: And they shed innocent blood. Then the earth was killed with blood and polluted with the works of their hands as they killed themselves in their souls and polluted themselves with their works. And they fornicated with their inventions. He calls inventions which the Greeks call epitedeumata. This word is found in the Greek codices both here and above where it was written: And they irritated him with their inventions, while here and there he calls inventions those in which they imitated others. Let us not believe, then, that they were called inventions because they were established by them, without preceding any example of others whom they imitated. Hence some of our translators preferred to write not adinventiones, inventions, but studia, propensities; and others, affectiones or affectationes, inclinations or passions; and, finally, others, voluptates, appetites. Also the same ones who wrote adinventiones, wrote studia elsewhere. I wanted to remember this so that the name adinventionis, invention, would not promote the dispute here that they themselves devised those things, but that they imitated them from others. est terra in sanguinibus, inspectis graecis codicibus videremus. Quid est ergo, Interfecta est terra, nisi hoc referatur ad homines qui habitabant in ierra, tropica locutione, qua significatur per id quod continet, id quod continetur, sicut dicimus malam domum, in qua mali habitant, et bonam in qua boni? Ipsi namque interficiebant animas suas immolando filios suos, et effundendo sanguinem parvulorum a consensione illius sceleris alienorum: unde dictum est, Effuderunt sanguinem innocentem. Ergo, Interfecta est terra in sanguinibus, et contaminata est in operibus eorum, cum ipsi interfecti sunt in anima, et contaminati in operibus suis. Et fomicati sunt in adinventionibus suis.

Has dicit adinventiones, quas Graeci i-m-n-iStúíiara appellant: nam hoc verbum est in codicibus graecis et hoc loco, et superius, ubi dictum est, Irritaverunt eum in adinventionibus suis; cum et illic et hic eas dicat adinventiones, in quibus aJios imitati sunt. Non itaque sic dictas arbitremur adinventiones, quasi ab ipsis insdtutas, nullo in allus praecedente quod imitarentur exemplo. Unde alii interpretes nostri, non adinventiones, sed studia; alii vero affectiones, vel affectationes, alii voluptates dicere maluerunt: et iidem ipsi qui dixerunt adinventiones, alii loco studia posuerunt. Hoc commemorare volui, ne quaestionem faceret nomen adinventionis in ea re, quam non a seipsis excogitaverunt, sed alios imitati sunt. S.Ag. 21

32 [v. 40-43]. And the Lord was filled with fury against his people. Some Latin interpreters did not want to translate the Greek word thimos by anger, but some translated it by mind; others, out of indignation, and others, out of encouragement. Whatever word of these is recorded, it must be understood that there is no disturbance in God, but that this name receives the meaning of vindictive power through metaphorical use. 33. And he abhorred his inheritance. And he delivered them into the hands of the nations, and those who hated them dominated them, and their enemies troubled them, and they were brought low under their hands or power. When God called them an inheritance, it is evident that he did not hate them to lose them, but he abhorred them and gave them into the hands of their enemies to correct them. He then continues and says: Many times he delivered them. 34. But they exaggerated his plan. This is what he said above: They did not keep his advice. The advice or ruling of man, by which he seeks his own, but not that of God, is very harmful to man. In the inheritance of God, which is the same for us when He deigns to give Himself to us to enjoy Him, we will not endure hardships with the company of the saints for the love of our almost private property, because that most glorious city, once it obtains the promised inheritance, in which no one dies or is born, will not have citizens who each one will enjoy their own things in particular, because God will be all things to all. Anyone who sincerely longs for the company of God on this pilgrimage becomes accustomed to preferring things like this32 [v.40-43]. Et iratus est furore Dominus in populum suum. Noluerunt quidam interpretes nostri iram will put, in eo quod graecus habet Whose: sec [quidam posueruntmentem; quidam vero indignationem, quidam animum interpretati sunt. Hoc est quod superius ait, Non sustinuerunt consilium eius. Perniciosum autem est consilium hominis ipsi homini, quo ea quaerit quae sua sunt, non quae Dei sunt (Phil 2:21). In cuius haereditate, quod ipse nobis est, cum ad fruendum se praebere digntur, nullas patiemur cum sanáis societatis anxieties, dilectione rei nostrae quasi privatae. Gloriosissima quippe illa civitas adepta promissam haereditatem, in qua nullus morietur, nullus orietur, non habebit cives qui singuli gaudeant suis rebus, quia Deus erit omnia in ómnibus (1 Cor 15,28). Cuius societatem quisquís in hac peregrinatione fidelíter et flagrante! desidetaverit, assuesqt privatis praefer-

doll your own, not seeking your things, but those of Jesus Christ. So that, not by making himself wise and looking only for his own good, he may exaggerate God with his advice, but that, waiting for what he does not see, that is, patiently waiting for the eternal, which he does not see, he may not be in a hurry to make himself happy with the things he sees, but follow in the promises the advice of Him who asks for help in temptations. Therefore, he must be humble in his confession so that he does not resemble those of whom it is said: And they were humbled in their iniquities. 35 [v. 44. 45]. However, the most merciful God did not abandon them, for he looked upon them when they were troubled upon hearing their prayer. And he remembered his covenant, and repented according to his great mercy. He said he regretted it because it seems that he changed the ruling by which they would perish. In God all things are immutably established. God does not work by a sudden dictate; Nothing has happened since he did not know from eternity that he was going to do it, but in the temporal movements or impulses of the creature, which he wonderfully governs without moving in time, it is said that he executes as with a sudden will what he ordered by his immutable and most secret decree in the established causes of things, which, when known in due time, constitutes present the things that he made and future. And who is capable of knowing this? Let us listen to Scripture, which simply declares the most excellent things when it offers the little ones, who are to be fed, the things they should take, and the older ones, who are to exercise themselves in work, the things they are to investigate. And he looked upon them when they were troubled to hear his orare communia, non sua quaerendo, sed quae Iesu Christi: ne sibi sapiens et sibi consulens, exacerbet Deum consilio suo; sed sperans quod non videt, non festinet de his quae videntur fieri beatus, atque illud aeternum quod non vídetur patienter exspectans, eius in promissionibus sequatur consilium, cuius in tentationibus precatur auxilium. Ita erit et humilis in confessionibus suis, ne fiat istorum similis, de quibus dicitur: Et humiliati sunt in iniquitatibus suis. 35 [v.44.45]. Deus tamen plenus mercy, non neglexit eos; "Et vidit cum tribularentur, cum audiret orationem eorum.

Et memor fuet testamenti sui, et poenituit eum secundum multitudinem misericordiae suae." Poenituit dictum est, quia mutavit quod eos perditurus videbatur. Et apud Deum quidem disposita et fixa sunt omnia; nec aliud facit quasi sudden council, quod non ex aeternitate se facturum esse praescivit: sed in creaturae temporalibus motibus, quam gubernat mirabiliter, ipse non temporaliter motus, quasi sudden volúntate faceré dicitur quod ordinaris rerum causis consilii sui secretissimi immutabilitate disposuít, qua suis quaeque temporibus agnita, et praesentia facit, et future iam fecit. Et ad haec quis idoneus? Audiamus itaque Scripturam, humiliter excelsa dicentem, cum et parvulis nutriendis sumenda porrigit, et maioribus exercendis perscrutanda proponit. "or", and he remembered his alliance, no doubt of the eternal Testament that he established with Abraham, not of the Old, which was abolished, but of the New, which is hidden in the Old. And he repented according to his great mercy. He did what he had established, but he had foreseen that this would be granted to the contrite postulants; Well, although his prayer did not yet exist, without a doubt, having existed, it was not hidden from God. 36 [v.46]. And he used mercies on them so that they would be free of mercy and not of wrath. I think he used the plural, saying "he gave them mercies," because each one receives a particular gift from God: one and another. And he showed them mercy in the sight of all those who had captivated them. Now, whoever you read these things, you will know, by reading in the apostolic letters or by searching the prophets, the grace of God, by which we are ransomed to eternal life by our Lord Jesus Christ, and you will see the Old Testament revealed in the New, and the New hidden in the Old. Remember whom the apostle Saint Paul called prince of aerial power, which works in the children of unbelief; and what he says about some: that they realize the snares of the devil, in those who are held captive by him, according to his will; and the words of our Lord Jesus Christ by which He says He cast out the devil from the hearts of believers: Now the prince of this world was cast out; and those of the Apostle himself, who says: And He brought us out of the power of darkness and transferred us to the kingdom of the Son of His love. Thinking of these and other similar things, raise your spirit also towards the Old quod disposuit ad Abraham, non veteris quod aboletur, sed novi quod etiam in vetere absconditur. Et poenituit eum secundum multitudinem misericordiae suae. Hoc fecit quod disposuerat, sed contribulatis et orantibus se id concessurum esse praesciverat; quia et ipsa orado eorum, cum adhuc non esset, sed future esset, Deum procul dubio non latebat. 36 [v.46]. Et dedit eos in misericords. Ut essent non vasa irae, sed vasa mercye (Rom 9,22.23). Ideo autem puto pluraliter misericordis dictates, in quas eos dedit, quia unusquisque proprium donum habet a Deo, alius sic, alius autem sic (1 Cor 7,7). Dedit ergo eos in misericords, in conspectu omnium qui ceperant eos.

Age nunc, quisquís haec legis, et gratiam Dei, qua in aeternam vitam per Dominum nostrum Iesum Christum redimimur, legendo in apostolicis Litteris, in propheticis autem scrutando cognoscis, et Vetus Testamentum in Novo revelatum, in Vetere Novum velatum vides; I collected quem dixerit apostolus Paulus principem potestatis aeris, qui operatur in filiis infidelitatis (Eph 2,2), et illud ubi ait de quibusdam, ut resipiscant de diaboli laqueis, captivati ab ipso secundum ipsius voluntatem (2 Tim 2,26): et verba Dominí Iesu Christi, ubi eum expellens de fidelium cordibus ait, Nunc princeps huius mundi missus est joras (lo 12.31); et ipsius itidem Apostoli dicetis, Qui eruit nos de potestate tenebrarum, et transtulit in regnum Filii charitatis suae (Col 1,13). Haec atque huiusmodi ratiocinatus, intende animum et in litteras Veteris Testamenti, et vide quid cantetur in eo psalmo cuius

Testament and see what is sung in that psalm entitled When the house is built after the captivity. There, then, it is said: Sing to the Lord a new song. And so that you do not think that he was only referring to the Jewish people: Sing, he says, to the Lord, all the earth. Sing and bless his name; antmciad, or, rather, announce well. What do I say? Translating the same Greek word that was recorded, I will say: Evangelize the day that comes from the day, its health. Hence it comes that the Gospel was called that in which the day (which proceeds) of the day is announced, the Lord Jesus Christ, light of light, Son of the Father. This is your Health, because the Health of God is Christ, as we have already demonstrated before. Announce his glory among the nations, his wonders among all peoples. For the Lord is great and very worthy of praise; terrible upon all the gods, because all the gods of the nations are demons. These enemies, with their king the devil, held God's people captive. When we are freed from this captivity and the prince of the world is cast out, after the captivity the house is built, of which Christ is the Cornerstone, who raised up in himself two peoples in one new man, making peace, who when he came evangelized the Day that comes from the Day, to those who were near and to those who were far away, making both one and bringing other sheep that are not of this fold so that there may be one flock and one shepherd. So God, in the sight of all those who had taken them captive, granted mercy to his predestined ones, for [it is predestination] not of him who wills nor of him who runs, but of God, who has mercy. Then these enemies, the devil and his angels, had captivated those predestined for the kingdom and the est titulus, Quando domas aedificabatur post captivitatem: ibi enim dicitur, Cántate Domino canticum novum. Et ne existimes ad Iudaeorum populum tantummodo pertinere: Cántate, inquit, Domino, omnis terra; sing Domino, henedicite nomen eius, annuntiate, vel potius, bene nuntiate, imo ut ipsum verbum quod in graeco positum est, transferam, evangelízate diem ex die, salutare eius. Hinc enim Evangelium nuncupatum est, in quo annuntiatur dies ex die, Dominus Christus, lumen ex lumine, Filius ex Patre. Hoc enim est et salutare eius; quia salutare Dei Christus est, sicut et superius iam demonstravimus.

"Annuntiate in gentibus gloriam eius, in omnibus populis mirabilia eius. Quoniam magnus Dominus et laudabilis valde, terribilis est super omnes déos: quoniam omnes dii Gentium daemonia" (Ps 95,1-5). Isti ergo inimiri cum rege suo diabolo captivum tenebant populum Dei. De qua captivitate cum redimimur, et princeps huius mundi mittitur foras, aedificatur domus post captivitatem: cuius lapis angularis est Christus, qui duos condidit in se, in unum novum hominem, faciens pacem, quam dies ex die veniens evangelizavit eis qui erant prope, et eis qui erant longe, faciens utraque unum (Eph 2,13-22); et adducens alias oves quae non sunt de hoc ovili, ut sit unus grex et unus pastor (lo 10,16). Et ita Deus dedit in misericordias praedestinatos suos; quia non volentis ñeque currentis, sed miserentis est Dei (Rom 9,16): in conspectu omnium qui ceperant

glory of God. However, those who tend to dominate the unbelievers internally and fight the faithful externally were thrown out by our Redeemer. These fight, but do not assault those who occupy the tower of the fortress against the enemy. When fighting, the relics of weakness are perceived in us, for which we say: Forgive us our debts, for which we say: And do not lead us into temptation, but deliver us from evil. Having cast out these enemies, our Lord Jesus Christ brings about health in the Body, for which the Head is the same Savior of the Body, so that the third day may also take place in His own Body, for in this sense He said: I cast out demons and perform healings today and tomorrow, and on the third day I perish; That is to say, I attain health, I am perfected, all of us becoming perfect men to the measure of the age of the fullness of Christ. 37 [v.47.48]. Thus, having cast out the demons that had held us captive, he gained health. Therefore, after having said: And he gave them mercies in the sight of those who held them captive, as if they had cast out the demons, which had captivated them, he prays for complete salvation, saying: Save us, Lord, our God, and gather us from among the nations, or as other codices write: from among the nations. So that we may praise your holy name and glory in your praise. He then briefly records the praise: Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting, which is understood from everlasting to everlasting, that is, eternally, for without end he is praised—by those of whom it is said: Blessed are those who dwell in your house; eos. Hi ergo inimici, diabolus et angelí eius captivaverant praedestinatos in Dei regnum et gloriam: a Redemptore autem nostro foras missi qui dominai infidelibus solebant intrinsecus, fideles oppugnant extrinsecus. Be oppugnant, non expugnant eos qui apprehendunt turrem fortirudinis a facie inimici (Ps 60,4). Ut autem oppugnent, sentiunt in nobis esse infirmitatis relics, propter quas dicimus, Dimitte nobis debita nostra; propter quas dicimus, Ne nos inferas in tentalionem, sed libera nos a malo (Mt 6,12.13). His itaque inimias eiectis, perfecit Dominus Christus sanitates in corpore, cui caput est ipse Salvator corporis (Eph 5,23), ut in eo ipso corpore suo tertia consummetur.

Sic enim dixit, Ecce eicio daemonia, et sanitates perfido hodie et eras, et tertia consammor (Luke 13:32); id est, perfkior, oceurrentibus omnibus nobis in virum perfectum, in mensuram aetatis plenitudinis Christi (Eph 4:13). 37 [v.47.48]. Itaque eiectis daemoniis, a quibus captivi tenebamur, perficit sanitates. Ideo et hic cum dixisset, Et dedit eos in misericords, in conspectu omnium qui ceperant eos; tanquam eiectis daemoniis qui ceperant, fit oratio ut perficiat sanitates. Salvos nos fac, Domine Deus nosíer, et congreganos de nationibus, vel, sicut alii codices habent, de Gentibus; ut confiteamur nomini sancto tuo, et gloriemur in laude tua. Deinde breviter subiecit ipsam laudem, Benedictus Dominus Deus Israel, a saeculo et usque in saeculum: quod intelligimus, ab aeterno usque in

forever and ever they will praise you. This is the third perfection of the Body of Christ, for as soon as the demons have been cast out and health has been achieved, until the immortality of the body itself, the eternal kingdom of those who praise consummately will have been reached, because it is of those who love eminently; of those who love completely, because they contemplate face to face. Then what was requested at the beginning of this psalm will be fulfilled: Lord, remember us, with benevolence towards your people. Visit us with your Health so that we may see the goodness of your chosen ones and rejoice in the joy of your people, and you may be glorified with your inheritance. He not only gathers from among the nations the sheep that perished of the house of Israel, but also those that are not of that flock, so that, as was said, there may be one flock and one shepherd. The Jews thinking that this prophecy referred to their visible kingdom, since they did not know how to rejoice in the hope of invisible goods, fell into the snares of him of whom the Lord said: I came in the name of my Father, and you did not receive me; another will come in his own name, and you will receive him. The apostle Saint Paul also says of this: For the man of sin will be revealed, the son of perdition, who opposes and exalts himself against everything that is called God or receives worship, until he sits in the temple of God, showing himself to be God; and a little later the same Apostle adds: Then the wicked will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus Christ will kill with the breath of his mouth and destroy with the manifestation of his presence. The coming of this wicked one will be carried out by the operation of satan with all power, with signaeternum; quia sine fine laudabitur ab eis de quibus dicitur, Beati qui habitant in domo tua, in saecula saeculorum laudabunt te (Ps 83,5). Ipsa est tertia consummatio corporis Christi, eiectis daemoniis et perfectis sanitatibus, usque ad ipsius corporis immortalitatem, regnum sempiternum perfecte laudantium, quia perfecte amantium: perfecte autem amantium,' quia facie ad faciem contemplantium. Tune enim perficietur quod in primordio psalmi huius oratum est: "Memento nostri, Domine, in beneplácito populi tui; visita nos in salutari tuo, ad videndum in bonitote electorum tuorum, ad laetandum in laetitia gentis tuae, ut Iauderis cum haereditate tua."

Non enim de Gentibus solas congregat oves quae perierunt domus Israel (Mt 15,24), sed etiam eas quae non sunt de illo ovili; ut sit grex unus, ut dictum est, et unus pastor. ludaei vero cum putant ad suum regnum visible istam pertinere prophetiam, quia spe invisibilium bonorum gaudere non norunt; in laqueos illius ruituri sunt, de quo Dominus ait: "Ego veni in nomine Patris mei, et non suscepistis me; alius veniet in nomine suo, hunc suscipietis" (lo 5,43). De quo apostolus Paulus dicit, "Quia revelabitur homo peccati, filius interitus, qui adversatur et superextollitur supra omne quod dicitur Deus, aut quod colitur, ita ut in Templo Dei sedeat, ostendens se tanquam sit Deus." Et paulo post, "Tune revelabitur", inquit, "iniquus, quem Dominus Iesus interficiet spiritu oris sui, et evacuabit illuminatione praesentiae suae eum, cuius est praesentia secundum operationem satanae, in omni virtute et

them and portents of lies and with all deception of iniquity for those who perish in payment for not having received the love of the truth to save themselves; and therefore God sends them a work of deception, so that they may believe a lie and all those who did not believe the truth, but took pleasure in iniquity, may be judged. For this I will flee (from her); Because of this one who is exalted above all that is called God or that receives worship, it seems to me that it must be thought that this prophecy is fulfilled in the people of the carnal Israelites, in response to which it was said: Save us, Lord, our God, and gather us from among the nations, because being he the guide and being as it were in the presence of their visible enemies, who had visibly captivated them, they thought that they would obtain visible glory. In this way they believed the lie, because they did not receive the love of the truth, for which they desired spiritual goods and not carnal goods. So they were so deceived by the devil that they killed Christ when they said: If we leave Him like this, everyone will believe in Him, and the Romans will come and take away our place and nation. When Caiphas, one of them, being pontiff of that year, said to them: You know nothing, nor do you think that it is good for us that one man should die for the people and the whole nation not perish, this is what the evangelist says: He did not say it on his own, but, being pontiff of that year, he prophesied that Jesus must die for the whole nation; and not only for the nation, that is, for the sheep that had perished of the house of Israel, but also that the scattered children of God might be gathered together in one. So he had other sheep that did not belong to this flock. To all these, both to the procesignis et prodigiis mendacii, et in omni seductione iniquitatis his qui pereunt, pro eo quod dilectionem veritatis non receperunt, ut salvi ieront; et ideo mittet illis Deus operationem erroris, ut credant mendacio, et iudicentur omnes qui non crediderunt veritati, sed consenserunt iniquitati" (2 Thess 2,3-11). Per istum refugam, per istum qui se extollit supra omne quod dicitur Deus, aut quod colitur, videtur mihi populum Israelitarum carnalium putaturum implen istam prophetiam qua dictum est, Salvos nos fac, Domine Deus noster, et congreganos de Gentibus; quod illo duce, velut in conspectu inimicorum suorum visibilium, qui eos visibiliter captivaverant, habituri sint visibilem gloriam.

Sic credent mendacio, quia dilectionem veritatis non receperunt, ut non bona carnalia, sed spiritualia concupiscerent. Sic enim a diabolo decepti sunt, ut occiderent Christum, quando dixerunt, "Si dimittimus eum sic, omnes credent in eum, et venient Romani, et tollent nostrum et locum et gentem": quando "Caiphas unus ex ipsis, eum esset pontifex anni illius, dixit eis, Vos nescitis quidquam, nec cogitatis quia expedit nobis ut moriatur unus homo pro populo, et non tota gens pereat. Hoc autem." sicut Evangelista intellexit, "non a seipso dixit, sed eum esset pontifex anni illius, prophetavit quia Iesus moriturus erat pro gente; et non tantum pro gente", id est, pro ovibus quae perierant domus Israel, "sed ut filios Dei quieront dispersi, congregaret in unum" (lo 11,48-52).
Benignity of divine providence

Before Israel as well as those of the Gentiles, the devil had captivated them. Once the yoke of the devil's domination is broken, in the presence of the evil spirits, who had captivated them, they cry out to be saved and perfected eternally with this prophetic voice: Save us, Lord, our God, and gather us from among the nations. For this reason, so that, based on your greed for food, you arrogantly rush against those who are in danger due to boredom. Recognize that this was given to you too, and it was not given to you because of your pretty face. What do you have that you haven't received? Recognizing this and finding yourself in danger from this vice and lukewarmness, do as follows: And they cried to the Lord when they were troubled, and he delivered them from their needs. And since the lukewarmness came from not delighting, he sent his word, and healed them. See what evil boredom brings with it, see why it half delivers Him to whom the bored cries out. He sent his word, and healed them and delivered them. Where from? Not from error, not from hunger, not from the difficulty of overcoming sins, but from their depravity. Depravity or corruption of the mind consists in becoming bored with what is pleasant. Taita talk about the fourth temptation, in which we are all in danger, since we are all in the ship; some work, others are transported; However, we were all in danger at the same time in the storm and we were all saved when we arrived at the port. Waters often symbolize people, as the Apocalypse of Saint John attests, ñeque hinc alíqua infletis arrogantia, et avidus cibi, in eos qui annoying periclitantur superbe insilías. Intellige etiam tibi praestitum esse hoc, non a te tibi esse. Quid enim habes quod non accepisti? (1 Cor 4:7). Hoc ergo intelligens, et hoc vitio atque languore periclitans, fac quod sequitur: Et exclamaverunt ad Dominum, cum tribularentur, et de necessitatibus eorum liberavit eos. Et quia languor erat non delectan: Misit verbum suum, et sanavit eos. Vide quid mali habeat fastidium; vide unde liberat ille, ad quem clamat fastidiens. Misit verbum suum, et sanavit eos: et eripuit eos. Where? Non de errore, non de fame, non de difficultate vincendi peccata, sed de corruptela eorum. Quaedam corruptela mentís est, annoying quod dulce est.

for there, where the apostle asks: "What are the waters?" The answer is: The people. Then those who traffic in the immense waters will see the works of God and his wonders in the deep. What is deeper than human hearts? There originate the winds and storms of seditions and dissensions that disturb the ship. And what is done in them? God wanting the captains and passengers to cry out to Him: He said, and the storm wind took hold. What does it mean to take hold? It remained, it endured, it still disturbs, it still lashes out, it rages and does not pass. So he said, or spoke, and the wind of the storm took hold. And what did this stormy wind do? And its waves became rough. They ascend to the heavens, hearing; and they go down to the abysses, fearing. They rise to the heavens and descend to the abysses. Outside there are struggles, inside fears. His soul was consumed by dangers. They were disturbed and staggered like a drunk. Those who sit at the helm and those who faithfully love the ship perceive what I say: They were troubled and staggered like a drunk. Certainly when they speak, when they read, when they expound, they seem wise, but woe to the storm! Well he says: And all his knowledge vanished. Sometimes all human advice is missing. Wherever one turns, the wind rages, the storm rages, the arms fail, the captains do not see at all where to direct the bow, with what wave the side will be swept, where the driven ship will be dragged, how it will be supported so that it does not perish among the rocks. your needs. And he commanded the storm, and it changed into a breeze. It did not remain a storm, but became a breeze. And the waves of the sea fell silent. Hear on this matter the voice of a certain experienced, humiliated and saved helmsman: I do not want, he says, brothers, for you to ignore my tribulation in Asia, since I was burdened excessively beyond my strength, in such a way, he says, that it caused me boredom to the point of living. Here I see all your knowledge vanished. And? Should I abandon those who were fainting? Did they not fail so that he could find glory by being with them? What's next? But I had the answer of death within myself, so that I should not trust in myself, but in God, who raises the dead. And he sent the storm, and it became a breeze. Those from whom all their wisdom had vanished had already had a response of death from themselves and with them. And the waves of the sea fell silent. And they rejoiced, because they were silent, and he led them to the port of his will. Praise the Lord for his mercies. In every place, in every part, praise the Lord completely; not our merits, nor our strength, nor our wisdom, but his mercies. Be loved in all our liberation who is invoked in all our works. Let the people and the elders, the traffickers and the helmsmen, praise him and exalt him. What did he do in this congregation, in this Church? What did he establish? Where did you get it from? What did he give you? Resist the proud and give grace to the humble. To the proud, that is, to the first Jewish people, proud and conceited to be from the lineage of Abraham and to have received the oracles of God. But these things did not serve them for health, but rather for puffing up their hearts, and therefore rather for swelling than for greatness. What did God do by resisting the proud and giving grace to the humble, by cutting off the branches for pride and grafting the wild olive tree for humility? What did God do? Hear these two things; first, how God resists the proud; then, how he gives grace to the humble. He turned the rivers into a desert. There the waters flowed, the prophecies flowed. Why don't you find prophets among the Jews now? He turned the rivers into a desert, and the springs of water into dryness. He turned the rivers into a desert. Say, then, with Psalm 73:9: There is no longer a prophet and he will not know us from now on. He turned the rivers into a desert; and the springs of water, in dryness; and the fruitful land, in salobreña. You ask there for the faith of Christ, for the prophets, for the priest, for the sacrifice, for the temple, and you do not find them. And why this? Because he turned the rivers into a desert; and the springs of water, in dryness; and the fruitful land, in salt mines. As? For what reason? Because of the evil of those who live in it. See how he resists the proud. Hear how he gives grace to the humble: He turned the deserts into pools of water, and the land without water into springs of water. And he made the hungry dwell there. in hac Ecclesia? quid constituit? unde illam eruit? quid ei praestitit? Quemadmodum superbis restitit, humilibus gratiam dedit (Iac 4,6): superbis, scilicet primo populo Iudaeorum, arroganti et extoüenti se de genere Abrahae, et quod illi genti sint credita eloquia Dei (Rom 3,2). Non eis haec valebant ad sanitatem, sed ad exaltationem cordis, ad tumorem potius quam ad magnitudeinem. Quid ergo fecit Deus, superbis resistens, humilibus dans gratiam; natural branches propter superbiam amputans, oleastrum propter humilitatem inserens? (ib. 11,17-24) quid fecit Deus? Audite haec duo: Deus primo quemadmodum superbis resista!, deinde quemadmodum humilibus det gratiam. Posuit illuminates in desertum.

Currebant ibi aquae, currebant prophetiae: quaere moda apud ludaeos prophetam, non invenís. "Posuit" enim "illuminates in desertum, et exitus aquarum in sitim. Posuit illuminates in desertum." Dicant, "Iam non est propheta, et nos non cognoscet adhuc" (Ps 73,9). "Posuit illuminates in desertum, et exitus aquarum in sitim, terram fructiferam in salinas." Quaeris ibi fidem Christi, non invenís; quaeris prophetam, non invenís; quaeris priestem, non invenís, quaeris sacrificium, non invenís; quaeris templum, non invenís. Quare hoc? Quia, "Posuit illuminates in desertum, et exitus aquarum in sitim; terram fructiferam in salinas." Well, what merit? "A malitia inhabitantium in ea". Ecce quomodo superbis resistit: audi quomodo humilibus det gratiam. "Posuit desertum in stagna aqua-

As it was said to Him: You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek, you seek the sacrifice among the Jews, and you do not find it according to the order of Aaron, because he turned the rivers into a desert; You look for him according to the order of Melchizedek, and you do not find him in them, but he sacrifices himself throughout the world in the Church. From the rising of the sun until the setting of the sun the name of the Lord is praised, God says to those for whom he turned the rivers into a desert: I do not love you nor will I receive a sacrifice at your hands, because from the rising of the sun until the setting of the sun a pure sacrifice is offered in my name. Where all the sacrifices were unclean, when all the people were desert, when they were uncultured, when they were brackish, now there are fountains there, there are rivers there, there are pools of water there, there are springs of water there. Then he resisted the proud and gave grace to the humble. He established the hungry there, for the poor will eat and be satisfied. And they built a habitable city. Now we live in hope, because he who hears me, says the Lord, will live in hope. And they built a habitable city. And they sowed fields, and planted vineyards, and harvested wheat fruit. Faced with this fruit, the worker rejoices, saying: I am not looking for the gift or what I gave, but I ask for the fruit. And he blessed them, and they multiplied exceedingly and their donkeys did not decrease. This persists: God's foundation remains solid, because the Lord knows the saints. In the Church, pedestrians are simply called donkeys and beasts, but useful ones; not with much tum, et terram sine aqua in exitus aquarum. Et habitare fecit illic esurientes".
