science, but full of faith. Then he blessed both the spiritual and the carnal; and he multiplied them exceedingly, and their donkeys did not decrease. 14 [v.39-42]. And they were reduced to few and mistreated. Where did this contrast or deviation come from? From within, because the small number came from us, but they were not from us. That is why he speaks of them as those he previously spoke of so that they may be distinguished perceptively, because he speaks as of the same ones because of the common sacraments. They belong, then, to the people of God, if not by virtue, certainly by the appearance of piety. We have heard the Apostle say about them: In the last times sinister days will come, because there will be selfish men, lovers of themselves. The first evil is being selfish, that is, pleasing oneself. If only they would displease themselves and please God! Oh that they would cry out in difficulties to be delivered from needs! But by boasting excessively about themselves, they were reduced to few. It is evident, brothers, that all those who distance themselves from unity become few. They are many, but in unity, as long as they do not deviate from it; but as soon as the multitude of unity begins not to belong to them, they are few in heresy or schism. And they were reduced to few and mistreated by the tribulation of evils and the dollar. The princes were despised, for they were rejected by the Church of God. Because they wanted to be princes, they were mainly despised, and became tasteless salt, which was thrown out, and for this reason was trampled by men. Princes were despised and led down paths bulantia, sed utilia; non multum learned, sed fide plena. Ergo et spirituales et carnales benedixit eos, et multiplicati sunt nimis, et iumenta eorum non sunt deminuta. 14 [v.39-42]. Et pauci facti sunt, et vexati sunt. Unde hoc, transverse? Imo internal. Ut enim pauci ieront, ex nobis exierunt, sed non erant ex nobis. Ideo autem tanquam de his dicit, de quibus antea loquebantur, ut cum intellectu discernantur; quia tanquam de hisdem loquitur, propter communia Sacramenta. Primum malum, seipsos lovers; utique sibi pleasants.

Utinam sibi displicerent, et Deo pleasurerent; utinam in difficultatibus exclamarent, et a necessitatibus liberaentur. Sed multum de se praesumentes, pauci facti sunt. inaccessible and not by the way. What does it mean for them to be excluded? Let those tested with the divine word appear, let them stand out. For, when heretics are answered out of necessity, Catholics are usefully edified. This feeling was clearly explained to him by the apostle Saint Paul when he said: It is fitting that there be heresies so that those who are tested may be manifested in you. It is convenient that there are seductive bulls so that those proven as silver appear, that is, they are excluded. What does tested as silver mean? Congregado taurorum, id est cervicatorum et superborum; congregatio taurorum inter vaccas populorum. Vaccas dicit seductiles animas, quae facile consentiunt seductoribus tauris. Sed quare hoc?

Ut exclude hi qui probad sunt argento (Ps 67.31). Quid est, ut excludantur? Ut appareant, ut emineant illi qui sunt ptobati in eloquio Dei. Cum enim respondertur haereticis ex necessitate, aedificantur Catholici ex utilitate. Hanc sententiam plañe Paulus expressit: "Oportet enim", inquit, "haereses esse, ut probati manifesti fiant in vobis" (1 Cor 11,19). Therefore, see that it was not a trivial thing to say that princes, that is, bulls, were despised. Why were they despised? Because they announced other things. What does "they were despised" mean? They were anathematized. If anyone evangelizes to you anything other than what you received, let him be anathema. And what is more despicable than vanished or distorted salt, which is thrown out and trampled underfoot? See if they are not princes, listen to Paul himself: If I or an angel from heaven evangelize to you anything other than what you received, let it be anathema. They are princes, they are doctors, they are great, they are precious stones. What more do you have to say? Are they angels too? Certainly, because the devil himself is an angel fallen from heaven, and yet if an angel from heaven evangelizes you, denies what you received, let him be anathema. Then the princes were despised, And he helped the poor in their need. What is this, brothers? Were the princes despised and the poor helped? The proud were rejected and the poor were protected. He did this, and, by doing this, he helped the poor man in his destitution. He is a beggar who, without attributing anything to himself, expects everything from the mercy of God and knocks daily at the door of the Lord, and, having his eyes fixed on the ground, hurting his chest, and trembling and finding himself naked, he knocks so that it will be opened. God helps in a special way this beggar, this poor man, this humble one, even in the disintegration of the heretics, because they were reduced to a few and mistreated and taken to inaccessible places and not along the road. Anyway, what did he do to help the poor man? What made these diminished deceived, mistreated and reduced to few? And he increased families like sheep. Aliud annuntiantes. Quid sunt contempti? Anathematizati. Quisquís enim vobis annuntiaverit praeterquam quod accepistis, anathema sit. Quid tam contemptum quam sal infatuatus, qui foras proiectus conculcatur? Et videte si non principes sunt; ipsum Paulum audite: Hacet si nos, aut angelus de cáelo evangelizaverit vobis praeterquam quod accepistis, anathema sit (Gal 1,8.9). Principes sunt, docti sunt, magni sunt, lapides pretiosi sunt. Quid adhuc dicturus is; numquid angelí sunt? Et tamen, "etsi angelus de cáelo vobis annuntiaverit praeterquam quod accepistis, anathema sit": quia et ipse diabolus angelus de cáelo lapsus est.

"Effusus est" ergo "contemptus super principes. Et adiuvit paupetem a mendicitate." Quid est hoc, fratres, Contempti sunt principes, et adiutus est pauper? Abiecti sunt superbi, et instructus est humilis. Hoc fecit, et hoc making adiuvit pauperem a mendicitate. Mendicus est ille, nihil sibi tribuens, totum of mercy Dei exspectans; ante ianuam Dominicam quotidie clamat, pulsans ut aperiatur ei, nudus et tremens ut veStiatur, oculos in terram deiiciens, et pectus tundens. Istum mendicum, hunc pauperem, hunc humilem adiuvit Deus plurimum, etiam de ipsa sepatatione haereticorum; Quia pauci facti sunt, et vexati sunt, et seducti in invio et non in via. Denique quid posts ex illis deminutis, seductis, paucis factis, vexatís, in adiuto paupete quid fit? And posit sicut your families. Quasi unum pauperem et unum mendicum intelligebas, de quo

You believed that it was spoken of as a poor man, a single beggar, of whom it was said: And he helped the poor man in need; but this poor person is many heads of families, this poor person is an immense people, just as a church, a town, a family, a sheep, are many churches. These are great mysteries and great sacraments. How deep they are and how full of secrets they are! The more hidden they are, the sweeter they are found. Then the upright will see it and rejoice. And all iniquity will dine on his mouth. The charlatan iniquity that speaks without sense against unity, forced to manifest the truth, will, convinced, close its mouth. 15 [v. 43]. Who is the wise one who keeps these things and understands the mercies of the Lord? See how the psalm concludes: Who is the wise one who keeps these things? What things must the wise man keep? That is, if he is poor, he keeps them; If he is not rich, that is, if he is not arrogant, if he is not conceited, keep these things. Why do you keep these things? For he will understand the mercies of the Lord; not his merits, his own strength, his own power, but the mercies of the Lord, who guided the wanderer and fed the needy along the way; who freed him who fought against the opposition of sins and released him who was bound with the chains of custom; who restored with the medicine of his word those who, tired of the word of God, are about to die from boredom; that led to the port, calming the sea, which was in danger between the turbulent and dangerous storms; that, finally, he established him in that town in which he gives grace to the humble, and not in the other one in which he resists the proud; and he made it his own, so that, remaining within, it might magnify itself, not so that, coming out, it would say, Et adiuvit pauperem a mendicitate: pauper istemulae familiae sunt, pauper istemulae plebes sunt; Multae Ecclesiae an Ecclesia, a plebs, a family, an ovis est. And posit sicut your families. Magna mysteria ista, magna sacramenta, quam profound, plena mysteriorum; quam dulciter inventa, quia diu latentia. Ergo, Videbunt redi, et iucundabuntur; et omnis iniquitas oppilabit os suum. Iniquitas illa garriens contra unitatem, et cogens manifest! veritatem, convicta oppilabit os suum. 15 [v.43]. "Quis sapiens? et custodiet haec, et intelliget miserationes Domini."

Videte quo fine clausit: "Quis sapiens? et custodiet haec." Et quid custoditurus est sapiens? Id est, si pauper sit, custodit; si non sit dives, id est, non sit superbus, non sit inflatus, custodit haec. Quare enim custodit haec, Quia intelliget miserationes Domini: non merita sua, non vires suas, non potentiam suam; sed miserationes Domini, qui errantem et egentem in viam deduxit et pavit; qui pugnantem adversus difficultatem peccatorum, et colligatum vinculis consuetudinis solvit et liberavit; qui fastidientem verbum Dei, et taedio quodam penis morientem, missa medica verbi sui recreavit; qui periclitantem Inter naufraga et procellosa discrimina, mari plaqueto ad portum perduxit: qui eum denique constituit in eo populo, ubi humilibus dat gratiam, non in illo ubi superbis resistit; et fecit eum suum, ut intus manens multiplicaretur, non

I will sing and salmear; arise, my glory; and in this: I will sing and praise in my glory. There it was said: Arise, so that people could sing and praise in it. It is also said there: Because your mercy has been magnified to the heavens, or as others translated: it was exalted, and here it is said: Because your mercy is greater than the heavens. It was said, then, that there she was exalted to the heavens, giving us to understand that she was in the heavens; and this is what he meant here when he wrote about or greater than the heavens. Also in Psalm 59 it is written: I will rejoice and divide Shechem; and here: I will exalt myself and divide Shechem. In which it is demonstrated that by what was symbolized in the division of Shechem the future event was predicted after the exaltation of the Lord; and also that that joy was due to this exaltation, so that he might rejoice because he is exalted. Therefore he says in another place: You changed my mourning into joy; You tore my coat and girded me with joy. It is also said in Psalm 59: And Ephraim is the strength of my head; here: And Efrcám is the protection of my head. Apo y ando constitutes strength, that is, supporting makes us strong, bearing fruit in us. For Ephraim means fruitfulness. Support or welcome can refer either to Christ, when we welcome Him, or to us, when He, who is the Head of the Church, welcomes us. In short, it is identical to say there: To those who trouble us, and here: to our enemies, because they are the same. 2. This psalm rightly warns us to understand, according to prophecy, the titles that are recorded as historical, according to the sixth dicitur, Cantabo, et psallam; exsurge, gloria mea; in isto autem, Cantabo et psallam in gloria mea. Ad hoc enim dictum est illic, Exsurge, ut in illa cantoretur et psalleretur. item ibi, "Quoniam magnificara est usque ad caelos tua mercy"; vef, sicut alii interpretati sunt, "elevata est": hic autem, "Quoniam magna est super cáelolos mercy tua." Ideo enim magnificata est usque ad cáelos, ut magna sit in caelis; hoc enim voluit dicere, super caelos. item in quinquagesimo nono, Laetabor, et dividam Sichimam: hic autem, Exaltabor, et dividam Sichimam. Ubi ostenditur quod de dividenda Sichima significatum est, post Domini exaltationem praedictum futurum, et illam laetitiam ad hanc exaltationem pertinere; ut ideo laetetur, quia exaltatur.

Unde alibi dicit, "Convertisti luctum meum in gaudium mihi; conscidisti saccum meum, et accinxisti me laetitia" (Ps 29,12). item ibi, "Et Ephraem fortitudo capitis mei": hic autem, "Et Ephraem susceptio capitis mei." Suscipiendo enim fit fortitudo, id est, suscipiendo fortes facit, fructificans in nobis: interpretatur enim Ephraem Fructificatio. Susceptio autem ad utrumque referri potest, sive cum suscipimus Christum, sive cum ipse nos suscipit, qui est caput Ecclesiae. Et quod ibi ait, tributantes nos; hic autem, inimicos us: utique iidem ipsi sunt. 2. Admonemur sane isto psalmo, eos titles qui tanquam de historia positi sunt, rectissime fieri ut secundum prophetiam intelligamus,

We notice that the psalms are inscribed. For what could be more contrary to history than what is recorded in the title of Psalm 56, which reads: Mesopotamia, Syria and Syria of Shobal, and when Joab returned he killed twelve thousand in the valley of the salt marshes? Because, except for what was recorded: for the inscription of the title, for David and for the end, the other things are so diverse in the two psalms, that the first reveals David's humiliation, and the second his strength; the first the escape, the second the victories. And yet, from the last parts of these two psalms, of which the titles are so diverse, this psalm 107 is composed. Therefore it is indicated that both flow together to mean something special, not as regards the historical appearance, but as regards the sublimity of the prophecy, when both endings come together, forming a single psalm, whose title: Psalm Song for David, is unlike the other two, apart from what is also here. It was recorded: for David. As God, as the Epistle to the Hebrews declares, spoke in times past many times and in many ways to the patriarchs through the prophets, so he also spoke through Him who sent that the words of the prophets might be fulfilled, for all the promises of God, in Him, in Jesus Christ, have been yes (that is, fulfilled). secundum quod videmus psalmos esse conscripts. Quid enim tam díversum secundum historiam, quam id quod est in titulo quinquagesimi sexti, "In fínem, ne corrumpas; ipsi David, in tituli inscriptionem, cum fugeret a facie Saül in speluncam": et in titulo quinquagesimi noni, "In finem, his qui immutabuntur, in tituli inscriptionem, ipsi David, in doctrinam, cum succendit Mesopotamiam, Syriam, et Syriam Sobal, et convertit Ioab, et percussit in valle salinarum duodecim millia?" Nam praetet id quod positum est, "In tituli inscriptionem", et, "ipsi David", et, "in finem"; caeteta ita divetsa sunt, ut Ole habeat humilitatem David, iste fortitudinem; lie fugam, these victories.

Et tamen ex istorum duorum postetioribus partibus, quorum tam diversi tituli sunt, psalmus iste componitur. Ubi significatur ad unum aliquid concurrere utrumque, non superficial historiae, sed akitudine prophetiae, copulatis utriusque finibus in hoc uno, cuius est titulus, Canticum psalmi, ipsi David; neuter ílli titulo similis, ptaeter quod hic etiam positum est, ipsi David. Quoniam multis pattibus et multis modis, sicut ad Hebtaeos Epistle loquitur, olim Deus locutus est Patribus per Prophetas (Hebr 1,1); eum tamen locutus est quem misit postea, ut complerentur eloquia Prophetarum: Quolquot enim promissiones Dei, in illo etiam (2 Cor 1,20). 1. Whoever faithfully reads the Acts of the Apostles, recognizes that this psalm speaks of Christ, since this is evident where it was prophesied about Judas, the one who betrayed Christ, what the psalm recorded: Let his days be few and another receive his episcopate, Matthias being, therefore, ordained in place of Judas and counted the twelfth in the number of the apostles. But, if we try to understand from that one man everything that was said here regarding evil, in no way or hardly will the essence of the narrative be adapted. However, it seems to me that everything can be clarified more clearly if we understand the genus of bad men, that is, of the Jews, ungrateful and enemies of Christ. For just as many things are said that seem to refer properly to the apostle Saint Peter, and yet would not be understood perfectly if they did not refer to the Church, which it is recognized that he figuratively represents due to the primacy he had over the disciples, as it is said: I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven, and also taking into account other similar testimonies, in the same way, Judas symbolizes, in a certain way, the Jews, enemies of Christ, who then hated, and now, remaining this class of men, they also hate him for the continuation of his impiety. Of this class of men and of this people we can understand very perfectly not only the things that we read clearly about them in this psalm, but also

those that are properly and expressly said of Judas, such as what I commemorated: Let his days be few and another receive his episcopacy. Which will be declared, God helping us, when we reach the verses, which are to be treated in order. 2 {v.2}. The psalm begins like this: O God, do not silence my praise, for the mouth of the sinner and the traitor is opened against me. By this he demonstrates that the reproach uttered by the sinner and the traitor is false, and the praise that God proclaims is true. God is true, but every man is a liar, because there is no true man unless God speaks in him. The supreme praise is that of the only begotten Son of God, by which that which is is said to be the only begotten Son of God. This was not declared, but was hidden under the apparent weakness when the mouth of the sinner and the traitor was opened against Him; and it was opened because its power was hidden. Hence the psalmist says: The mouth of the traitor was opened, because the hatred that he maliciously concealed burst forth into a voice. This is said more clearly in the following verses. 3 {v.3]. They spoke against me with a deceitful tongue. This happened when with deceitful flattery they praised him as a good Teacher. Therefore it is said in another place: And those who praised me conspired against me. And as they later burst out crying: Crucify, crucify!, he then added: And they surrounded me with words of hate. But since they spoke with a deceitful tongue words of love, not hate, that is why the psalmist said against me, because they did this by lying. But then he writes in words, not of devious and malicious love, but of manifest hatred: verum etiam illa quae proprie de ipso luda dicuntur expressius; sicuti est quod commemoravi, Fiant dies eius pauci, et episcopatum eius accipiat alter. Quod apparebit, adiuvante Domino, cum ad eos versus tractandi ordine venerimus. 2 [v.2}. Incipit ergo ita Psalmus: Deus laudem meam ne tacueris; Quia os peccatoris et os dolosi super me apertum est. Unde apparet et falsem esse vituperationem quam non tacet peccator et dolosus, et veram esse laudem quam non tacet Deus. Deus enim verax, omnis autem homo mendax (Rom 3,4); quia non est homo verax, nisi in quo loquitur Deus. Hoc autem non apparebat, sed apparente infirmitate eius latebat, cum os peccatoris et os dolosi super eum apertum est; et ideo illud apertum est, quia operta virtus huius Fuit.

As the pious love Christ freely, so the wicked hate him without cause; For as truth by itself does not demand any useful end from the most good men outside of itself, so neither does iniquity demand it from the most perverse men. For this reason it was also said in writings of worldly authors of a certain terrible man: Rather he was evil and cruel without reason, 4 [v.4]. Instead of loving me, they insulted me. There are six differences that exist in this way of acting, which by simply mentioning them can be very easily seen: returning goods for evils, not returning evils for evils, returning goods for goods, returning evils for evils, not returning goods for goods and returning evils for goods. The first two ways of acting are typical of the good, and the first of them is the best; The last two are typical of the bad ones, and the last of them is the worst; The two intermediate ones are typical of the somewhat medium ones, but the first of them is closer to the good ones and the second one is closer to the bad ones. This should be observed in Holy Scripture. The same Lord returns goods for evils, who justifies the wicked and who, hanging from the cross, said: Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they do, whose example Saint Stephen followed when, while kneeling, he prayed for those who were stoning him, saying: Lord, do not impute this crime to them. To this way of acting belongs that precept: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you and pray for those who persecute you. The apostle Saint Paul says that evil should not be returned for mal tionis, sed aperti odii circumdederunt me, et expugnaverunt me gratis. Sicut autem pii gratis amant Christum, sic impii gratis oderunt; quia sicut veritas nullo extra eam proposito commodo propter seipsam expetitur ab optimis, ita iniquitas a pessimis. Unde et apud auctores saecularium litterarum dictum est de quodam písimo: Gratuito potius malus atque crudelis erat (SALLUST., De Bello Catil.). 4 [v.4]. Pro eo, inquit, ut diligerent me, detrahebant mihi. The last one, that there is no worse thing, belongs to those of whom this psalm speaks: Instead of loving me, they reviled me. The two intermediate ones, which we said belonged to the somewhat mediocre men, are such that the first of them, which consists of returning goods for goods, is carried out by the good, and also by the good and bad mediocre ones. That is why the Lord does not prohibit this way of acting, but he does not want only his disciples to act this way, because he wants to lead them to greater things, and that is why he tells them: If you love those who love you, that is, if you return goods for goods, what reward will you have? That is, what extraordinary thing do you do? Don't publicans also do this? He wants them to do this and much more; That is, they not only love their friends, but also their enemies. Finally, remembering the patience of Christ, who, as if awakened, as happened in the ship, calms the disturbance and the storm of our hearts, let us pray, with the spirit now appeased and calmed, for our detractors so that we can say with certainty: Forgive us, as we forgive. Sed Saulus rememberatus est faceré Misericordiam; et qui mane rapiebat, ad vesperum divisit escás (Gen 49,27): et ipse compunctus corde, ut etiam in illo ipsi persequerentur inopem, volentes mortificare compunctum corde. Hoc quippe oderant in Paulo apostólo, quia compunctus corde praedicabat quem fuet ante persecutus. Inopem quippe et mendicum et compunctum corde in membris suis et ipse ut mortify, persequens, audivit de cáelo, Saule, Saule, quid me persequeris? et factus compunctus corde, coepit talia pati, qualia faciebat compunctis corde (Act 9,1-24). 20 [v.18}. Deinde sequitur Psalmus: Et dilexit maledictionem, el veniet ei. Quanquam et ludas maledictionem dilexerit, et furando de loculis, et Dominum vendendo atque tradendo; tamen apertius populus ille dilexit maledictionem, quando dixit: Sanguis eius super nos et super

filios nostros (Mt 27,25). Et noluit benedictionem, et elongabitur ab eo. Et ludas quidem, quia Christum noluit, in quo est aeterna benedictio; sed apertius noluit benedictionem populus Iudaeorum, cui dixit ille illuminatus a Domino: Numquid et vos vultis discipuli eius fieri? Et noluit benedictionem, et pro maledicto habuit; et respondit, Tu sis discipulus eius (lo 9,27 et 28): et longe facta est ab eo benedictio, quia transitum fecit ad Gentes. And induit maledictionem sicut vestimentum: sive ludas, sive ille populus. Et intravit sicut aqua in interiora eius. Ergo et foris et intus; foris sicut vestimentum, intus sicut aqua: quoniam in eius incidit ¡udicium, qui potest et cotpus et anímam occidere in gehenna (Mt 10,28); corpus foris, animam intus. Et sicut oleum in ossibus eius. Ostendit eum cum delectatione malefacere, et comparare sibi maledictionem, hoc est, poenam aeternam; quia benedictio vita aeterna est. Modo quippe malefacta delectant, sicut aqua in interiora, et sicut oleum in ossibus; sed ideo maledictio vocatur, quia talibus Deus storm praedixit. Tanquam in ossibus autem oleum est maledictio, cum homines inde se fortes putant, quia licet eis mala tanquam impune committere. 21 {v.19}. Fiat et sicut vestimentum quo operitur. Cum superius iam dixerit de vestimento, quid est quod repetit? An quia dixerat, Induit maledictionem sicut vestimentum, differt ab eo vestimentum quo non induitur, sed operitur? Induitur enim quisque tunic, operitur pallio. Et quid est hoc, nisi etiam in conspecm hominum de iniquitate gloriari? et
Ennarrations on the Psalms

boast about iniquity before men? And as a belt with which he always girds himself. Men mainly gird themselves in order to be freer to work, and thus the dress does not embarrass them with the folds. Then he who does not attack with a sudden evil, but rather a calculated one, is girded with the curse, learning in this way to do evil, so that he is always prepared. For this reason it says here: And as a belt with which he always girds himself. 22 fv.20}. This is the work before the Lord of those who speak evil of me. He did not say "this is his reward", but his work, because it is evident that by the clothing, the wrapping, the water, the oil and the girdle he declared those works with which the eternal curse is purchased. Therefore it is not of one Judas, but of many, of whom he says: This is the work before the Lord of those who speak evil of me. Although he could use the plural number for the singular, as when, after Herod died, it was said by the angel: Those who sought to kill the Child died. But who most insults Christ before the Lord but those who discredit the very words of the Lord, saying that He is not the one to whom the law of the Lord and the prophets prophesied? And those who speak say evil against my life, denying that He was able to resurrect when He wanted, even though He said: I have power to give up my life, and power to take it again. 23 [v.21]. And you, Lord, Lord, work with me. Some believed that mercy should be implied, others added the word; but the most select codices write the following: And you, Lord, Lord, work with me for your name. Therefore there is no sicut zona, inquit qua semper praecingitur. Máxime homines ideo praecinguntur, ut ad operandum sint aptioies, ne vestís sinibus praepedianmr. Ergo maledictione se praecingit, qui malum non repentinum, sed dispositum aggredítur, et ita discit malefacere, ut semper paratus sit: unde et hic ait, Et sicut zona qua semper praecingitur. 22 [v.20]. Hoc opus eorum qui detrahunt mihi apud Dominum. Non dixit, merces eorum; sed, opus eorum: manifestum est enim quod indumento, et opertorio, et aqua, et oleo, et zona, ipsa opeta desctibebat quibus aeterna maledictio comparatur. Non ergo est unus ludas, sed multi, de quibus dicitur, Hoc opus eorum qui ietrahtmt mihi apud Dominum. Quanquam et pluralís numetus poní potuit pro numero singulari; sicut, Herode mortuo, dictum est ab angelo: Mortui sunt qui quaerebant animam pueri (Mt 2,20).

Sed qui magis detrahunt Christo apud Dominum, nisi illi qui ipsis verbis Domini detrahunt, dicentes non esse ipsum quem Lex Domini et Prophetae praenuntiarunt? Et qui loquuntur, inquit, mala adversus animam meam: denying eum, cura voluisset, potuisse resurgere; cum dícat, Potestatem drool ponendi animam meam, et potestatem drool iterum sumendi eam (lo 10,18). 23 [and.211. Et tu, Domine, Domine, jac mecum. Quidam subaudiendam putaverunt misericordion, quidam vero et addiderunt; sed emendatiores codices sic habent: Et tu, Domine, Domine, jac mecum, propter nomen tuum. Unde sensus altior non est praetermittendus, ita dixisses
Imprecative prayer against the enemy

A more sublime meaning must be overlooked, and thus it must be understood that the Son said to the Father: Work with me, because the works of the Father are those of the Son. Therefore, even if we understand that it refers to mercy, since the psalm goes on to say: for your mercy is kind, yet because it did not say "work it in me" or "work it on me," or anything like that, but work it with me, we perfectly understand that the Father and the Son jointly work mercy in the vessels of mercy. Work with me can also be understood as "help me." We observe this in the ordinary way of speaking when we say of something that is on our side that works with us. The Father helps the Son through his form as a servant, insofar as God helps man. The Father is God of this man and Lord of this form of servant. Because the Son, as He is God, does not need help, since He is equally omnipotent with the Father, and for this reason He is also Man's helper. As the Father resurrects and gives life to the dead, so also the Son gives life to whomever he wills. And the Father does not resurrect some and the Son to others, or the Father in one way and the Son in another, since the Son acts the same and equally as the Father. For this reason, since the Son of God is Man, God raised him from the dead, that is, the Father, to whom he says in the psalm: Raise me and I will give to them. And since He is God, He Himself was resurrected, therefore He says: Destroy this temple, and in three days I will rebuild it. This was what he stated here, if anyone examines it carefully. We must bear in mind that He ordered the Scriptures to be diligently investigated, which testifies to Him, and not Pilium Patri, Fac mecum, quia eadem sunt opera Patris et Filii. Ubi etiamsi misericordiam intelligamus (sequitur enim, Quia suavis est misericordia tua), et ipsam quia non dixit, Fac in me; vel Fac super me; vel aliquid huiusmodi; sed ait, Fac mecum; bene intelligimus et Patrem et Filium simul faceré misericordion in vasa misericordiae (Rom 9:23). Potest hoc etiam sic intelligi: Fac mecum, id est, adiuva me. Quod in quotidiana loquendi consuetudine habemus, cum de aliqua re quae partibus nostris est, dicimus: Nobiscum facit. Pater quippe adiuvat Filium, in quantum Deus hominem, proptet formam servi: cui homini Deus, et cui formae servi etiam Dominus est Pater. Nam in forma Dei, Filius adiutorio non indiget; aequaliter enim cum Patre omnipotens est, ex quo et ipse adiutor est hominis.

Sicut enim Pater suscitat mortuos et vivificat, sic et Filius quos vult vivificat (lo 5,21): nec alios Pater, alios Filius, aut aliter Pater, aliter Filius; quia et eadem facit, et similiter. Unde in quantum homo est Filius Dei, Deus suscitavit illum a mortuis, hoc est Pater, cui dicit in Psalmis, Suscita me, et reddam illis (Ps 40,11): in quantum autem Deus est, etiam ipse se suscitavit; propter quod dicit, Solvite templum hoc, et triduo suscitabo illud (lo 2,19). Quod etiam hic significavit, si quis diligenter intendat: scrutari enim iussit Scripturas, quae testimonium perhibent de illo (ib. 5,39), non in superficial pertran-
Ennarrations on the Psalms

go through it lightly. He did not only say: You, Lord, Lord, work with me, but also you. What does it indicate to us and you but me and me? Not having said Lord once, but twice, saying: Lord, Lord, contains the affection of the one who prays, like that which was said: God, my God. As you add by your name after you have said work with me, remember grace. For by no preceding merit of works was human nature elevated to such sublime excellence that all together, the Word and the flesh, that is, God and man, are called the only begotten Son of God. This was done so that he who had created might seek, through what had not perished, what had perished; Therefore the psalm continues: For your mercy is kind. 24 [v.22}. Deliver me, for I am poor and needy. Destitution and poverty is the weakness, for which he was crucified. And my heart was troubled within me. This refers to what he says when the passion approaches: Sad is my soul until death. 25 [v.23]. Like a declining shadow, I was taken away. For this it meant death. As night is derived from the intensifying shadow, so death is derived from mortal flesh. Tossed like locusts. I think this should be understood more adequately from its members, that is, from its faithful. He preferred to say like the locusts and not "like the locust" to make it a little clearer, although many could have been understood under the singular, as happened when he said: He said or spoke, and the locust came; but it would be darker. Then they were shaken, that is, they escaped from the hands of the persecutors the faithful, of whom, siri. Non enim tantummodo ait, Tu, Domine, Domine, fac mecum; sed ait, Et tu. Quid est, Et tu, nisi quia et ego? Quod autem non semel Domine, sed repetens ait, Domine, Domine; habet in hoc orantis affectum: sicuti est, Deas, Deus meus (Ps 21,2). Quod vero, cum dixisset, Fac mecum, addidit, propter nomen tuum; gratiam commendavit. Nuüis enim operum meritis praecedentibus in tantam celsitudinem subvecta est humano natura, ut totum simul Verbum et caro, hoc est Deus et homo, unigenitus Filius Dei diceretur. Hoc autem factum est, ut ab illo qui creaverat, per id quod non perierat, id quod perierat quaereretur: unde et hic sequitur, Quia suavis est misericordia tua. 24 [v.22}. Libera me, quia egenus et pauper ego sum. Egestas et paupertas, infirmitas est, ex qua crucifixus est. Et cor meum conturbatum est intra me.

Hoc ad illud refertur, quod ait propinquante passione, Tristis est anima mea usque ai mortem (Mt 26,38). 25 [v.23]- Sicut umbra cum declinat, ablatus sum. Hoc ipsam mortem significavit. Sicut enim ex umbra declinante fit nox, sic ex mortali carne fit mors. Excussus sum sicut locustae. Hoc iam in membris eius, hoc est fidelibus eius, convenientius intelligi existimo. Quod ut aliquanto apertiusponeret, maluit dicere, sicut locustae, quam sicut locusta: quamvis et numero singulari possent accipi etiammultae, sicut illud est, Dixit, e\ venit locusta (Ps 104,34); sed esset obscurius. Excussi sunt ergo, id est,
Imprecative prayer against the enemy

Under the name of locusts, he wanted to make known either the crowd or that they moved from one place to another. 26 {v.24}. My knees became weak from fasting. We read that our Lord Jesus Christ fasted for forty days. But did that diet have such a great effect on Him that it weakened His knees? Or is this best understood from its members, that is, from its saints? And my flesh was exchanged for oil, that is, for spiritual grace. Hence Christ is called by chrism, since chrism is anointing. Then the flesh was changed for the better, not for the worse, by the oil, namely, resurrecting from the contumelia of death to the glory of immortality. Therefore, after having said: My knees were weak from fasting, which I believe symbolized those who seemed strong in their members, as if the bread with which they sustained themselves had disappeared from their presence, they fainted in their passion, until they came to deny him, as was manifested with Peter. But to confirm them, lest they fall completely by succumbing, he adds: and my flesh was exchanged for oil. In this way, when they fainted because of my death, I strengthened them with my resurrection and anointed them by sending them the Holy Spirit, which would not have descended on them if I had not turned away. For he had said: If I do not go, He will not be able to come; and the evangelist said: The Holy Spirit had not yet been given, because Jesus had not yet been glorified. His flesh had not yet been bartered. Whether the Holy Spirit is symbolized by water, considering ablution or irrigation; already by the oil, looking at the exaltation and the kindling of charity, it is not disfugati a persecutoribus fideles eius, quorum vel multitudinem mean voluit nomine locustarum, vel quod transilierunt de loco in locum. 26 [v.24]. Genua mea infirmata sunt a ieiunio. Legimus Dominum Christum quadraginta dierum habuisse ieiunium (Mt 4,2): sed tantumne valuit in eo illa inedia, ut genua eius infirmarentur? An et hoc in membris eius, hoc est sanctis eius, aptius intelligitur? Et caro mea immutata est propter oleum: propter gratiam spiritualem. Unde et Christus appellatur a chrismate: chrisma autem unctio est. Caro autem propter oleum non in deterius, sed in melius immutata est, hoc est, a mortis contumelia in gloriam immortalitatis exsurgens.

Cum ¡taque dixisset, Genua mea injirmata sunt a ieiunio, ubi significatum esse arbitror eos qui in membris eius fortes videbantur, tanquam praesentia pañis quo sustainbantur abstracta, in eius passione defecisse usque ad negationem, quae apparuit in Petro; tanquam ad eos confirmandos, ne succumbendo penitus caderent, Et caro mea, inquit, immutata est propter oleum, ut eos mea morte deficient, mea resurrectione firmarem, et misso Spiritu sancto ungerem, qui non ad eos venisset, nisi ego abiissem. Hoc enim dixerat, Non potest Ule vinore, nisi ego abiero (lo 16,7): et Evangelista dixit, Nondum erat Spiritus datus, quia lesus nondum fuet glorificatus (ib. 7,39). Nondum erat immutata caro eius. Sive autem per aquam propter ablutionem vel irrigationem, sive per oleum propter exsultationem et inflammationem charitatis, significctur Spiritus sanctus; no idea is a
Ennarrations on the Psalms

red of itself because the signs are diverse. The lamb and the lion are very different, and yet both symbolize Christ; the lion, for one thing, and the lamb, for another, and, yet, Christ is not different. The lamb is not strong, nor the lion innocent, and yet Christ is innocent as the lamb, and strong as the lion. Jesus Christ himself says through Isaiah: The spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me. 27 [v.25}. I became their reproach by dying on a cross. For Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us. They saw me, and shook their heads. They saw him hanging on the cross, but they did not see him resurrected; They saw him when his knees weakened, but not when he bartered his flesh. 28 [v. 26]. Help me, Lord, my God; save me according to your mercy. This can be applied to the whole, that is, both the Head and the Body; to the Head, by the form of a servant; to the Body, by the very nature of the servants. For in these he could say to God: Help me and save me, in the same ones in which he said to Saul: Why do you persecute me? In which he added: according to your mercy, free grace is implied, not due by works. 29 [v.27J. And know that this is your hand and that you, Lord, made it. He said, know for those who, being cruel, He prayed, since among those for whom He was considered a reproach, shaking their heads and mocking Him, were those who later believed in Him. Let those who attribute bodily form to God huseipso diversus, quia signa diverse sunt, learn. Multum enim diverse sunt etiam leo et agnus, et tamen utroque significatus est Christus. Leo propter aliud, agnus propter aliud; non tamen alius: quia nec fortis est agnus, nec innocens leo; Christus autem et innocens est ut agnus, et fortis ut leo. Dicit autem apud Isaiam ipse lesus Christus: Spiritus Domini super me, propter quod unxit me (Is 61,1). 27 [v.25]. Et ego factus sum opprobriitm Mis: per mortem crucis. Christus enim redeems us from maledicto Legis, factus pro nobis maledictum (Gal 3:13). Viderunt me, et movetmt capita sua. Quia viderunt pependisse, non viderunt resurrexisse; viderunt quando genua eius sunt infirmata, non viderunt quando es caro immutata. 28 [v.26]. Adiuva me, Domine Deus meus, salvum me fac secundum misericordiam tuam.

Hoc ad totum refetri potest, id est et ad caput, et ad Corpus: ad caput, propter formam servi; ad Corpus, propter ipsos servos. Potuit enim et in eis dicere Deo, "Adiuva me", et, "salvum me fac"; in quibus Saul said, "Why are you persecuting me?" (Acts 9,4). Quod autem addidit, "secundum misericordiam tuam"; gratuitous gratia commemoratur, non ex operum debito. 29 [v.27]. Et sciant quoniam manus tua haec, et tu, Domine, fecisti eam. De his dixit, sciant, pto quibus saevientíbus et oravit; Quia in eis quibus factus est opptobrium moventibus in eius illusionem capita sua, erant etiam hi qui in eum postea ctediderunt. Discant autem qui fotmam
Imprecative prayer against the enemy

It flows like the hands of God. Because if what he does he does it with his hands, did he perhaps make his own hands with his own hands? Then in what sense was it said here: And let them know that this is your hand and that you, Lord, made it? Let us understand, then, that the hand of God is Christ; Therefore it was said in another place: And the arm of the Lord, to whom has it been revealed? This hand existed, and it also made this one, because the Word existed in the beginning, and the Word was made flesh. It existed without time, as to divinity, and was made by Him from the seed of David according to the flesh. 30 [v. 28]. They will curse and you will bless. Therefore the false curse of the sons of men, who love vanity and seek lies, is useless. But the Lord, when he blesses, does what he says. Let those who rise up against me be confounded. They think that it is of some benefit to them to rise up against me; But, when I am exalted above the sky and my glory begins to be over the entire world, they will be confused. But your servant will rejoice. Being now at the right hand of the Father or now living in hope in his jubilant members in the midst of temptations; and after temptations, eternally in reality. 31 [v.29]- Those who speak evil of me should dress in modesty. That is, be ashamed of having spoken ill of me. This can be understood in a good sense; for example, when correcting itself. "Et operiantur sicut diploidem confusionem suam": And cover yourselves with confusion as with a double layer. Diplois means double pallium. Some Latin interpreters translated this verse as follows: Et operiantur sicut humani corporis Deo tribuunt, quomodo habeat Deus manum. Si enim quod facit, manu facit, numquid et ipsam manum suam manu facit? Quomodo ergo hic dictum est, Et sciant quoniam manus tua haec, et tu, Domine, fecisti eam? Intellígamus itaque manum Dei esse Christum: unde alibi dicitur, Et brachium Domini cui revelatum est? (Is 53,1). Haec manus et erat, et fecit eam; quia, in principle erat Verbum, et Verbum caro factum est (lo 1,1.14): et erat sine tempore secundum divinitatem, et factus est ei ex semine David secundum carnem (Rom 1,3). 30 [v.28], Maledicent Mi, et tu blesses. Vana est etgo et false maledictio filiorum hominum, diligentium vanitatem, et quaerentium mendacium (Ps 4,3); Deus autem cum benedicit, facit quod dicit. Qui insurgunt in me, confundantur.

Ut enim insurgant alíquid se adversus me proficere arbitrantur; sed cum exaltatus fuero super cáelos, ec esse coeperit super omnem terram gloria mea, confundentur. Servas autem tuus laetabitur: sive in dextera Patris, sive in membris suis laetantibus, et inter temptationes in spe, et post temptationes in aeternum. 31 [v.29]. Induantur qui detrahunt mihi divinorem: id est, seguirat eos detraxisse mihi. Sed hoc potest et in bonus accipi, dum corriguntur. Et operiantur sicut diploidem confusionem suam. Diplois duplex pallium est. Nam quídam etiam sic interpretati sunt istum versum: Et operiantur
Ennarrations on the Psalms

pallium duplex confusionem suam. It is understood that they are ashamed internally and externally, that is, before God and men. 32 [v. 30]. "Confitebor Domino nimis in ore meo": I will confess and praise the Lord with my mouth greatly. The word nimis, in the extreme, is usually applied ordinarily in Latin conversation, meaning more than it should; Contrary to it is the word parum, which means less than what is owed. But nimis is said in Greek agan, and in this verse it is not written agan, but sphodra. This was translated by our Latin interpreters sometimes as nimis, too much, and other times as valde, greatly. But if it is written nimis because it means valde, it can be applied to praise, because this confession means praise... Well, this is how the psalm continues: "Et in medio multorum laudabo eum": And in the midst of the crowd I will praise him. It is also said in another psalm: In the midst of the Church I will sing to you. Therefore, if the Church itself sings, which is the Body of Christ, how does the Church sing in the midst of the Church? So it is also here (and that is why it is asked): "If when the crowd praises, being members of Christ, because they are His members, He praises because they are His members, how does He praise in the midst of the crowd when, praising these members, He is said to praise? Does He praise in the midst of the multitude because He remains here in the Church until the consummation of the world, so that what He says in the midst of the multitude we understand in the sense that He is honored by these members? It is said that one thing is in the middle when it is to which the main honor is given. And if the heart is like the middle of the man, nothing is better understood than "in the hearts of the many (of the multitude) I will praise him." That is why he says sicut pallium duplex confusionem suam. [v.30].

Quod quídam nostri sic intetptetati sunt, ut pro eoponerent aliquando nimis, aliquando valde. Be si nimis pro eo quod est valde intelligatur, potest et in laude poni; nam et is confessio laudem significat. Ita enim sequitur: Et in medio multorum laudabo eum. Dicit etiam in alio psalmo, ln medio Ecclesiae cantabo te (Ps 21,23). Sed eum ipsa cantat Ecclesia, quae corpus est Christi, quomodo in medio Ecclesiae cantat Ecclesia? Ita et hic multi eum sint membra Christi, si eum ipsi laudant, ille laudat, quia membra sunt eius; quomodo in medio multorum laudat, quando ipsis multis laudantibus dicitur ipse laudare? An ideo laudat in medio multorum, quia eum Ecclesia sua est hic usque in consummationem saeculi (Mt 28,20); ut quod ait, in medio multorum, hoc accipiamus quod ab eisdem multis honoratur? In medio quippe esse dicitur, cui honor praecipuus exhibitiontur. Si autem cor est tanquam hominis medium; nihil melius intelligitur dictum, quam in cordibus multorum laudabo eum. Habitat enim Christus
The Messiah, king and eternal priest

with my mouth, that is, with the mouth of my Body, which is the Church. For with the heart one believes for righteousness and with the mouth one confesses for health. 33 [v. 31]. Because he stood at the right of the poor. Of Judas, who wanted to increase his wealth by selling Christ, it was said: And the devil be at his right. However, here it was written: "The Lord stood at the right hand of the poor," so that the Lord himself would be the wealth of the poor. He placed himself at the right of the poor not to multiply the years of life, which will someday end; nor to increase his money, or to make him robust in body, or temporally unharmed, but to save—he says—my soul from the persecutors. The soul is saved from the persecutors if it does not agree with them in evil; and he will not consent to them when the Lord places himself at the right hand of the poor so that he does not succumb through poverty, that is, through weakness or weakness. This help was given to the Body of Christ in all the holy martyrs.
[ELMESSIAH, KING AND PRIEST SERMON TO THE

1. As far as the Lord grants me, who made me a minister of his word and sacrament in order to serve you with the fatness of his mercy, I undertake as I can, with the help of Him who per fidem in cordibus nostris (Eph 3:17): et ideo ait, in ore meo, id est in ore corporis mei, quod est Ecclesia. Corde enim creditur ad iustitiam; pray autem confessio fit ad salutem (Rom 10:10). 33 [v.31]. Quia astitit a dextris pauperis. De luda dictum erat, Et diabolus stet a dextris eius; qui suas divitias augere voluit Christo vendito: hic autem Domínus astitit a dextris pauperis, ut divitiae pauperis sint ipse Dominus. Astitit quippe a dextris pauperis, non ut ei multiplícaret annos vitae quandoque finiendae, ñeque ut eius augeret pecuniam, aut eum faceret corporis viribus fortem, vel ad tempus incolumern; sed ut salvam faceret, inquit, a persequentibus animam meam. Salva fit autem a persequentibus anima, si non eis consentiatur ad malum; non eis autem consentitur, eum assistit Dominus a dextris pauperis, ne ipsa paupertate, id est ínfirmitate, suecumbat. Hoc adiutorium praestitum est corpori Christi in sanctis martyribus omnibus.

Perhaps this psalm also gives us something to know about this matter by which we can glimpse how Christ is the Son and Lord of David. Let us listen to him and study him; let us call with mercy and unravel with love, since we cannot contradict the Lord, who says that David in spirit calls him Lord. For without any doubt, without any difficulty, the simple and total title of this psalm is: Psalm of David. What does David say? The Lord said to my Lord: "Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies your footstool." This is what David heard.

He heard it in spirit, where we, when he heard it, did not hear it, but we believe him who declared and wrote what he heard. He certainly heard, he heard in a certain hidden place of truth, in a certain sanctuary of mysteries; there where the prophets heard in secret what they later preached openly; There David heard, with great certainty, saying: The Lord said to my Lord: "Sit at my right until I make your enemies your footstool." We know that Christ sat at the right hand of the Father after his resurrection from the dead and his ascension into heaven. This happened. We didn't see it, but we believe it; We read it in the Books, we have heard it in preaching, we retain it by faith. Hence, because Christ was the son of David, he was made Lord of David. For what was born of the line of David was so honored that he became Lord of David. You marvel at this as if this same thing did not happen in human things. If the son of any ordinary man happens to be king, will he not be lord of his father? It is even more admirable what can also happen, that not only is the son of an ordinary father who has become a king the lord of his father, but that the son of a layman who has been made a bishop is the father of his father. Therefore, for the same reason that Christ took the flesh and died in it, rose again, ascended to heaven and is seated at the right hand of the Father, in the same flesh honored and glorified in this way and changed into a celestial habit, he is also the Son of David and Lord of David. Dixit, inquit, Dominus Domino meo. Audivit hoc David, audivit in spiritu: ubi nos, quando audivit.

non audimus; sed loquenti quod audivit et scribenti credidimus. Audivit ergo prorsus, audivit in quodam secretary veritatis, in quodam mysteriorum sanctuario: ubi Prophetae in oceulto audierunt, quod in aperto praedicaverunt; ibi audivit David, who eum fiducia magna dicit, Dixit Dominus Domino meo, Sede a dextris meis, doñee ponam inimicos tuos scabellum pedum tuorum. Novimus Christum sedere ad dexteram Patris post resurrectionem a mortuis, et in cáelos ascensionem. Factum est iam; nec vidimus, sed credidimus: in Libris legimus, praedicatum audimus, fide retinemus. Unde et eo ipso quod erat filius David Christus, factus est Dominus David. Illud enim quod natum est ex semine David, ita honoratum est, ut esset et Dominus David. Ita admiraris hoc, quasi et in rebus humanis ista non fiant. Si enim contingat filium cuiusquam regem fieri patre privato, nonne erit dominus patris? Admirabilius est quod potest contingere, ut non solum rex factus privati ​​filius, dominus sit patris sui; sed episcopus factus laici filius, sit pater patris sui. Ergo et eo ipso quod carnem accepit Christus, quod in carne mortuus est, quod in eadem carne resurrexit, quod in eadem ascendit in caelum et sedet ad dexteram Patris, et in eadem ipsa carne sic honorata, sic clarifya, sic in caelestem habitum commutata, et filius est David, et Dominus est David. Secundum hanc enim dispensationem transitus Christi, etiam illud ab Apostólo dicitur: Propter quod illum exaltavit a mortuis, et donavit

At the name of Jesus, every knee of the inhabitants of heaven, earth and hell should bow. He gave him—he says—the name that is above all names. To Christ as a man, to Christ who died, rose again and ascended into heaven according to the flesh, he gave the name that is above every name, so that, before the name of Jesus, the inhabitants of heaven, earth and hell may kneel. Where will David be found other than Christ Lord? Whether he is in heaven, on earth or in hell, He who is Lord of the inhabitants of heaven, earth and hell will always be Lord of him. Let David rejoice with us, honored with the birth of his Son and freed with his power; and, rejoicing, let him say and be heard by those who rejoice: The Lord said to my Lord: "Sit at my right until I make your enemies your footstool." 8. Sit not only on high, but also in secret, standing out so that you may dominate and hiding so that you may be believed. What would be the merit of faith if what we believe were not hidden? The reward of faith is to see what we have believed before we see it. Scripture proclaims it this way: The righteous live by faith. There would be no justice (arising from) faith if what had been announced was not hidden and we believed, and by believing, we came to see it. How great, Lord, is the abundance of your sweetness, which you have hidden for those who fear you! You hid her. So they were left without it? There is no such thing, you have fulfilled those who wait for you. Admirable is the mystery of Christ seated at the right hand of the Father; It was hidden so that it would be believed, it was removed from My nomen quod est super omne nomen; ut in nomine lesu omne genu flectatur, caelestium, terrestrium et infernorum (Phil 2,9.10). Donavit, inquit, ei nomen quod est super omne nomen: Christo secundum hominem, Christo secundum carnem mortuo, resurgenti, ascendenti, donavit nomen quod est super omne nomen; ut in nomine lesu omne genu flectatur, caelestium, terrestrium et infernorum. Ubi erit David, ut non e¡ sit Dominus? In cáelo sit, in terra sit, in inferno sit; Dominus eius erit qui est Dominus caelestium, terrestrium et infernorum. Gaudeat ergo nobiscum et David, filii sui nativitate honoratus, dominatu liberatus; et gaudens dicat, a gaudentibus audiatur: Dixit Dominus Domino meo, Sede a dextris meis, doñee ponam inimicos tuos scabellum pedum tuorum. 8.

Sede, non solum in alto, sed et in oceulto: excellens ut domineris, iatens ut credaris. Quae enim esset merces fidei, nisi lateret quod credimus? Merces autem fidei est, videre quod credidimus antequam videremus. Sicut autem Scriptura personat, lustus ex fide vivit (Rom 1:17). Non ergo esset iustitia fidei, nisi esset absconditum quod praedicatum crederemus, et credendo ad videndum petveniremus. Quam enim fines multitudo dulcedinis tuae, Domine, quam abscondisti timentibus te! Ergo abscondisti, et remanserunt? Absit: Perfecisti autem sperantibus in te (Ps 30,20). Mirabile ergo mysterium Christi sedentis ad dexteram Dei: occultatum est ut crederetur, subtractum est ut speraretur. Spe enim salvi facti sumus. Spes autem quae videtur, non est spes: quod enim videt quis,

the look so that it was expected. With hope we have been saved. Alas, the hope that is seen is not hope, because what one sees, what do you expect? These are the words of the Apostle. You know it, but I remember it because of the clumsies. What does the Apostle say? With hope we have been saved. But the hope that is seen is not hope, because what one sees, what is one waiting for? Then, if we hope for what we do not see, we wait patiently. Therefore, since what is seen is not hope, you hid sweetness from those who fear you; And since we hope for what we do not see, you have fulfilled it for those who wait for you. Finally, dear brothers, listen and receive what I am going to say. Our righteousness comes from faith, and by faith our hearts are purified so that we can see what we believed. Both things are recorded, since it is written: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God; and also: With faith cleanse your hearts. Therefore, since the righteousness of faith consists in believing what you do not see and in arriving at the vision in due time by the very merit of faith, (hence) the Lord, when promising the Holy Spirit in the Gospel, says this: He will accuse the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment. What sin? Of what justice? Of what judgment? Continuing Jesus Christ himself, he exposes it and does not admit opinions of men. Of sin, he says, for not having believed in me. How many other sins did the Jews not have! And yet, as if they had this alone, he said: Of sin, for not having believed in me. This is that sin of which he says in another place: If he had not come, they would have no sin. Did you come to the righteous and make them sin sperat? Apostoli verba sunt. Recognoscitis quidem, sed propter rudes commendo. Quid ergo ait Apostolus? Spe, inquit, salvi facti sumus. Spes autem quae videtur, non est spes: quod enim videt quis, quid sperat? Si autem quod non videmus speramus, cum patientia exspectamus (Rom 7,24,25). Quia ergo quae videtur non est spes; Abscondisti dulcedinem timentibus te. Quia quod non videmus, speramus, et per patientiam exspectamus; Perfecisti sperantibus in te. Denique, charissimi, try to accipite quod dicturus sum.

Quoniam iustitia nostra ex fide est, et fide mundantur corda nostra, ut quod credidimus, videre possimus: utrumque enim positum est; et, Beati mundicordes, quoniam ipsi Deum videbunt (Mt 5,8); et, Fide mundans corda eorum (Act 15,9). Quia ergo haec est iustitia fidei, credere quod non vides, et ipso merit fidei ad visionem suo tempore perveníre; Dominus in Gospel cum promitteret Spiritum sanctum, hoc ait: Ipse arguet mundum de peccato, et de iustitia, et de indica. What sin? of what iustitia? What do I hear about? Ipse sequitur et exponit; coniecturas hominum non admittit: De peccato quidem, inquit, quia non creiiderunt in me. Quanta alia peccata Iudaeorum! Et tamen quasi hoc unum sit, ita said: De peccato quidem, quia non crediderunt in me. Hoc est illud peccatum, de quo alibi dicit: Si non venissem, peccatum non haberent (lo 15,22). Quid est hoc, Si non venissem, peccatum non haberent? Ergo ad iustos venisti, et eos peccatores fecisti? Sed exceptis alus peccatis, quae possent remitti per fidem, hoc unum peccatum nominavit, quod si non admitteretur, omnia relaxarenmr. Of sin qui-

dores? Ignoring other sins that can be forgiven by faith, he named this one sin, which, if it had not been committed, all the others would have been forgiven. Of sin, he says, for not having believed in me; and in another place: If he had not come, they would have no sin. By coming and not believing in Him, they fell into sin. If they had not committed this sin, all the others could have been forgiven by the clemency of grace sought by faith. Then (he will accuse them) of sin, for not having believed in Him; of justice, because I am going to the Father, and you will see me no more. This is justice, that you go to the Father, and they will no longer see you. This justice comes from faith, since the righteous person lives by faith, and he certainly lives by faith when he does not see what he believes. Therefore, since it belongs to justice to live by faith and no one lives by faith unless he sees what he believes, in order to establish this justice in men, that is, that they believe what they did not see, he says: [I will argue with them] about justice, because I am going to the Father, and you will no longer see me. This he says must be your righteousness, that you believe in Him whom you do not see, and thus, purified by faith, you will later see Him in whom you believed on the day of resurrection. 9. Then Christ is seated at the right hand of God; To the right of the Father is the Son in the arcana. Let's create it. In fact, these two things he says here, because God said: Sit at my right, and added: until I make your enemies your footstool, that is, under your feet. You cannot see Christ sitting at the right hand of the Father; Still, you can see how he puts his enemies under his feet. footstool? To those who, meditating on vain things, are told: Why do the nations roar and the people meditate on vain things? The kings of the earth met, and the princes united against the Lord and against his Christ, and said: Let us break their chains and shake off their yoke from us. Do not dominate us, do not subjugate us. He who dwells in heaven will laugh at them. You were an enemy; You will be under his feet or adopted or defeated. Then he sits at the right hand of God until he puts his enemies under his feet. This happened, this happens, and, if carried out slowly, this is done without ceasing. The people roared and the people meditated on vain things. The kings of the earth met and the princes united against the Lord and against his Christ; But will they, by roaring, by meditating on vain things, by banding together against Christ, succeed in ensuring that it does not come to pass: I will give you the nations as an inheritance, and the ends of the earth as your possession? It will be completely fulfilled, and, as they roar and meditate on vain things, I will give you the ends of the earth as your inheritance and your possession. They meditate on vain things; but that it might be fulfilled: I will give you the nations as your inheritance, and the ends of the earth as your possession, I know that it was not a charlatan who told me this, but the Lord. Likewise we can say in this psalm he said, not just anyone, not those who raged and pondered vain things, but: The Lord said to my Lord: "Sit at my right hand until I put your

dem, ait, quia non crediierunt in me: et alibi, Si non venissem, peccatum non haberent. Eo enim ipso quo venit et non crediderunt in eum, incident in peccatum: quod si non incidenterent, omnia caetera peccata dimitti possent per indulgentíam gratiae impetratam per fidem. Ergo de peccato, quia non crediderunt in me: de iustitia, quia ad Patrem vado, et iam non videbitis me (ib. 16,8-10). Haec est iustitia, quia ad Patrem vadis, et iam non videbunt te: haec iustitia enim ex fide est. lustus enim ex fide vivit; et tune ex fide vivit, si non videat quod credit. Quia ergo ad iustitiam pertinet ex fide vivere, et ex fide nemo vivit, nisi non videndo quod credit; ut ipsam iustitiam faceret in hominibus, id est, ut crederent quod non viderent, Ve iustitia, inquit, quia ad Patrem vado, et iam non videbitis me. Haec, inquit, erit iustitia vestra, ut credatis in eum quem non videtis, et fide mundati, eum in quem credidístis, in die resurrectionis postea videatis. 9. Sedet ergo a dextris Dei Christus, a dextris Patris Filius in occulto est: credamus. Qui habitat in caelis, irridebit eos: inimicus eras; eris sub pedibus eius, aut adoptus, aut victus. Quaere ergo quem locum habeas sub pedibus Domini Dei mi; nam necesse est ut habeas, aut gratiae, aut poenae. Sedet ergo ad dexteram Dei, doñee ponantur inimici eius sub pedibus eius. Hoc fit, hoc agitur: etsi paulatim peragitur, indesinenter agitur. Fremuerint enim gentes, et populi meditati sint inania; astiterint reges terrae, et principes convenerint in unum, adversus Dominum et adversus Christum eius: numquid fremendo, numquid meditando inania, numquid in unum adversus Christum conveniendo, efficient ut non impleatur, Dabo tibi gentes haereditatem tuam, et possessionem tuam terrae terms? Apparet, fratres, evidentissime apparet non de illo regno Christi Prophetam loqui, quo regnat semper apud Patrem, rerum Dominum quae per illum creatae sunt: quando enim non regnat in principle Verbum Deus apud Deum? Dicitur enim: "Regi autem saeculorum invisibili, incorruptibili, soli Deo honor et gloria, in saecula saeculorum" (1 Tim 1:17). "Regi saeculorum honor et gloria, in saecula saeculorum": cui "regi saeculorum? Invisibili, incorruptibili.” In eo enim quod et Christus est cum Patre invisibilis et incorruptibilis, quia Verbum eius est, et Virtus eius, et Sapientia eius, et Deus apud Deum, per quem facta sunt omnia; vocavit in aeternitatem, regnum eius incipit a Christianis; est. Why do you despair of the end of the company? The Almighty began it. The Almighty promised that he would carry out what he began. Where did it start from? I will bring forth the scepter of your power from Zion. Zion is Jerusalem. Hear from the Lord himself: It was fitting that Christ should suffer and rise from the dead on the third day. Since then he has been seated at the right hand of God the Father, where he went when he was resurrected. Sitting at the right hand of the Father, what is done to make his enemies his footstool? What is done? Hear Him, who teaches and explains it: And repentance and forgiveness of sins will be preached in His name to all nations, beginning at Jerusalem, because from Zion the Lord will bring forth the scepter of your power. The scepter of your power is the kingdom of your strength, for you will rule them with a rod of iron. The Lord will cause them to leave Zion, because they will begin at Jerusalem. 11. As soon as he has brought forth the scepter of his power from Zion, what will he do? Dominate in the midst of your enemies. Firstly, dominate among your enemies, that is, among the people who roar. But will he dominate among his enemies later, when the saints have received their glory, and the wicked their condemnation? What wonder that He then rules, when the righteous reign with Him eternally and the wicked burn in eternal torments? Is it any wonder that he then dominates? At present, in the midst of your enemies; now, now in this passing of the centuries, in this procreation and succession of human mortality; Now, as the torrent of time rolls by, the scepter of your power is straightened from Zion so that you may rule in the midst of your enemies. Dominate, dominate in the midst of the pagans, of the Jews, nipotens coepit, omnipotens se promisit impleturum esse quod coepit. Unde autem coepit? Virgam virtutis tuae emittet Dominus ex Sion. Quae Sion, ipsa est Ierusalem. Audi ipsum Dominum: Oportebat Christum pati et resurgere a moríais tertio die. Hinc sedet ad dexteram Dei Patris, resurgendo ubi Fuit. Deinde illo setente ad dexteram Patris, quid agitur? ut ponantur inimici eius scabellum pedum eius, quid agitur?

Audi illum docentem et exponentem: "Et praedicabitur in nomine eius poenitentia et remissio peccatorum per omnes gentes, incipientibus ab Ierusalem" (Le 24,46.48); quia, "Virgam virtutis tuae emittet Dominus ex Sion. Virgam virtutis tuae", hoc est regnum poíentiae tuae; quia, "Reges eos in virga ferrea" (Ps 2,9): "emittet Dominus ex Sion"; quia, "Incipientibus ab Ierusalem." 11. Cum ergo emiserit ex Sion virgam virtutis eius, quid fiet? Et laminare in medio inimicorum tuorum. Prius dominare in medio inimicorum tuorum: inter frementes gentes. Numquid enim postea cum acceperint honorem suum sancti, et suam damnationem impii, in medio inimicorum suorum dominabitur? Et quid mirum si tune dominabitur, secum in aeternum regnantibus iustis, et aeternis poenis ardentibus impiis-? quid mirum si tune? Modo in medio inimicorum tuorum, never in isto transitu saeculorum, in this propagatione et successione mortalítatis humanoe, never dum torrens temporum praeterlabítur, ad hoc direct est

of the heretics, of the false brothers. Dominate, dominate, O son of David, O Lord of David!, in the midst of the pagans, the Jews, the heretics, the false brothers. This little verse: Dominate in the midst of your enemies, we would not understand it if we did not see that it is already happening. Then sit at the right hand of God, hide yourself until the time of the nations is fulfilled for you to be believed. For thus it is written: It was fitting that heaven should welcome him until the time of reparation for the nations was fulfilled. You died to be resurrected, you were resurrected to ascend to heaven, you ascended to sit at the right hand of the Father; then you died to sit at the right hand of the Father. The resurrection is derived from death; the ascension, of the resurrection; sitting at the right hand of the Father, of the ascension; then all this derives from death. The excellence of e? This glorification is based on humility. Thus, while you are seated at the right hand of the Father, the time of the nations is fulfilled, all enemies are made your footstool; To achieve this, you will first dominate in the midst of your enemies; and to achieve this, the Lord brought forth the scepter of your power from Zion. Blindness came to the Jews so that you would die, and through your death the decree against sinners would be canceled and penitence and the remission of sins would be preached to all nations, beginning with Terusalem. The blindness of some served to enlighten others. For blindness came in part to Israel so that the fullness of the nations could enter, and thus all Israel would be saved. The blindness that partly came to Israel killed you; dead you rose again, you destroyed with your blood virga virtutis tuae ex Sion, ut domineris in medio inimicorum tuorum. Dominare, dominare in medio Paganorum, Iudaeorum, haereticorum, falserum fratrum. Dominare, dominare, fili David, Domine David, dominare in medio Paganorum, Iudaeorum, haereticorum, falserum fratrum. Dominare in medio, inimicorum tuorum. Hunc versum non recte intelligimus, si non fieri iam videmus. Sede ergo a dextris Dei, occultare ut credaris, doñee impleantur tempora gentium. Sic enim scriptum est: Quem oportebat caelum recipere, doñee impleantur tempora gentium (Act 3,21). Ut enim resurgeres, mortuus is; ut ascendes, resurrecti; ut seders ad dexteram Patris, ascendisti: ergo ut ad dexteram Patris seders, mortuus es.

De morte enim resurrectio, de resurrectione ascensio, de ascensione ad dexteram sessio: hoc totum ergo coepit a morte. Excellentia claritatis huius, príncipium habet humilitatis. Te itaque sedent ad dexteram Patris, implentur tempora gentium, ponuntur inimici omnes scabellum pedum tuorum, et ad hoc ut perveniatur, prius dominaberis in medio inimicorum tuorum: ad hoc enim virgam virtutis tuae emittet Dominus ex Sion. Ut autem morereris, et per mortem tuam deleretur chirographum peccatorum (Col 2,14), et praedicaretur poenitentia et remissio delictorum per omnes gentes, incipientibus ab Ierusalem, caecitas Iudaeorum fecít. Alus illuminandis, aliorum caecitas militavit: "Caecitas" enim "ex parte Israel facta est, ut plenitudo Gentium intraret, et sic omnis Israel salvus ièret" (Rom 11:25). "Caecitas ex parte Istael facta" occidit te; occisus resurrexisti, sanguine tuo peccata Gentium diluisti, ad dexteram Patris sedens undique relatives et ad te confugientes col-
The Messiah, king and eternal priest

the sins of the people, you gathered from all sides, sitting at the right hand of the Father, the patient and those who take refuge in You. Therefore, blindness came partly to Israel; It came so that the fullness of the nations could enter and so that all your enemies would be your footstool. This happens now. Then what? 12 {v.3J. With you is the beginning in the day of your power. What is this day of his power? When is the beginning with Him, or what principle is it, or how is the beginning with Him, since He is also the beginning? May the Lord help us so that I do not disturb me by speaking and you by hearing. Well, I see that it has already happened, and I see it with you with the eyes of faith. I also see with carnal eyes what happens, and I also hope to see with you with the eyes of faith what is to happen. What happened, what is happening and what will happen? Christ suffered, died, rose again on the third day, ascended to heaven, as we know, after forty days; He is seated at the right hand of the Father; This has already happened, we have not seen this, but we believe it. Now, what happens? He rules in the midst of his enemies, the scepter of his power having come out of Zion; This happens, this is done. The servants then saw the servant form present, and now the servants believe in Him absent. What we can perceive regarding the form of a servant while we are still servants, we believe. And this is the milk of children, which moderated the fatness of the bread by offering it through the flesh. The bread of the angels in the beginning was the Word, but so that man could eat the bread of the angels, the Creator of the angels became man. In this way the incarnate Word became receiveable, since it did legisti. "Facta est" ergo "caecitas ex parte Israel, facta est ut plenitudo Gentium intraret, et sic omnis Israel salvus ièret", et omnes inimici tui essent scabellum pedum tuorum. Sed hoc nunc, post quid? 12 [v.3]. Tecum príncipium in die virtutis tuae. Quis iste dies est virtutis eius? Quando cum illo príncipium, vel quod príncipium, vel quomodo cum illo príncipium; quandoquidem et ipse príncipium? Adiuvet Dominus, ut nec mihi dicere perturbetur, nec vobis audire. Video enim quod iam factum est, et vobíscum video oculis fidei: oculis quoque carnis video quod iam fit, rursusque oculis fidei vobiscum spero quod futurum est.

Quid ergo factum est? quid fit? what futurum is? Christus passus est, mortuus est, resurrexit tercia die, ascendit in caelum, ut novimus, quadragesimo die, sedet ad dexteram Patris: hoc iam factum est, hoc non vidimus, sed credimus. Why never fit? Dominatur in medio inimicorum suorum, emissa virga virtutis eius ex Sion; fit hoc, id agitur. Formam servi et praesentem tune viderunt servi, et absentem nunc credunt servi. {BENEANDANCES OF THE RIGHTEOUS} SERMON TO THE PEOPLE

1. I believe, brothers, that you attended to the title of this psalm and that you retain it in your memory. It goes like this: Return of Haggai and Zechariah. These prophets did not yet exist when these things were sung, since from David to the transmigration of the people of Israel to Babylon there are fourteen generations, as attested by the divine Scripture and especially by the evangelist Saint Matthew, and the reconstruction of the destroyed temple was expected to be done, according to the prophecy of the holy Jeremiah, seventy years after the captivity. After these years were completed under the empire of Darius, king of Babylon, these two prophets, Haggai and Zechariah, were flooded with the Holy Spirit, and both, one after the other, began to prophesy within the same year what seems to belong to the reconstruction of the temple, as predicted so long before. Whoever materially fixes the gaze of the heart on these facts and does not direct spiritual knowledge towards grace, resides with his thoughts in the stones of the temple, with which the visible fabric is built, made with the hands of men, and he does not become a living stone carved and adapted to that temple that the Lord first of all foreshadowed in his body when he said: Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. About another psalm 113 12 [v.l]. Not to us, Lord; not to us, but give glory to your name. This grace of the water that flows from the stone, and the stone was Christ, was given not by virtue of preceding works, but by the mercy of Him who justifies the wicked. In fact, Christ died for the wicked so that men would not seek their own glory, but the glory of the name of God. 13 [v.2]. For your mercy—he says—and your truth. Notice how these two things: mercy and truth, come together many times in Holy Scripture. By his mercy he called the wicked and with his truth he judges those who were called and did not want to come. Lest people say, "Where is your God?" At the end of the world his mercy and truth will appear when the sign of the Son of Man is seen in heaven. But then all the people of the earth will weep and will not say: Where is your God?, when it is no longer preached to them to be believed, but shown to them to be feared. 14 [v.3]. But our God is not in heaven as if, with heaven gone, He feared ruin by being left without a throne. He did everything he wanted in heaven and on earth. For your mercy and truth, so that people do not say: "Where is your God?", because we worship the invisible God, who is not known to any corporeal eye, but to the most pure eyes of the heart and of few; As if by this the Gentiles could say: "Where is their God?", since they can show their gods to the eyes, first the psalmist induced us to perceive the presence of God by his works, because, being up in heaven, he did whatever he wanted in heaven and on earth; and then, as if to say to the Gentiles; "Show us your gods" (since you do not have them), he adds: The simulacrums of the nations are gold and silver, works of the hands of men. This is as if he were saying: Even though we cannot show our God to your carnal eyes, whom you should know by his works, do not want to drag us into your vanities because with your finger you can show what you worship. It would be much more decorous for you not to have what you can show than to show the blindness of your heart in what is shown to your eyes by you. For what do you show if not gold and silver? They have simulations of bronze, wood, clay and other similar and different materials; But the Holy Spirit preferred to remember what was most precious about them, because when someone is ashamed of that which is most esteemed, it is easier for them to turn away from the veneration of what is vile. In another place in Scripture it was said of the worshipers of simulacra that they say to the wood: "You are my father"; and to the stone: "Tú me 6cilicet ac superior. Namque eum in illo dictum sit, "Non nobis, Domine, non nobis, sed nomini tuo da gloriam: super misericordia tua et veritate tua: nequando dicant Gentes, Ubi est Deus eorum?" quia invisibilem Deum colimus, qui nullorum corporeis oculis, cordibus autem paucorum mundissimis notus est: tanquam ideo possint dicere Gentes, Ubi est Deus eorum?

But so that you do not seem to be more warned because God did not call the wood and the stone, but the gold and the silver, pay attention, apply the ear of your heart to the following: The simulacra of the Gentiles are gold and silver.
