Do not lay hands on man to that from the metal that the true God made you make a false god. What do I say? A false man, whom you worship as a true God, and who, if anyone received him in his friendship instead of a man, would be considered crazy. The representation of the beauty and the imitation of the structure of the limbs attracts and drags, by a low inclination, the weak hearts of mortals. But just as you show, oh human vanity! por los que te arrastra la efigie. 2 [ v. 5 ]. Pues tienen boca, y no hablan; ojos, y no ven; oídos, y no oyen; narices, y no huelen; manos, y no palpan; pies, y no andan; no gritarán con su garganta. Luego el artífice es mejor que ellas, porquepudo fabricarlas mediante el arte y el movimiento de sus miembros; y, sin embargo, a ti te daría vergüenza adorar a tal artífice. Mejor eres You, even if you do not perform these simulations, because you do what they cannot do; the beast is better, since for this reason it was added: They will not cry out with their throat. When saying previously: They have a mouth, and they do not speak, what need was there, after having passed through all the members from the head to the feet, to speak again of the cry of the throat, unless,

As I believe, he did it because we perceive that what is commemorated by the remaining members is common to men and beasts, since they see, hear, smell, walk and some, like monkeys, feel with their hands? But what he had spoken from the mouth belongs only to man, since beasts do not speak. So that no one would refer the things that were said only to the operations of the human members, and, for the same reason, only put men before the gods of the nations, after enumerating them all, he added: They will not shout in their throat, which is also (operation) common to men and beasts. If, when he began to enumerate all the members, starting with the mouth, he had then said: "They have a mouth, and they do not cry," all the members would refer to the nature of man in such a way that the perspicacity of the listener would hardly perceive there anything in common with the beasts. But by saying, after the enumeration of the parts of the body, which seemed to have ended with the commemoration of the feet, about the mouth, what is proper to man, that they will not shout with their throat, he gives a special touch to the attention of the reader or listener so that, when asking why this was added, he sees that he is warned that he must put not only men, but also beasts, before the simulacra of people. So that, if you are ashamed to worship a beast, which God made endowed with eyes, ears, smell, movement and a voice in its throat, see how shameful it is not to worship a dumb simulacrum that lacks life and meaning, to which he added the similarity of the members so that the soul, given over to carnal sensations, would apply affection to living beauty.

qui hoc non ligno et lapidi dixerit, sed auto et argento; huc aspiciat, huc aurem cordis intendat: Simulacra Gentium argentum et aurum. Noli ergo addere manus hominum, ut ex eo metallo quod fecit verus Deus, velis facete falsum deum; imo falsum hominem, quem pro vero venereris Deo; quem quisquís pro vero nomine in amicitiam reciperet, insaniret. Ducit enim, et affectu quodam Ínfimo rapit infirma corda mortalium formae simílitudo, et membrorum imitata compago: sed sicut fabricata singula ostendis, sic ostende officia singulorum, quorum te effigies, o humano vanitas, trahit. 2 [v.5-7]. Iam ergo artifex melior est eis, quia ea potuit membrorum motu atque officio fabricare: quem tamen artificem te utique Porqueret adorare. Ne quis autem ad sola humanorum membrorum opera referret quae dicta sunt, et diis Gentium solos nomines anteponeret; post omnia subdidit, they say, Non clamabunt in faucibus suis: quod rursum hominibus pecoribusque commune est. Quod si primo dixisset, cum ab ore coepit membra percurrere, Os habent, et non clamabunt; cuneta etiam sic ad naturam hominis referrentur, nec facile ibi quidquam de communione ferarum sensus audientis adverteret. Cum vero illud de ore dixit, quod hominis proprium est, et post enumerationem partium corporis quam commemoratis pedibus terminasse videbatur, adiunxit, Non clamabunt in faucibus suis; lectorem vel auditorem fecit intentum, ut dum quaerit cur additum sit, admoneri se inveniat simulacris Gentium non tantum nomines, sed etiam belluas se debenré praeponere: ut si podert adorare bestiam, quam fecit Deus videntem, audientem, odotantem, contrectantem, ambulantem, clamantem in faucibus suis, viderent quam pudendum esset adorare mutum, et carens vita sensuque simulacrum; cui ad hoc inesset simílitudo membrorum, ut anima carnalibus sensibus dedita, quasi vivost atque animatae formae applicaret

Then how much better are the mice, and the snakes, and the other kinds of animals, which in a certain way, so to speak, judge from the simulacra of people, since, not perceiving human life in them, they do not concern themselves with their human figure! And so they often make their nests in them; and, if they are not separated by human noises or movements, they do not seek for themselves more defended dwellings. Then the man moves in such a way that he separates the living beast from his god and venerates as powerful the one who does not move and from whom he removed the best. He separated from the blind the one who sees, from the deaf to the one who hears, from the mute to the one who screams, from the immobile to the one who walks, from the insensitive to the one who feels, from the dead to the living. What do I say? Of a lower status than a dead person, since it is evident that a dead person does not live, so it is evident that he lived in another time. Therefore, without a doubt, the dead precede the god who does not live and did not live. 3. What is clearer than this, my dear brothers? What is more obvious? What child, when asked, will not answer with complete certainty that the simulacra of the Gentiles have mouths, and do not speak; eyes, and do not see, and the other things that the divine speech narrated? Then why does the Holy Spirit take great care to insinuate and inculcate these things in many places of Scripture as ignorant, as if they were not very patent and well known to all, if it is not because the beauty of the members, which is naturally seen living in animals and which we are accustomed to perceive in ourselves, although, as they affirm, it was made with skill and placed in situ emiaffectum, cum ea videret quae in suo live body at that animate feeling. Quanto ergo melius mures atque serpentes, et id genus animantium caetera, de simulacris Gentium, si ita digandum est, quodammodo iudicant, in quibus quia non sentiunt humanom vitam, non curant humanora figuram? Itaque in eis plerumque nidificant, et nisi humanis motibus deterreantur, nulla sibi habitacula munitiora conquirunt. Movet ergo se homo, ut vivostem bestiam a suo deo deterreat; et illum non se moventem, quasi potentum colit, a quo meliorem deterruit.

Deterruit enim videntem a caeco, audientem a surdo, clamantem a muto, ambulantem ab immobili, sentientem ab insensato, vivostem a mortuo, imo deteriore quam mortuo. Mortuum quippe sicut manifestum est non vívete, ita manifestum est aliquando vixisse. Quapropter deum qui nec vivit nec vixit, profecto et mortuus antecedit. 3. Quid hoc manifestius, fratres mei dilectissimi? evidentius quid? Quis puer interrogatus, non hoc certum esse responderat, quod Simulacra gentium os habent, et non loquent-ur; oculos habent, et non videbunt, et caetera quae divinus sermo contexuit? Cur ergo tantapere Spiritus sanctus curat Scripturarum plurimis locis haec insinuare atque inculcare velut inscientibus, quasi non omnibus apertissima atque notissima; nisi quia species membrorum, quam naturaliter in animantibus vivirtem videre, atque in nobismetypsis will feel consuevimus, quanquam, ut illi

ment as a sign of something, when it begins to be revered and honored by the multitude, it engenders in each one the most filthy affection of error, so that, not finding vital movement in that figure, they believe in a hidden divinity; and, therefore, seduced by the form and carried away by the authority of the wise masters whom the crowds obey, do you judge that the effigy, similar to a living body, is not found without a living inhabitant? Hence this affection or propensity of men encourages the perverse demons to retain the simulacra of the Gentiles and to spread and multiply the deadly errors due to the various fallacies of these defenders. In other places the divine Scripture addresses these deceptions so that no one says when simulacra are ridiculed: "I do not worship the visible, but the deity that invisibly dwells in them." Scripture condemns the same deities in another psalm in this way: The gods of the Gentiles are demons; but the Lord made the heavens. The Apostle also says: Idols are nothing, but what people sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons, not to God. I don't want you to become partners with demons. 4. Those who say: "I do not worship a simulacrum or demons, but I consider as a sign the corporeal effigy of that which I must worship," believe themselves to be of a purer religion; And so they explain the simulacra by saying that one symbolizes the earth, which is why they usually dedicate a temple to the earth; another symbolizes the sea, like the idol of Neptune; another the air, like that of Juno; another the fire, like that of Vulcan; another the star, like that of Venus; another the asserunt, in signum aliquod fabrefacta atque eminenti collocata suggestu, cum adorari atque honorari a multitudine coeperit, parit in unoquoque sordidissimum erroris affectum, ut quoniam in illo figmento non invenit vitalem motum, credat numen occultum; effigiem tamen vivosti corpori similem, seductus forma et commotus auctoritate quasi sapientium instituterum obsequentiumque turbarum, sine vivo aiiquo habitatore esse non putat? Hinc et mala daemonia ad possidenda Gentium simulacra talis hominum affectus invitationt, quorum praesidentium varia fallada mortiferi seminantur et multiplicantur errors.

Alus itaque locis et contra ista divinae Litterae vigilant, ne quisquam dicat, cum irrisa fuerint simulacra: Non hoc visibile coló, sed numen quod illic invisibiliter habitat. Ipsa ergo numina in alio psalmo eadem Scriptura sic damnat: Quoniam dii Gentium, inquit, daemonia; Dominus autem cáelos fecit (Ps 95.5). Dicit et Apostolus: Non quod idolum sit aliquid, sed quoniam quae immolant Gentes, daemoniis immolant, et non Deo. Nolo vossocias fieri daemoniorum (1 Cor 10,19 et 20). 4. Videntur autem sibi purgatioris esse religionis, qui dicunt: Nec simulacrum, nec daemonium coló; sed effigiem corporalem eius reí signum intueor, quam colere debeno. Itaque interpretantur simulacra, ut allio mare, significari terram, unde templum solent appellare Telluris; alio mare, sicut Neptuni simulacrum; alio aerem, sicut Iunonis, alio ignem, sicut Vulcani; alio luciferum, sicut Veneris; alio solem, alio lunam, quorum

sun, another the moon, to whose idols they impose names like that of the earth; another this or the other star, or this and the other creature, since we are not able to list them all. Well, when they again begin to be reproached for these things, because they worship bodies, and mainly the earth, the sea, the air and the fire, of which it is evident that we use, since, regarding the celestial ones, they are not so ashamed, because we cannot touch and grasp them with our body, except with the rays of the eyes, they dare to respond that they do not worship the bodies themselves, but the deities who preside over their government. But the Apostle in a sentence declares the punishment and condemnation of these, saying that they changed the truth of God into a lie and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever and ever. In the first part of this sentence he condemned the simulations, and in the second, the conjectures about the simulations. By calling, then, the effigies made by the sculptors with the names of the things that God created, they change the truth of God into a lie; and, having and worshiping the same things as gods, they serve the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever and ever. 5. Who worships or prays to the simulacrum not to be so moved that he thinks he is heard by it and hopes that what he longs for will be granted? This is why men chained with such superstitions often stand with their backs to the sun and pray to the statue they call the sun; and, upon hearing the roar of the sea behind them, they groan at the sensitive statue of Neptune, which they worship instead of the sea itself. This it does and in certain

This is achieved in this way, by force, by the shape of the members, so that the spirit that lives in the senses of the body believes that it feels the body that it sees more similar to its body than the round sun, and the waters of the sea, and everything it sees without those forms with which the beings that are used to seeing alive are endowed. Against this affection or propensity with which human and carnal weakness can be chained, the Scripture of God proposes things exceedingly known, with which it remembers and excites the minds of men, numbed by dealing with bodies (and thus it says): The simulacra of people are gold and silver. But God created gold and silver. And he adds: and works of the hands of men. Therefore, they venerate what they themselves made of gold and silver. 6. We also use, in the celebration of the mysteries, many instruments and vessels of the same material and metal, which, consecrated for this ministry, are called saints in honor of Him who is served for our health. Yet even these instruments and vessels, what are they if not works of the hands of men? However, do they have mouths and do not speak? Do they have eyes and do not see? Do we beseech them, pleading with God through them? The main cause of senseless impiety is based on the fact that the form similar to the living, which causes them to ask for it, has more force in the affections of the miserable than what is evident, the fact that it does not live; and, therefore, it must be despised by the living. More powerful are they to break the unhappy soul.

Thus, then, the psalmist continues so that what is recorded in this psalm may be carried out, namely: Let all who make them and all who trust in them become like them. Then see these with sensitive and open eyes and worship with obtuse and dead minds the simulacra that they neither live nor see. 8 [v. 9-11]. But the house of Israel waited for the Lord. The hope that is seen is not hope, because what one sees, what do you expect? If we hope for what we do not see, we wait patiently for it. But so that this patience lasts to the end, the Lord is his helper and protector. Or is it that perhaps the spiritual, by whom the carnal are instructed in a spirit of meekness, since they as superiors pray for the inferiors, already see, and, therefore, they already possess the things that are still hope for the inferiors? It is not so, because the house of Aaron also waited on the Lord. Then that they may reach out with perseverance towards the things before them and run without interruption until they have grasped that by which they are grasped, and know how they are known, the Lord is their help and protector, since both fear the Lord and have hoped in the Lord, who is their helper and their protector. 9 [v. 12-13]. For we did not anticipate the mercy of God with our merits, but the Lord remembered

of us and blessed us. He blessed the house of Israel, he blessed the house of Aaron. Blessing both, he blessed all who fear the Lord. You ask: "To both?" You are answered: To the small ones and to the great ones. That is, to the house of Israel with the house of Aaron; to those of that people who believed in the Savior Jesus, since God was not pleased with all of them. Since some of them do not believe, will their disbelief nullify God's faithfulness? There is no such thing. For not all the descendants of Israel are Israelites, nor are all those who are descendants of Abraham sons, but as it is written: "The remnant will be saved." In the person of those who were to believe in Him it is said: If the Lord of hosts had not left us seed, we would have been like Sodom, and we would have been like Gomorrah. But he left seed, which multiplied and spread throughout the earth. 10 [v. l 4-18 J. Therefore the great men of the house of Aaron said, May the Lord add to you; on you and on your children. And so it came to pass, for the sons of Abraham, raised from the stones, were added to them. Sheep that were not from that fold were added so that there would be one flock and one shepherd. The faith of all nations approached, and the number not only of wise prelates, but also of obedient people increased; adding the Lord not only on the parents, who would lead others to imitate them in the service of Christ, but also on their children, who would follow in the pious footsteps of the parents. For the Apostle says thus to those whom he had begotten by the Gospel in Christ: Be imitators of me as I am of

habent, aures habent, nares habent, raanus habent, pedes habent, quam ad corrigendam quod non loquentur, non videbunt, non audient, non odorabunt, non contrectabunt, non ambulabunt. 7 [v.8]. Itaque sequitur ut illud quoque fiat quod etiam in hoc psalmo sequitur; ut scilicet, Similes Mis fiant omnes qui faciunt ea, et omnes qui conjidunt in eis. Spes" enim "quae videtur, non est spes: quod enim videt quis, quid sperat? Si autem quod non videmus speramus, per patientiam exspectamus" (Rom 8,24,25). An fortasse spirituales (a quibus carnales instruuntur in spiritu mansuetudinis, quia ipsi tanquam superiors pro inferioribus supplicant) iam vident, et illis iam res est quae adhuc inferioribus spes est? Ergo, ut etiam ipsi perseveranter extendantur in ea quae ante sunt, et perseveranter currant, doñee apprehendant in quo apprehensi sunt (Phil 3,12-14), et cognoscant sicut et cogniti sunt (1 Cor 13,12), Adiutor eorum et protector eorum est. Hoc est, domum Israel cum domo Aaron, eos utique qui ex ipsa gente crediderunt in salvatorem Iesum; quia "non in omnibus illis beneplacuit Deo (ib. 10,5). Sed si quidam illorum non crediderunt, numquid incredulitas illorum fidem Dei evacuabit? Absit (Rom 3,3). Ñeque enim omnes qui sunt ex Israel, hi sunt Israel; ñeque qui semen sunt Abraham, omnes filii": sed, sicut scriptum est, Reliquiae salvae factae sunt. Then, if we take the great ones as heaven and the little ones as earth, since the little ones growing up must be heaven, and in this same hope they must be fed with milk, then in such a way the great ones are heaven of the earth by nourishing the little ones, that they also believe that they are heaven from heaven when they think of the hope with which the little ones are nourished. But since they no longer take from man or through man, but from God himself, the purity and abundance of wisdom, they do not refuse to take charge of the infants, who certainly must be heaven, realizing from this that they are heaven of heaven even though they are still earth to whom they say: I planted, Apollo watered, but God gave the growth. To these sons of men for whom he made heaven, he who knows how to provide for the earth through heaven gave land to work on. Let heaven and earth therefore remain in their God, who made them, and live on Him, confessing Him and glorifying Him, for if they want to live on themselves, they will die, as it is written: The praise of the dead perishes as nothing. 1. We have heard, brothers, that the Holy Spirit admonishes us and exhorts us to offer the sacrifice of confession to God. Confession is either praise to God or it is about our sins. The confession by which we confess our sins to God is known to everyone, and in such a way that the common people moderately educated in the Holy Scripture believe that only this is called "confession"; and so, when the reader pronounces this word, the pious noise of those beating their chests is instantly heard. But you must note how it was said in another psalm: I will enter the place of the marvelous tabernacle, even to the house of God, with the voice of rejoicing and confession {praise} of the sound of one who keeps a feast. Here it is patently declared that the word and sound of confession does not refer to the affliction of penitence, but to the joy of a crowded festival. If anyone still doubts such evident testimony, what is to be said about that which was recorded in Ecclesiasticus: Bless the Lord for all his works; exalt his name and confess, praising him with songs of lips and with zithers; and say in this way in confession that all the works of the Lord are extremely good? Audi ergo quod sequitur: Dominus mihi adiutor, et ego despiciam inimicos meos. Ex quolibet genere inimici exsurgant, sive ex numero malorum hominum, sive ex numero malorum angelorum; in Domini adiutorio despicientur cui confitemur laudem, cui cantamus Alleluia. 5 [v.8.9]. Despectis autem inimicis, non sic mihi tanquam bonus homo se amicus opponat, ut ipse in se spem meam iubeat collocari: Bonum est enim confidere in Domino, quam confidere in homine. Nec quisquís secundum quemdam modum dici potest angelus bonus, sic a me cogitetur, ut in eo confidere debenam: nemo enim bonus, nisi solus Deus; et cum videntur adiuvare homo vel angelus, cum hoc vera dilectione

to the Lord, and he heard me in the breadth. The anguish of our tribulation is over; However, the breadth to which we pass has no end, for who will accuse God's elect? 4 [v.6-7}. The Lord is my helper; I will not fear what man does to me. Does the Church only have men as enemies? What is man given to flesh and blood but flesh and blood? But the Apostle says: Our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the princes and rulers of this world of darkness, that is, against the rulers of the wicked, who love this world, and who, therefore, are darkness, for we too were once darkness, but now we are light in the Lord. Against evil spirits, that is, against the devil and his angels, since this devil is called in another place prince of the power of the air. Then hear what follows: The Lord is my helper, and I will despise my enemies. Whatever kind of enemies arise against me, whether from men or from evil angels, I will despise them with the help of the Lord, whom I praise, to whom I sing the Hallelujah.
Ennarrations on the Psalms

love, however, is done for them by the One who made them good according to their ability. Therefore it is better to wait on the Lord than on princes. Angels are also called princes, as we read in Daniel: Michael, our prince. 6 [v. 10. 11]. All nations surrounded me, and I took revenge on them in the name of the Lord. They closely surrounded me, and I took revenge on them in the name of the Lord. What it says: All the nations surrounded me, and I took revenge on them in the name of the Lord, symbolizes the sufferings and victory of the Church. But as if wondering how he could overcome such innumerable evils, he looked at the model and said what he first suffered in his Head, adding the following: They closely surrounded me; and with reason it was not repeated by all nations, because it was only executed by the Jews. And I punished them in the name of the Lord, because then the same pious people, who constitute the Body of Christ, felt the hand of the persecutors, from whose lineage that crucified flesh was taken; but also in favor of this people it was done with immortal power by that interior divinity through the exterior flesh, everything that was carried out mortally. 7 [v. 12]. They surrounded me like bees surround the honeycomb; and they caught fire like fire in the thorns, and I took vengeance on them in the name of the Lord. Here the discourse is interwoven following the order of the events. Because we rightly understand that the Lord himself, Head of the Church, was surrounded by persecutors as bees surround the honeycomb. What was carried out by the ignorant, the Holy Spirit declares faciunt, ille per eos facit, qui eos pro moda eorum bonds fecit. Bonum est ergo sperare in Dominum, quam sperare in principes. Nam et Angelí dicti sunt principes, sicut in Daniele legimus, Michael princeps vester (Dan 12:1). 6 [v.10.11]. "Omnes gentes circumdederunt me, et in nomine Domini ultus sum eos: circumdantes circumdederunt me, et in nomine Domini ultus sum eos."

Quod ait, "Omnes gentes circumdederunt me, et in nomine Domini ultus sum eos", significat Ecclesiae labores atque victoriam; sed quasi causa quaereretur unde tanta mala surpasse potuerit, respectum est ad exemplum, et dixit quid primo passa sit in capite suo, addendo quod sequitur, Circumdantes circumdederunt me: et bene ibi non repetitum est, omnes gentes; quod a Iudaeis solis factum est. Et in nomine Domini ultus sum eos: quia illic ipse pius populus, quod est corpus Christi, persecutors sensit, de quorum genere caro illa suscepta et suspensa est, et pro quo factum est quidquid ab illa interiore divinitate per exteriorem carnem virtute immortali mortaliter factum est. 7 [v.12]. "Circumdederunt me sicut apes favum, et exarserunt sicut ignis in spinis, et in nomine Domini ultus sum eos." Hic iam ex ordine gestarum rerum, etiam verborum ordo contexitur. Nam ipsum Dominum caput Ecclesiae recte accipimus circumdatum a persecutoribus, sicut circumdant apes favum. Quid enim ab ignorantibus gestum sit, mystica subtilitate Spiritus sanctus loquitur. Mel quippe apes operantur in favis:

with mystical delicacy. The bees certainly work the honey in the combs; Well, the ignorant persecutors of the Lord made him for us through the sweetest passion, so that we may taste and see how gentle the Lord is, who died for our sins and rose again for our justification. What follows: and they became enraged or enraged like fire in the thorns, is best understood as what happened in his Body, that is, in his people spread throughout the whole world, whom all nations surrounded, since he was gathered from all nations. They became enraged, then, like fire in the thorns when they burned with the fire of persecution the sinful flesh and the most annoying affections of this mortal life. And I took revenge on them in the name of the Lord, either because they themselves, having extinguished their malice, with which they persecuted the righteous, were associated with the Christian people, or also because the rest of them, who at this time despised the mercy of the one who called them, will finally perceive the truth of the one who will judge them. 8 [v. 13]. Like a heap of sand, I was pushed to fall, but the Lord protected me. Even if the multitude of believers were already great, so that they should be compared to the innumerable sand, and were gathered together in a single community like a heap of sand, yet what is man if you do not remember him? He did not say: "The multitude of people could not overcome the abundance of miturba", but the Lord protected me. The persecution of the people was not able to push to the point of overthrowing the multitude of the faithful who live together in unity of faith when they believe in him who supports nescientes autem persecutors Domini, fecerunt eum nobis ipsa passione dulciorem; ut gustamus et videamus quam suavis est Dominus (Ps 33,9), qui mortuus est propter delicta nostra, et resurrexit propter iustificationem nostram (Rom 4,25). Iam vero quod sequitur, Et exarserunt velut ignis in spinis: in eius corpore, hoc est, in populo ubique diffuso melius intelligirur; quem circumdederunt omnes gentes, cum sit collectus de omnibus gentibus. Exarserunt quippe velut ignis in spinis, quando peccatricem carnem atque huius mortalis vitae molestissimas compunctiones, persecutionis fuego cremaverunt.

Et in nomine, inquit, Domini ultus sum eos: sive quia et ipsi, malitia quae in eis iustos persequebatur exstincta, christiano populo sociati sunt; sive quia caeteris eorum qui contempserunt hoc tempore vocantis misericordis, veritatem iudicantis in fine sensuri sunt. 8 [v.13]. Tanquam cumulus arenae impulsus sum ut caderem, et Dominus suscepit me. Quamvis enim esset iam magna multitudo credentium, quasi arenae innumerabili comparanda, et in unam societatem tanquam in cumulum ducta; also quid est homo, nisi quod memor es eius? (Ps 8,5). Non dixit, Abundantiam numeri mei, numeras gentium superare non valuit; thirst, Dominus, inquit, suscepit me. Multitudinem ergo fidelium in unitate fidei sinrul habitantem persecutio gentium quo impelleret, ut deiiceret, non habebat: quando in eum creditum est, qui et
Ennarrations on Psalms

everyone and everyone everywhere, because he can never abandon those who call on him. 9 [v. 14]. The Lord is my strength and my praise and he became my health. Who falls when pushed? Those who want to be their strength and praise for themselves. No one falls in the fight but he from whom his strength and praise fell. Therefore, he to whom the Lord is strength and praise does not fall, just as the Lord does not fall. Their health was made for them not because they became something that was not before, but because they, by believing in Him, became what they were not; and, therefore, no longer for Him, but for them, it began to be health; It began to be health for the converts, because it was not far from the separated ones. 10 [v. 15). Voice of joy and health in the tents of the righteous, in which they believed that there were only sobs of sadness and destruction those who raged against the bodies of the saints, since they did not perceive the interior joys of the saints coming from hope in the future. Hence the Apostle also says: As sad, but always happy; and also: Not only this, but we also glory in tribulations. 11 [v. 16]. The right hand of the Lord has done mighty things. What do you call feats? The right hand of the Lord lifted me up. It is a great feat to exalt the humble, deify the mortal, perfect the weak, give glory to the abject, victory to the suffering and help in tribulation so that the true health of God would be evident in the afflicted and the vain health of man would remain in those who afflict. Great is this feat; but what do you admire? Oi que lo resigulos et omnes et ubique susciperet; quia eis invokentibus nusquam deesse potuisset. 9 [v.14]. Fortitudo mea et laudalio mea Dominas; et factus est mihi in salutem-. Qui ergo cadunt, cum impelluntur, nisi qui sua sibi fortitudo, et sua sibi volunt esse laudatio? Nullus quippe in certamine cadit, nisi cuius fortitudo et laudatio cadit. Quapropter cuíus fortitudo et laudatio est Dominus, tam non cadit quam non cadit Dominus. Et ideo eis factus est in salutem; non quia ipse aliquid factus est quod ante non erat, sed quia ipsi cum in eum crederent, quod non erant facti sunt, et iam ipse non sibi, sed illis, quod aversis a se non erat, salus coepit esse conversis. 10 [v.15].

Vox laetitiae et salutis in tabernaculis iustorum: ubi vocem moeroris et exitii putabant esse, qui in eorum corpora saeviebant. Non enim sentiebant interiora gaudia sanctorum de spefutura. Unde et Apostolus dicit, Quasi tristes, semper autem gaudentes (2 Cor 6,10); et iterum, Non solum autem, sed etiam gloriamur, inquit, in tribulationibus (Rom 5:3). 11 ¿v.16}. Dextera Domini fecit virtutem. Quam virtutem dicit? Dextera, inquit, Domini exaltavit me. Magna virtus exaltare humilem, deificare mortalem, praebere de infirmitate perfectionem, de subiectione gloriam, de passione victoriam, I will give auxilium de tribulatione; ut afflictis vera salus Dei patesceret, affligentibus autem vana salus hominis rema-

beep. Man did not exalt himself, he did not perfect himself, he did not give himself glory, he did not conquer, he was not health for himself. The right hand of the Lord did mighty things. 12 [v. l 7 j. I will not die, but I will live and tell the works of the Lord. As they carried the ruin of death throughout the world, they thought that the Church of Christ died, and see that it now announces the works of God. Christ is the glory of the blessed martyrs everywhere. He conquered by whipping those who hurt, enduring the impatient and loving the cruel. 13 [v. 18]. However, tell us why you endured so many affronts in the Body of Christ, the holy Church, and! adopted town. The Lord punished me severely, but did not hand me over to death. Let not the rage of the wicked think that he could do something by his own strength, for he would not have had this power if it had not been given to him from above. Frequently, the father of a family orders his sons to be punished for being very perverse servants, so that the inheritance is reserved for the former, and the fetters for the latter. What is this inheritance? Is it gold, silver, precious stones, farms, delightful meadows? See where you enter and know which one it is. 14 [v. 19]. Open to me—he says—the doors of justice. We have heard of doors. What's inside? Entering—he says—through them, I will confess the Lord. This confession of praise is admirable even in the house of God, {for it is made) with the voice of rejoicing, and of praise, and of the sound of one who celebrates a festival. This is the eternal happiness of the righteous, for which the Neret are blessed. Magna haec; thirsty who will you look? audi quid repeat. Non homo se exaltavit, non homo se perfecit, non sibi homo gloriam dedit, non homo vicit, non homo sibi salus Fuit: Dextera Domini fecit virtutem. 12 [V.17J. Non moriar, sed vivam, et enarrabo opera Domini. At illi stragem funerum ubique facientes, Ecclesiam Christi morí arbitrabantur. Ecce never enarrat opera Domini. Locate Christus beatorum martyrum gloria est. Vicit beating ferents; kicking, impatient; diligent, wise. 13 [v.18]. Tamen cur tanta indigna pertulit corpus Christi, sancta Ecclesia, populus in adoptionem; index nobis. Bmendans, inquit, emendavit me Dominas, et morti non tradidit me. Non ergo quidquam viribus suis licuisse arbitretur fremitus impiorum: non haberet istam potestatem, nisi sibi data esset desuper.

Saepe filios paterfamilias per nequissimos servos emendari iubet; cum illis haereditatem, illis compedes praeparet. What is this Haeredites? Auri est, an argenri, an gemmarum, aut fundorum, amoenorumque praediorum? Vide qua intretur, et cognosce quid sit. 14 [v.19]. Aperite, inquit, mihi portas iustitiae. Ecce audimus portas. What is intus? Ingressus, inquit, in eis confitebor Domino. Illa confessio laudis est admirabilis usque ad domum Dei, irz voce exultatioms et confessionis, soni festivitatem celebrantis (Ps 41,5): haec est aeterna
Ennarrations on the Psalms

who dwell in the house of God, praising him forever and ever. 15 [v. 20]. But see how you enter through the doors of justice. These, he says, are the gates of the Lord, through them the righteous will enter. No unjust person will enter through them into the Jerusalem that does not receive the uncircumcised and where it is said: Away with the dogs! It is enough to have dwelt in my long pilgrimage in the tents of Cedar and with those with whom, hating peace, I was peaceful. I endured the mixture of evil to the end; but these are the gates of the Lord, and only the righteous will enter through them. 16 [v.21}. I will confess to you, Lord, because you heard me and became my salvation. This confession is frequently declared to be one of praise; and, therefore, that he does not show the wound to the doctor, but gives thanks for the reception of health. The same doctor is health. 17 [v. 22]. But what do we call this one? A stone rejected by the builders, but which was here made the head of the corner to erect the two in one new man, making peace and reconciling both in one body with God, that is, circumcision and the foreskin. 18 [v.23}. By the Lord it was done to him; that is, by the Lord it was made a corner head. For, although he had not been made a cornerstone, if he had not suffered, yet it was not made by those who gave him the passion. They who were building certainly reproved him; But because the Lord builds secretly, he constituted as the head of the corner what they rejected. And it is admirable in our eyes; in the eyes intebeatitudo iustorum, qua beati sunt qui inhabitant in domo Dei, in saecula saeculorum laudantes eum (Ps 83,5). 15 [v.20]. Sed vide quemadmodum intretur in portas iustitiae. Hae portae Domini, inquit, iusti intrabunt in eas. Has saltera nemo intret iniustus, in illam Ierusalem quae non recipit incircumeisum, ubi dicitur, Canes foris (Rev 22:15). Satis sit quod in longinqua peregrinatione mea inhabitavi cum tabernaculis Cedar, et cum his qui oderunt pacem eram pacificus (Ps 119,5): pertuli usque in finem permixtionem malorum, sed hae portae Domini; iusti intrabunt in eas. 16 [v.21]. Confitebor, tibi, Domine, quoniam exaudisti me, et factus es mihi in salutem. Quam saepe ostenditur laudis esse ista confessio, non vulnera medico ostendens, sed de percepta sanitate gratias agens. Ipse autem medicus salus est.

17 [v.22]. At istum quem dicimus? "Lapidem quem reprobaverunt aedificantes": nam "hic factus est in caput anguli; ut duos conderet in se, in unum novum hominem, faciens pacem, et connecteret utrosque in uno corpore Deo (Eph 2,15.16), circumeisionem scilicet et praeputium. 18 [v.23]. A Domino factus est ei: id est, capiti anguli a Domino factus est. Quamvis enim hoc non esset factus, nisi passus esset; non tamen hoc ab eis a quibus passus est, fecit in caput;

lords of man, in the eyes of those who believe, hope for yaman; but not in the carnal eyes of those who, despising him as a man, rejected him. 19 [v. 24]. This is the day that the Lord made. This man remembers saying in an earlier psalm commemorating his ancient days: He inclined his ear to me, and in my days I called upon him. That is why he now says: This is the day that the Lord made, that is, the day in which he gave me health. This is the day of which he said: In an acceptable time I heard you and on the day of salvation I helped you; namely, this is the day on which, Mediator, he became the head of the corner. Then let us rejoice and be glad in Him. 20 [ v. 25]. Oh Lord, save me; Oh Lord, make the path prosperous. Because it is a day of health, save me; since, returning from a very long pilgrimage, we have separated ourselves from those who hated peace, with whom we were peaceful, and when we spoke to them they fought us without cause. Make the path prosperous for those who return, because you made our path. 21 [v. 26]. Blessed then is he who comes in the name of the Lord. Therefore cursed is he who comes in his own name; for the Lord says in the Gospel: I came in the name of my Father, and you did not receive me; But if another comes in his own name, you will receive him. We blessed you of the house of the Lord. I believe that this is the voice of the great to the little, that is, of those great who, as they can in this life, perceive with their minds the Word of God in God, and yet temper their speech in attention to the little ones; so that thus anguli quod illi reprobaverunt. Et est mirabiüs in oculis nostris: in oculis interioris hominis, in oculis credentium, sperantium, diligentium; non in oculis carnalibus eorum qui quasi hominem containing reprobaverunt. 19 [v.24). "Hic est dies quem fecit Dominus." Meminit iste homo se dixisse in superioribus psalmis, Quoniam inclinavit aurem suam mihi, et in diebus meis invokevi (Ps 114,2); dies suos commemorans veteres: unde modo dicit, Hic est dies quem fecit Dominus; id est, quo mihi salutem dedit. Hic est dies de quo dixit, Tempore acceptabili exaudivi te, et in die salutis adiuvi te (Is 49,8); id est, dies quo ille mediator factus est in caput anguli. Exsultemus ergo et iucundemur in eo. 20 [v.25]. O Domine, salvum me fac; or Domine, bene prospera iter vero.

Quia dies salutis est, salvum me fac: quia de longinqua peregrinatione revertentes seiungimur ab eis qui oderant pacem, cum quibus eramus pacifici, et cum loqueremur eis, debellabant nos gratis; bene prospera iter redeuntibus, quia tu nobis factus es via. 21 [v.26]. Benedictus enim qui come in nomine Domini. Maledictus ergo ille qui venit in nomine suo; sicut in Gospel dicit: Ego veni in nomine Patris mei, et non accepistis me: si alius venerit in nomine suo, illum accipietis (lo 5,43). Benediximus vos de domo Domini. Credo quod ista vox magnorum est ad pusillos, eorum scilicet magnorum qui Verbum Deum apud Deum, sicut in hae vita possunt,mente contingunt; et tamen sermonem suum propter infants temperant, ut possint sinceriter dicere
Ennarrations on the Psalms

They can sincerely say what the Apostle writes: Whether we go out with our minds for God, whether we temper ourselves for you, the love of Christ always impels us. They bless the little ones from within the house of the Lord, where there will be no lack of praise forever and ever; and, therefore, hear what they announce from there. 22 [v.27]. God is Lord and he enlightened us. The Lord, who came in the name of the Lord, whom the builders rejected and became the head of the corner; The Mediator between God and men, the man Jesus Christ, who is God equal to the Father, enlightened us so that we could understand what we believe, and thus we could preach to you who are still ignorant, but already believers. So that you may also understand: Establish a solemn holiday up to the corners of the altar, that is, to the interior of the house of the Lord, from which We blessed you and in which the prominences of the altar are found. Establish a holiday, not coldly and lazily, but solemnly. This is the voice of joy and sound of him who celebrates a festival, of those who walk in the place of the marvelous tabernacle to the house of God. For if there is a spiritual sacrifice, an everlasting sacrifice of praise, there is also an eternal priest and an eternal altar, that is, the same calm spirit of the righteous. I will tell you this more clearly, brothers. All those who want to understand the Word God, do not be content with the flesh, because the Word became flesh for their benefit so that they might be fed with milk; nor on earth be content with this festival day on which the Lamb was slain, but let it be established in the solemnities, until it comes, elevated our minds quod ait Apostolus: Sive enim mente excessimus Deo, sive temperantes sumus vobis; chantas enim Christi compellit nos (2 Cor 5,13 et 14). Ipsi benedicunt infants of the interior domo Domini, ubi laus illa in saecula saeculorum non deficit: et ideo videte quid inde annuntient. 22 [v.27]. Deas Dominas, et illuxit nobis. Dominus ille qui comet in nomine Domini, quem reprobaverunt aedificantes, et factus est in caput anguli (Mt 21,9.42); mediator ille Dei et hominum homo Christus Iesus (1 Tim 2:5), Deus est, aequalis est Patri, et illuxit nobis, ut quod credidimus intelligeremus, et vobis nondum intelligentibus, sed iam credentibus, enuntiaremus.

Ut autem et vos intelligatis, Consútuite diem festum in confrequentationibus, usqae ad cornua altaris: id est, usque ad interiorem domum Dei, de qua vos benediximus, ubi sunt altaris excelsa. Constituite diem festum, non tepide ac segniter, sed in confrequentationibus. Ipsa est enim vox exsaltationis, soni festivitatem celebrantis, ambulantium in loco tabernaculi admirabilis usque ad domum Dei. Si enim est ibi spirituale sacrificium, sempiternum sacrificium laudis, et sacerdos sempiternus est, et altare sempiternum pacata mens ipsa iustorum. Hoc apeitius dicimus, fratres: quicumque Deum Verbum intelligere volunt, non eis sufficiat caro, quod propter eos Verbum factum est, ut lacte nutrirentur; nec in terra sufficiat iste dies festus quo agnus occisus est: sed constituatur in confre-

for the Lord, within the divinity, of the One who deigned to offer those who should feed the exterior humanity with milk. 23 [v.28.29}. And what else will we sing there except his praises? What else will we say but: You are my God, and I will praise you; You are my God, and I will exalt you; I will praise you, oh Lord!, because you heard me and became my salvation? And we will not say this with the noise of words, but the love that unites us to Him utters this voice by itself, since love itself is this voice. Therefore, as the psalmist began by praising, so he ends with the same praise: Confess the Lord, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever. The psalm begins and ends with these words, since there is nothing more healthily pleasing of all that we have spoken from the beginning to the end, to which we have arrived, than the praise of God and the everlasting Hallelujah. quentationibus, quousque perveniatur, exaltatis a Domino mentibus nostris, usque ad eius divinitatem interiorem, qui nobis exteriorem humanitatem lacte nutriendis praebere dignitatus est. 23 [v.28.29]. Et quid ibi aliud, nisi laudes eius cantabimus? Quid ibi aliud dicemus, nisi, Deus meus es tu, et confitebor tibi; Deus meus es tu, et exaltabo te: confitebor tibi, Domine, quoniam exaudisti me, et factus es mihi in salutem? Non strepitu verborum ista dicemus, sed dilectio inhaerens illi per seipsam clamat istam vocem, et dilectio ipsa vox est ista. Itaque sicut coepit laudem, ita terminat: Confitemini Domino, quoniam bonus, quoniam in saeculum misericordia eius. Hinc coepit Psalmus, huc desinit; quoniam sicut ab initio quod deseruimus, ita in finem quo redimus, non est aliquid quod salubrius delectet, quam laus Dei, et semper Alleluia.
